[Lemma lem:asm-inf of arXiv:2605.19419, 'Tail exponents of the three-dimensional uniform spanning tree and Abelian sandpile'] Suppose $d\geq 3$. Then the avalanche caused by adding one grain at any fixed vertex $v$ to $H$ is $\mathbf{P}$-almost surely finite. If $N(v,x)$ denotes the number of topplings at $x$, then
\[
\mathrm{AvC}(v;H):=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^{d}:N(v,x)\geq 1\}
\]
and
\[
\mathrm{Av}(v;H):=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^{d}}N(v,x)
\]
are almost surely well defined. We abbreviate
\[
\mathrm{Av}:=\mathrm{Av}(0;H),\qquad \mathrm{AvC}:=\mathrm{AvC}(0;H).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:asm-inf of arXiv:2605.19419

[Corollary cor:FormylaT of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $T=[M]_{\mathcal{B}}^{\mathcal{B}}$ be the matrix of the operator $M$ in the basis $\mathcal{B}$. For $0\leq j\leq n-1$ 
    \[T(j, j) = 2^{-j-1}(1+(-1)^{j}) =\begin{cases}
        2^{-j} &  \text{if } j \text{ is even},\\
        0 & \text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}\]
    And, for $0\leq j< k\leq n-1$, we have
    \[ T(j, k) = 2^{-1-j}c_{n-1}(j, k) =  2^{-1-j}(-1)^{j}(n-1-j)^{\underline{k-j}}\binom{k}{j}=2^{-1-j}(-1)^j\frac{(n-1-j)!}{(n-1-k)!}\binom{k}{j}\;.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be a random vector with INDEPENDENT, mean-zero, sub-Gaussian coordinates with sub-Gaussian norms bounded by K, and let A be an n by n real matrix. Then there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every t >= 0, P( | X^T A X - E[X^T A X] | > t ) <= 2 exp( - c min( t^2 / (K^4 ||A||_F^2) , t / (K^2 ||A||_op) ) ), where ||A||_F is the Frobenius norm and ||A||_op the spectral norm. The two regimes are the sub-Gaussian one governed by the Frobenius norm and the sub-exponential one governed by the operator norm; this is the quadratic-form analogue of Bernstein's inequality and reduces to it for diagonal A. The coordinates must be INDEPENDENT and sub-Gaussian: independence cannot be weakened to uncorrelatedness, and heavier tails change the shape of the bound. E[X^T A X] equals the trace of A when the coordinates have unit variance, but in general it is sum_i A_{ii} E[X_i^2]. A standard corollary is a concentration bound for the Euclidean norm of a random vector, ||BX||_2 concentrated around ||B||_F within K^2 ||B||_op scales. [Hanson and Wright (1971); modern proof in Rudelson and Vershynin, 'Hanson-Wright inequality and sub-gaussian concentration', arXiv:1306.2872]
coordinates of X independent, mean zero, sub-Gaussian with psi_2 norms at most K
A an arbitrary real n by n matrix; no symmetry is required
c is an absolute constant

body: [Lemma 35 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $[S,T]\subseteq\Rsf$ be an interval, and let $n\in\Nsf$. Let $p\in [1,3)$, let $\omega$ be a control function on interval $[S,T]$, and let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional branched rough path on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p$ and control $\omega$. Let $M$ be a manifold and let $f:M\to R_n^2M$ be a compactly supported admissible rough velocity field. Then there exists $\varepsilon\in (0,\infty)$ such that for every $Y_0\in M$ and every $S_0\in [S,T]$, there exists an integral curve $Y: [S_0, (S_0+\varepsilon)\wedge t]\to M$ of $f$ driven by $X$ that satisfies $Y(S_0)=Y_0$.

[Theorem 36 (Euclidean and Sol long-time limits) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(g(t)\), \(t\geq0\), be an immortal Ricci flow on the orientable total
space \(M\) of a \(\TT^2\)-bundle over \(S^1\), under the
\hyperref[par:working-cover-convention]{working-cover convention}.  Let
\(H\in\SL(2,\ZZ)\) be its monodromy, as
in Subsection~\ref{subsec:torus-bundle-conventions}.  Assume either that
\(H=I\), so that \(M\cong\TT^3\) is in the Euclidean case, or that \(H\) is
hyperbolic, so that \(M\) is in the Sol case.  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(M\) has Euclidean type (equivalently, \(H=I\)), then for every
\(m\geq0\), \(g(t)\) converges
exponentially fast in the \(C^m\)-norm of any fixed smooth background metric,
as \(t\to\infty\), to a flat metric on \(M\).
\item If \(M\) has Sol type (equivalently, \(H\) is hyperbolic), then there
are constants \(0<c_-<C<\infty\) such that
\[
        c_-\sqrt t\leq \diam(M,g(t))\leq C\sqrt t,
\]
for all sufficiently large \(t\).  In addition, the Gromov--Hausdorff limit of
\((M,t^{-1}g(t))\) is a circle.  For every basepoint
\(\widetilde m\in\widetilde M\), the lifted blowdown flows
\[
        (\widetilde M,\widetilde m,s^{-1}\widetilde g(s\tau)),
        \qquad \tau>0,
\]
converge, as \(s\to\infty\), in the pointed Cheeger--Hamilton sense to a
pointed flow isometric to the Sol expanding soliton solution
\[
        (\RR^3,0,e^{-2z}dx^2+e^{2z}dy^2+4\tau\,dz^2),
        \qquad \tau>0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Euclidean and Sol long-time limits

[Proposition prop:fixed-box-distance-rec of arXiv:2608.25201, 'Recurrence of strong-decay inhomogeneous long-range percolation clusters'] Suppose that \(G\) is stationary, ergodic, and locally finite, that its degree
measure has finite intensity, and that for all $L \geq 0$ there exists \(\eta>0\) such that
\begin{equation}

  \mathbb{P}\big(\mathcal D(R)\big)\longrightarrow1
  \qquad\text{as }R\to\infty,
\end{equation}
where
\[
  \mathcal D(R)\coloneqq 
  \left\{
    \operatorname{d}_{G}(v,w)\ge\eta|v-w|
    \text{ for all }v\in V\cap Q_L(0),\
    w\in V\cap Q_R(0)^{\mathsf c}
  \right\}.
\]
Then almost surely every connected component of
\(G\) is recurrent.

The linear single-index teacher is g=(s+t)/4 and each label has independent plus/minus 1/2 noise. Train f=m^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j.x) in BOTH layers by simultaneous GD of step 1/2 on squared residual norm divided by 8, using derivative zero at zero. Initialize w_j iid N(0,I_3) and a_j=nu epsilon_j with independent centered signs independent of label noise. Q is clean test MSE averaged over all sixteen training-noise patterns conditional on network initialization. The full limiting tangent kernel has entries [k(r)+nu^2 r kprime(r)]/4, where r=x_i.x_l and k(r)=[sqrt(1-r^2)+(pi-arccos r)r]/(2pi). Its Walsh eigenvalues satisfy lambda1~nu^2 e/(2pi), lambda2~lambda12~nu^2 e^2/(4pi), lambda0 tending to (1+nu^2)/2. Put b_h=-log(1-lambda_h/2), B=log(b1/b2). In the width-first then e-to-zero probability limit, four explicit ordered risk times in the proof have strict descent-rise-descent differences. Every maximizer on the integer interval from floor((B-1)/b1) to ceil((B+1)/b1) is interior and b1 k_peak-B tends to zero. Its leading peak time is (4pi/nu^2)e^(-1)log(2/e). [Lemma lem:CMT of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] Let $(Z^N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a binary branching process with individual birth rate $\lambda_N \geq 0$ and individual death rate $\mu_N \geq 0$. Further, let $\varphi_N$ and $b\in[0,1)$ as in Definition~(def:moderate-selection of the paper) and denote $b_N=-\log_N\varphi_N$. Lastly, let $\beta_N\geq b_N$ for all $N$, assume that $\beta:=\lim_{N\to\infty}\beta_N$ exists and let the initial conditions satisfy $Z^N(0) = \lfloor N^{\beta_N} \rfloor$.
\begin{enumerate}[a)]
    \item \emph{(Slightly supercritical case.)}   
    Assume that $\lambda_N = 1+a \varphi_N$ for some $a>0$ and some sequence $(\varphi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive numbers, and $\mu_N=1$.
   
    In case $\beta=b$ assume additionally that $N^{\beta_N}\gg \varphi_N^{-1}$. Then, for any $T,\delta>0$
    \[
      \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P} \Big(  \sup_{t \leq T} \Big| \log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ) - (\beta+at) \Big| >\delta \Big)
        = 0,
    \]
    i.e.\ $(\log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ))_{t\in[0,T]}$ converges uniformly in probability to $(\beta+at)_{t\in[0,T]}$.
    \item \emph{(Slightly subcritical case.)}  Assume that $\mu_N = 1+a \varphi_N$ for some $a>0$ and for some sequence $(\varphi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ of positive numbers, and $\lambda_N=1$.

    Let $\beta>b$ and $(\varepsilon_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a non-negative sequence tending to 0 such that $N^{-\varepsilon_N}\to0$ as $N\to\infty$.
    Then, for  $T_N := \frac{\beta_N-b_N-\varepsilon_N}{a}$ and for any $\delta>0$,
    \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}  \mathbb{P} \Big(  \sup_{t \leq T_N} \Big| \log_N(Z^N(t \varphi_N^{-1} \log N) ) - (\beta-at) \Big| >\delta \Big)=0. \]
    In particular, for any $s<\frac{\beta-b}{a}$, $(\log_N(Z^N(t\varphi_N^{-1}\log N)))_{t\in [0,s]}$ converges uniformly in probability to $(\beta-at)_{t\in [0,s]}$ as $N\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 47 (Uniform lifted Ricci--DeTurck continuous dependence) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(N\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let \(s(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\),
be a Ricci flow satisfying \(\PBG_N(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) for some \(\Lambda\geq1\).
There are constants \(\eta_{\mathrm{cd}}>0\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{cd}}<\infty\), depending only on these data and an upper bound for
\(b-a\), with the following property.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Hypotheses.}
If \(v(a)\) is a smooth Riemannian metric and
\[
 \|v(a)-s(a)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,s(a))}<\eta_{\mathrm{cd}},
\]

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Conclusion.}
Then the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(v(t)\) relative to \(s(t)\) exists on
\([a,b]\) and
\begin{equation}
 \|v-s\|_{X_s^N[a,b]}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{cd}}\|v(a)-s(a)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,s(a))}.
\end{equation}
The constants are uniform under collapse of the quotient.

body: Every real or complex m by n matrix A factors as A = U Sigma V^* (for real A equivalently U Sigma V^T with U, V orthogonal), where U is m by m unitary, V is n by n unitary, and Sigma is m by n rectangular-diagonal with nonnegative entries sigma_1 >= sigma_2 >= ... >= 0, the singular values. The columns of U and V are left and right singular vectors, the rank equals the number of nonzero singular values, and truncating Sigma to its k largest values gives a best rank-k approximation in the operator and Frobenius norms (Eckart-Young-Mirsky, in fact in every unitarily invariant norm).

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let N,P,M be positive integers with M>=N+P+1. Let U in R^(N by M) and V in R^(P by M) have independent standard real Gaussian entries, independent of each other. B=UV^T/sqrt(N) has an everywhere finite, strictly positive log-concave density on R^(N by P). Indeed stack T=[U;V]; its Wishart Gram density is proportional to det(S)^((M-N-P-1)/2) exp(-tr(S)/2) on the positive-definite cone and is log-concave. B is its scaled off-diagonal block. Prekopa marginalization preserves log-concavity under this linear projection. Every B has a positive-definite completion with diagonal blocks tI for t>sqrt(N)||B||_op; the determinant-trace bound gives fiber integrability. This is a standard consequence recorded as an unaudited supporting lemma of claim w718-T287-013 version 3, not an established novelty claim.

## 2. The Gaussian product has a log-concave density

Put h=N+P and stack the factors into the h by M Gaussian matrix
T=[U_G; V_G]. Its Wishart Gram matrix S=T T^T has density proportional to

    det(S)^k exp[-tr(S)/2], S>0,
    k=(M-h-1)/2 >= 0.                                 (3)

The density is with respect to the h(h+1)/2 independent symmetric matrix
coordinates; only a positive normalization constant is omitted. Its domain
is the convex positive definite cone. Log det is concave there, as follows
from the second directional derivative

    -tr(S^(-1)H S^(-1)H)<=0, H symmetric.

Thus (3), extended by zero outside S>0, is log-concave. Its upper-right
block is exactly U_G V_G^T. Write the block coordinates as

    S = [ A, sqrt(N) B; sqrt(N) B^T, C ].              (4)

This is an invertible linear change between symmetric S and the independent
coordinates A in Sym_N, C in Sym_P, B in R^(N by P), with a constant
positive Jacobian. Prékopa's marginalization theorem, integrating A,C,
therefore makes the B density log-concave.

The marginal is positive for every B: the fiber contains the positive
definite block matrix with A=t I_N,C=t I_P whenever
t>sqrt(N)||B||_op, together with an open neighborhood in the fiber. It is
finite for every B as well. On the positive cone, A,C are positive
definite and det(S)^k is at most ((tr(A)+tr(C))/h)^(h*k). Hence its fiber
integral is bounded by a polynomial times exp[-(tr(A)+tr(C))/2] integrated
over the two positive definite cones. This is finite, since their traces
dominate their Frobenius norms. No regularity or integrability assertion
about the marginal is being inferred from a value on a null set.

The exact marginal theorem is recorded in Saumard-Wellner, arXiv:1404.5886,
Theorem 3.3, with two proofs following it; the result is due to Prékopa.

body: In probability theory, statistics and related fields, a Poisson point process is a type of mathematical object that consists of points randomly located on a mathematical space with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another. The process's name derives from the fact that the number of points in any given finite region follows a Poisson distribution. The process and the distribution are named after French mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson. The process itself was discovered independently and repeatedly in several settings, including experiments on radioactive decay, telephone call arrivals and actuarial science.

[Lemma lem:couprLPP of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $I=\llbracket a,b\rrbracket$ for some $-\infty \le a < b \le \infty$. Take  $\{A_i,B_i\}_{i\in I}$ and $\{C_i,D_i\}_{i\in I}$ to be two families of independent random variables, such that either
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1)] $A_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$, $B_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$, $C_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$, $D_i\sim \operatorname{Exp}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$, where $\gamma_0<\gamma_1$ and $\{\beta_i\}_{i\in I}$ are real parameters, such that $\gamma_0+\beta_i>0$ for each $i\in I$; or
    \item[(2)] $A_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_0\beta_i)$, $B_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_1\beta_i)$, $C_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_1\beta_i)$, $D_i\sim \operatorname{Geo}(\gamma_0\beta_i)$, where $\gamma_0>\gamma_1$ and $\{\beta_i\}_{i\in I}$ are positive parameters, such that $\gamma_0\beta_i\in (0,1)$ for each $i\in I$.
\end{itemize}
Then these two families of random variables can be coupled so that almost surely, for any $x\le y\in I$,
\[
\max_{j\in\llbracketx,y \rrbracket} \sum_{i=x}^j A_i + \sum_{i=j}^y B_i
=
\max_{j\in\llbracketx,y \rrbracket} \sum_{i=x}^j C_i + \sum_{i=j}^y D_i .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:couprLPP of arXiv:2604.10020

[Proposition p:covario-new of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ be a real-valued random field in $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in  Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast mixing correlations as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper), bounded reduced  Palm intensity function~(equation bdedreduced of the paper), and independent of the random field $M$.
Consider empirical covariogram $\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}$ of $M$ based on $\mathcal{P}$, as in (equation e.sigma-covariogram-new of the paper), for some value $h$ and tolerance $\delta>0$ .
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
If  $M$ has $p$-moment conditions for all $p>1$ (i.e., ~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) holds with  $\zeta(x,M(x))=M(x)$) then the central limit theorem holds  for
    $(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, i.e., as $n \to \infty$

\[   ({\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) )^{-1/2}\Big( \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z
  \]
for $f\in\mathbb{B} (W_1)$, provided the random    ${\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f) = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item 
Further, if the random field $M$ and the point process $\mathcal{P}$ are  stationary (necessarily jointly so, due to their independence), with $\rho$ the intensity  of $\mathcal{P}$,
then the  expectation and variance asymptotics and multivariate central limit
theorem hold {\em mutatis mutandis} for 
$(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
as in Proposition~(expvar of the paper) and Theorem (t:multcltmarkedpp of the paper)
under $p=(2+\epsilon)-$ or $p=(4+\epsilon)$--~moment condition for $M$ i.e.,~~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with $\zeta(x,M(x))=M(x)$, respectively.
Precisely, the limiting expectation takes the form $\rho \, \bar\gamma(h)$
of~(equation e:covario-mean of the paper)
and the covariance of the empirical covariogram at two values  
$\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h)}(f)$ and $\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h')}(f)$, with $h,h'\in\mathbb{R}^d$, (and for the simplicity, we assume  the same tolerance $\delta>0$ such that $\delta<\min\{|h|, |h'|, |h-h|', |h+h'|\}$) takes the form

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac 1n {\rm Cov}(\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h)}(f)),\sigma_{n}^{\gamma(h')}(f)))=
\sigma^2(h,h')\int_{W_1}f(x)^2\,\mathrm{d} x\in (-\infty,\infty),$$

 where 

\begin{align}  
&\sigma^2(h,h') :=\\
&\quad \frac{\rho}{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}} \int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(\0) - M(y'))^2\big]\rho^{(3)}(\0, y,y')\, \mathrm{d} y \, \mathrm{d} y' \nonumber\\
&\quad +
\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\biggl(\frac1{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)\cap B_\delta(z\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(z) - M(y))^2\big] \rho^{(3)}(\0,z,y)\mathrm{d} y \nonumber\\
&\qquad +\frac1{16\theta^2_d \delta^{2d}}\int_{B_\delta(\0\pm h)}\int_{B_\delta(z\pm h')}\mathbb {E} \big[(M(\0) - M(y))^2(M(z) - M(y'))^2\big] \rho^{(4)}(\0,z,y,y') \, \mathrm{d} y \, \mathrm{d} y'  \nonumber\\
&\hspace{10cm} - \rho^2 \, \bar\gamma(h) \, \bar\gamma(h') 
\biggr) \mathrm{d} z \in (-\infty, \infty). \nonumber
\end{align}

\end{enumerate}
title: Limit theory for empirical covariogram

body: Thevenin (Vertices with fixed outdegrees in large Galton-Watson trees, Electron. J. Probab. 25 (2020), Section 6.2) conjectured that for a Galton-Watson tree T_n conditioned to have n vertices, the number N_A(n) of vertices whose outdegree lies in a fixed set A satisfies (N_A(n) - n mu_A)/sqrt(n) -> N(0, mu_A(1 - mu_A)) for every subcritical offspring law with no exponential moment and every critical offspring law with infinite variance. Both clauses are false, by a pair of explicit counterexamples (two lacunary offspring laws). Theorem 1.1: an explicit subcritical offspring law with finite third moment and no exponential moment (pi_1 = 1/4, rare atoms at H_r +- sqrt(n_r), n_1 = 256, n_{r+1} = n_r^4) for which (N_1(T_{n_r}) - n_r/4)/sqrt(n_r) converges to the Gaussian mixture (1/2)N(-a, v) + (1/2)N(a, v) with a = 0.99990793915708 and v = 1.7283757730977e-5. Theorem 1.2: a critical offspring law of infinite variance with limit (1/2)N(-1, 3/16) + (1/2)N(1, 3/16). The centering n mu_A and the scale sqrt(n) are the right ones and the limit exists along the subsequence; it is not Gaussian. Mechanism: by the cycle lemma the outdegrees are i.i.d. conditioned on their sum being n - 1, and for a lacunary tail the condensation vertex takes one of two values 2 sqrt(n) apart, each with probability tending to 1/2.

body:
[Lem 83 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $0<\epsilon < 1/2$ and any $x\in\R$,
    \[
    2\epsilon^{1/2}
    +\frac{2(|x|-1)^2}{\epsilon^{1/2}} \ge x^2-1\,.
    \]
\begin{proof}
We can suppose without loss $x\ge0$, and make the change of variables $y=x-1$. Then the desired inequality rearranges to
    \[
    \bigg(\frac{2}{\epsilon^{1/2}}-1\bigg) y^2
    - 2y+2\epsilon^{1/2}\ge 0\,.
    \]
The left-hand side is a quadratic function of $y$ which is strictly positive at $y=0$ and has negative discriminant for the range of $\epsilon$ given in the statement of the lemma. It follows that the left-hand side never reaches zero, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

solution of $\ip{q}{\xi_i}=\eta_i$, $\ip{q}{\xi_j}=\eta_j$ and

$\varepsilon>0$ some five-point strictly convex selection has

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited); independent proof, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K and 0<=ell<=r be integers. Of N contexts with K candidate facts each, d disjoint pairs each contain exactly one arbitrary A and one systematic S context; other contexts are known S. All K candidates are true in S; each A has an independent uniform random r-subset true. The factual law chooses contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Observe n iid factual samples (context,candidate) WITH exact A/S tags. After training a verifier independently supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each variable context, including S contexts, certifying identities without new orientation labels. This verifies gamma=ell/r of arbitrary truths. Let U count untouched pairs,m=U/N,beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K and alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j),alpha=alpha_ell. For known A contexts let D_j count j DISTINCT identities in the union of observed candidates and verifier truths,ell<=j<=r. Define B_j=D_j*(r-j)/(N*r),T_j=sum_{h=j}^r B_h,M=m*(2-gamma-q). For arbitrary generators g and exact-level source calibration Mis_infinity(g,p)=TV(p_Pi,g), where Pi is determined by g probability levels and p_Pi is uniform coarsening, require calibration <=c in every compatible world. For c in [0,1], the exact worst-world false-mass frontier is V(c)=alpha*((T_ell+M-c)_+ +(T_ell-c)_+)/2 +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+. The same conditional value holds for the uniform-compatible-world posterior-average game. The oracle given orientations but no extra truths has O(c)=alpha*(T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c)_+ +sum_{j>ell}(alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+. Put t=T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c. Then V-O=alpha*((t+m*(1-q))_+ +(t-m*(1-gamma))_+ -2*t_+)/2, between zero and kappa*m/2. A polynomial-representation ERM-version-space generator, starting from the posterior mean factual law and removing mass in decreasing false-risk order to a known S reservoir, attains V in every world. For fixed c, exact minimax expectation is E[V(c)], with the world-invariant histogram distribution induced by the specified sampling. At the explicitly DATA-DEPENDENT budget c_D=T_ell+m*(1-gamma), O=0 and V=kappa*U/(2N). Thus E[V(c_D)]=kappa*d/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, equal to kappa/2 times the minimax ERM classification error. For n,d>=1,N=4max(n,d), this lies between (kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and (kappa/8)*min(1,d/n). When ell=r, c_D=0 is fixed and V(c)=(kappa*U/N-c)_+/2. No matching lower rate at an arbitrary fixed c is asserted. The lower bound allows coarser score bins, but matching upper bounds here use infinity only. Untagged factual training, unequal arbitrary verifier schemes and intermediate-bin upper frontiers remain open.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:0617927194536d9fb29dc79823884209783444351d0592763a143f303914f60d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/06/0617927194536d9fb29dc79823884209783444351d0592763a143f303914f60d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:83006746c78e96a8f4eca569c934517a7ee7103f7578cf8209d631bee1667591","bundle_entry_key":"tagged-factual-vc-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-tagged-factual-histogram-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:tagged-factual-vc-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Tagged factual training plus partial truth verification

Candidate T379-C009 v2; OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT, proof (unaudited).
Targets 1/2. This draft retains factual candidate identities in training,
but STILL REQUIRES partition tags. It does not solve untagged learning.
The hardest extension is removing those tags: then a sampled pair can
remain unoriented, and the density/risk ordering below need not hold.

## Experiment and conditional histogram

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K. There are d variable pairs
with exactly one arbitrary A and one systematic S context, plus N-2d
known S contexts. S has all K candidates true; A has an independent
uniform random r-subset true. A world's factual law p chooses a context
uniformly and then a true candidate uniformly. The orientation class has
VC dimension d. Observe n iid factual samples (context,candidate), EACH
WITH its true A/S tag. Thus every touched pair's orientation is known.

After training, a perfect verifier independently supplies a uniform
ell-subset of truths in EACH variable context, 0<=ell<=r. It certifies
identities only, including ell truths in paired S contexts, without
disclosing additional orientations. Its fraction of arbitrary truths is
gamma=ell/r. Set beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K and
alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j), for ell<=j<=r. No denominator vanishes since r<K.

Let U count pairs untouched by training, m=U/N. In every known A context
let j be the number of DISTINCT candidate identities certified by the
union of its factual observations and verifier output. Repeats count
once. Then ell<=j<=r. Let D_j count known A contexts with this j, so
sum_j D_j=d-U. Put

 B_j=D_j*(r-j)/(N*r),    T_j=sum_{h=j}^r B_h.

The unknown-pair uncertified group has posterior mass
M=m*(2-gamma-q). Define alpha=alpha_ell. The proposed exact robust
Mis_infinity hallucination frontier over ALL generators, conditional on
the observed samples/tags/verifier output, is

 V(c)=alpha/2*[(T_ell+M-c)_+ +(T_ell-c)_+]
      +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+,
                                                        0<=c<=1.    (1)

Zero-mass risk groups and absent histogram entries contribute zero. The
same value holds in the specified uniform-compatible-world posterior
average game. The oracle given all orientations, but NO extra truths,
has exact value

 O(c)=alpha*(T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c)_+
      +sum_{j=ell+1}^r (alpha_j-alpha_{j-1})*(T_j-c)_+.                (2)

For T=T_ell+m*(1-gamma)-c, the exact excess is

 V(c)-O(c)=alpha/2*[(T+m*(1-q))_+
                          +(T-m*(1-gamma))_+ -2*T_+].               (3)

In particular 0<=V-O<=kappa*m/2. The data-measurable calibration
threshold c_D=T_ell+m*(1-gamma) gives O(c_D)=0 and
V(c_D)=kappa*U/(2N). This budget is DATA DEPENDENT; it is not a claim
that some unspecified fixed c achieves that equality. When ell=r,
T_ell=0 and c_D=0 is fixed, and V(c)=(kappa*m-c)_+/2.

## Posterior under actual factual observations

Put the uniform prior on orientations and random A supports. A factual
sequence with q_x samples from a known A context has likelihood
(1/(Nr))^q_x if every distinct observed identity belongs to its support,
and zero otherwise. Verifier likelihood is 1/binom(r,ell) if its
certified subset is contained in that support. Thus the posterior support
is UNIFORM over r-subsets containing the UNION of all j certified truths.
No independent multiplication of candidate events is used.

An untouched pair has no factual samples in either context. Its verifier
sets have identical likelihood in both orientations: a uniform random
r-subset followed by a uniform ell-subset of truths produces a uniform
ell-subset of [K], exactly as in S. The untouched orientations remain
independent fair bits; the rest are determined by tags.

Let mu=E[p|data] and s(y)=P(y false|data). Uncertified atoms in a known
A context with j known truths have

 mu_j=(r-j)/(N*r*(K-j)),     s=alpha_j.

Their total mu mass at that j is B_j. The untouched-pair uncertified
atoms have density mu_M=(mu_ell+1/(NK))/2 and risk alpha/2; their total
mu mass is M. Certified atoms are safe with density 1/(Nr) in known A
and (1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2 in unknown pairs. Known S atoms have density
1/(NK) and risk zero, regardless of observed identities. Since

 mu_j decreases as j grows, alpha_j increases as j grows,
 mu_j<=mu_ell<=mu_M<=1/(NK),

mu-density is nonincreasing with false risk. Equalities do not cause
problems, including ell=0 or j=r. The fixed S reservoir is nonempty.

## Lower bound with arbitrary mixed score bins

If E is any upper-risk threshold set, each inside atom has density at
most every outside atom. For every uniform coarsening Pi this implies
mu_Pi(E)>=mu(E). Proof: in each cell, the mean density inside is no
larger than outside, so averaging the entire cell cannot reduce its
inside mass. This is the l(L+H)/(l+h)>=L calculation in C008 and also
handles empty intersections.

For any arbitrary g, its score bins Pi(g) are fixed when worlds are
averaged. Linearity and finite triangle inequality give
TV(mu_Pi,g)<=E[Mis(g,p)]. Thus robust or stated posterior-average
feasibility at budget c forces g(E)>=(mu(E)-c)_+ for every upper-risk
threshold E. Express posterior false mass by the finite layer-cake
identity: a cost with risk levels 0<s1<...<sL has expectation
sum_t (s_t-s_{t-1})*g({s>=s_t}), with s0=0.

Here the lowest positive level is alpha/2 on unknown uncertified atoms,
then alpha on known-A uncertified atoms, then alpha_j as j increases.
Their posterior tail masses are T_ell+M, T_ell, and T_j. The resulting
lower bound is exactly (1). Worst-world H dominates this posterior
average. This bound covers all generators and all partitions of score
levels, with no purity, context-uniformity or plug-in restriction.

## Attainment and oracle

Begin with mu. Remove up to c mass from positive-risk groups in
DECREASING risk order, uniformly within each group; groups of zero mu
mass contribute no removal. This means known A groups in decreasing j,
then the unknown-pair uncertified group. Transfer removed mass uniformly
to the fixed S reservoir. This g is normalized, nonnegative and has
TV(mu,g) equal to removed mass, at most c. Finite layer cake or direct
piecewise mass removal gives posterior cost (1).

Every known-A context has two invariant-mass subgroups: its certified
j atoms of known p mass j/(Nr), and its remaining atoms with total
p mass (r-j)/(Nr). The construction is constant on each subgroup.
For each unknown pair, all its certified atoms have the SAME g value,
and all its uncertified atoms have the same g value, shared across
both siblings. Their pairwise p masses are fixed independently of
orientation/support. Known S context fibres stay uniform. Therefore each
exact g-level bin is a union of invariant-mass groups, even if levels
merge or vanish, and p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world.

Since g_Pi=g, TV(p_Pi,g)=TV(mu_Pi,g_Pi)<=TV(mu,g)<=c. In each removed
risk group the fraction of atoms false is exactly its posterior risk
in EVERY world: (K-r)/(K-j) in a known A group, and alpha/2 in the
unknown group. All receive equal g within group. Thus actual H equals
(1) worldwise, not just after averaging. This proves attainment for
Mis_infinity. The finite-coarse-bin lower bound is valid; its matching
upper bound is not asserted, since g need not be constant in coarse bins.

For the oracle, each formerly unknown pair has a known A context with
exactly ell certified truths and no factual observations. It contributes
mass m*(1-gamma) to B_ell; higher B_j stay unchanged. The same argument
gives (2). Subtracting (2) gives (3); split T at -m*(1-q),0,
m*(1-gamma) to check its nonnegativity and maximum kappa*m/2.

## Expected minimax and learning error

For fixed c, algorithms robustly feasible conditional on each observed
outcome have exact minimax expected value E[V(c)]. A uniform world prior

fixed world: permute sibling contexts to change orientations and rename

body:
[Proposition prop:Rfail of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] Let $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ and take the projective directions and masses
\[
\begin{aligned}
&d_0=(-1,-1,0,0),\qquad d_1=e_1,\qquad d_2=e_2,\\
&d_3=(0,0,-1,-1),\qquad d_4=e_3,\qquad d_5=e_4,\\
&d_6=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3),\qquad d_7=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
(s_0,\dots,s_7)=\tfrac1{2700}\,(399,400,401,399,400,401,100,200).
\]
Then $\sum_is_id_i=0$ and $M=\sum_is_id_id_i^{\top}\succ0$, so
Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper) realizes a whitened system in $\mathbb{R}^4$. It is a
rectangle system: its positive circuits are exactly
$\{0,1,2\}$, $\{3,4,5\}$, $\{1,4,6\}$, $\{2,5,7\}$, and no subset of at
most five directions positively spans. Its four circuit-plane energies are
$\frac49,\frac49,\frac13,\frac{167}{450}$, all below $\frac12$; and its
anchor costs satisfy
\[
\min_it_i=\tfrac{32003064046811}{144192302726400}\approx0.2219>\tfrac15,
\quad
\min_{i<j}t_{ij}\approx0.4439>\tfrac13,
\quad
\min_{i<j<k}t_{ijk}\approx1.1097>1 .
\]
Hence both branches of (equation eq:R of the paper) fail, and so do the single- and
triple-anchor variants. The system is nevertheless cheap for the selector:
the single point $0$ gives ratio about $1.2219$, and an explicit five-point
strictly convex objective on the support $\{0,4,5,6,7\}$ gives exact ratio
$\frac{2452861}{2000000}=1.2264\ldots<2$.

Let X_1, ..., X_N be real random variables (not necessarily independent) such that each X_i is centered and sub-Gaussian with parameter sigma^2 (i.e. E[exp(lambda * X_i)] <= exp(lambda^2 * sigma^2 / 2) for all lambda). Then E[ max_{1 <= i <= N} X_i ] <= sigma * sqrt(2 * log N), and for any t >= 0, P( max_{1 <= i <= N} X_i >= sigma * sqrt(2 * log N) + t ) <= exp(- t^2 / (2 * sigma^2)).
Each X_i is sub-Gaussian with parameter sigma^2
N >= 1

Let
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{\zeta(2)\pi}{XY}
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{\substack{N\in[X,X+Y]\\P\nmid N}}
\frac12H_1(-4P^kN).
\]
If $k$ is even, then
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{AP^{k/2}}{\sqrt X}
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
(PXY)^\varepsilon
\left(
\frac{P^{k/2-1}}{\sqrt X}
+
\frac{P^{k/2+1/6}X^{1/12}}{Y^{5/6}}
+
\frac{P^{k/2}Y}{X^{3/2}}
\right)
\right).
\]
If $k$ is odd, then
\[
\mathcal P_k
=
\frac{AP^{k/2}}{\sqrt X}
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
(PXY)^\varepsilon
\left(
\frac{P^{k/2-1}}{\sqrt X}
+
\frac{P^{k/2+3/38}}{Y^{16/19}}
+
\frac{P^{k/2}Y}{X^{3/2}}
\right)
\right).
\]

[Proposition 63 (Discontinuity of exact support projectors) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $e,h$ be orthonormal, put $Z=I_1(h)$, and let $Y_n=I_n(y_n)$ be normalized with
\[
 y_n\propto\Sym(h\otimes e^{\otimes(n-1)}).
\]
For
\begin{equation}
 F_n=Z+e^{-n^2}Y_n,
 
\end{equation}
one has $F_n\to Z$ in every fixed analytic Fock norm
$\sum_q\rho^{2q}(1+q)^m\norm{P_qF}_2^2$.  Nevertheless
\begin{equation}
 h\in\cN_1(F_n)\quad\text{for every }n,
 \qquad
 \cN_1(Z)=\{0\}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus $P_{\cN_1(F_n)}h=h$ while $P_{\cN_1(Z)}h=0$.

body: [Theorem mainthm2 of arXiv:2607.05418, 'On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes'] Let $\{\mathcal{C}_n\}$ be a sequence of binary linear codes of length $n$ and dual distance $d_n^\bot$. Let $\widetilde{\Phi}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$ be the $p_n \times n$ 0-1 random matrix as constructed above, with $y:=p_n/n \in (0,1)$ fixed. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$ be the Gram matrix of $\frac{2}{\sqrt{n}}\widetilde{\Phi}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$, and $\tilde{\lambda}_1$ denote the largest eigenvalue of $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathcal{C}_n}$. If $d_n^\bot \geq 5$ for all $n$, then as $n \to \infty, \tilde{\lambda}_1-(p_n+1+y)$ converges in distribution to the Gaussian distribution with mean $0$ and variance $4y$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

PRIVATE SCAR, author-recorded. A tempting argument: quasi-multiplicativity alpha_4(1,R) asymp alpha_4(1,rho) alpha_4(rho,R) makes f(R) = -log alpha_4(1,R) approximately subadditive in log R, so lim f(R)/log R exists by the de Bruijn-Erdos approximate-subadditivity lemma, giving the four-arm exponent on Z^2. The step is invalid as written: approximate subadditivity needs alpha_4(rho,R) asymp alpha_4(1,R/rho), i.e. dependence on the ratio of radii up to constants (scale invariance up to constants), which on Z^2 is exactly as unproved as the exponent; on the triangular lattice it comes from the SLE(6) computation. What quasi-multiplicativity rigorously gives is alpha_4(1,2^n) asymp prod_{k<n} alpha_4(2^k,2^{k+1}) with each factor bounded between constants by RSW; the exponent exists iff the logarithms of the dyadic factors are Cesaro convergent, which is open. So both the existence and the value (conjecturally 5/4) of the four-arm exponent on Z^2 are open, as the Garban-Steif notes state. Route refuted for the existence claim; do not reuse.

Let m>=3 and q>=2 be integers satisfying q>=sqrt(m)/ln(m). Let Z have independent uniform coordinates in [q], and let K=|Unique(Z)|. Then E[K]=q*(1-(1-1/q)^m). With C=q*(1-exp(-m/q)), P(|K-C|>2*sqrt(m)*ln(m))<=2*exp(-(ln(m))^2). In particular, K lies between C-2*sqrt(m)*ln(m) and C+2*sqrt(m)*ln(m) with probability1-negl(m), where negligible means smaller than every inverse polynomial for sufficiently large m. The restrictions m>=3,q>=2 make the logarithms and the proof intermediates valid.
Integers m>=3,q>=2; q>=sqrt(m)/ln(m).
The length-m string consists of independent uniform alphabet symbols.

 g_p=(p,q),\quad A=q/g_p,\quad x=p/g_p,

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: 'the operator −Δ' or 'the Schrodinger operator H = −Δ + V' is not defined by its formula; the domain is part of the data, and essential self-adjointness on a chosen core is a theorem, not a convention. What fails without it: two different self-adjoint operators can agree on a common dense domain, with different spectra, different semigroups and different dynamics; semiboundedness does not select a unique extension either. Counterexamples. (1) −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(ℝ) is essentially self-adjoint with closure the operator on H²(ℝ); but −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(0, ∞) in L²(0, ∞) has deficiency indices (1, 1), and its self-adjoint extensions are the Dirichlet realization {f ∈ H²(0,∞) : f(0) = 0} and the Robin family {f ∈ H²(0,∞) : f'(0) = α f(0)}, α ∈ ℝ. All extend a nonnegative symmetric operator, yet for α < 0 the Robin extension has the eigenvalue −α² with eigenfunction e^{αx}: the lower bound 0 valid on C_c^∞(0,∞) is not inherited by every self-adjoint extension. The Friedrichs extension (here the Dirichlet realization) is the one that always inherits the lower bound; the Robin extensions with α ≥ 0 happen to stay nonnegative as well, so the lower bound alone singles out nothing. (2) −d²/dx² on C_c^∞(0, 1) has deficiency indices (2, 2); the Dirichlet, Neumann and periodic realizations are distinct self-adjoint extensions with eigenvalues {(kπ)² : k ≥ 1}, {(kπ)² : k ≥ 0} and {(2πk)² : k ∈ ℤ} respectively. (3) −Δ on C_c^∞(ℝⁿ ∖ {0}) is essentially self-adjoint if and only if n ≥ 4; for n ≤ 3 removing a single point changes the operator, and the extensions in n = 3 are the point-interaction ('delta potential') Hamiltonians. Audit rule: a claim 'H is self-adjoint' must name the domain or the core, and a claim that a computation on smooth compactly supported functions determines the operator must cite an essential self-adjointness theorem (Kato-Rellich, Faris-Lavine, Nelson's analytic vectors, or a limit-point analysis).
the operator is given by a differential expression on a domain with boundary or on a punctured space
essential self-adjointness on the chosen core is not verified

[Corollary cor:hard-lower-bound of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Suppose $\bm{X}$ is in the domain of non-normal attraction of $\bm{Z}$. Then  for any measurable $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, such that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$, we have $\bm{e}_j^\intercal \bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t)\bm{e}_j \to \infty$ and $\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$ for all $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and non-decreasing functions $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$ as $t \to \infty$, respectively, it holds that
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{K}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t),\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )\notin L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(A,B\in O(d)\), let \(D_\xi \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) be a Rademacher diagonal, and
	let \(\pi\) be an independent uniform permutation on \(S_d\). Let \(0<\eta<1/2\) and set $U=AD_\xi P_\pi B$. Suppose that
	\[
	\norm{A}_\infty\norm{B}_\infty
	\le
	\frac{1}{\sqrt{d \log(d/\eta)}}.
	\]
	Then, with probability at least \(1-\eta\),
	\[
	\norm{U}_\infty
	\le
	4\frac{\sqrt{\log(d/\eta)}}{\sqrt{d}}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.18557

body: [Theorem thm:bound of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $C$ admit a cyclic cover of degree $n$ with a model (eq:model of the paper) in which $h$ is separable, and let $g\ge 2$. Then $n\le 2g+2$, and the bound is attained by $y^{2g+2}=x^2-1$. If $C$ is not hyperelliptic, then $n\le g+2$, and the bound is attained by $y^n=x^3-x$ with $3\mid n$, $n\ge 6$.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.15874, '2608.15874'] Fix $u>1$. For every $a\geq1$, writing $x=\log a$ and $c=\log u$,
\[
  \varpi([a,ua])=\frac{e+1}{2}\roundb[\bigg]{\frac{1}{e+\log(e+x)}-\frac{1}{e+\log(e+x+c)}}.
\]
The map $a\mapsto\Delta_\varpi(a,u)$ is nondecreasing on $[1,\infty)$. Moreover,
\[
  \Delta_\varpi(a,u)=\log\log a+2\log\log\log a+O_u(1), \qquad a\to\infty.
\]

[Lem flux of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$ be $p$-harmonic in $B_R(x_0)$.  For every $0<r<R$ for which the trace identity is valid,
$$
  D(r)=\int_{\partial B_r(x_0)} A v\partial_\nu u\,dS.
$$
In particular the identity holds for all small $r$ in the setting of Theorem (thm:main of the paper) below.

[Lemma 17 (\citet{brezis2011functional}, Theorem~7.3) of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Let $(E,\norm{\cd})$ be a Banach space and let $\cH:E\to E$ be globally Lipschitz; that is, there is
$L<\infty$ such that
$$
        \norm{\cH\theta-\cH\theta'}\le L\norm{\theta-\theta'},
        \qquad \theta,\theta'\in E.
$$
Then, for every $\theta_0\in E$, there exists a unique continuously differentiable function
$\vartheta:[0,\infty)\to E$ satisfying
$$
        \vartheta(t)=\theta_0+
        \int_0^t\cH\vartheta(s)ds,
        \qquad t\ge0 .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let mu and nu be sigma-finite measures on a measurable space (X, Sigma) with nu absolutely continuous with respect to mu (nu(A)=0 whenever mu(A)=0, written nu << mu). Then there exists a non-negative measurable function f = dnu/dmu, unique mu-almost-everywhere, such that nu(A) = integral over A of f dmu for every A in Sigma. f is the Radon-Nikodym derivative; the theorem is the measure-theoretic foundation of conditional expectation and of probability densities.

[Theorem of arXiv:2506.09364, 'A collection of results relating the geometry of plane domains and the exit time of planar'] Suppose $D$ is a Jordan* domain with boundary given by a Jordan* curve $\hat C$, and with complementary Jordan* domain $\tilde D$. Define a new domain $U$ by $U:=D \cup \tilde D \cup V$, where $V$ is an open subset of $C$. Suppose there are closed sets $K \subset D, \tilde K \subset \tilde D$ with the following properties.

    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\sup\{E_a[T(K^c)^p] : a \in \tilde K\} < \infty$.
        \item $\sup\{E_a[T(\tilde K^c)^p] : a \in K\} < \infty$.
        \item $\inf\{P_a(T(U)<T(\tilde K^c)): a \in K\} > 0$ or $\inf\{P_a(T(U)<T(K^c)): a \in \tilde K\} > 0$.
    \end{itemize}

    Then $bh(U) = \min\{bh(D), bh(\tilde D)\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop compactplanarlatching of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is a $\Phi$-horizontal foliation on $M$, where $\Phi$ is nonwandering and $\aleph$-obstructed, and that $\mathcal{F}$ has finitely many compact planar leaves and no degeneracy $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar minimal sets. Assume that the fine boundary multislope of $\mathcal{F}$ is of the form
    $$\big(\underset{k_\flat}{\underbrace{s_1^\flat, \dots, s_{k_\flat}^\flat}}, 
    \underset{k_\sharp}{\underbrace{t_1^\sharp, \dots, t^\sharp_{k_\sharp}}}, 
    \underset{k_\circ}{\underbrace{w^?_1, \dots, w^?_{k_\circ}}},
    \underset{k_\aleph}{\underbrace{\aleph, \dots, \aleph}}\big),$$
where
\begin{itemize}
    \item The first $k_\flat$ boundary components of $M$ are $\flat$-latching,
    \item The next $k_\sharp$ boundary components of $M$ are $\sharp$-latching,
    \item The next $k_\circ$ boundary components of $M$ are nonlatching and have unconstrained types,
    \item The last $k_\aleph$ boundary components of $M$ are of $\aleph$ type.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$\prod_{i=1}^{k_\flat} \big(s_i - \varepsilon, s_i\big) \times \prod_{i=1}^{k_\sharp} (t_i, t_i+\varepsilon) \times \{(w_1, \dots, w_{k_\circ})\} \times \mathbb{R}^{k_\aleph} \subset \mathcal{Z}(\Phi).$$
title: Prop compactplanarlatching of arXiv:2608.30031

body:
[Theorem Szarek of arXiv:2605.05193, 'Grokability in five inequalities'] Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) be even and \(n\ge 4\). Let \(x\) be distributed uniformly on
\[
\Omega_n:=\Bigl\{x\in\{-1,1\}^n:\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=0\Bigr\},
\]
and let \(a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Then
\[
c_n \sqrt{\mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\Big|^2}
\le
\mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\Big|,
\]
where
\[
c_n=\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)}}
\]
is optimal. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Balanced Szarek's inequality

body:
[Lem 61 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have $\sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0)$. 

\begin{proof}
    This is a consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-centered}.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$. Then, there exists
    \[
        (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)
    \]
    such that $\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta) = \mu$.
    Let $\tilde p$ denote the restriction of $p$ to $[q_*,1] \subseteq [q_0,1]$.
    We will argue that $(b,\sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfies the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-centered} with $q_*$ in place of $q_0$.
    Indeed, conditions~\ref{it:1.1}, \ref{it:2.1}, \ref{it:3.1}, \ref{it:4.2}, \ref{it:5.1}, and \ref{it:6.1} exactly correspond to assumptions~(\ref{i:IAMP-main-coefs}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-diffusivity}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-p}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-budget}), (\ref{i:IAMP-main-endpt}), and (\ref{i:IAMP-main-init}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}, while condition~\ref{it:1.1} also provides the additional assumption in Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-centered} that $w(t,\cdot)$ is even and $\zeta^\Ising$ is symmetric. By Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-centered}, there exists $\iota = \iota(\epsilon)$ with $\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0} \iota(\epsilon) = 0$ such that for all (sufficiently large) $N$, there exists a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$ with
    \[
        \max\Big(
            \bbW_2(\mu(\cA_N), \mu),
            \bbW_2(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N), \cP(\{\pm 1\}))
        \Big) \le \iota
    \]
and
    $\bbE[\cA_N(\bG,\bg^\aux)] = \bzero$.
    This implies $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 0$.
    Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip.q0}, we have $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;C(L,\epsilon),\iota(\epsilon))$.
    We have thus shown
    \[
        \cM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;C(L,\epsilon),\iota(\epsilon))\,.
    \]
    Thus, for $\cB_\epsilon$ as defined in \eqref{e:W2.ball.notation},
    \[
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)\Big)
        \subseteq \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;C(L,\epsilon),\iota(\epsilon))\Big)\,.
    \]
    Taking a union over $L>0$ shows
    \[
        \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)\Big)
        \subseteq \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;L,\iota(\epsilon))\Big)
        \subseteq \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;L,\tilde\epsilon)\Big)\,,
    \]
    where $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon) = \max(\epsilon,\iota(\epsilon))$.
    Since $\lim_{\epsilon\rightarrow 0} \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon) = 0$, taking an intersection over $\epsilon$ yields
    \begin{align*}
        \sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0)
        &\stackrel{\eqref{e:measure.classes.simplification.without.L0}}{=}
        \adjustlimits
        \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)\Big) \\
        &\,\,\subseteq
        \adjustlimits \bigcap_{\epsilon>0} \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}}{=} \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,0)\,. \qedhere
    \end{align*}
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 61 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Prop lim of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\phi: \Bbb R\to \Bbb R$ be bounded and continuous. For all $n\in\Bbb N,$ and all $(x_1,...,x_n)\in\Bbb R^n$, we have $$\lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \int_{\Bbb R^n } \Bbb E \bigg[ \prod_{j=1}^n Z_{0,t}^\epsilon (x_j, y_j) \bigg] \prod_{j=1}^n \phi(y_j) dy\cdots dy_n = \mathbf E_{\mathrm{BM}^{\otimes n}}^{(x_1,...,x_n)} \bigg[ e^{\sigma_p^2  \sum_{1\le i<j\le n} L_0^{W^i-W^j}(t) } \prod_{j=1}^n \phi(W^j_t)\bigg] .$$
    Here $\sigma_p^2 = \int_\Bbb R (\varphi * \varphi^{(2p-1)}(x))^2dx,$ with $\varphi$ as in Theorem (mr2 of the paper). The above convergence is uniform on compact subsets of $(x_1,...,x_n)$.

[Lem 145 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $U^k$ be the state evolution limits from \eqref{e:state.evol.U}, and let $Y$ be the solution of the SDE \eqref{e:IAMP.Y.SDE}.  Then, for all $0\le \ell\le\ubl-1$, we have
  \beq
  \bigg|\frac{\E[(U^{\ell+1}-U^\ell)^2
  ]^{1/2}}{\delta^{1/2}}
  - \E w^\ell
    (Y(q_0+\ell\delta)) \bigg|
  \le C\delta^{1/4}
  +C_0\epsilon^{1/2}
  \,,\eeq
where $C=C(L,\alpha)$ while $C_0=C_0(\alpha)$.
As a consequence, for $\gamma$ and $\prxgamma$ as defined by \eqref{eq:proxy-C-ell-delta-def}, we have
  \[\max\bigg\{
  \Big|\gamma(\ell,\delta)-
  \E w^\ell
    (Y(q_0+\ell\delta))\Big|
  ,\Big|\prxgamma(\ell,\delta)-
  \E w^\ell
    (Y(q_0+\ell\delta))\Big|
    \bigg\}
  \le C\delta^{1/4}
  +C_0\epsilon^{1/2}
  \]
for all $0\le\ell\le\ubl-1$.

\begin{proof}
We apply the state evolution recursion \eqref{eq:state-evolution-setup}, where $f_{\ell,k}$ and $a_{i,\ell,k}$ are defined by \eqref{e:u.ellp1.decomp} and \eqref{e:f.l.k.explicit}:
  \begin{align*}
  f_{\ell,k}(V[[\ell]], X[0])
  &= \ind\{k\le\ell\}
  a_k (M^\ell-M^{k-1})
  +\ind\{k\ge1\}
  \delta^{1/2} 
  b^{k-1}(\prxX^{k-1})\,,\\
  a_{i,\ell,k}
  &= \ind\{i=k\le\ell\} c_k(\epsilon)\,,
  \end{align*}
for $0\le k\le\ell+1$. It follows 
using \eqref{eq:state-evolution-setup}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:orthogonal-increments} that
  \[
  \E\Big[(U^{\ell+1,k})^2\Big]
  =\ind\{k\le \ell\}\bigg\{
  \alpha (a_k)^2 \E 
  \Big[ (M^\ell-M^{k-1})^2\Big]
  + c_k(\epsilon)^2\bigg\}
  +\ind\{k\ge1\}
  \alpha \delta \E \Big[
    b^{k-1}
      (\prxX^{k-1})^2\Big]\,.
  \]
Recall also from \eqref{eq:state-evolution-setup} that $U^{\ell_1,k_1}$ and $U^{\ell_2,k_2}$ are uncorrelated for $k_1\ne k_2$.
Summing the above calculation over $k$, and again recalling 
Lemma~\ref{lem:orthogonal-increments}, gives
  \begin{align}
  \nonumber
  &\E\Big[(U^{\ell+1}-U^\ell)^2\Big]
  = \E\Big[(U^{\ell+1})^2\Big]-\E\Big[(U^\ell)^2\Big]
  = \sum_{k=0}^{\ell+1}
  \E[(U^{\ell+1,k})^2]
  -\sum_{k=0}^\ell
  \E[(U^{\ell,k})^2]\\ 
  \nonumber
  &\qquad
  = \sum_{k=0}^\ell
  \bigg\{
  \alpha (a_k)^2 \E 
  \Big[ (M^\ell-M^{k-1})^2\Big]
  + c_k(\epsilon)^2\bigg\}
  + \sum_{k=1}^{\ell+1} 
  \alpha \delta\, \E\Big[ 
  b^{k-1}
  (\prxX^{k-1})^2\Big]\\ 
  \nonumber
  &\qquad\qquad- 
  \sum_{k=0}^{\ell-1}
  \bigg\{
  \alpha (a_k)^2 \E 
  \Big[ (M^{\ell-1}-M^{k-1})^2\Big]
  + c_k(\epsilon)^2\bigg\}
  - \sum_{k=1}^{\ell} 
  \alpha \delta\, \E\Big[ b^{k-1}(\prxX^{k-1})^2\Big] 
  \\ 
  \nonumber
  &\qquad=\alpha\,
  \E \Big[(M^\ell-M^{\ell-1})^2\Big]
  \sum_{k=0}^\ell (a_k)^2
  +\alpha\delta\,\E\Big[ b^\ell(\prxX^\ell)^2\Big]
  + c_\ell(\epsilon)^2 
  \\
  &\qquad=
  \alpha p^\ell
  \E \Big[(M^\ell-M^{\ell-1})^2\Big]
  + \alpha\delta\,\E\Big[ b^\ell(\prxX^\ell)^2\Big]
  + c_\ell(\epsilon)^2\,.
  
  \end{align}
\textbf{Note that \eqref{e:state.evol.var.increment.u} is precisely what one would naturally expect from the form of the iteration \eqref{eq:u-amp-def}, and we highlight this calculation for later use.}
Recalling \eqref{e:state.evol.x.y.increments}, we can further simplify

  = \frac{\E[(\sigma^\ell(\prxX^\ell)-1)^2]}{(p^\ell)^2}

[Lemma 5 (Lemma 3.2 in \cite{Isotropic_local}) of arXiv:2608.29872, 'Local Laws and Outlier Eigenvalues for Spiked Separable Covariance Matrices'] Let $\xi$ and $\zeta$ be families of nonnegative random variables.
\begin{itemize}
  \item[(i)] Suppose that $\xi (u,v)\prec \zeta(u,v)$ uniformly in $u\in U$ and $v\in V$. If $|V|\le n^C$ for some constant $C$, then $\sum_{v\in V} \xi(u,v) \prec \sum_{v\in V} \zeta(u,v)$ uniformly in $u$.

\item[(ii)] If $\xi_1 (u)\prec \zeta_1(u)$ and $\xi_2 (u)\prec \zeta_2(u)$ uniformly in $u\in U$, then $\xi_1(u)\xi_2(u) \prec \zeta_1(u)\zeta_2(u)$ uniformly in $u$.

\item[(iii)] Suppose that $\psi(u)\ge n^{-C}$ is deterministic and $\xi(u)$ satisfies $\mathbb E[\xi(u)^2] \le n^C$ for all $u$. Then if $\xi(u)\prec \psi(u)$ uniformly in $u$, we have $\mathbb E\xi(u) \prec \psi(u)$ uniformly in $u$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma decoupling of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] Let ${\bf x} = \{x_j\}_{j = 1}^n$ be a sequence of independent random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_j = 0$ for all $j = 1 ,\dots, n$. Let $\{{\bf B}_{{\bf i}}\}_{{\bf i}\in {\mathcal T}_n^d}$ be a multi-indexed sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Then for $1\leq t \leq \infty$
    $$
    {\mathbb E} \norm{\sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}_n^d} {\bf B}_{{\bf i}} \cdot x_{i_1} \dots x_{i_d}}_{2t} \leq d^d \cdot {\mathbb E} \norm{\sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}_n^d} {\bf B}_{{\bf i}} \cdot x_{i_1}^{(1)} \dots x_{i_d}^{(d)}}_{2t}, $$
    where  ${\bf x}^{(1)}, \dots,  {\bf x}^{(d)}$ denote $d$ independent copies of ${\bf x}$.

Let A_1, ..., A_n be pairwise independent events with p_i = P(A_i), S = sum_i p_i > 0 and Q = sum_i p_i^2. Then P(A_1 or ... or A_n) >= S^2/(S^2 + S - Q). The right side is at most 1, because Q <= S, and strictly greater than S/(1 + S), because Q > 0. Mutually independent events have union probability exactly 1 - prod_i (1 - p_i), but pairwise independence does not give that formula: for the three even-parity events on the uniform law on {000, 011, 101, 110} the union has probability 3/4, which equals this bound, while 1 - prod_i (1 - p_i) = 7/8.

body:
For integers a,b and a positive integer n, a is congruent to b modulo n, written a congruent to b (mod n), if n divides a-b. Congruence modulo n is preserved by addition and multiplication, so the residue classes form the quotient ring Z/nZ with operations induced from the integers.
a and b are integers
n is a positive integer
title: Congruence and Modular Arithmetic

To remind, P2 (V) is the set of all 2-element subsets of V. Thus, a simple graph is a pair (V, E), where V is a finite set, and E is a set consisting of 2- element subsets of V.

S(p,q,j,n) = \left( \sum_{I \in \Q_j} \left( \sum_{J \in \Q_n , J \subset I} \nu_n(J)^q \right)^{p/q} \right)^{1/p}.
$$
Then, we have
\begin{equation}
\E (S(p,q,j,n)) \lesssim b^{-j\widetilde{\tau}(p) / p  - (n-j) \widetilde{\tau}(q)/q}. 
\end{equation}
Note that $\lim_{p \rightarrow \infty} \widetilde{\tau}(p)/p =\alpha_{\min}$. Thus, in \eqref{eq:E(S(p,q,j,n))}, we adopt the convention $\widetilde{\tau}(\infty) / \infty =\alpha_{\min}  $ if $p=\infty$ or $q=\infty$.

Unreviewed draft reduction. Let T be a nonnegative integer duration, Q=P(.|E), P(E)=q>0, d>=2, and let environment events A(x,r) satisfy P_env(A(x,r))<=exp(-a r^d), a>0. Fix c>0 and r(t)=floor(c log(t+2)). Suppose eventually Q(T>t)<=epsilon_t+Q(union_{|x|_infinity<=t} A(x,r(t))), with epsilon_t>=0 and sum epsilon_t finite. A union bound gives a summable term q^(-1)(2t+1)^d exp(-a r(t)^d), hence E_Q T is finite. The classification premise for actual regeneration is unproved.

body:
[Definition 24 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix a set $\Sigma = \llbracket 1, N \rrbracket$ with $N \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, $T_1 \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, $q \in (0,1)$, and $c \in [0, q^{-1})$. A $\Sigma$-indexed geometric line ensemble $\mathfrak{L}$ on $\llbracket 0, T_1 \rrbracket$ satisfies the {\em interacting pair Gibbs property} if it is interlacing, meaning that $L_i \succeq L_{i+1}$ for all $i \in \llbracket 1, N - 1 \rrbracket$, and for any $T \in \llbracket 1, T_1\rrbracket$ and any $k\in\llbracket 1,\lfloor(N-1)/2\rfloor\rrbracket$ the following holds. Suppose that $g$ is an increasing path on $\llbracket 0, T\rrbracket$, and $\vec{y} \in \mathfrak{W}_{2k}$ are such that $\mathbb{P}(A) > 0$, where $A$ denotes the event 
$$A =\{  \vec{y} = ({L}_{1}(T), \dots, {L}_{2k}(T)), L_{2k+1} \llbracket 0,T \rrbracket = g \}.$$
Then, we have for any $\{ B_i \in \Omega(T,y_i) \}_{i = 1}^{2k}$ that 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\left( L_{i}\llbracket 0,T \rrbracket = B_{i} \mbox{ for $i \in \llbracket 1, 2k \rrbracket$} \, \vert  A \, \right) = \mathbb{P}^{T, \vec{y}, g}_{\ice; q,c} \left( \cap_{i = 1}^{2k} \{Q_i = B_i\} \right),
\end{equation}
where $\mathfrak{Q} = \{Q_i\}_{i = 1}^{2k}$ has law $\mathbb{P}^{T, \vec{y}, g}_{\ice; q,c}$.
title: Definition 24 of arXiv:2603.24616

body:
[Proposition 11 (Three-point representation of four centered moments) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(X\) be a real random variable satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \E X=0,
 \qquad
 \E X^2=v>0,
 \qquad
 \E X^4<\infty.
\end{equation}
Put
\begin{equation}
 a:=\frac{\E X^3}{v^{3/2}},
 \qquad
 b:=\frac{\E X^4}{v^2},
 \qquad
 c:=b-a^2.
\end{equation}
Then \(c\ge1\).  Define
\begin{equation}
 \alpha:=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+4c}-a}{2},
 \qquad
 \beta:=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+4c}+a}{2},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 p_-:=\frac{1}{\alpha(\alpha+\beta)},
 \qquad
 p_+:=\frac{1}{\beta(\alpha+\beta)},
 \qquad
 p_0:=1-\frac1c.
\end{equation}
These numbers are nonnegative and sum to one.  If \(Q\) has the three-point
law
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(Q=-\alpha)=p_-,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(Q=0)=p_0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(Q=\beta)=p_+,
\end{equation}
then \(\widehat X:=\sqrt v\,Q\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \E\widehat X^q=\E X^q,
 \qquad q=1,2,3,4.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 |\widehat X|
 \le2\sqrt{\frac{\E X^4}{v}}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma existence of XnR of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let the conditions in Proposition (Proposition-(q u) of the paper) hold. Then, for any $n,R\ge1$ and for any $\mathcal F_0$-measurable $\mathbb H^s$-valued random variable $\Xi$, the Cauchy problem
		(equation approximation scheme C of the paper) admits a unique solution $X_n^{(R)}(t)\in D([0,\infty);\mathbb H^s)$ such that
		\begin{align}
			X_n^{(R)}(t)-\Xi\  = \ & \int_0^t G_{n,R}(X_n^{(R)}(t')){\,\rm{d}} t'+\int_0^t \mathbf Q_{1,n} X_n^{(R)}(t'){\,\rm{d}} W(t')+\int_0^tH_R(t',X_n^{(R)}(t')){\,\rm{d}} \widetilde W(t')\notag\\
			\ & + \int_0^t\int_{|l|\le1} \Big\{\mathbf M_n\big(1,l,X_n^{(R)}(t'-)\big)-X_n^{(R)}(t'-)\Big\}\, \widetilde{\eta}({\rm d}l,{\rm d}t')\notag\\

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Asymptotic uniformity of the final discovered vertex structural calculation Result: Let K(x,y) be the probability that y is last when the walk starts at x. Automorphism equivariance and transitivity imply every row sums to1 and every column has the same sum, hence K is doubly stochastic and pi*K=pi. This proves exact uniformity after a uniform start. However K can be far from the constant matrix: on the complete graph, K(x,x)=0 and K(x,y)=1/(n-1) for y different from x, giving total-variation distance exactly1/n. Check: The complete-graph value follows by permutation symmetry of all vertices other than the start. For a generic doubly stochastic equivariant kernel, the identity kernel is a counterexample to uniform row convergence, so double stochasticity alone cannot solve the walk-specific question. Obstruction: A useful proof must exploit discovery dynamics or show decorrelation from the initial vertex. The symmetry calculation does not do this, and randomizing the initial vertex would erase the actual question.

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT, independently checked proof, T326-w697-C02 v3; reviewer claude-738954b6 PASS on this exact version recorded in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. In exactly infinite-context population training, fix d>=1, M>=1 task vectors w_i in R^d and rho>=0. Let z(w)=(w,||w||^2/d+rho), J=[I_d,0], C=(1/M)sum_i z(w_i)z(w_i)^T, and P the orthogonal projector onto range C, Q=I-P. Direct Euclidean/Frobenius gradient flow of L(G)=(1/2M)sum_i||G z(w_i)-w_i||^2, with arbitrary initial d by (d+1) matrix G_0 and no ridge, selects G_infinity=JP+G_0Q. Its right-nullspace action remains G(t)Q=G_0Q at all times. For G_0=aJ, a fixed real scalar, and a fresh standard Gaussian task independent of the pool with query covariates N(0,I_d/d), the normalized excess prediction risk is (1-a)^2[d+1-r-q+(eta-1)q(1-q)]/d, where r=rank C, q=Q_(d+1,d+1), eta=(1+rho)^2+2/d. For iid Gaussian task vectors r=min(M,d+1) almost surely. For M<=d, the bracket divided by d differs from (d-M)/d by a number in [0,(1+(eta-1)/4)/d]; for M>=d+1 it is zero. At fixed rho,a, M/d->kappa therefore gives risk ->(1-a)^2(1-kappa)_+, including kappa=1. In the square audit proxy z=w, J=I_d, the exact selector is P+G_0(I-P), with new-task risk ||(G_0-I)(I-P)||_F^2; for G_0=aI it is (1-a)^2(d-r) before division by d. This is a direct effective-matrix statement with its coordinates specified, and applies classical least-squares implicit bias. General attention-factor dynamics are not inferred from it. The written argument uses the finite-dimensional spectral limit exp(-tC)->Q and the uncentered second moment E[zz^T]=diag(I_d,eta); 1540 exact-rational checks support those calculations. Two Lean attempts timed out, so no Lean certification is asserted.
Exactly infinite context and a fixed finite task pool
Direct Euclidean gradient flow of the effective matrix; no explicit regularizer
Fresh Gaussian task independent of the pool for the risk formula
Fixed rho>=0 and a for the high-dimensional law; training time limit taken first

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A deadline-success value must carry remaining slack as well as remaining work. For a job arriving at a with size x, slack at t is a+D-t-x_remaining. Two equal-work jobs can have opposite feasibility depending on arrival age. Moreover an admission rule using only current feasibility ignores the opportunity cost of accepted work: a size close to D may be feasible now but block many later short jobs. In a finite-horizon control equation the immediate reward is a unit success at completion before the deadline, rather than the running holding cost used for mean response. Check: Check two residual-size 0.2 jobs with slacks 0.1 and -0.1: the latter cannot succeed even with immediate exclusive service. This separates a feasibility state from a workload-only state without assuming an optimal policy. Obstruction: The stationary success-maximizing policy, admissible preemption/drop rules and its verification remain unresolved.

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] There exists a unique random element \(\bm Y\) taking values in
	\(\mathcal D([0,T], (\mathscr S^\dagger )')\) such that, for every test function \(\bm f\in \mathscr S^\dagger \),
	\[
	W_t(\bm f)
	=
	\left\langle \bm Y_t,\bm f\right\rangle
	-
	\left\langle \bm Y_0,\bm f\right\rangle
	-
	\int_0^t
	\left\langle \bm Y_s,\mathcal A^\dagger\bm f\right\rangle
	\,\mathrm d s
	\]
	  and
	\[
	N_t(\bm f)
	=
	W_t(\bm f)^2
	-
	\int_0^t
	\mathcal Q_s(\bm f,\bm f)
	\,\mathrm d s
	\]
	are martingales with respect to the natural filtration. Moreover, the initial field
	\(\bm Y_0\) is a centered Gaussian field with covariance
	\[
	\mathbb E\left[
	\bm Y_0(\bm f)\bm Y_0(\bm g)
	\right]
	=
	\sigma(\bm f,\bm g),
	\qquad
	\bm f,\bm g\in\mathscr S^\dagger,
	\]
	where \(\sigma\) is the initial covariance form defined in Theorem \ref{th2.3}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 12 of arXiv:2607.23640

[Proposition 21 (Tree-graph inequality; Aizenman and Newman
\cite{AN84}) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] For all $m\ge1$ and \emph{all} $x_1,\dots,x_m\in\Z^d$ (not necessarily
distinct, and not necessarily distinct from $0$),
\begin{equation}
\tau_{m+1}(0,x_1,\dots,x_m)\;\le\;
\sum_{T\in\T_m}\ \sum_{(z_v)_{v\in V_{\mathrm{int}}(T)}\in(\Z^d)^{V_{\mathrm{int}}(T)}}
\ \prod_{\{a,b\}\in E(T)}\tau_2(w_a,w_b),
\end{equation}
where $w_0:=0$, $w_i:=x_i$ for leaves and $w_v:=z_v$ for internal vertices.
The bound holds verbatim when some of the points coincide: with the
convention that a repeated point is not repeated in the connection event,
$\tau_{m+1}(0,x_1,\dots,x_m)$ is then a connection function of the distinct
points among $0,x_1,\dots,x_m$, which is still dominated by the displayed
sum (the right-hand side only grows when leaves are placed at coinciding
positions). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 3.1 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] The process $({\bar{X}}^{\varepsilon}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ with state space $\{0,1\}$ and càdlàg trajectories defined by $\forall t\geq 0,\quad{\bar{X}}^{\varepsilon}_{t}=\sum_{k\geq 0}{\mathbf{1}}_{t\in[e_{2k+1}^{\varepsilon},e_{2k+2}^{\varepsilon})}$ converges in law to the jump Markov process $({\bar{X}}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ defined in Section 1. Notation from the paper: $X^{\varepsilon}$ is the resetting process on $[0,1)$ that follows the flow $\varepsilon\dot{x}_{t}=\varepsilon f(x_{t})+x_{t}h(x_{t})$, $x_{0}=0$, and is reset to $0$ at rate $\varepsilon^{-1}h(x_{t})$, where $f,h$ are $C^{2}$ on $[0,1]$ with $f(1)<0<f(0)$, $h(1)=0$, $h'(1)\neq 0$ and $h>0$ on $[0,1)$; $y_{*}^{\varepsilon}=1-\varepsilon^{\beta}$ with $\beta\in(0,1/2)$; $e_{0}^{\varepsilon}=0$, $e_{2k+1}^{\varepsilon}=\inf\{t\geq e_{2k}^{\varepsilon}:X_{t}^{\varepsilon}>y_{*}^{\varepsilon}\}$ and $e_{2k+2}^{\varepsilon}=\inf\{t\geq e_{2k+1}^{\varepsilon}:X_{t}^{\varepsilon}=0\}$; and $(\bar{X}_{t})_{t\geq 0}$ (Section 1) is the pure jump Markov process on $\{0,1\}$ with rate $f(0)$ to jump from $0$ to $1$ and rate $-f(1)=|f(1)|$ to jump from $1$ to $0$ (Section 1 of the paper prints this rate as $f(1)$; since $f(1)<0$, the rate is $-f(1)$, the parameter of the exponential limit of the holding time $e_{2}^{\varepsilon}-e_{1}^{\varepsilon}$ in Proposition 2.5).

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.06193, 'Peng's Maximum Principle for McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations with Common N'] We say that $\varphi \in C_b^{1,1}(\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d),\R^m)$,
    if there exists for all $\vartheta \in L^2(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^d)$ an $\cL(\vartheta)$-modification of $\partial_\mu \varphi(\cL(\vartheta))$, again denoted by $\partial_\mu \varphi(\cL(\vartheta))$, such that $\partial_\mu \varphi: \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d) \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{m\times d}$ is bounded and Lipschitz continuous, i.e. there is some $C>0$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $|\partial_\mu \varphi(\mu)(y)| \leq C$, for all $ \mu \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $ y \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and
        \item $|\partial_\mu \varphi(\mu)(y)-\partial_\mu \varphi(\mu^{\prime})(y^{\prime})| \leq C(W_2(\mu, \mu^{\prime})+|y-y^{\prime}|)$, for all $ \mu, \mu^{\prime} \in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $ y,y^{\prime} \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
    \end{enumerate}

\[
16\mid h(-pq),\qquad 16\mid h(-2pq).
\]
In particular,
\[
h(-2pq)\equiv h(-pq)\pmod{16}.
\]
Thus the class number conditions modulo $16$ in
\cite[Thm.~4.9(ii), Thm.~5.4(1)]{Qin22} do not separate the layer
\eqref{eq:layer}.

[Theorem thm:neighbourhood of arXiv:2603.16824, 'Age-dependent random connection models with arc reciprocity: clustering and connectivity'] Let \(\beta>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), \(\delta>1\), and \(\Gamma\geq 0\). Almost surely, the root \(\0\) in \(\mathscr{D}_o\) has finite degree. More precisely, for \(k\in\mathbb{N}_0\), we have 
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item 
    	   for the indegree
    	   \begin{equation*}
    		  \begin{aligned}
    		      & \mathbb{P}_o\big(\sharp\mathscr{N}^{\text{in}}=k\big)\asymp k^{-1-\nicefrac{1}{\gamma}}. 
    		  \end{aligned}	
    		\end{equation*}
    	\item 
            For the outdegree, we have, 
            \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
            	\item
            		if \(\Gamma>\gamma\), then \(\sharp\mathscr{N}^{\text{out}}\) is Poisson distributed with parameter \(\lambda\asymp \tfrac{\omega_d \delta \beta}{\delta-1}(\tfrac{1}{(\Gamma-\gamma)}+\tfrac{1}{\gamma})\), where \(\omega_d\) denotes the volume of the \(d\)-dimensional unit ball.
            	\item 
            		If \(\Gamma=\gamma\), then
            			\[
            		        \mathbb{P}_o\big(\sharp\mathscr{N}^{\text{out}}=k\big) \asymp \int_0^1 \frac{u \log(1/u)^k}{k!} \,\mathrm{d} u = 2^{-(k+1)}.
            			\]
            	\item 
            		If \(\Gamma<\gamma\), then 
            		\[
                		\begin{aligned}
               	    			& \mathbb{P}_o\big(\sharp\mathscr{N}^{\text{out}}=k\big)\asymp k^{-1-\nicefrac{1}{(\gamma-\Gamma)}}.
               	 		\end{aligned}
            		\]
            \end{enumerate} 		
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions (arXiv:2610.16069, October 2026) proves the Fourier entropy-influence inequality of Friedgut and Kalai (the spectral entropy of f is at most a constant times its total influence) for every linear threshold function f, with arbitrary real weights and arbitrary threshold; the arXiv abstract gives a constant below 8.937. The argument also gives logarithmic bounds for Boolean combinations of regular functions and for unions with bounded variable overlap, and, under arbitrary product measures, the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition for symmetric thresholds. The unrestricted FEI conjecture and the product-biased FEI+ for arbitrary weighted thresholds remain open. body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a probability-preserving system and $A: X \to M_d(\mathbb{R})$ a measurable matrix-valued function. The linear cocycle generated by $A$ over $T$ is $A^n(x) = A(T^{n-1}x) \cdots A(Tx)\,A(x)$ for $n \ge 1$, $A^0 = I$; it satisfies the cocycle identity $A^{n+m}(x) = A^m(T^n x) A^n(x)$. (If $T$ is invertible and $A(x) \in GL_d$, one also sets $A^{-n}(x) = A^n(T^{-n}x)^{-1}$.) The cocycle is (forward) integrable if $\log^+ \|A\| \in L^1(\mu)$, where $\log^+ t = \max(\log t, 0)$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm; it is two-sidedly integrable if also $A(x)$ is invertible a.e. and $\log^+\|A^{-1}\| \in L^1$. For $v \in \mathbb{R}^d \setminus \{0\}$ the (forward) Lyapunov exponent of $v$ at $x$ is $\lambda(x, v) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac1n \log \|A^n(x) v\|$ when the limit exists (in $[-\infty, \infty)$); more generally $\bar\lambda(x, v) = \limsup$. The function $v \mapsto \bar\lambda(x, v)$ takes finitely many values and satisfies $\bar\lambda(x, u + v) \le \max(\bar\lambda(x,u), \bar\lambda(x,v))$, so for each $x$ the sets $\{v : \bar\lambda(x, v) \le c\} \cup \{0\}$ are linear subspaces and form a filtration of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The prototype is the derivative cocycle $A(x) = Df_x$ of a smooth map $f$ on a manifold (trivialised bundle), whose exponents measure exponential rates of divergence of nearby orbits. Warning: $\|A^n(x)\|^{1/n}$ and $|\text{eigenvalues of } A^n(x)|^{1/n}$ are different things; Lyapunov exponents are the growth rates of SINGULAR values of $A^n(x)$, not eigenvalues, and for non-commuting products the two can differ.
T is measure-preserving on a probability space
A is measurable
integrability of log^+ ||A|| is the standing hypothesis for the multiplicative ergodic theorem

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Consider two full-space directed landscapes $\mathcal{L}^{1}$, $\mathcal{L}^{2}$.

For any $\mathcal{O} \subseteq \R^2$ and $k\in \lbr 2 \rbr$, write 
$\mathcal{L}^{k}_{\mathcal{O}} := (\mathcal{L}^{k}(x,s;y,t))_{(x,s;y,t) \in (\mathcal{O})^2_{\uparrow}}$ for the restriction of $\mathcal{L}^{k}$ to $(\mathcal{O})^{2}_{\uparrow}$.
There exists $c,C>0$ such that for all $i\in \Z$ and $n\in N$ there exist a coupling $\mathbf{P}^i_n$ of $\mathcal{L}^{1}$ and $\mathcal{L}^{2}$ under which
\begin{equation}
\mathbf{P}^i_n\left( \mathcal{L}^{1}_{\mathcal{O}^{i,1}_n} =   \mathcal{L}^{2}_{\mathcal{O}^{i,3}_n} \text{ and } \mathcal{L}^{1}_{\mathcal{O}^{i,2}_n} =   \mathcal{L}^{2}_{\mathcal{O}^{i,2}_n} \right) \geq 1 - C\exp(-cn^{2}). 
\end{equation}

body: Algebraic varieties are the central objects of study in algebraic geometry, a sub-field of mathematics. Classically, an algebraic variety is defined as the set of solutions of a system of polynomial equations over the real or complex numbers. Modern definitions generalize this concept in several different ways, while attempting to preserve the geometric intuition behind the original definition.
title: Algebraic variety

body: In Vapnik–Chervonenkis theory, the Vapnik–Chervonenkis (VC) dimension is a measure of the size of a class of sets. The notion can be extended to classes of binary functions. It is defined as the cardinality of the largest set of points that the function class can shatter—that is, for which all possible binary labelings can be realized by some function in the class. It was originally defined by Vladimir Vapnik and Alexey Chervonenkis.
title: Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension

Let N>=0 be an integer and nu a real signed Borel measure on R with all absolute polynomial moments finite. Suppose integral f(t)^2 dnu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial f of degree<=N. There are unique monic polynomials q_0,...,q_(N+1) with deg(q_i)=i which are pairwise orthogonal under nu. For each 1<=i<=N+1, q_i has i distinct real roots. For 2<=i<=N+1, the roots of q_i and q_(i-1) strictly interlace, with a root of q_i on either side of the roots of q_(i-1). Squared norms of q_0,...,q_N are positive. No positivity assertion is made for the squared norm of q_(N+1). This is Cohn-Kumar Lemma3.5.
N>=0; signed Borel measure with all absolute polynomial moments finite
strict squared-norm positivity for every nonzero polynomial of degree<=N
the family extends through degree N+1, while guaranteed positive norms extend only through degree N

[Openproblem Quenched complexity of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] The present paper concerns annealed complexity.  In energy regimes where
the Gaussian first- and second-moment exponents coincide, typical
critical-point counts are known to concentrate
[Subag,SubagZeitouni].  A second-moment/Kac--Rice route to a
non-Gaussian quenched theorem would require a comparison of two-point
functionals.  Already the non-Gaussian energy and covariance structures
depend not only on the overlap \(N^{-1}\ip\sigma\tau\) but on the joint
empirical coordinate profile
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{(\sigma_i,\tau_i)}.
\]
The full derivative jet additionally requires corresponding joint frame
profiles.  Such a variational comparison and localization analysis
remain open.  In a window with exponentially many typical points, the
natural target is a probability limit of
\(N^{-1}\log\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)\); the bounded observable
\(Q_N^J(B)\) in (equation eq:sample-log-count of the paper) instead also covers empty
windows.  By (prop:quenched-cutoff of the paper), convergence in probability of
the latter is equivalent before and after the entrywise cutoff.  This
removes quadratic-scale entries from that auxiliary problem but does not
supply the missing two-point comparison. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Quenched complexity

Draft author claim, independent review pending. On a finite simple graph G=(V,E), let u be uniform independent integer-q spins and gamma_beta its free zero-field unit-bond Potts Gibbs law. For q>=2 and beta>=0, D(u||gamma_beta)>=|E|*c_q(beta), where c_q(beta)=log((exp(beta)+q-1)/q)-beta/q. Equality holds on forests, and the bound is strict when beta>0 and G has a cycle. On Z^d boxes the limiting deficit per vertex is at least d*c_q(beta)>0 for beta>0. For any fixed full-support product law pi, an induced matching gives the alternative positive lower bound 2*(min pi)^4*tanh(beta/2)^2/(3*2^(d-1)) per vertex. Thus neither uniform nor full-support fixed product trials satisfy a vanishing-deficit hypothesis at positive beta.

integer q>=2, beta>=0
zero field and unit ferromagnetic bonds
growing n^d lattice boxes for limiting statements
full support for the nonuniform product bound
title: Product Potts trials have an extensive entropy deficit (unreviewed draft)

[Lemma 23 (Continuity of coercive half-line resolvents) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $\varrho_n\to\varrho$ in $[0,1]$, let $V_n,V\in L^\infty(\R_+)$ be real
with $V_n\to V$ in $L^\infty$, and let $g_n\to g$ in $L^2(\R_+)$.  Denote by
$\mathfrak a_n$ and $\mathfrak a$ the forms of
$-\partial_y^2+V_n$ and $-\partial_y^2+V$, respectively, with the indicated
$\varrho_n$ and $\varrho$ boundary conditions.  Suppose that, for some
$m>0$,
\[
 \mathfrak a_n[h]\geq m\|h\|_2^2,
 \qquad \mathfrak a[h]\geq m\|h\|_2^2
\]
on the corresponding form domains.  If
\[
 z_n=(-\partial_y^2+V_n)^{-1}g_n,
 \qquad z=(-\partial_y^2+V)^{-1}g,
\]
then $z_n\to z$ in $H^1(\R_+)$.  In fact the convergence is in $H^2$ and
hence in $C_b^1$.
