[Dfn 69 (generalized budget constraint) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the set $\incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ defined in Definition~\ref{d:incr.p}.
For $p\in \incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ and a generalized ``budget'' function $f \in L^1([q_0,1];[0,+\infty))$, let
$\Adm(q_0;p,f)$
denote the set of progressively measurable control processes $(b,\sigma)$, with $\sigma \ge 0$,
satisfying
    \beq
    \bbE\bigg[
    (b_t)^2 + \frac{tp'(t)}{p(t)} (\sigma_t-1)^2
    \bigg]
    \le f(t)\eeq
for all $t \in [q_0,1]$. Then let
	\[
    \cM(q_0;p,f) = \bigg\{
        \mu(q_* = q_0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta = \delta_0) : (b,\sigma)
        \in \Adm(q_0;p,f)
    \bigg\}\,,
\]
where we recall from \eqref{e:control.problems.endpoint.measures} that $\mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)$ denotes the law of $X(1)$ where $X$ is given by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main} with parameters $(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)$. (Note that in order to accommodate controls $(b,\sigma)$ where the budget constraint is only satisfied in the averaged sense of condition~\ref{it:4.1}, we allow $f$ to map into $[0,+\infty)$. On the other hand, all classes of measures that we will represent using Definition~\ref{d:X.adm} will have $q_* = q_0$ and $\zeta = \delta_0$, so we will set these parameters in the definition.)

body: Publication record. Open Problem 4.49(ii) of D. Aldous and J. A. Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, attributed to Sinclair, asks whether log n can be replaced by the diameter of the transition graph in the multicommodity flow bound on the relaxation time. For general chains the answer is negative for a simple reason (add transitions of small probability between all pairs of states of the random walk on an expander). Y. Shmalo, Multicommodity flow, the relaxation time and the diameter (2026) shows that the answer is negative also for simple random walks on graphs, for every constant and already on graphs of diameter two. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/flow-parameter-diameter (commit 243299cc4eda); ResearchGate record 414372242. Not refereed.
title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.49(ii) (Sinclair) answered negatively: the multicommodity flow parameter, the relaxation time and the diameter (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/flow-parameter-diameter)

body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.29713, '\textbf{A Cartan geometry from a correspondence space in Riemannian geometry}'] A Cartan geometry $(q:\mathcal{P}\to M,\omega)$ of type $(\operatorname{Euc}(n),O(n))$ canonically determines a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ by
$$
g_{x}(v,w):=\left\langle \phi_{u}(v),\phi_{u}(w)\right\rangle,
\qquad v,w\in T_{x}M,
$$
where $u\in\mathcal{P}$ is any point with $q(u)=x$. Moreover, after fixing the canonical orthonormal basis $(E_{1},\ldots,E_{n})$ of $\mathbb{R}^{n}$, the map
\[
\mathcal{P}\longrightarrow \mathcal{F}_{g}(M),
\qquad
u\mapsto\big(\phi_{u}^{-1}(E_{1}),\ldots,\phi_{u}^{-1}(E_{n})\big),
\]
is an isomorphism of $O(n)$-principal fiber bundles over $M$.
Here the right action on $\mathcal F_g(M)$ is the usual one:
\[
(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\cdot A
=
\left(
\sum_{i=1}^{n} e_i A_{i1},
\ldots,
\sum_{i=1}^{n}e_i A_{in}
\right),
\qquad A=(A_{ij})\in O(n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.29713

body: In mathematics, the classification of finite simple groups is a result of group theory stating that every finite simple group is either cyclic, or alternating, or belongs to a broad infinite class called the groups of Lie type, or else it is one of twenty-six exceptions, called sporadic. The proof consists of tens of thousands of pages in several hundred journal articles written by about 100 authors, published mostly between 1955 and 2004.
title: Classification of finite simple groups

body: In applied mathematics, Arnold diffusion is the phenomenon of instability of nearly-integrable Hamiltonian systems. The phenomenon is named after Vladimir Arnold who was the first to publish a result in the field in 1964. More precisely, Arnold diffusion refers to results asserting the existence of solutions to nearly-integrable Hamiltonian systems that exhibit a significant change in the action variables.
title: Arnold diffusion

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb N$, and let $\varrho\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$ be a
nonnegative function. Let
$f\in \mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^k;\mathbb R^k)$,
and let $A_f:=\operatorname{adj}(J_f)$ denote the adjugate matrix of the Jacobian $J_f$.
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every unit vector $\theta\in\mathbb R^k$,
every $t>0$, and every $\varphi\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$ satisfying
\[
\|\varphi\|_\infty\le t,
\quad
\|\partial_\theta\varphi\|_\infty\le 1,
\]
one has
\begin{align*}
\biggl|
\int_{\mathbb R^k}(\partial_\theta\varphi)(f)\varrho\,dx
\biggr|
&\le
\int_{\mathbb R^k} I_{\{(\det J_f)^2\le 2\varepsilon^2\}}\varrho\,dx
\\
&\quad
+
t\varepsilon^{-1}
\int_{\mathbb R^k}
\bigl|\langle \nabla\varrho,A_f\theta\rangle\bigr|\,dx
+
18t
\int_{\mathbb R^k}
\frac{\bigl|\langle \nabla\det J_f,A_f\theta\rangle\bigr|}
{(\det J_f)^2+\varepsilon^2}
\varrho\,dx.
\end{align*}

body:
DRAFT, proof (unaudited), T411-w740-C002/C003 v1. Let d>=2 and R>=72, T_R(z)=z+(z-R)_+, and let Z,W,Z2,...,Zd be independent standard Gaussians. Set P0=Law(Z+W,Z2,...,Zd) and P1=Law(T_R(Z)+W,Z2,...,Zd). Both priors have positive smooth densities and log-Sobolev constant at most 5 in the convention Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E||grad f||^2. The exact OU forward score of P0 has squared L2 error at most exp(-R^2/2)/4 under the forward law of P1 at every time. Under additive Gaussian smoothing with standard deviation u, the squared error is at most Pr(Z>R)/[(1+u^2)(2+u^2)]. For the normalized observation A=e1^T, noise variance 2/5, and fixed y=2R, the posteriors of P0 and P1 differ in TV by more than 3/8. The posterior of P1 has C_P and C_LS at least exp(R^2/960)/8, although the prior ratio ||A||^2 C_LS/sigma^2 is at most 25/2. A common approximate-score oracle therefore cannot guarantee posterior TV error 1/8 for every fixed observation; adding n independent exact prior samples requires n Pr(Z>R)>1/8. These are rare-observation obstructions only: they do not establish exact-score computational hardness, do not refute high-probability-over-observations posterior sampling, and do not claim that these explicitly described posteriors are hard to sample. No novelty or independent-check claim is made.
R>=72; d>=2
Independent standard Gaussian inputs
LSI convention Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E||grad f||^2
Fixed exceptional observation; not a typical-observation guarantee
Score-only input model for the information-obstruction consequence

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:de3310a71477ab01682964c4e277ad250513d544cd8c6c6670c8e76427a9b90c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/de/de3310a71477ab01682964c4e277ad250513d544cd8c6c6670c8e76427a9b90c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:26ccb33825d24af37e9af2397e7ef37d8df43febc52d49dcaff4d7102a2d2205","bundle_entry_key":"draft-constant-lsi-rare-observation-posterior-instability","bundle_id":"population.w740-t411-constant-lsi-rare-observation-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"posterior sampling and functional inequalities","draft":"w740/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.sampling:draft-constant-lsi-rare-observation-posterior-instability","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A constant-LSI prior does not make posterior sampling robust to unconditional score error

Status: proof draft, unaudited. Target: T411 Target 1. This is an oracle-model obstruction, not an exact-score hardness theorem and not a claim that a particular posterior is hard to sample from an explicit prior description.

## Statement

Use the convention Ent_mu(f^2) <= 2 C_LS E_mu ||grad f||^2. Fix R >= 40 and d >= 2. There are two everywhere positive smooth priors P_0,P_1 on R^d, both with C_LS <= 5 and polynomially bounded moments, and a single explicit forward score oracle s(t,x), such that:

1. s is the exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck forward score for P_0.
2. At every t >= 0, its squared L2 error under the forward law of P_1 is at most Pr{Z>R}/2 <= exp(-R^2/2)/4, where Z is standard Gaussian.
3. For A = (sqrt(5/2),0,...,0), sigma=1 and y=sqrt(10)R, the two posterior laws have TV distance greater than 3/8.
4. Both instances satisfy ||A||^2 C_LS / sigma^2 <= 25/2. Thus they satisfy the target's proposed bound for every c>0 once log d >= 25/(2c), independently of R.

Equivalently, normalize the observation operator to A=(1,0,...,0), take sigma^2=2/5 and y=2R. This is exactly the same conditioning problem after rescaling Y by sqrt(5/2); the dimensionless ratio is unchanged and ||A||=1 as in the primary paper.

Consequently a sampler whose only prior information is this approximate score oracle, common bounds on the priors, and (d,A,sigma,y), cannot be within TV 1/8 of both posteriors. This remains true even with unlimited computation: the inputs are identical. If at most n independent exact prior samples are also supplied, TV 1/8 for both requires n Pr{Z>R} > 1/8. For R=d this excludes a polynomial number of prior samples.

This disproves the worst-observation, inverse-polynomial-unconditional-score-error interpretation of Target 1. It does not decide a high-probability-over-observations interpretation, an exact-score oracle model, or an accuracy requirement calibrated to the observation's likelihood.

## Construction and regularity

Let T_R(z)=z+(z-R)_+. Let Z,W,Z_2,...,Z_d be independent standard Gaussians. Define

P_0 = Law(Z+W,Z_2,...,Z_d),
P_1 = Law(T_R(Z)+W,Z_2,...,Z_d).

T_R is increasing and 2-Lipschitz. The map from (Z,W,Z_2,...,Z_d) to the P_1 vector is sqrt(5)-Lipschitz: the first row of its almost-everywhere derivative is (T_R'(Z),1), of squared norm at most 5, and the remaining rows are disjoint unit rows. Applying the Gaussian LSI to f composed with this map proves C_LS(P_1)<=5 directly by the chain rule. P_0 has C_LS<=2. Gaussian convolution makes the first-coordinate densities positive and C-infinity. The transform's kink is not a kink of either prior density. Since |T_R(z)|<=2|z| for R>=0, the first second moment is at most 5; all moments have Gaussian-size bounds uniformly in R. The product coordinates add no difficulty.

## Uniform score error along the entire forward process

Write beta=exp(-t), v=1+beta^2, delta(Z)=(Z-R)_+ and J(Z)=1_{Z>R}. The first-coordinate forward law for P_1 is that of

X=beta T_R(Z)+W.

Indeed the original smoothed noise and the OU noise combine into an independent standard W. The corresponding P_0 forward law is N(0,v). Set s_0(t,x)=-x/v on coordinate one and -x_j on all other coordinates.

For a smooth compactly supported scalar test function f, Gaussian integration by parts first in Z and then in W gives

E[X f(X)] = v E[f'(X)] + E[(beta delta(Z)+beta^2 J(Z)W) f(X)].

If s_1 is the true score of X, E[s_1(X)f(X)]=-E[f'(X)]. Therefore

s_1(X)+X/v = E[beta delta(Z)+beta^2 J(Z)W | X]/v

almost surely. The identity first holds distributionally; the smooth positive density identifies its score. Conditional Jensen and independence of W,Z yield

E |s_1(X)+X/v|^2 <= (beta^2 E delta^2 + beta^4 p)/(1+beta^2)^2,

where p=Pr(Z>R). There is no cross term because E W=0. Integration of Gaussian tails gives

E delta^2=(1+R^2)p-R phi(R)<=p,

using R p<=phi(R), obtained by integrating R phi(z)<=z phi(z) on z>=R. Hence the error is <= p beta^2/(1+beta^2)<=p/2. The elementary Gaussian tail bound p<=exp(-R^2/2)/2 for R>=0 follows by differentiating exp(R^2/2)Pr(Z>R) and the same Mills inequality (with the endpoint R=0 handled directly). All other coordinate scores coincide. This proves the uniform, unnormalized d-dimensional squared L2 bound.

The same conclusion holds for the additive Gaussian smoothing used in the primary paper. If the extra smoothing standard deviation is u>=0, put eta^2=1+u^2. The first coordinate has law X=T_R(Z)+eta W, and its common approximate score is -x/(2+u^2). Repeating the integration by parts gives

E |s_1(X)+X/(2+u^2)|^2 <= [E delta^2+p/eta^2]/(1+eta^2)^2 <= p/[(1+u^2)(2+u^2)].

Indeed the residual is delta+J W/eta. In particular u^2 times this squared score error is at most p. The other coordinate scores are -x_j/(1+u^2). For R=d and each fixed C, p<d^(-C) for all sufficiently large d. Thus the same explicit linear networks witness the polynomial-precision score requirement in Definition 1.1 at every d^(-C)<=u<=d^C, for either prior. Their coefficients are bounded and the covariance operator is bounded by 5. This observation does not alter the exceptional-observation limitation.

## Exact posterior calculation

Observe Y=aX_1+epsilon with a=sqrt(5/2), epsilon independent N(0,1), at y=sqrt(10)R. In particular ay=5R. Under P_0,

X_1 | Y=y ~ N(5R/3,1/3).

Under P_1, integrating W out of Y gives the conditional latent density

p(z|y) proportional to phi(z) exp((10R/7)T_R(z)-(5/14)T_R(z)^2).

On z<=R its exponent is

-(6/7)(z-5R/6)^2 + 25R^2/42.

On z>R its exponent is

-(27/14)(z-10R/9)^2 + 25R^2/42.

The two normalizing tail factors are both Phi(R/sqrt(21)). The standard deviations are sqrt(7/12) and sqrt(7/27). Thus the posterior latent law is exactly the mixture

weight 3/5: N(5R/6,7/12) restricted to z<=R;
weight 2/5: N(10R/9,7/27) restricted to z>R.

Conditionally on z and y, X_1 is Gaussian with mean (2/7)T_R(z)+10R/7 and variance 2/7. If the upper branch's truncation is temporarily removed, its X_1 marginal is N(16R/9,10/27). This marginal is only used to bound a probability; the actual posterior remains truncated.

Let B={x_1>31R/18}. Under P_0, the Gaussian tail bound gives

P_0(B|y)<=exp(-R^2/216).

The untruncated upper-branch marginal satisfies Pr(B^c)<=exp(-R^2/240). Its latent truncation event has probability Phi(R/sqrt(21))>=1/2. Dividing the bad-event probability by that probability gives

P_1(B|y)>=(2/5)(1-2 exp(-R^2/240)).

Therefore

TV(P_1(.|y),P_0(.|y)) >= 2/5-(4/5) exp(-R^2/240)-exp(-R^2/216).

For R>=40 each exponential is less than 1/100: R^2/240>=20/3, and the fourth-degree Taylor lower bound for exp(20/3) exceeds 100. The displayed TV lower bound is then greater than 191/500>3/8. Extra coordinates remain independent standard Gaussians under both posteriors, so the same bound holds in dimension d.

## Oracle consequence and exact scope

The same s_0, same observation, and common upper bounds C_LS<=5 and E||X||^2<=d+4 are valid inputs for both priors. Any algorithm with only these inputs has the same output law Q in the two cases. The triangle inequality rules out TV(Q,P_i(.|y))<=1/8 for both i, since their mutual distance exceeds 3/8.

If n independent exact prior samples are available, couple them by using the same Gaussian variables. Each P_0/P_1 sample pair is identical unless Z>R. Their n-sample transcript laws differ in TV by at most np, and data processing gives the same bound for algorithm output laws Q_0,Q_1, even if score queries are adaptive. Then

3/8 < TV(P_0(.|y),P_1(.|y)) <= 1/8 + np + 1/8,

which forces np>1/8. This is an information limitation of this approximate-oracle interface. Exact prior scores, a prior's full description, or a conditional sampler are different interfaces and are not covered.

The observation is rare as R grows. The construction deliberately does not refute a theorem averaged over Y, a high-probability observation guarantee, or a theorem requesting exponentially fine unconditional score accuracy. Neither prior nor its explicit posterior is asserted computationally difficult when its complete construction is disclosed.

This distinction is load-bearing: Gupta, Jalal, Parulekar, Price and Xun, arXiv:2402.12727v2, Definition 1.5 (PDF p.4, printed p.2), require correctness with probability 1-delta over the observation. Their error notion is coupling closeness (Definition 1.2), not TV. Their Definition 1.1 requests polynomial-precision forward scores. C002 therefore does not contradict their theorem or settle their high-probability setting after adding an LSI assumption.

Indeed TV(P_0,P_1)<=p by the explicit coupling. For any common observation channel K, write M_i=P_i K and let m_i be its Y marginal. The triangle inequality, applied after adding and subtracting m_0(y)P_1(dx|y), gives

E_{Y~m_0} TV(P_0(.|Y),P_1(.|Y)) <= TV(M_0,M_1)+TV(m_0,m_1) <= 2p.

Here TV(M_0,M_1)=TV(P_0,P_1) because the joint law retains X, and marginalization contracts TV. Hence Markov's inequality bounds the m_0 probability of posterior TV exceeding eta by 2p/eta. This explicitly confirms why a rare observation cannot refute a high-probability target.

## Checks and source obligations

Checks that could fail: LSI convention and the Lipschitz-map dimension; integration-by-parts coefficients; the OU noise variance; equal branch free energies; exact truncation probabilities and mixture weights; the posterior variances; the sign of the tail-event separation; use of conditioning in the upper branch; and the distinction between approximate and exact score access.

The finite algebraic identities and exponential lower bound are checked in scripts/check_C002.py using exact rational arithmetic. Numerical tail probabilities, if reported, are explicitly supplementary. Lean certification is attempted only for the algebraic coefficient identity; it cannot certify this analytic theorem. The Gaussian LSI input is supplied by brain card claim_4bdeb13cc86ab526b0013e02b6024d3dede00f91d34eca4a10273fa64375e52c (Gross). Primary-paper comparison and a novelty check remain obligations before describing this construction as new.


# Constant prior LSI and constant observation ratio do not bound posterior LSI

Status: proof (unaudited). This is a failure of the proposed functional-inequality transfer for arbitrary observations, not a computational sampling lower bound. Use the exact smooth P_1 prior and observation from C002. The normalized observation is A=e_1^T, sigma^2=2/5, y=2R. For R>=72,

C_P(P_1(.|y)) >= (1/8) exp(R^2/960),

and therefore the same lower bound holds for C_LS in the convention Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E|grad f|^2. Yet C_LS(P_1)<=5 and ||A||^2 C_LS(P_1)/sigma^2<=25/2.

The single hardest step inherited from C002 is its exact posterior branch calculation. Everything below is a direct test-function argument using those branches.

## Density domination

C002 proves that the conditional latent branches have weights 3/5 and 2/5, and each latent truncation event has probability Phi(R/sqrt(21))>=1/2. Dropping each truncation and dividing by its probability bounds the corresponding X_1 marginal density from above. Consequently its full posterior density rho satisfies

rho(x) <= (6/5) phi_{1/3}(x-5R/3) + (4/5) phi_{10/27}(x-16R/9),

where phi_v is the centered Gaussian density of variance v.

Put t=31R/18, the midpoint between the two untruncated means. For x in [t-1,t+1] and R>=36, its distance from either mean is at least R/18-1>=R/36. Both variances are at most 10/27 and both Gaussian normalizing prefactors are less than 1 (since both variances are at least 1/3). Therefore

rho(x) <= 2 exp(-R^2/960)  on [t-1,t+1].

No normalization constants of the actual posterior have been dropped: the factors 6/5 and 4/5 include the worst-case truncation probabilities.

## A test function with separated mass

Let f(x) be 0 for x<=t-1, (x-t+1)/2 for t-1<x<t+1, and 1 for x>=t+1. It is an admissible Lipschitz Sobolev test function. Its gradient energy is bounded by

E_rho |f'|^2 <= (1/4) * 2 * 2 exp(-R^2/960) = exp(-R^2/960).

On the lower latent branch, the probability X_1>t-1 is at most 2 exp(-R^2/960): first use the untruncated N(5R/3,1/3) tail, then divide by the latent truncation probability >=1/2. The exponent uses the weaker variance upper bound 10/27. Similarly, on the upper branch, Pr(X_1<t+1) <= 2 exp(-R^2/960).

For R>=72, exp(R^2/960)>=exp(27/5)>10; the quadratic Taylor lower bound 1+27/5+(27/5)^2/2 already exceeds 10. It follows that

rho(X_1<=t-1) >= (3/5)(4/5)=12/25,
rho(X_1>=t+1) >= (2/5)(4/5)=8/25.

For two independent copies X,X', Var(f(X))=(1/2)E(f(X)-f(X'))^2. The pairs from the two displayed events alone contribute at least

Var(f(X)) >= (12/25)(8/25)=96/625>1/8.

The Poincare variational inequality, applied to f, now gives the claimed lower bound. The same one-coordinate test applies to the d-dimensional posterior. Finally C_P<=C_LS follows by linearizing LSI at a constant function, so the LSI lower bound follows without an additional mixing argument.

## Consequence and limitations

Fix any c>0 and any dimension with c log d>=25/2. Letting R grow shows that the target ratio and the dimension cannot, by themselves, bound a worst-observation posterior LSI constant. Setting R=d makes the lower bound exponential in d^2 while keeping the observation polynomial in d. Thus the proposed route that replaces a bounded support radius by the prior LSI constant cannot be valid uniformly over observations.

This does not exclude another polynomial sampling algorithm: the explicit posterior here is a two-branch truncated-Gaussian construction and can be sampled efficiently when its description is provided. It does not refute a high-probability-over-observations theorem. The natural high-probability Target 1 from Gupta et al. remains open in this work.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:5911abb36446a9d302a7b7208166c75c3721fe92a58496470f0ecdd3a79b763f","revision_digest":"sha256:9a4cfee7532e1d359fb034449676f341a43f25f9d713fd07004d3bd13051134c","source_id":"owner:T411:w740:C002-v1:C003-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 11 (uniqueness for the homogeneous wave equation) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $0<T<\infty$ and let $u\in C^1([0,T];L^2(\Rn))$ satisfy
$\mathcal Bu\in C([0,T];L^2(\Rn))$,
\[
 \Box u=0\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'((0,T)\times\Rn),
 \qquad
 u(0)=\partial_tu(0)=0 .
\]
Then $u\equiv0$ on $[0,T]$. The same conclusion holds componentwise for
vector- and matrix-valued $u$.

Let $T\in(0,\infty]$ and let $u\ge0$ be continuous on $\mathbb R^n\times[0,T)$, of class $C^2_1$ on $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$, and satisfy $u_t-\Delta u=0$ in $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$. Then, with $\Phi(x,t)=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2/(4t)}$, $u(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Phi(x-y,t)u(y,0)\,dy$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$ and $0<t<T$; in particular $\int e^{-|y|^2/(4t)}u(y,0)dy<\infty$ for every $t<T$. Consequently a nonnegative solution in this class with $u(\cdot,0)\equiv0$ vanishes identically, and two nonnegative solutions with the same initial values coincide -- no growth hypothesis is needed, one-sided boundedness replaces it. (Widder 1944 for $n=1$; the general statement, with arbitrary nonnegative initial traces given by Borel measures when continuity at $t=0$ is dropped, is due to Widder and Aronson; the divergence-form analogue is Aronson's.)
u >= 0 on R^n x [0,T)
u continuous on R^n x [0,T), C^2_1 on R^n x (0,T)
u solves the heat equation on R^n x (0,T)

[Lemma 14 (Special case of the result in \cite{halko2011finding}) of arXiv:2609.02790, 'Full-Model Optimality for Tunable Linear Generative Priors in Compressed Sensing'] Let
$\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n),    \sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n>0,$
and fix \(1\le k\le m-2\). Partition
\[
    \Sigma=
    \begin{pmatrix}
    \Sigma_1 & 0\\
    0 & \Sigma_2
    \end{pmatrix},
    \qquad
    \Sigma_1\in\mathbb R^{k\times k},
    \qquad
    \Sigma_2\in\mathbb R^{(n-k)\times(n-k)}.
\]
Let \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) be a standard Gaussian matrix and
partition it as
\[
    \Omega=
    \begin{pmatrix}
    \Omega_1\\
    \Omega_2
    \end{pmatrix},
    \qquad
    \Omega_1\in\mathbb R^{k\times m},
    \qquad
    \Omega_2\in\mathbb R^{(n-k)\times m}.
\]
Let \(Y=\Sigma\Omega\), and let \(P_Y\) denote the orthogonal projector
onto \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Then
\[
   \mathrm E_{\Omega}
    \bigl\|(I-P_Y)\Sigma\bigr\|_F^2
    \le
    \left(1+\frac{k}{m-k-1}\right)
    \|\Sigma_2\|_F^2 .
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Homogenisation of the Green function at all scales plus the DGFF argument. Result: The quenched Green function of the random conductance model in d=2 is g_eff log|x-y| + O(1) up to the scale where homogenisation holds; the concentric decomposition needs the O(1) error to be controlled uniformly over all dyadic scales near a point, which is a quenched local limit theorem at every scale. This is available for uniformly elliptic ergodic conductances by Andres-Deuschel-Slowik type estimates for the heat kernel, so the intermediate level sets (which only need two-point covariances) follow the DGFF proof with g replaced by g_eff. The extremal-process cluster law, however, depends on the local geometry of the conductances around the maximiser and is therefore itself random (not a constant law), which changes the STATEMENT of the Theorem 9.3 analogue: the cluster law becomes a random law indexed by the environment at the maximiser. This suggests the problem as posed needs reformulation for the extremal process. Obstruction: The analogue of the cluster law is environment-dependent; the statement of Theorem 9.3 must be modified before it can be proved.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0010-dgff-over-an-ergodic-uniformly-elliptic-random-conductance-model-level

    Fix $\alpha >0$. Suppose that $G$ is an infinite graph with maximum degree $3\leq d < \infty$ and $p_c(G,x_0) <1$. It holds that
    $$\frac\alpha{d-2}\leq \lambda_c(\alpha) \leq \frac{d+\alpha}{1 - p_c(G,x_0)^{1/d}} .$$ 
    Thus, 
    $\lambda_c(\alpha) = \Theta(\alpha)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

type-compatible interfaces, insert bounded maps
$G_1,\ldots,G_s$, and retain the cuts until the complete contraction is
closed to a scalar.  Suppose that the $G_j$ contain no hidden
unnormalized cup or cap.  Then the estimate of
(prop:multiport-closed of the paper) is multiplied by at most
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^s\|G_j\|,
\tag{2.6.14c}

assertion holds when one coefficient component carries the indivisible
paired marked-root token: after its two fronts are closed in the terminal
scalar, its color weight is $\beta_j^2$.

body: In computational complexity theory, the space hierarchy theorems are separation results that show that both deterministic and nondeterministic machines can solve more problems in (asymptotically) more space, subject to certain conditions. For example, a deterministic Turing machine can solve more decision problems in space n log n than in space n. The somewhat weaker analogous theorems for time are the time hierarchy theorems.
title: Space hierarchy theorem

body: For G_1=[Z] with Z standard normal, P(s_min(G_1)<=t)=erf(t/sqrt(2)) for t>=0; its derivative at zero is sqrt(2/pi). Thus 1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is not the exact finite-n Gaussian least-singular-value CDF. It is the limiting CDF as n tends to infinity (Rudelson-Vershynin ICM 2010 survey). The finite-n bound P(s_min(G_n)<=t/sqrt(n))<=t is a separate statement. This corrects only the exact-law sentence in the 2026-09-07 C0029 attempt record.

[Proposition prop:9 of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix a bounded open set $U$. Set $\varepsilon_n=2^{-n}$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$. Then almost surely, the following holds for all $n$ large enough. First, with $\mathcal{H}_n=((\frac{\varepsilon_n}{2})^{1/\chi}\mathbb{Z}^2)\cap U$, for all $u\in U$, there exists a $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z}\in \mathcal{H}_n$ such that $D_h(u,\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z})\leq \varepsilon_n / 2$.

  Further, for any fixed $\alpha>0$, there exist random $0<\boldsymbol{\varphi}<\boldsymbol{\psi}<\alpha/20$ depending only on $U$ and $\alpha$ such that the following almost surely holds for all $n$ large enough. For all $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z}\in \mathcal{H}_n$, all $w\in U$ satisfying $D_h(w,\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z})\geq \alpha$, and every $D_h$-geodesic $\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},w}$, there exists a $(z,r)\in \mathbb{C}\times [\varepsilon_n^{1/(2\chi')},\varepsilon_n^{1/ (4\chi')}]$ 
  satisfying the following properties.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item  There exists a $z'\in z+\mathcal{Z}$ such that for the points $u_+,u_-,v_+,v_-$ corresponding to $z'$ and the radius $\rho r/A^2$, the event $\mathscr{X}^{u^+,v^+}_{u_-,v_-}$ occurs.
  \item 
    With $P_+=\Gamma_{u_+,v_+}, P_-=\Gamma_{u_-,v_-}$ being the unique $D_h$-geodesics corresponding to the points $u_-,u_+,v_-,v_+$ associated to the $z'$ above and with $\tau^-<\tau^+$ being such that $P_-\cap P_+=\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},w}\lvert_{[\tau^-,\tau^+]}$, we have $[\tau^-,\tau^+]\subseteq [\boldsymbol{\varphi},\boldsymbol{\psi}]$. 
  \item  $P_+$ (resp.\ $P_-$) intersects $\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},w}$ on its left (resp.\ right) side.
  \item We have $P_+\cup P_- \subseteq B_{\varepsilon_n^{1/(4\chi')}}(P_+\cap P_-)$.
  \item  
    The set $B_{16(2048\varepsilon_{n})^{1/\chi'}}(\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},w}\lvert_{[\tau^--2(25\times 2048\varepsilon_{n})^{\chi/(4\chi')},\tau^+ + 2(25\times 2048\varepsilon_{n})^{\chi/(4\chi')}]})$ does not intersect any of $u_-,u_+,v_-,v_+$.
 \end{enumerate}

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. For the exact critical zero-bias tanh fresh-Gaussian-row two-input Gram chain with Q0=R0=s in (0,1], initial correlation c0 in [-1,1], and its deterministic GP correlation cbar_L, set D_L=1-c_L and Dbar_L=1-cbar_L. For every fixed 0<eps<1 there is an explicit finite Aeps depending only on eps and the universal C010/C015 constants K,Lambda such that ||D_L-Dbar_L||_2 <= Aeps(1-|c0|)sqrt(L/n) for every integer n>=1769472(1+K), 0<=L<=n^(1-eps). If c0<1, ||D_L/Dbar_L-1||_2<=exp(14688s)Aeps sqrt(L/n). At c0=1 both gaps are identically zero and no ratio is asserted. Constants and all steps appear in the proof.
Exact conditional iid Gaussian rows and tanh; equal positive deterministic initial marginal variances <=1; valid initial correlation; fixed eps in (0,1); n threshold as stated. Uses exact reviewed C002 v2/C004 v1 and unaudited C010/C011/C012/C014/C015/C017/C018 v1. No independence of the two input columns or future variance weight is assumed.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cdce85629f4b759d6e74117dbf16e5f365661272280d7cc057e93f7f1ac810c7","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cd/cdce85629f4b759d6e74117dbf16e5f365661272280d7cc057e93f7f1ac810c7.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9138c5443483530cf54b1a06c687e69720935bb33f5c63fd52bd253978ea992a","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_relative_angular_error_iteration","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c019-relative-angular-error","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and stochastic Gram propagation","draft":"w712/bundle_014.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-relative-angular-error-sublinear-depth","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C019 v1: unstopped relative angular error over sublinear depth

Kind: moved. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified.
This closes the multilayer angular-error iteration for two equal-norm
inputs. It does not yet assert the final fixed-probe GP transport bound.
All cited C010--C018 inputs remain unaudited; only C002 v2 and C004 v1
among the inputs below have exact-version reviewer PASS.

## Statement

Use the exact critical, zero-bias, fresh-Gaussian-row tanh Gram chain of
C017: Q0=R0=s in (0,1], C0=s c0, c0 in [-1,1]. At layer l, conditionally
on the completed past, sample n iid centered Gaussian pairs with covariance
[[Q_l,C_l],[C_l,R_l]] and update the three Gram entries by empirical
averages of tanh(A)^2, tanh(B)^2 and tanh(A)tanh(B). Define

    c_l=C_l/sqrt(Q_l R_l), D_l=1-c_l, e_l=Q_l-R_l,
    S_l=Q_l+R_l, V_l=Q_l^2+R_l^2, H_l=sum_(j=1)^l 1/j.

All finite-depth marginal variances are positive almost surely and at
most one. Let sbar_0=s, sbar_(l+1)=F(sbar_l), where
F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2. Let cbar_0=c0 and propagate the deterministic
population correlation map at equal variance sbar_l. Put Dbar_l=1-cbar_l.

Let K,Lambda be the finite nonnegative uniform moment constants in
C010/C015, and fix 0<eps<1. Define finite constants symbolically by

    B=8650752 exp(1059/2), M=12K+3Lambda^4,
    Ceps=exp(192+M/4)[1+61 B(1+1/(exp(1)eps))],
    R=17 Ceps+61 exp(192)B, J=1+4Lambda^2,
    G=1+2/(exp(1)eps),
    Aearly=sqrt(J) R+exp(192)[61 B G+480 exp(96)sqrt(192)+K R],
    Aeps=max{Aearly,sqrt(96)(Ceps+exp(96))}.

For integer n>=1769472(1+K) and integer 0<=L<=n^(1-eps),

    ||D_L-Dbar_L||_2 <= Aeps (1-|c0|) sqrt(L/n).       (1)

In particular the weaker right side Aeps D0 sqrt(L/n) also holds.
If c0<1, then Dbar_L>0, and C012's deterministic lower bound gives

    ||D_L/Dbar_L-1||_2 <=exp(14688s) Aeps sqrt(L/n).   (2)

At c0=1 the gaps vanish identically and the ratio in (2) is not defined.
Constants are not asserted sharp; no floating-point evaluation is needed.

## 1. Exact error decomposition

For current variances q,r let Phi(q,r,d) be the population postactivation
gap at input correlation 1-d. Write delta_l=Phi(Q_l,R_l,D_l), and set

    E_l=D_l-Dbar_l,
    eta_(l+1)=D_(l+1)-E[D_(l+1)|F_l],
    b_l=E[D_(l+1)|F_l]-delta_l,
    h_l=Phi(Q_l,R_l,Dbar_l)-Phi(sbar_l,sbar_l,Dbar_l).

Choose the secant alpha_l of d->Phi(Q_l,R_l,d) between D_l and
Dbar_l; when they coincide choose its derivative. The angular derivative
bound C004 gives |alpha_l|<=1+8V_l. These choices and h_l,b_l are
F_l-measurable; eta is conditionally centered. Exactly, with no remainder,

    E_(l+1)=alpha_l E_l+eta_(l+1)+h_l+b_l.            (3)

C011 and C010 give

    |h_l|<=61 e_l^2+20 Dbar_l(|Q_l-sbar_l|+|R_l-sbar_l|),
    |b_l|<=K delta_l/n.                             (4)

The first constant rounds 121/2 upward. The normalized covariance is
defined at every finite depth almost surely; the zero-gap case is exact
column coincidence, not a cancellation of a zero denominator.

## 2. Uniform amplitude of the population gap

First prove a bound with D0=1-c0; symmetry will strengthen it at the end.
C017 gives ||D_l exp(96S_l)||_2<=Ceps D0 on our depth range.
Its population comparison inequality and V_l<=2 give

    delta_l<=(1+8V_l)D_l+61 e_l^2<=17D_l+61 e_l^2.

C014 with T=1 gives z_l:=||e_l^2||_2<=B D0 H_l/n; its actual
constant 8650752s exp(1059/2) is at most B. Since l<=n and H_l<=l
for l>=1 (and z_0=0), and S_l<=2, the triangle inequality yields

    ||delta_l exp(96S_l)||_2<=R D0.                 (5)

No eighth radial moment, inverse stability product, or stochastic
independence between the angular gap and the radial weight is used.

## 3. Weighted energy iteration

Let U_l=||E_l exp(96S_l)||_2. C018, with x=E_l and the predictable
alpha_l in (3), applies since n>=1769472(1+K). Taking total expectations,
then an L2 triangle inequality and S_(l+1)<=2, gives

    U_(l+1)<=sqrt(U_l^2+J R^2 D0^2/n)
                        +exp(192)||h_l+b_l||_2.    (6)

In this triangle step the future weight on h_l+b_l is bounded pointwise,
not factored out by independence. For x,y,t>=0,

    sqrt((x+y)^2+t)<=sqrt(x^2+t)+y,

because the square of the right side minus the square of the left side
is 2y(sqrt(x^2+t)-x)>=0 and both sides are nonnegative. With U_0=0,
induction in (6) therefore gives, for every integer L in range,

    U_L<=sqrt(J) R D0 sqrt(L/n)
                          +exp(192)sum_(l=0)^(L-1)||h_l+b_l||_2. (7)

The induction step has exactly one new noise variance term and one
new forcing term; there are L terms at time L, none at time zero.

## 4. Sum the forcing for L<=n/96

C002's independently checked relative estimate and deterministic decay are

    E(Q_l/sbar_l-1)^2<=192l/n, sbar_l<=6/(l+1), l<=n/96.

Thus, for either marginal and including its zero error at l=0,

    sigma_l:=||Q_l-sbar_l||_2
       <=6sqrt(192)/sqrt(n(l+1)),
    sum_(l=0)^(L-1)sigma_l<=12sqrt(192)sqrt(L/n).    (8)

The same norm holds for R_l by the identical marginal transition law;
this equality does not assert that the two marginals are independent.
The sum bound uses sum_(j=1)^L j^(-1/2)<=2sqrt(L). C004's
deterministic amplification gives Dbar_l<=exp(96s)D0<=exp(96)D0.
Equations (4), (5), (8) give

    sum ||h_l+b_l||_2
       <=61 sum z_l+480 exp(96)sqrt(192)D0 sqrt(L/n)
                                      +K R D0 L/n. (9)

For L>=1, C014 and monotonicity of H give

    sum_(l=0)^(L-1) z_l<=B D0 L H_L/n.

On L<=n^(1-eps), H_L<=1+log L<=1+log n and

    sqrt(L/n) H_L<=n^(-eps/2)(1+log n)<=1+2/(exp(1)eps)=G.

For the last inequality put t=log n>=0 and maximize t exp(-eps t/2),
whose derivative exp(-eps t/2)(1-eps t/2) changes sign at 2/eps;
the maximum is 2/(exp(1)eps). The remaining exponential is at most one.
Consequently sum z_l<=B G D0 sqrt(L/n). Also L/n<=sqrt(L/n)
because L<=n. Substitution in (7)--(9) proves

    ||E_L||_2<=U_L<=Aearly D0 sqrt(L/n)             (10)

for 1<=L<=min(n/96,n^(1-eps)); the assertion at L=0 is immediate.

## 5. Remaining depths, symmetry, and relative normalization

If n/96<L<=n^(1-eps), use C017 and the deterministic amplitude directly:

    ||E_L||_2<=||D_L||_2+Dbar_L
       <=(Ceps+exp(96))D0
       <=sqrt(96)(Ceps+exp(96))D0 sqrt(L/n).        (11)

This step does not extend C002's relative estimate beyond its stated
range. The two depth cases cover all integer L in the theorem.

Oddness of tanh allows replacing the second input and every second-column
preactivation by its negative in the same Gaussian coupling. Marginal
variances stay fixed, c_l and cbar_l change sign, and the new error is
-E_l. The initial gap becomes 1+c0. Applying (10)--(11) to this equally
admissible chain and taking the smaller bound proves (1). At c0=+1
or -1 the columns are exactly equal or opposite; both errors are zero.

Finally C012 gives Dbar_L>=exp(-14688s)D0. For c0<1 this lower bound
is positive. Divide the D0 version of (1) by it to prove (2); no
claim about a relative ratio at c0=1 is made.

## Scope, checks, and remaining step

Load-bearing assumptions: fresh independent rows within each conditional
layer supply C010/C015/C018; equal deterministic initial variances supply
C014 and the shared scalar comparison; s>0 makes normalization legitimate;
s<=1 keeps the quoted compact-range estimates applicable; eps>0 is
needed for the uniform logarithmic absorption. Independence of the two
inputs is neither assumed nor used. The case eps=0 is not proved here:
the radial immigration estimate used above then leaves a log n factor.

Potential failures to test: predictable secant placement in (3), constant
rounding in (4), the same-row weighted innovation in (6), the term count
in (7), radial depth range in (8), logarithmic absorption, c0 endpoints,
and the positivity needed for (2). The real-variable algebra in section 3
is proved explicitly above. A small exact-arithmetic script is supporting
author verification, not an independent audit or numerical bound for the
random chain. Any Lean analogue has only its exact formal scope; failure
or missing environment certification leaves that formal target unverified.

This proves the stated angular-error lemma conditional on the explicitly
cited unaudited prior lemmas, and is recorded as proof (unaudited), never
as independently checked. The remaining Target 1 step is the fixed-probe
two-input GP trajectory coupling, with its covariance square-root and
deterministic spectral-gap estimates and a precisely specified metric.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:ec316fe9ff8be687dead5d1c41f015a2e147b1094c989f6df8b9f6d379f184a7","revision_digest":"sha256:9a7e2e614edcdb2e6b6ffa198c4566fc17c7b6766ad78472474fc1ff051425da","source_id":"owner-own-work:T250-w712-C019-v1","source_revision":"C019-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

  \mathcal D_u\mathcal R+G^\top\mathcal R
  =2\nu\sum_{k=1}^3(\partial_kM)^\top(\partial_kN),\qquad \mathcal R(0)=0.

[Proposition 32 (Range--duration identity) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] For every $N\geq2$ and $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation}

        D_N^\gamma(t)
        =
        1+\int_0^tR_N^\gamma(s)D_N^\gamma(s)\,ds
        =
        \exp\left\{\int_0^tR_N^\gamma(s)\,ds\right\}.
\end{equation}
If $R_\infty^\gamma(t)<\infty$, then
\begin{equation}

        D_\infty^\gamma(t)
        =
        \exp\left\{\int_0^tR_\infty^\gamma(s)\,ds\right\}<\infty.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
        t_{\mathrm d}^\gamma=t_{\mathrm{sus}}^\gamma,
\]
and, for every $t<t_{\mathrm{sus}}^\gamma$,
\begin{equation}

        D_N^\gamma(t)\longrightarrow D_\infty^\gamma(t).
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem thm:higher-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $d\geq2$, and let $Z$ be a standard Borel space equipped with
a Borel action of $\mathbb Z^d$. There is a Borel family
$z\mapsto P_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $P_z$ are uniformly Delone;

\item
\[
    P_{n.z}=P_z-n
    \qquad
    (n\in\mathbb Z^d,\ z\in Z);
\]

\item
if
\[
    P_w=P_z-u,
    \qquad
    z,w\in Z,\quad u\in\mathbb R^d,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z^d
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=u.z;
\]

\item
for every $z\in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1)^d
\]
in the sense of tempered distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:higher-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616

body: [DERIVED + CHECKED 09-08 07:3x] Bernoulli 2/3: rescaling a block by v=(3/2)^n w turns Q^2 into a RIESZ PRODUCT with ratio 3/2, and the criterion's coefficient c(n) is its Fourier coefficient at frequency (3/2)^(n+1). That frequency is provably NOT in the product's spectrum - if (3/2)^(n+1) = sum eps_i (3/2)^i with eps in {0,+-1} then 3^(n+1) = sum eps_i 3^i 2^(n+1-i), and mod 3 induction forces every eps_i = 0 (brute-forced n=1..9 too). So |c(n)| is pure window leakage rather than a spectral line, which is why it measures ~0.08 not order one. LIMIT: summing leakage over the 3^(n+1) characters overshoots by 2^n (the linearising failure), and the nearest line can sit within 2^-(n+1), so a proof needs a COUNT of near-coincidences, not an exactness statement

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): Five exact facts about the batching. (1) The batches B_s partition the matching edges, so the V_s are disjoint. (2) Hence the U_s = E_s cap V_s are pairwise disjoint. (3) |U_s| >= a_s + 1 (tag 6): the witness edge contributes both endpoints and each of the other a_s - 1 edges in B_s contributes at least one distinct endpoint. (4) E_t cap U_s = empty for t < s (tag 7): had E_t met an endpoint of a still-present edge of B_s, that edge would have been removed at stage t. (5) E_s meets no endpoint belonging to a later batch, so after fixing coordinates outside the union of the U_s, the indicator of the s-th selected constraint is a function of X_{U_1},...,X_{U_s} only (tag 8). Notes: The proof uses U_s, NOT the larger V_s - S7 states this explicitly. These five facts are the exact structural content the harness re-verifies by brute force.

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C009 v1). For a nondegenerate d-simplex S with d>=1, any full-essential-support law on S which is (d+1)-CM must have mean at the geometric simplex centroid. Each nonnegative barycentric coordinate has essential maximum one, forcing its mean >=1/(d+1); summing forces equality. Uniform S is mixable, but the continuous strictly positive density 1+epsilon*(lambda_0-1/(d+1)) relative to Unif(S), for 0<|epsilon|<1, shifts its mean and is not (d+1)-CM. Total variation and uniform density differences tend to zero with epsilon. This refutes unqualified density-stability shortcuts; it says nothing against uniform laws on deformed bodies or fixed-centroid perturbations.
Nondegenerate d-simplex with d>=1
Full essential support
n=d+1
Density tilt epsilon nonzero and |epsilon|<1

For each n>=3 there is a distinct-weight assignment on K_n such that the MST is a Hamilton path of diameter n-1, while a sublevel including all edges has intrinsic diameter 1. Assign the n-1 path edges the smallest weights and every other edge larger weights. Hence a cluster intrinsic-diameter bound at one threshold does not imply the reverse MST-diameter inequality. This refutes that generic upper-bound route, not torus or hypercube scaling.

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): (Lemma 2.1, cycle two-shadow quotient.) Let S_n = {0} u {u_i : 1<=i<=n} u {u_i+u_{i+1} : 1<=i<=n} in F_2^n, u_i the standard basis, indices cyclic. For EVERY subspace W <= F_2^n of dimension w, the number of occupied cosets obeys |S_n/W| >= 2n+1-3w. Proof: pick Q subset [n], |Q|=n-w, whose singleton cosets are a basis of F_2^n/W; deleting the w vertices of [n]\Q from a cycle destroys at most 2w edges, so at least max{0,n-2w} edges have both endpoints in Q; their images are sums of two distinct basis vectors, mutually distinct and distinct from 0 and every singleton. Count 1+(n-w)+max{0,n-2w}; for w<=n/2 this is the bound, for w>=n/2 the first two terms already are. Notes: The coefficient 3 is EXACT: quotienting by <u_i> identifies the three pairs 0~u_i, u_{i-1}~u_{i-1}+u_i, u_{i+1}~u_i+u_{i+1}, and widely separated choices of i make the bound an equality (S10 (19), p.160). This is the whole source of the n/3 rate and of 'one residual direction pays three quotient mergers'.

body: In computer science and telecommunications, Hamming codes are a family of linear error-correcting codes. Hamming codes can detect one-bit and two-bit errors, or correct one-bit errors without detection of uncorrected errors. By contrast, the simple parity code cannot correct errors, and can detect only an odd number of bits in error. Hamming codes are perfect codes, that is, they achieve the highest possible rate for codes with their block length and minimum distance of three. Richard W. Hamming invented Hamming codes in 1950 as a way of automatically correcting errors introduced by punched card readers. In his original paper, Hamming elaborated his general idea, but specifically focused on the Hamming(7,4) code which adds three parity bits to four bits of data.

[Theorem 18 (\cite{NuPe,NP-book}) of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Fix an integer $n\geq 1$ and consider a sequence 
	$(F_k=I_n(f_k), k\geq 1)$ of square integrable random variables 
	in the $n$th Wiener chaos. Assume that
	\begin{equation}
		\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbf{E}[F_k^2] 
		= \lim_{k\to\infty}n!\|f_k\|^2_{H^{\odot n}} = 1.
	\end{equation}
	Then the following statements are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $(F_k)$ converges in distribution to $N(0,1)$ as 
		$k\to\infty$.
		\item $\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathbf{E}[F_k^4]=3$.
		\item $\lim_{k\to\infty}\|f_k\otimes_l f_k\|_{H^{\otimes 2(n-l)}}
		=0$ for $l=1,2,\ldots,n-1$.
		\item $\|DF_k\|_H^2$ converges to $n$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ as 
		$k\to\infty$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $\mathcal{K}$ be an essentially small tensor-triangulated category. A thick subcategory $\mathcal{P} \subsetneq \mathcal{K}$ is a prime thick $\otimes$-ideal if $a \otimes b \in \mathcal{P} \implies a \in \mathcal{P}$ or $b \in \mathcal{P}$. The Balmer spectrum $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathcal{K})$ is the topological space whose underlying set is the set of all prime thick $\otimes$-ideals, topologized by the closed basis $Z(a) = \{\mathcal{P} \in \operatorname{Spc}(\mathcal{K}) \mid a \notin \mathcal{P}\}$ for $a \in \mathcal{K}$.

[Definition def:ribbon-record of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] A rooted orthogonal-Weingarten ribbon record $\Gamma$ of degree $m$
consists of the dart set
$\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{L_0,L_1,R_0,R_1\}$; its coefficient boxes and
color labels; perfect matchings $p,q,r$ giving the row,
coefficient-column, and rooted trace wiring; all local wedge and
direct/cross signs; the distinguished root boundary; and the following
orthogonal-Weingarten path data.

Partition the darts into the independent Haar-color classes
$\mathscr H_\Gamma$ (there is one class when all entries come from one
Haar matrix).  If $a\in\mathscr H_\Gamma$ contains $m_a$ coefficient
occurrences, put $k_a=2m_a$, so it has $2k_a=4m_a$ darts, and denote by
$p_a,q_a$ the restrictions of $p,q$.  The rooted dart order chooses a
deterministic relabelling $\sigma_a$ with
$\sigma_a\cdot e_{k_a}=p_a$, where
\[
 e_k=\{\{1,2\},\{3,4\},\ldots,\{2k-1,2k\}\},
\]
and put
$\mathfrak m_a=\sigma_a^{-1}\cdot q_a\in\mathcal P_2(2k_a)$.
The orthogonal Weingarten graph has vertex set
$\bigsqcup_{j\ge0}\mathcal P_2(2j)$.  At level $j$ it has a solid arrow
\[
 \mathfrak n\longrightarrow(i,2j-1)\cdot\mathfrak n,
 \qquad 1\le i<2j-1,
\]
and it has a dashed arrow
$\mathfrak n\dashrightarrow\mathfrak n^\downarrow$ when
$\{2j-1,2j\}\in\mathfrak n$, where $\mathfrak n^\downarrow$ is
obtained by deleting that pair.  The record chooses, for every $a$, one
\emph{individual} path $\gamma_a$ from $\mathfrak m_a$ to the empty
pairing.  It uses exactly $k_a$ dashed arrows; write $s_a$ for its number
of solid arrows.  If $\mu_a$ is the coset type of $\mathfrak m_a$, define
\[
 d_a:=|\mathfrak m_a|=k_a-\ell(\mu_a)
      =k_a-\#(p_a\vee q_a),
 \qquad
 g_a:=s_a-d_a\ge0,
 \qquad
 g_{\rm Wg}:=\sum_{a\in\mathscr H_\Gamma}g_a.
\]
Thus $g_{\rm Wg}$ is the total number of solid arrows beyond shortest
orthogonal-Weingarten paths; unlike the unitary excess, it need not be
even.

Let $w_\Gamma$ be the scalar coefficient of this chosen product path,
including the bounded local wedge and direct/cross coefficients.  Write
$\operatorname{Contr}^{\rm raw}_{\Gamma,\tau}$ for the typed raw
contraction determined by the record and its circuit state, and put
\[
 F_\Gamma=\#(p\vee r),\qquad
 \ell_\Gamma=\#(p\vee q)
      =\sum_{a\in\mathscr H_\Gamma}\#(p_a\vee q_a),\qquad
 \omega_\Gamma=n^{F_\Gamma}w_\Gamma,\qquad
 \mathcal A_\Gamma=w_\Gamma
       \operatorname{Contr}^{\rm raw}_{\Gamma,\tau}.
\]
Thus $w_\Gamma$ is a scalar coefficient, not the value or norm of an
open contraction; $\omega_\Gamma$ merely expresses the same coefficient
in once-normalized original-circuit units.
title: Rooted ribbon record and raw coefficient

STATEMENT AND LIMIT
Consider UNCORRECTED Adam, b=9/10,d=999/1000, epsilon outside the square
root, on a positive diagonal quadratic with two eigenvalues. Suppose
eta*lambda_i/epsilon>38 for i=1,2. Let K be a compact fully invariant
set of physical states (nonnegative raw variances), and let pi be an
invariant Borel probability measure on K. Suppose pi-almost surely

 sum_i lambda_i*y_i^2*w_i,next*(w_i,next-2)=0.              (1)

Here y_i=x_i/(c*eta), c=1/19, and w_i=c*eta*lambda_i/
(sqrt(v_i)+epsilon). Equation (1) says that scaled active curvature is
38 wherever the gradient is nonzero, with its numerator identity
extended by zero at zero gradients.

Then pi is supported on the nine product states obtained by choosing
in each coordinate either the origin or one of the two cycle phases

 (y,mu,V)=(0,0,0), or (+/-a,-/+c*a,a^2),
 a=1/2-e, e=epsilon/(c*eta*lambda), mu=m/(c*eta*lambda),
 V=v/(c*eta*lambda)^2.

Equivalently pi is a convex combination of the origin atom and the four
uniform measures on the product/axis two-cycles (two axis cycles and two
relative-phase product cycles). If zero gradient has pi-probability zero,
the origin atom is absent.

This is a stationary equality classification. It does NOT show that an
ordinary corrected trajectory with active curvature tending to38 converges
to one of these cycles. Sparse excursions or heteroclinic pieces of an
omega-limit set are not excluded by this proof. In particular it does not
settle the two-supercritical target or upgrade claim016 to that range.

1. THE SOURCE POTENTIAL APPLIES TO BOUNDED FULL ORBITS
Use Fong--Yang arXiv2608.20638v2, Appendix H.1.2, equations105,117--123,
Lemma H.5 and its six-case proof, pp.54--58. Source notation in a scalar
coordinate is p=w_t,w=w_(t+1),u=w/p,y=y_t,z=y_(t-1),Delta=y-z.

Every state in K has a bounded full orbit: repeatedly select predecessors
in K using F(K)=K. The variance recursion gives V_t>=nu*y_(t-1)^2 and
the second-moment/speed identities F1/F2. The eventual condition F3
(p>1 implies w>c) in the source in fact holds at every point of such a
full bounded orbit. Unroll its momentum and variance from time t-N.
The source Step1 argument bounds sqrt(V_next)+e by

 (1+b)*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e + O(b^N*p*|mu_(t-N)|).

Here p<=1/e and boundedness makes the last term tend to zero. Moreover
d/(d-b^2)<9 and e<1/2, so the remaining bound is less than
3*(1+b)+1/2<1/c. Thus F3 holds strictly. All the source's remaining
identities and inequalities are pointwise, with no initialization
condition. Its potential inequality therefore holds at every point of K.

The previous position is a single-valued continuous function of the
current state: z=y+p*mu/c, since y=z-p*mu/c. Hence the printed piecewise
potential Phi is a BOREL function of the scalar state. It is bounded on
K: e>0 bounds p, positions and moments are bounded, and Gamma is bounded.
No continuity of Phi is asserted; claim018 records its boundary jump.

2. EQUALITY CASES OF THE SCALAR MARGIN
Set Psi=Phi(Fz)-Phi(z)-y^2*w*(w-2). The source proves Psi>=0.
The following stricter conclusions are extracted from its proof.

(a) p,w<=1. The exact quadratic expression from Step3 has a positive
definite (Delta,y) matrix. Its determinant is

 (c/2)*w*[(1-b^2*u^2)*(2-w)-(c/2)*(1+b)^2*w],

and its first diagonal entry is c*(1-b^2*u^2)/2>0. Since
u^2<=1/d and 0<w<=1, strict positivity follows from

 1-b^2/d-(c/2)*(1+b)^2 =697/7400>0.

Thus Psi=0 requires y=Delta=0, hence mu=0. The scalar state is a point
on the pure-variance axis y=mu=0 with p,w<=1.

(b) p<=1<w. Step4 has a positive definite quadratic part. For its
coefficients A,B,C the determinant identity printed there is

 AC-B^2/4=c*C/2+b^2*u^2/(1+b)*[c/2-(1-b/2)*(w-1)^2].

The bracket is strictly positive because 1<w<=d^(-1/2)<=1+c.
If y=Delta=0, the quadratic vanishes but V_next=d*V<V and the upward
crossing makes Gamma(V)-Gamma(V_next)>0. Thus Psi>0 always.

(c) p>1>=w. Step5 gives Psi>=y^2*H(w)>0; y is nonzero in this case
by the variance recursion. F3 proved above supplies w>c as required.

(d) p,w>1 and y=0. Step6 gives Psi>=A*Delta^2+
Gamma(V)-Gamma(dV). A>0 and the unclipped Gamma is strictly increasing
for V>0. Thus equality forces Delta=0 and V=0, giving the origin.

(e) p,w>1 and y!=0, u<=b. The source's strict lower bound is
Psi/y^2>=171/50000-6/2375>0.

(f) p,w>1 and y!=0, b<=u<d^(-1/2). Source Step6 bounds Psi/y^2
below by a quadratic form in X=p-2, Z=Delta/y-2, tau=u-1. The (X,Z)
block is positive definite with determinant >=(6/25)*w^2. Its Schur
complement in tau is strictly positive: writing U=1/p in (0,1), the
available coefficient exceeds (243/10)*U while the cost is at most
(625/27)*U^2. Their difference is at least (311/270)*U>0.
Consequently equality forces tau=X=Z=0. Thus p=w=2 and Delta=2*y.
The variance recursion then gives V=V_next=a^2 and |y|=a; the previous
step relation gives mu=-c*y. These are exactly the cycle phases.

The source partition writes u<d^(-1/2). At the endpoint equality in
the speed bound would require y=0 and e=0 or V=0. With e>0 and y!=0,
u=(sqrt(V)+e)/(sqrt(dV+nu*y^2)+e)<d^(-1/2), as required.

Thus the only possible zero-margin scalar states are the origin, the
cycle phases, and a segment of the pure-variance axis below curvature1.
Any positive-variance point on that axis exits this last zero-margin
region after finitely many iterates: V decays geometrically to zero and
eventually crosses w=1, where case(b) has strictly positive margin.

3. INTEGRATE THE BOUNDED BOREL POTENTIAL
Let L=sum_i lambda_i*Phi_i, also bounded Borel. Since pi is invariant,
integral(L composed F-L) d pi=0. Equation (1) and the source inequality
give, pi-almost surely,

 L(Fz)-L(z)=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i(z)>=0.

Its integral is zero, so each nonnegative Psi_i vanishes almost surely.
Invariance implies that, on a single pi-full set, Psi_i(F^n z)=0 for
every integer n>=0 and both coordinates (a countable intersection).
Section2 excludes every positive pure-variance state from this set.
Thus each scalar marginal lies on the origin or exact two-cycle.
The nine product states and the invariant weights stated above follow.

passage of integrals of discontinuous functions under weak convergence
was used. In particular one must not apply this proof to empirical weak
limits before establishing equation(1) for that invariant limit measure.

[Conj 6 (Algebraic Integrability Conjecture) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $K/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ be an algebraic extension of fields. Let $\F$ be a foliation on $K$, which admits a model over the ring of integers $\cO_L$, where $L$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}$.

    The following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The foliation $\F$ is algebraically integrable, i.e., it is of the form $\F=\op{Der}_{W}(K)$ for a subfield $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\subset W\subset K$.
        \item For almost all primes $p$ and all maximal ideals $q$ over $p$ in $\cO_L$ the reduction modulo $q$ of $\F$ is $p$-closed, i.e., it defines a $1$-foliation.
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Algebraic Integrability Conjecture

Let f:[0,1]->R be 1-Lipschitz and 0<epsilon<1/2. Set n=2 ceil(4 epsilon^(-3)). There exists an even real polynomial p(z)=p_0+sum_{j=1}^{n/2} p_(2j) z^(2j), of degree at most n, such that sup_{z in [0,1]}|p(z)-f(z)|<=epsilon and |p_(2j)|<=2^n for j>=1. The constant coefficient p_0 is not bounded uniformly over all such f; additive constants of f are unrestricted. The coefficient bound is exponential 2^n, not the product 2n.
f is real-valued and 1-Lipschitz on [0,1]
0<epsilon<1/2
only nonconstant coefficients have the uniform bound

[Definition 37 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] Given $n$ and $r$ we define the chain complex $(\mathsf{TT}(n,r), d_{\mathsf{TT}})$ as follows.  The underlying graded vector space is

$$ \mathsf{TT}(n,r) = \left(\ds\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lfloor (n-r+1)/2\rfloor} \Sigma^{2i-r+2}\mathsf{T}(n,2i+1,r-2)\right)\oplus \Sigma^{1-r}\mathsf{T}(n,0,r-1).$$	
The differential $d_{\mathsf{TT}}$ is of the form $d_{\mathsf{TT}}= d_{\mathsf{T}} + (-1)^{E} d_R$ 
where $d_\mathsf{T}$ is the differential on each summand, and where $d_R\colon \mathsf{T}(n,1,r-2) \to \mathsf{T}(n,0,r-1)$ is defined to take the unique blue marking and turn it red. 

The fact that $d_{\mathsf{TT}}^2 = 0$ follows immediately from the fact that edge contraction and changing the color of a marking commute; the sign ensures they anti-commute.
title: Definition 37 of arXiv:2609.04033

Let N be a positive integer and X a random variable with values in D(N); put F(n) = P(X | n) for n | N (the event that X divides n). Then P(X = n) = sum_{d | n} mu(n/d) F(d), with mu the arithmetic Moebius function. Conversely, a real function F on D(N) equals n -> P(X | n) for some law on D(N) if and only if F(N) = 1 and every value p(n) = sum_{d | n} mu(n/d) F(d) is nonnegative. Monotonicity cannot replace nonnegativity: on D(6), F(1) = 0, F(2) = F(3) = 3/5, F(6) = 1 is order-preserving with F(6) = 1, yet p(6) = F(6) - F(2) - F(3) + F(1) = -1/5.
N is a positive integer
X takes values in the positive divisors of N
X | n means that X divides n

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] This is the proved kernel inequality used for the campaign answer to Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). Let mu be a probability measure on R whose support has diameter at most one, and for R>0 define xi_R(u)=the integral over x in the real line of [(x-u)^2+R^2]^(-1) mu(dx). If xi_R'(u_0)=0 and xi_R''(u_0)>=0, then xi_R(u_0)>=1. Equality forces R^2=3/4 and mu=(delta_{u_0-1/2}+delta_{u_0+1/2})/2, where delta_a denotes a unit point mass at a. The proof decomposes the mean-zero-derivative constraint into one- and two-atom extreme measures and checks the two polynomial inequalities written out in the record. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
mu is a probability measure with support diameter at most one.
R>0; u_0 is stationary with nonnegative second derivative.

The three quantities in
play are
$$F = \int \varphi \, d\mu = \xi_R(0), \qquad G = \int \frac{d}{(d^2+s)^2}\,d\mu = -\tfrac12 \xi_R'(0),
\qquad H = \int \frac{3d^2-s}{(d^2+s)^3}\,d\mu = \tfrac12\xi_R''(0),$$
and the hypotheses are $G = 0$ and $H \ge 0$. All three are linear in $\mu$.

Consider the set $K$ of probability measures $\nu$ on $\operatorname{supp}\mu$ with $G(\nu)=0$. It is
convex and weak-* compact, and its extreme points carry at most two atoms, since a measure subject to
normalisation and one further linear constraint can be perturbed inside $K$ as soon as its support has
three points. By Choquet's theorem $\mu$ is a barycentre of extreme points, and $F$, $G$ and $H$
integrate accordingly. An extreme point with a single atom must be $\delta_0$, because $G(\delta_x)=0$
forces $x=0$. So it is enough to understand a *pair*: atoms at $-a$ and $b$ with $a,b>0$ and
$a+b \le 1$.

For such a pair the condition $G=0$ determines the two weights, and writing $A = a^2+s$, $B = b^2+s$ and
$\Delta = bA^2+aB^2 > 0$,
$$F - 1 = \frac{\Phi}{\Delta}, \qquad H = \frac{\Psi}{\Delta AB}, \qquad
\Phi = bA(1-A) + aB(1-B), \qquad \Psi = bB(3a^2-s) + aA(3b^2-s).$$
In terms of $D = a+b$ and $m = ab$ both collapse:
$$\frac{\Psi}{D} = 3m^2 + s(6m - D^2) - s^2, \qquad
\frac{\Phi}{D} = 3m^2 + m(1-D^2) + s(1-2m) - s^2 .$$

**Lemma A.** *If $\Psi \ge 0$ then $s \le \tfrac34 D^2$.* The quantity $\Psi/D$ is increasing in $m$, so
it is largest at $m = D^2/4$, where it equals $(3D^2-4s)(D^2+4s)/16$. For that to be nonnegative,
$s \le \tfrac34 D^2$.

**Lemma B.** *If $0 \le s \le \tfrac34$ and $D \le 1$ then $\Phi \ge 0$.* The quantity $\Phi/D$ is
concave in $s$, so on $[0,\tfrac34]$ it is least at an endpoint. At $s=0$ it is $m(1+3m-D^2) \ge 0$. At
$s = \tfrac34$ it is a convex function of $m$ whose derivative at $m = D^2/4$ is $(D^2-1)/2 \le 0$, so it
decreases on $(0, D^2/4]$ and is least at $m = D^2/4$, where it equals $(1-D^2)(D^2+3)/16 \ge 0$.

## Putting it together

Let $\mu$, $R$ and $u_0$ be as in the proposition, and decompose $\mu$ into extreme points as above.

Since $H(\mu) \ge 0$, some extreme point $\kappa$ has $H(\kappa) \ge 0$. It cannot be $\delta_0$, for
which $H = -1/s^2 < 0$. So $\kappa$ is a pair, and Lemma A gives $s \le \tfrac34 D_\kappa^2 \le \tfrac34$.

Now every extreme point has $F \ge 1$. For $\delta_0$ this is $F = 1/s \ge 4/3$. For a pair it is Lemma
B, which needs only $s \le \tfrac34$ and diameter at most one, and in particular does not care about the
sign of that pair's own $H$. Averaging, $F(\mu) \ge 1$, which is the proposition.

Equality is rigid. Lemma B is an equality only at $D=1$, $m=D^2/4$ and $s = \tfrac34$, that is, two atoms
of equal weight at $\pm\tfrac12$ with $R^2 = \tfrac34$: the symmetric Bernoulli law at its critical
radius, rescaled. So the symmetric Bernoulli is the unique extremal measure, which is why the constant it
produces is the answer.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:41d53089fc9154dfc68427cb689fc659cab94c6fae196dceb869ccf188d76c60","revision_digest":"sha256:9b4c7b6d3b0ec8dff2722e778fc17fe40b74161b32c5838f250300a75f180ac4","source_id":"doi:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15","source_revision":"problem source: ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374; own campaign record: 2026-09-14","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: [Theorem 1.2 (Colorful Tverberg theorem) of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let d, t ≥1, let (X, C) satisfy VC(C) ≤d, and let S1, . . . , Sd+1 ⊆X be pairwise disjoint finite sets. If |Si| ≥d(t −1) + 1 for every i ∈[d + 1], then there exist pairwise disjoint transversals T1, . . . , Tt of the color classes whose convex hulls have a common point; that is, t\ j=1 conv(Tj) ̸= ∅. We also compare the strong Helly number with two refinements from the literature.

body: The characteristic-function route to the quadratic-form bounded-density conjecture is VIABLE, not a dead end (correction of an earlier note). ||p||_inf <= (1/2pi) integral|phi_Q|. Three large eigenvalues each contribute a stationary-phase factor |t|^{-1/2}, so |phi_Q(t)| ~ |t|^{-3/2}, just inside integrability; two give |t|^{-1}, divergent - that is why three. The 'dead end' rested on the 3-D uniform ball (|phi|~1/t), which is not a projection of a product of 1-D densities and so not a valid instance. Measured integral|phi|/(2pi): 6.3 separable-uniform, 6.5 delocalized, 3.3 bimodal, 4.5-6.0 for the adversarial edge law 1{cos(s x^2)>1/2} - its bump at frequency s is killed by the other two directions and shrinks as s grows. So the whole conjecture reduces to ONE uniform oscillatory-integral estimate integral|phi_Q| <= 2 pi C over all A with three large eigenvalues and all laws <=1 (C~7; sharp density constant 3sqrt2). The per-direction van der Corput is still non-uniform; the estimate must be joint over the three directions.

Proof: q^ is orthogonal to w, so its part on I_1 is orthogonal to w and P is a function of (D, X_R); given (D, X_R) the hub law and z = s - lambda (V - v_0)^2 - F_0 - F_1 P are fixed and x* = z/(2t); the dilation bathtub of Proposition 3.14 (kappa = 0) gives sup_l g(l|D) log(1 + 1/|z|), and the Fresnel small-ball bound for z as a quadratic in X_R gives E[log(1+1/|z|) | D] <= 2 + log(1 + 2 pi^4/|lambda|). Window laws on I_1: M_D <= sum |w_i| (Cauchy projection of a unit cube), so <= 10.8 for |I_1| = 2, |lambda| >= 1; support length K: M_D <= K^{|I_1|-1} sum |w_i|. v may have a part on I_1 (automatically orthogonal to w) with |lambda| |v_R|^2 in place of |lambda|. AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let r_n<=q_n tend to infinity with r_n/q_n->gamma in (0,1], and let B_n be biorthogonally invariant real r_n by q_n signals with finite second moments. Let mu_n be their empirical singular-value laws after dividing the matrices by sqrt(r_n). If E W2(mu_n,mu)^2->0 for a deterministic finite-second-moment probability law mu on [0,infinity), then i_n(s)=I(B_n;sqrt(s)B_n+G_n)/(r_n*q_n) converges locally uniformly on s>=0 to a finite concave function i_mu. The law mu may have atoms, including a zero atom, and need not have finite logarithmic energy. Apply Theorem 4 only to regular spectral approximations with bounded smooth densities on compact intervals away from zero; shared-Haar Gaussian information continuity then pays the limit exchange. For X_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N), with independent arrays of fixed centered iid real unit-variance factor laws of sizes N by M and P by M, finite fourth moments, and positive finite limits P/N,M/N, the Gaussian-factor reference B_N has the needed expected spectral W2 convergence by unaudited claim 008. At every differentiability point s>0 of its limiting normalized MI, m_B_N(s)->2*i_mu_prime(s) and limsup_N[m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)]<=0, where m_Q=E||Q-E[Q|sqrt(s)Q+G]||_F^2/(NP). This follows from the Haar comparison in unaudited claim 006. The possible exceptional SNR set is at most countable; pointwise MMSE extremality there remains open. Raw-product loss gaps are divided by N. Novelty of this continuity consequence and application is unestablished; all new proof dependencies remain unaudited.
Real matrices and standard independent Gaussian channel noise; Frobenius error divided by the number of entries.
Generic extension: biorthogonal invariance, finite second moments, positive finite rectangular aspect limit and expected spectral W2 convergence after dividing the signal by sqrt(number of rows).
Product consequence: positive finite limits P/N,M/N; independent fixed centered iid unit-variance real factor laws with finite fourth moments.
Published Theorem 4 is used only for compact bounded spectral densities away from zero and bounded deterministic singular profiles; its Assumptions 2,3 and aspect bound are checked.
The existing entropy/coupling arguments in claims 006 and 008 remain unaudited dependencies.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6a6ca6a63166d44d3d9cf9391583d684e5e68cfd473148bf446c647856003226","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6a/6a6ca6a63166d44d3d9cf9391583d684e5e68cfd473148bf446c647856003226.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4ff0a7bdc107601cb716445557a06517fa517d47ab08abe6e8d67724f83df970","bundle_entry_key":"rotational-mi-limit-spectral-atoms-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-mi-limit-spectral-atoms-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:rotational-mi-limit-spectral-atoms-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Extending a rotationally invariant MI limit through spectral atoms

Target 2, proof draft, unaudited. Novelty is unestablished. The extension
uses a published theorem for regular spectral densities and our existing
entropy-continuity lemma; it is not a new derivation of the published
spherical-integral formula.

## 1. Statement and the external input

Let r_n<=q_n be positive integers, r_n->infinity, and r_n/q_n->gamma in
(0,1]. Let B_n be biorthogonally invariant real r_n by q_n matrices with
finite second moments. Let mu_n be the empirical distribution of the r_n
singular values of B_n/sqrt(r_n). Assume that a deterministic probability
measure mu on [0,infinity), of finite second moment, satisfies

    E W2(mu_n,mu)^2 -> 0.                              (1)

The claim is that

    i_n(s)=I(B_n;sqrt(s)B_n+G_n)/(r_n*q_n)

converges to a finite concave function i_mu(s) for every s>=0, locally
uniformly in s. Here G_n has independent standard real Gaussian entries.
No density, finite logarithmic moment or finite logarithmic energy of mu
is required. In particular mu may have a zero atom.

The external input is Pourkamali-Macris, arXiv:2403.04615, Theorem 4,
equation (14), PDF p6. In its real Gaussian model this establishes the
normalized MI limit for biorthogonally invariant signals S_n whose
empirical singular-value laws converge almost surely to a compactly
supported density satisfying Assumption 2 (including finite logarithmic
moment and logarithmic energy of its symmetrization), and whose empirical
second moments are almost surely bounded (Assumption 3), when q_n/r_n
is bounded. The source uses noise of entry variance 1/r_n: its posterior
Gaussian quadratic has exponent -r_n||Y-sqrt(s)S||_F^2/2 (equation (65)).
Set S_n=B_n/sqrt(r_n) and multiply the observation by sqrt(r_n); the MI
and normalization are exactly i_n(s) above. Theorem 4 is invoked as stated,
not reproved here. Its proof explicitly includes fixed singular values
with independent Haar frames, in Section 5.6.1, equation (68), PDF p19.

## 2. Approximating laws that meet every spectral hypothesis

There exist measures mu_k with bounded smooth densities supported in
[a_k,b_k] subset (0,infinity), such that W2(mu_k,mu)->0. One construction
is to couple A~mu with

    A_k=min(A,R_k)+2*epsilon_k+epsilon_k*Z,

where R_k->infinity, epsilon_k->0, and Z is independent with a smooth
bounded density compactly supported in [-1,1]. The resulting density is
smooth, bounded and supported inside [epsilon_k,R_k+3*epsilon_k].
The L2 coupling error tends to zero by the finite second moment of A
and the triangle inequality. This proves the W2 approximation assertion.

For each k, let mu_(n,k) put mass 1/r_n on the mid-quantiles
F_k^(-1)((j-1/2)/r_n), j=1,...,r_n. They converge in W2 to mu_k;
bounded support and convergence of the quantile step functions almost
everywhere give this by dominated convergence. Define B_(n,k) to have
these singular values multiplied by sqrt(r_n), with independent Haar
left and right frames.

In the source convention S_(n,k)=B_(n,k)/sqrt(r_n), its limiting spectral
density is mu_k. Its symmetrization is a bounded density supported in
two compact intervals separated from zero. Thus its log absolute moment
is finite. Its logarithmic energy is finite as well: the singularity
|log|x-y|| is locally Lebesgue integrable and the density is bounded,
while the support is compact. The empirical second moments are bounded
deterministically by b_k^2. The aspect bound follows from gamma>0.
These verify Assumptions 2,3 and the aspect condition separately for
each fixed k. Theorem 4 gives a finite limit

    i_k(s)=lim_n I(B_(n,k);sqrt(s)B_(n,k)+G_n)/(r_n*q_n).

## 3. Continuity pays for the two limits

Couple B_n and B_(n,k) by the same Haar frames and pair their decreasing
singular values. The normalized squared cost is

    delta_(n,k)^2
      = (r_n/q_n) E W2(mu_n,mu_(n,k))^2.

By (1), the deterministic quantile convergence and the L2 triangle
inequality for the random W2 distance,

    limsup_n delta_(n,k) <= sqrt(gamma)*W2(mu,mu_k).    (2)

The Gaussian-smoothed entropy continuity bound from claim 006 gives

    |i_n(s)-i_(n,k)(s)| <= sqrt(s)*delta_(n,k).        (3)

Applied also to two deterministic-quantile approximating models, it gives

    |i_j(s)-i_k(s)| <= sqrt(s*gamma)*W2(mu_j,mu_k).    (4)

Here the finite empirical quantile W2 distances converge to the distance
between their limiting laws. Equation (4) shows that i_k are Cauchy
uniformly on every [0,S]. Denote their limit by i_mu. Passing n->infinity
in (3), then k->infinity using (2), proves i_n(s)->i_mu(s). More precisely
the same argument with sup_(0<=s<=S) in (3) proves locally uniform
convergence, because the regular-model i_(n,k) converge locally uniformly.
For that last assertion, pointwise convergence from Theorem 4 plus the
common Lipschitz bound on i_(n,k) suffices: their derivatives are at most
E||B_(n,k)||_F^2/(2*r_n*q_n)<=b_k^2/2. A finite grid proves uniform
convergence on [0,S], including zero, without any derivative interchange.

The limits are finite: the zero estimator and I-MMSE give
0<=i_n(s)<=s E||B_n||_F^2/(2*r_n*q_n), whose upper bounds stay finite
by (1). Finite-dimensional Gaussian-channel information is concave in s;
therefore its finite limit is concave too. This proves the statement.

## 4. Gaussian-factor reference at all positive finite aspect ratios

Let B_N=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N), with factors N by M and P by M and independent
standard Gaussian entries. Transpose when needed, set r=min(N,P),
q=max(N,P), and use the singular-value law of B_N/sqrt(r). Claim 008,
Section 3, supplies expected W2 convergence to a deterministic finite-
second-moment law; its scaling from sqrt(N) to sqrt(r) is deterministic
and has a positive finite limit. This dependency remains unaudited.
Positive finite limits P/N and M/N ensure r/q->gamma>0 and bounded
normalized second moments. The preceding result therefore supplies a
finite Gaussian-reference MI limit for every s>=0, including when the
limiting product spectrum has an atom at zero.

Now take fixed centered iid unit-variance real non-Gaussian factor laws
with finite fourth moments and the same dimensions. Claim 008 also
supplies their expected singular-profile coupling to the reference.
Apply the already proved abstract comparison in claim 006. At every
differentiability point s>0 of the finite concave reference limit i_mu,

    m_B_N(s) -> 2*i_mu'(s),
    limsup_N [m_X_N(s)-m_B_N(s)] <= 0.               (5)

The exceptional set is at most countable, fixed by the reference limit.
At an arbitrary s>0, the weaker left-derivative bound from claim 006
still holds. This does not assert a reference MMSE limit at a corner,
nor pointwise domination there. Raw product losses require division of
their gap by N, as in claim 014. The main all-SNR Target 2 remains open
at possible nondifferentiability points; differentiability has not been
proved by the smooth spectral approximations.

An explicit warning example is useful: concave C1 functions can converge
uniformly to min(s,1), which has a corner. For epsilon>0 take f_e(s)=s
on s<=1-epsilon, f_e(s)=1 on s>=1+epsilon, and
f_e(s)=1-(s-1-epsilon)^2/(4*epsilon) between. The pieces and first
derivatives match at both endpoints; the derivative decreases from one
to zero. The uniform error from min(s,1) is epsilon/4. Thus no
differentiability conclusion follows merely from smoothing and a
uniform MI estimate.

## 5. What is new here, and what remains unchecked

The compact-support wording in the header of source Proposition 2 does
not remove the density obligation by itself. Its Appendix D.1 proof,
specifically Lemma D.1, invokes Assumptions 2 and 3 and finite
non-commutative entropy when applying Theorem 1.1 of Guionnet-Huang.
An atomic input cannot be inserted on the strength of that header alone.
The present argument deliberately applies Theorem 4 only to the regular
mu_k, verifies those hypotheses there, and then uses a separate
dimension-uniform information-continuity estimate. This is why it pays
the obstruction recorded in mmse_source_obstruction.md rather than
ignoring that earlier source check.

This draft discharges the input-density and zero-atom obstruction to
using the published MI-limit theorem, under explicit expected-W2 input
control. It does not claim a new spherical-integral theorem or a new
formula for the reference MI. Novelty of this continuity extension and
its T287 application is not established. The least-trusted dependencies
are the existing unaudited spectral W2 proof (claim 008), and application
of the source theorem to the stated fixed-profile Haar approximants.
The latter is supported by the source's own equation (68), not by an
assumption that the finite-dimensional prior has a Lebesgue density.
The dimension-uniform expansion remainder in Target 1 is still open.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:25bcd81ad466af1f9b60ed4d72864af965cb06d0860dcf7c047c7f84ddd1d3e3","revision_digest":"sha256:9b5d4d7e9fe29a46884d44ce11f56d7089af1e16e119b1edf09451339216b4cb","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:rotational-mi-limit-spectral-atoms-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21 claim w718-T287-016 version 1, proof unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] Under assumption $H_1$, for each $\theta \in (0,1)$, there exist deterministic constants
		\[
		C=C(\theta)>0,\qquad N=N(\theta)>0,
