[Definition Bk class define of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let $d, m \ge 1$ and $\beta \ge 0$. We define
		\[
		\mathbb{B}^{\beta} \triangleq \left\{\mathcal B:\
		\text{there exist }\mathcal J={\mathrm{diag}}(\mathcal J_{1},\cdots ,\mathcal J_{m})\in\mathrm{OP}\mathbf S_0^\beta
		\text{ and }\mathcal V\in\mathrm{OP}\mathbf S_0^0\text{ such that  }
		\mathcal B=\mathcal J+\mathcal V
		\text{ and (Bk:(J V) of the paper)  holds}
		\right\},
		\]
		where condition (Bk:(J V) of the paper) is specified as follows:
		\begin{enumerate}[label={$(\mathbf{B}^\beta)$},leftmargin=0.79cm]
			\item  
			$\mathcal J_{i} \in {\mathrm{OP}}\mathcal S_0^{\beta}$ and $\mathcal J_{i} + \mathcal J_{i}^{*} \in {\mathrm{OP}}\mathcal S_0^{0}$ for $1 \le i \le m$. 
			Additionally, the symbols of $\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal V$ are commuting matrices.
		\end{enumerate}
		A subset $\mathscr{N} \subset \mathbb{B}^{\beta}$ is bounded if one can choose a decomposition
		$\mathcal B=\mathcal J_{\mathcal B}+\mathcal V_{\mathcal B}$ for every
		$\mathcal B\in\mathscr N$ such that 
		$
		\{\mathcal J_{i,\mathcal B}:\mathcal B\in\mathscr N,1 \le i \le m\}$
		is bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathcal S_0^\beta$, 
		$	\{\mathcal J_{i,\mathcal B}+\mathcal J^*_{i,\mathcal B}:\mathcal B\in\mathscr N,1 \le i \le m\}$  is bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathcal S_0^0$,  and $\{\mathcal V_{\mathcal B}:\mathcal B\in\mathscr N\}$
		are bounded in $\mathrm{OP}\mathbf S_0^0$.

body: Publication record. Problem 11 of N. N. Ganikhodzhaev and U. A. Rozikov, Quadratic stochastic operators: results and open problems (2009), asks whether their Theorem 6 (a strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on three types has a unique fixed point, and it is not attractive) extends to more types. Y. Shmalo, Fixed points of strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators in four or more types (September 2026) shows that it does not extend to four or more types; uniqueness at four types is left open and reduced to one determinant inequality by an index count. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/strictly-nonvolterra-qso-fixed-points (commit 0526854748f5); ResearchGate record 414323511. Not refereed.
title: Ganikhodzhaev-Rozikov Problem 11 answered: the fixed-point theorem for strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators does not extend to four or more types (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/strictly-nonvolterra-qso-fixed-points)

body:
[Corollary cor:finite-profile-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $H\geq1$ and $k\geq2$, and let $G$ be a nontrivial torsion-free abelian
group.  The following four collections of truncated profiles are identical:
\[
 \bigl\{(|jA|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:A\subset G,\ |A|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(|jB|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
\[
 \bigl\{(|P^{\times j}|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       P\subset\mathbb Z_{>0},\ |P|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(H_{C_B}(j))_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
where $P^{\times j}$ is the $j$-fold product set and $C_B$ is the projective
monomial curve attached to $B$ over an arbitrary field.  More strongly,
equip the subgroup generated by an additive realization with a
translation-invariant linear order.  Its complete equality-and-order table
through degree $H$ then has an integer exponent representative.  The
resulting sumset, product-set, and monomial-curve exponent models have
identical ordered tables, active ranks, and relation-birth degrees through
$H$.

Every such table has a primitive integer representative
$B=\{0=b_0<\cdots<b_{k-1}\}$ with
\begin{equation}
 b_{k-1}\leq dH^{d-1}\prod_{i=1}^r p_i
 \leq(k-1-r)H^{k-2},
 \qquad d=k-1-r,
\end{equation}
where $r$ and $p_i$ are its active rank and birth degrees through $H$.
The universal exponent $k-2$ for preserving the complete truncated table is
best possible.

body: Consider an autonomous C^1 planar vector field dx/dt = f(x) on an open subset of R^2, and a forward trajectory that stays inside a compact set for all t >= 0. The Poincare-Bendixson theorem states that its omega-limit set is nonempty, compact, connected, and is either a fixed point, a periodic orbit, or a union of finitely many fixed points joined by homoclinic or heteroclinic orbits; in particular, if the omega-limit set contains no fixed point, it is a single periodic orbit. The result is specific to the plane and fails for flows in dimension 3 or higher. Due to Henri Poincare and Ivar Bendixson.
title: Poincare-Bendixson theorem

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] [\textbf{Convergence of the Dynkin martingale}]
Let $H \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$. The sequence of martingales $\big\{ \big(  \mathcal{M}_t^n(H)  \big)_{0 \leq t \leq T}, \; n \in \mathbb{N}_+\big\}$ converges with respect to the Skorohod topology of $\mathcal{D}([0, T], \mathbb{R})$ to a mean zero Gaussian process $\mathcal{M}(H)$, as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{M}(H)$ is a continuous martingale on $[0, T]$ whose quadratic variation is $\langle \mathcal{M}(H) \rangle_t = t D_3 \mathcal{P}^{ \gamma} H$. body: In mathematical analysis, the Weierstrass approximation theorem states that every continuous function defined on a closed interval [a, b] can be uniformly approximated as closely as desired by a polynomial function. Because polynomials are among the simplest functions, and because computers can directly evaluate polynomials, this theorem has both practical and theoretical relevance, especially in polynomial interpolation. The original version of this result was established by Karl Weierstrass in 1885 using the Weierstrass transform.
title: Stone–Weierstrass theorem

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof} Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$.
Recall the notation \eqref{e:lam.mu.delta.ball}, and suppose
$(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda$ and 
 $(\lambda,\mu)\in B_\delta(\lambda',\mu')$. Given $\YY'\in S_\star(\lambda',\mu';\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$, we will construct $\YY\in S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ which is $o_\delta(1)$-close to $\YY'$. We set $\vwww$ as in Lemma~\ref{l:D.mu.continuity.w}, so that we have the bound $\|\vwww-\vwww'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2$. Recalling Lemma~\ref{l:p.polytope.bd.local.aux}, we see that
 $\vwww,\vwww'$ are confined to a compact domain $[0,9/\iota_0]^s$.
The $\Budget$ function is uniformly continuous on the compact domain
$[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}\times\Lambda$, so
	\[\sup\bigg\{
	\begin{array}{l}
	|\Budget(\YY;\mu)
	-\Budget(\YY';\mu')|
	:\YY,\YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s},
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\mu-\mu'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\|\YY-\YY'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2
	\end{array}
	\bigg\} \le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\]
where $o_\delta(1)$ denotes an error tending to zero as $\delta\to0$. 
For the purposes of this proof, let us abbreviate
	\begin{align*}
	c(\YY;\lambda)
	&\equiv \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
	+ \epsilon_1\alpha^2\iota^2(\|\vBBb\|_2)^2\,,\\
	g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	&\equiv c(\YY;\lambda) - \Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2\,.
	\end{align*}
Then we can similarly bound
	\[\sup\bigg\{\begin{array}{l}
	|c(\YY';\lambda)
	-c(\YY';\lambda')|
	: \YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}, 
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\end{array}
	\bigg\}
	 \le o_\delta(1)\,.
	\]
Combining the above bounds gives
	\beq
	c(\YY';\lambda)
	-\Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2
	\le g (\YY';\lambda',\mu') + o_\delta(1)
	\le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\eeq
uniformly over 
$(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')$ in $\Lambda$ within distance $\delta$,
and
$\YY,\YY'\in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$ within distance $\delta/\iota^2$.
If the above left-hand side is in fact $\le0$ then we are done, since we can then set
$\YY=(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
 to achieve
$g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$. If the above left-hand side is
 strictly positive, then it remains to choose 
 $\YY=(\vBBb,\vvvv,\vUUu,\vwww)$
 close to 
 $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$ to make $g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$.
In this case, consider the path in $\cD_\mu$ given by the line segment joining $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
to $\YY(1)\equiv(\vec{0},\vvvv'-\vUUu',\vec{0},\vwww)$. If we parametrize this segment as a linear function $\YY(t)$ of $t\in[0,1]$, then along the segment we have
	\[\Cost(\YY(t);\lambda)
	-\Cost(\YY(0);\lambda)
	=-(\lambda,\vBBb'+\vUUu')t
	\equiv -A(\YY')t\,.
	\]
Recall from \eqref{e:surplus.small.error.bound} that at the start of the line segment we have $g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu) \le o_\delta(1)$.  Let $\eta = g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu)$. We then divide into several cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item If  $A(\YY')\ge\eta^{1/2}$, then we can choose $t_0= \eta / A(\YY') \le \eta^{1/2}$ such that
	\[
	g(\YY(t_0);\lambda,\mu) 
	\le  \eta^{1/2} - A(\YY') t_0 
	\le 0\,,
	\]
and (since $\YY,\YY' \in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$) $\|\YY(t_0)-\YY(0)\|_2 \lesssim \eta^{1/2}$. In this case, we can conclude by setting $\YY = \YY(t_0)$.

\[

\]

\[

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $T:Z\to Z$ be a Borel automorphism of a standard Borel space.
There is a Borel family of sets
\[
    z\longmapsto P_z\subset\mathbb R
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $P_z$ are uniformly Delone;

\item
\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z);
\]

\item
if $z,w\in Z$ and $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
    P_w=P_z-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^u z;
\]

\item
for every $z\in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1)
\]
in the sense of tempered distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Aldous and Janson, The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II (arXiv:2303.02529), Open Problem 14 (pp. 54-55) asks to prove that L_n, the expected drawn length of DTCS(n) under their recursion (73) l(chi_m) = l(chi_i) + l(chi_{m-i}) + 2 + |h(chi_{m-i}) - h(chi_i)|, grows roughly like n log^4 n. Our result (id P0340, 2026-09-08): the drawn length is Theta(n), so the conjecture is FALSE. For every full binary tree the drawn length is at most the sum of all leaf depths, because the increment 2 + |h_R - h_L| is at most n_L + n_R (a full binary tree with k leaves has height at most k-1); with the authors' own Theorem 3 (the expected depth of a random leaf is asymptotic to (1/(2 zeta(2))) log^2 n = 3 pi^-2 log^2 n) this gives E[drawn length] <= n E[leaf depth] ~ (3/pi^2) n log^2 n = o(n log^4 n). The heuristic's error is a missing factor m: their heuristic (75) uses n a(n,m) as the mean count of size-m subclades where the correct count is (n/m) a(n,m); with the wrong count the conjecture is reproduced exactly, with the right one the scale sum converges (sum log^3 m / m^2) instead of diverging (sum log^3 m / m). Verification as the source words it: machine-checked in P0340.lean, together with the exact decomposition drawn(T) = sum of internal subtree heights + height(T); simulation gives L_n/n = 4.71, 4.78, 4.84, 4.83, 4.86 at n = 10^3 to 4 x 10^5 - flat across a 400x range while log^4 n grows 12x - with the sampler validated first against the paper's own clade counts and leaf-depth law. Prior art not cleared.
DTCS(n), the discrete critical beta-splitting tree of Aldous and Janson
drawn length defined by their recursion (73)

[Corollary 34 (Conditional convergence) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let either $W(\mu):=\mu(\varphi_0)$, with $\varphi_0\in\Cc$, $\varphi_0\not\equiv0$, fixed
and $\eps$ admissible in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:restricted} and small
enough that $\bN(\mu(\varphi_0)>\eps)>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:PZ}); or

here, since $\mu(\R^d)$ has no atoms under $\bN$ and
$\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)\in(0,\infty)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:totalmass}). Then
\[
\bP\bigl(\mu_n\in\cdot\;\big|\;W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)
\;\xRightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\;
\bN\bigl(\,\cdot\,\big|\;W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)
:=\frac{\bN(\,\cdot\,;\,W(\mu)>\eps)}{\bN(W(\mu)>\eps)}
\]
weakly as probability measures on $\cM$, and
$n^{2}\,\bP\bigl(W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)\to\bN\bigl(W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)\in(0,\infty)$.

[Lemma lem:ineqs of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $H_n$ be integer-valued and let $N_n(h),L_n(h)$ be nonnegative random
variables such that
$$
\{H_n\ge h\}=\{N_n(h)\ge1\},
\qquad
\{L_n(h)\ge1\}\subseteq\{H_n\ge h\}.
$$
If $\mathbb{E}[N_n(h_n)]\to0$, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to0$. If
$L_n(h_n)\to\infty$ in probability, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:t0-asymptotics of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Fix $\lambda_*>0$.  Uniformly for all $\lambda\geq\lambda_*$ and all
admissible solutions $(f,g)$ at $t=0$, with $u=\log g$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \lambda\|f\|_{C^0}=O(\alpha^{-1}),
 \qquad \|u\|_{C^0}\leq C,
 \qquad
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C} f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}=o(1)
 \quad (\alpha\to\infty).
\end{equation}
More precisely,
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\geq\lambda_*}
 \sup_{(f,g)\in\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}}
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{as }\alpha\to\infty,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}\) denotes the set of admissible
solutions at \(t=0\).

body: A finite affine plane of order n (n >= 2) has n^2 points and n^2 + n lines, each line containing n points and each point lying on n + 1 lines, such that any two distinct points lie on a unique line and, for every line L and point p not on L, there is a unique line through p that does not meet L. Equivalently, its points and lines form a 2-(n^2, n, 1) design.

[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}

Garg, Gunn and Wang, arXiv:2506.01854v2, Corollary 4: relative to any crypto oracle, there are no statistically secure pseudorandom codes robust to any constant rate of independent random binary errors. This already holds for secret-key zero-bit PRCs with negligible soundness and completeness errors and polynomial query complexity. Their noise parameter rho is correlation: N_rho refreshes each bit independently with probability 1-rho, equivalently flips each bit with probability (1-rho)/2; constant positive noise means rho is bounded away from 1. Section 1.1 interprets this as a fully black-box separation from primitives implemented by crypto oracles; footnote 3 specifies the additional PSPACE oracle used in that interpretation. The statistical oracle impossibility must not be read as an unconditional impossibility from existence of one-way functions.
Binary channel with a constant positive independent bit-flip rate below one half
Statistical security in the oracle model of the source
Polynomially many oracle queries and polynomial block length
Negligible completeness and soundness errors

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p < infinity, and F: X x Y -> [0, infinity] measurable for the product sigma-algebra. Then ( int_Y ( int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) )^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} <= int_X ( int_Y F(x,y)^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} dmu(x), both sides in [0, infinity]. Consequently, for complex measurable F with the right-hand side (computed with |F|) finite, int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) converges absolutely for nu-a.e. y and its L^p(nu)-norm is at most the right-hand side. In words: the L^p norm of an integral is at most the integral of the L^p norms. (For p = infinity the analogous statement with ess sup holds for F >= 0.)
(X, mu) and (Y, nu) are sigma-finite measure spaces
F is measurable with respect to the product sigma-algebra
F >= 0 (or the right-hand side is finite when F is complex)
1 <= p < infinity

The exponent obeys L_A(r)=L_B(r)+(tr A0+tr A1)/4. If one traceless part has nonzero imaginary eigenvalues +-i omega, a fixed real similarity and time scaling transform the traceless pair into J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] and eta H+sJ, H=diag(1,-1), eta>=0, s real; normalized rate rho=r/omega and the original traceless exponent equals omega times the normalized exponent at rho. For unscaled traceless matrices with spectral abscissae ki=sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)), there exist scalar shifts Ai=Bi-ai I making both individually Hurwitz with prescribed damping average abar iff abar>(k0+k1)/2. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:fe9deef0fb4c1dc2fd37af05e0411297191295e99ba0bd9b9fd07f9a34beeaa3","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/fe/fe9deef0fb4c1dc2fd37af05e0411297191295e99ba0bd9b9fd07f9a34beeaa3.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f8ff4440509bf25d23b1f813a193e1f47561ae62770e6b1d6dfd2632f3491f3c","bundle_entry_key":"canonical","bundle_id":"population.w658-hurwitz-disconnected-instability-002","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"randomly switched planar linear systems","draft":"w658/bundle_002_resubmit.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.switched.linear:elliptic-planar-pair-canonical-form-and-trace-shift","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# E0018-C3 v1: scalar traces and canonical elliptic-pair reduction
Status: proof (unaudited), 2026-10-14.

Let symmetric-rate switching alternate two real 2x2 matrices Ai. Put
Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I, so Bi is traceless. Let tau=(tr A0+tr A1)/4.
The top Lyapunov exponent satisfies L_A(r)=L_B(r)+tau whenever one exists.
This is an exact pathwise scalar factorization plus the two-state occupation law.
If B0 has purely imaginary nonzero eigenvalues +-i omega, omega>0, then after a
single fixed real similarity and time scale omega the pair is
B0/omega=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],
B1/omega=eta H+s J=[[eta,-s],[s,-eta]], eta>=0, s real, H=diag(1,-1).
The transformed switching rate is rho=r/omega. Thus (after removing traces) every
pair with a nonzero elliptic matrix reduces to two real parameters eta,s.

Proof of trace shift. Let c_i=tr Ai/2 and C(t)=integral_0^t c_{I_s}ds.
The fundamental matrix equals exp(C(t)) times the one for Bi: differentiate on
sojourns and use the commuting scalar factor and continuity at jumps.
The two-state symmetric occupation law gives C(t)/t->(c0+c1)/2=tau almost surely.
Fixed similarity preserves exponential norm growth since its condition number is
constant. Rescaling time t'=omega t divides both matrices and rate by omega and
scales the original exponent by omega.

Proof of elliptic canonical form. Cayley-Hamilton for a traceless real B0 gives
B0^2=-omega^2 I. Choose any real nonzero vector v; vectors v, B0v/omega are linearly
independent, since dependence would give a real eigenvalue. In that basis B0=omega J.
Every real traceless B1 in this basis decomposes uniquely into s0 J+R, where
s0=(B1_21-B1_12)/2 and R is symmetric traceless, R=[[a,b],[b,-a]].
Any real symmetric traceless R has eigenvalues +-eta0 with eta0=sqrt(a^2+b^2)>=0.
There is a determinant-one orthogonal matrix O (a plane rotation) with
O^T R O=eta0 H: select an orthonormal eigenbasis, flip its second eigenvector if
necessary to make determinant one. Every plane rotation commutes with J, so the
same O leaves B0 unchanged. Divide by omega to obtain eta=eta0/omega,s=s0/omega.
This transformation is fixed, independent of r, so preserves the full rate curve.

Exact diagnostic identities. Half the trace of (B1/omega)^2 equals eta^2-s^2;
half the trace of ((B0+B1)/(2omega))^2 equals [eta^2-(1+s)^2]/4.
Let k1=sqrt(max(eta^2-s^2,0)), kavg=(1/2)sqrt(max(eta^2-(1+s)^2,0)).
The symmetric occupation average of the individual spectral abscissae is k1/2.
Comparing these algebraic endpoints, kavg>k1/2 is possible only for s<-1/2
and eta>|1+s|; those two conditions are also sufficient. This statement compares
spectral abscissae only; it does not assert a stochastic slow/fast limit theorem.
For any traceless real Bi its eigenvalue spectral abscissa is sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)).
A scalar shift Ai=Bi-ai I is Hurwitz exactly when ai exceeds that abscissa.
Consequently a fixed scalar damping average abar can make BOTH Ai Hurwitz if and
only if abar>(k0+k1)/2: necessity by summing ai>ki; sufficiency choose

body: The number of primes up to x satisfies pi(x) ~ x / log x, equivalently pi(x) ~ Li(x), as x grows. Proved independently by Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin (1896) by showing zeta(s) has no zeros on the line Re(s) = 1; elementary proofs (Erdos, Selberg 1949) avoid complex analysis. The error term in the theorem is governed by the zero-free region - under the Riemann hypothesis the error is O(sqrt(x) log x).
title: Prime Number Theorem

[Lemma lem:prime-deleted-character-sum of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $X\geq2$ and $1\leq Y\leq X$.  Let $m,w,D\geq1$, and let $q,t\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $(t,D)=1$ and $wt\equiv q\pmod D$.
Let $P$ be a prime with $P\nmid D$, and put $\chi_m(\cdot)=(\frac{\cdot}{m})$.
Define
\[
\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)
=
\{\ell\mid m:\ \ell\text{ odd},\ v_\ell(m)\text{ odd},\
\ell\nmid q,\ (D,w,\ell)=1\}
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak m
=
\frac{m}{\displaystyle
\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)}(\sqrt\ell/2)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{M\in[X,X+Y]\\M\equiv t\ (\bmod D)\\P\nmid M}}
\mu^2(M)\chi_m(M)
\chi_m\left(\frac{wM-q}{D}\right)
&\ll
\sqrt X+\frac{\mathfrak mY}{mD}
+\frac{\log(2X)\sqrt{\mathfrak mY}}{\sqrt D},
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
with an absolute implied constant.

In the Gaussian linear-regression setting y=<x,theta*>+z, with independent x~N(0,diag(v_1,...,v_d)) and z~N(0,sigma^2), let n,d be positive integers, v_i>0, sigma^2>0, and theta*_i nonzero. Put a_i=v_i(theta*_i)^2 and b=sigma^2/n. For coordinate learning rates 0<=eta_i<=1/v_i define the deterministic surrogate risk of equation (2), Rbar_eta(t)=sigma^2+sum_i [a_i(1-eta_i v_i)^(2t) +b(1-(1-eta_i v_i)^t)^2], for integer t>=1. For any prescribed integer t_*>=1, choose eta_i=[1-(b/(a_i+b))^(1/t_*)]/v_i. Then each coordinate summand attains its minimum at t=t_*, and Rbar_eta(t_*)=sigma^2+sum_i a_i b/(a_i+b), the global minimum over all admissible coordinate rates and integer stopping times. These are oracle rates using the true signal coefficients and feature variances. This statement optimizes the source surrogate; approximating the random finite-sample prediction risk requires the separate hypotheses and conclusion of Theorem 1.

[Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564, 'Power-law and log-periodic degree tails for a family of probability generating function eq'] There exist $\theta>0$ and $M<\infty$, depending only on $p$, such that
\[
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M,
  \qquad
  \sup_{n\ge0}\mathbb{E}\exp\!\Bigl\{\theta\,\frac{D^*_n}{\lambda^{n}}\Bigr\}\le M^{j}.
\]
Consequently there are constants $C,c>0$ with
\[
  \mathbb{P}(D_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad
  \mathbb{P}(D^*_n\ge x\lambda^{n})\le C e^{-cx},\qquad n\ge0,\ x\ge0 .
\]
title: Lemma lem:expmom of arXiv:2607.12564

At a fixed parameter theta, let a single-example gradient g have finite second moment, mean G=grad L(theta) and covariance Sigma=E[(g-G)(g-G)^T]. Let H=grad^2 L(theta), and assume G^T H G>0. McCandlish et al. define B_noise=tr(H Sigma)/(G^T H G). When G!=0, they also define B_simple=tr(Sigma)/||G||_2^2. These are different statistics in general. They coincide when H is a positive scalar multiple of the identity. For the mean of B independent identically distributed gradients, the gradient covariance is Sigma/B. Interpreting B_noise as a local quadratic turning-point scale requires the one-step quadratic model; identifying it with a global empirically optimal critical batch size is an additional modeling step. In particular a common scalar step size does not make curvature isotropic.

[Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Consider  $\alpha>0$ and the following Hilbert space of space-time functions:
\begin{align}
\mathcal{H}_\alpha=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+, \mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)),  
\end{align}
    where $\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)$ is the Sobolev space introduced in Definition (sobo_def of the paper). On a complete probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{G},\mathbf{P})$ we define a centered Gaussian family $\{W(\phi); \phi\in \mathcal{H}_\alpha\}$, whose covariance is given by 
\begin{align}
\mathbf E\left[ W(\varphi) W(\psi)\right]
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+}\ \left\langle \varphi (t,\cdot) , \psi (t,\cdot)\right\rangle_{\mathcal{W}^{-\alpha}(M)}  dt \notag\\
=&
\int_{\mathbb{R}_+} \int_{M^2} \varphi (t,x)  \psi (t,y)G_{2\alpha}(x,y)dxdy dt
\, ,
\end{align}
for $\varphi$, $\psi$ in $\mathcal{H}_\alpha$. This family is called the fractional Gaussian fields on $M$.
title: Definition def-frac-Gaus-field of arXiv:2411.09614

body: [Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{stationary} if for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ the law of the weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ is the same as the law of the translated weighted graph $(\mathcal X_\omega+z,\mathcal E_\omega+z,\sigma_\omega(\cdot - z),\theta_\omega(\cdot - z))_{\omega\in\Omega}$. We call $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ \emph{ergodic} if all events $A\in \mathcal{A}$ that are invariant under translations in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ have probability $\mathbb{P}(A)\in\{0,1\}$.
title: Defi stationary of arXiv:2411.04157

The approximate-error identity in Zeng--Lee arxiv2310.17513v3 detailed Lemma9 (PDF25-26), f_adapt(x)-f_target(x)=ReLU((LR_(RL)(E)-E)x), is false under its stated assumptions. A counterexample has width D=2, depth L=1, rank budget R=1, base W1=I, target W=diag(2,3), target bias0, and bounded input set X={(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}. Here E=diag(1,2), LR1(E)=diag(0,2), all required nonsingularity assumptions hold, yet no rank-at-most-one update and any choice of output bias can satisfy the displayed identity on all X. This refutes that identity, not Lemma2's exact-realization conclusion at its larger sufficient rank, Theorem3's exact expressivity theorem, or by itself every version of the separate quantitative bound.

The only partial-product rank index in the source assumptions is j=0 because R(L-1)=0, giving I, so no hypothesis fails. Exact rational checks of the three forced affine equations and determinant are in ZENG_LEE_GAP_EXACT.json, rerunnable with zeng_lee_source_gap.py. Exact proof SHA256 f367eed1f9fb01baee0dabd6f699b418c16bcc3a5ecdfc7182dae660291f3339. No novelty or Lean certification is claimed. The following original submission text retains historical pre-audit status notices.

# Target 1: accelerated finite-feature GP prediction

Claim T336-w727-C002 v1. Rung: proof (unaudited), subject to recorded checks. The full theorem is not Lean-checked and no independent audit or novelty certification is claimed.

The hardest step is realizing both Chebyshev recurrences in normalized ReLU attention, including the previous-iterate registers and variance readout. Section 4 specifies every head.

## 1. Statement

Fix integers p>=1 and n>=0, reals s>0, B>=0, R>0, eps>0, and a feature map z:X->R^p with ||z(x)||<=R. The zero-mean GP prior has kernel k(x,x')=z(x)^T z(x'). Observations have independent N(0,s) noise. A prior scale tau^2 is absorbed into z. The prediction concerns a new **noisy observation**, not the latent function value.

Input tokens supply any t<=n context pairs (z_i,y_i), |y_i|<=B, and one query q=z(x_*). Zero padding fixes N=n+1 tokens. The supplied feature encoding is specified in Section 4. Its computation from arbitrary raw inputs is not included in the size bound.

Use the bidirectional residual normalized ReLU-attention architecture of Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1, PDF page 5, Eq. (1):

    h_i^+ = h_i + (1/N) sum_heads sum_j ReLU(<Q h_i,K h_j>) V h_j.

Q,K,V are real D-by-D matrices. There is no softmax, layer normalization, or causal mask. Feed-forward blocks are identities. Define

    n_+=max(1,n), L=s+n_+R^2, kappa=L/s, M=nR^2B/s,
    delta=min(1/2, s/(2R^2), sqrt(s eps)/(1+M), s sqrt(eps)/R^2),
    T=ceil((sqrt(kappa)/2) log(2/delta)).

An attention-only transformer of width D=7p+4, depth T+2, and at most five heads per layer outputs (mhat,vhat) with vhat>=s and

    KL(N(m,v) || N(mhat,vhat)) <= eps

uniformly over all these contexts and queries. Here (m,v) are the exact posterior noisy predictive mean and variance. A dense parameter bound is 15(T+2)D^2+2D, including a linear readout. All weights depend only on the fixed bounds, never the observed inputs or labels. They are explicit in Section 4.

If R=0, (mhat,vhat)=(0,s) is exact and the formulas dividing by R are unnecessary. No training, ERM generalization, arbitrary raw-feature complexity, softmax approximation, or infinite-rank truncation theorem is asserted.

## 2. Posterior and spectral interval

Set A=s I+sum_i z_i z_i^T and b=sum_i z_i y_i. Completing the square in the standard-normal weight prior and Gaussian likelihood gives posterior weight mean A^{-1}b and covariance s A^{-1}, hence

    m=q^T A^{-1}b, v=s+s q^T A^{-1}q.

For every r, s||r||^2<=r^T A r<=(s+nR^2)||r||^2<=L||r||^2. Thus A is symmetric positive definite, spec(A) is contained in [s,L], v>=s, and

    ||A^{-1}b||<=nRB/s, ||A^{-1}q||<=R/s.

These are deterministic bounds and use no independence among context features.

## 3. Accelerated iteration and its error

Put c=(L+s)/2, d=(L-s)/2, a=c/d. Since n_+>=1 and R>0, d>0,a>1. Define Chebyshev polynomials C_0(x)=1,C_1(x)=x,C_{j+1}(x)=2xC_j(x)-C_{j-1}(x).

For a right-hand side f start x_0=x_{-1}=0. Let eta_0=1/c,beta_0=0 and, for j>=1,

    eta_j=2C_j(a)/(d C_{j+1}(a)), beta_j=C_{j-1}(a)/C_{j+1}(a).

Take T updates

    x_{j+1}=x_j+beta_j(x_j-x_{j-1})+eta_j(f-Ax_j).

Every denominator is positive: for zeta=a+sqrt(a^2-1)>1 the polynomial recurrence gives C_j(a)=(zeta^j+zeta^{-j})/2>0.

For x*=A^{-1}f, induction gives

    x*-x_j=r_j(A)x*,
    r_j(lambda)=C_j((c-lambda)/d)/C_j(a).

At j=0 this is the identity; at j=1 it is 1-lambda/c. For the induction, C_{j+1}(a)+C_{j-1}(a)=2a C_j(a) gives 1+beta_j=eta_j c. Substitution in the error recurrence then gives exactly the recurrence for C_{j+1}. All coefficients are fixed independently of A and f.

For lambda in [s,L], (c-lambda)/d is in [-1,1]. By the cosine addition formula and induction, C_j(cos theta)=cos(j theta); thus |C_j(x)|<=1 there. Also

    zeta=(sqrt(kappa)+1)/(sqrt(kappa)-1), rho=zeta^{-1} in (0,1).

Orthogonal spectral decomposition gives ||r_T(A)||_op<=1/C_T(a)<=2rho^T. With u=1/sqrt(kappa) in (0,1),

    log((1+u)/(1-u))=integral_0^u 2/(1-x^2) dx>=2u.

The denominator is positive throughout the integration interval. Hence 2rho^T<=2exp(-2T/sqrt(kappa))<=delta by the stated T.

Apply the iteration simultaneously to f=b and f=q, with final iterates w_T,u_T. It follows that

    ||w_T-A^{-1}b||<=delta nRB/s,
    ||u_T-A^{-1}q||<=delta R/s.

Furthermore u_T=g_T(A)q, where g_T(lambda)=(1-r_T(lambda))/lambda. Since |r_T(lambda)|<=delta<=1/2 and lambda>=s>0, g_T(lambda)>0, so q^T u_T>=0.

## 4. Explicit attention heads

Each token contains seven p-dimensional registers

    (z_c,z_q,qbar,w,u,w_old,u_old)

and four scalars (y,one,mout,vout), for D=7p+4. Every token has one=1. Context i has z_c=z_i,z_q=0,y=y_i. The query has z_c=0,z_q=q,y=0. Padding has z_c=z_q=0,y=0. All working registers and mout start at zero; vout=s. This is a fixed role-dependent feature encoding with no query label.

Specifying linear Q and K coordinate lists of equal length and a linear V output defines ordinary D-by-D matrices, with all unspecified coordinates zero. Constant scores use the register one.

**Broadcast layer, one head:** Q=one,K=one, and V writes N z_q into qbar. Exactly one token supplies z_q, so after the normalized sum qbar=q on every token.

The four iterate registers are identical on all tokens at initialization. The following layers preserve that invariant.

**Solver layer j, five heads:** All expressions below use pre-layer registers; eta=eta_j,beta=beta_j.

1. Q=(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes N eta z_c into w. Its score is y_j-z_{c,j}^T w_i.
2. Q=-(w,one), K=(-z_c,y). V writes -N eta z_c into w.

Together these write eta sum_i z_i(y_i-z_i^T w), by ReLU(r)-ReLU(-r)=r.

3. Q=u,K=z_c. V writes -N eta z_c into u.
4. Q=-u,K=z_c. V writes N eta z_c into u.

Together these write -eta sum_i z_i z_i^T u.

5. Q=one,K=one. V writes the following, with **no N factor**:

       beta(w-w_old)-eta s w        into w,
       beta(u-u_old)+eta(qbar-s u)  into u,
       w-w_old                     into w_old,
       u-u_old                     into u_old.

The normalized sum in head 5 is the average of identical registers and equals the displayed expression. The residual connection makes the old registers equal to the pre-layer w,u. Summing all five heads produces exactly the recurrences of Section 3 for f=b,q. Context, feature, label, constant, and output registers are unchanged. Query and padding contribute zero to the data sums because z_c=y=0. This proves the invariant and exact implementation by induction.

**Readout layer, four heads:** Q=qbar,K=w,V writing one into mout, and Q=-qbar,K=w,V writing -one into mout, together produce q^T w_T. The factors 1/N cancel the sum over N identical w registers. Likewise Q=qbar,K=u,V writing s one into vout, paired with Q=-qbar,K=u,V writing -s one into vout, produces s q^T u_T. The preexisting vout=s supplies the noise floor. Thus the query token outputs are exactly

    mhat=q^T w_T, vhat=s+s q^T u_T>=s.

This is T+2 layers and at most five heads. Counting three D-by-D matrices per head gives the parameter bound. There is no nonlinear readout computing products or inverses outside the transformer.

## 5. Uniform forward KL

The errors obey

    |m-mhat|<=M delta<=sqrt(s eps),
    |v-vhat|<=R^2 delta<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)).

For the mean inequality use M/(1+M)<=1, also when M=0. Both variances are >=s. Put h=(v-vhat)/vhat, so |h|<=1/2 and 1+h>0. The exact Gaussian formula is

    KL=(h-log(1+h))/2+(m-mhat)^2/(2vhat).

For h in [-1/2,1/2], h-log(1+h)=integral_0^h x/(1+x) dx<=h^2. If h>=0, use x/(1+x)<=x. If h<=0, reverse the integral and use |x/(1+x)|<=2|x| on [h,0]. All denominators remain >=1/2. Consequently

    KL<=|v-vhat|^2/(2s^2)+|m-mhat|^2/(2s)<=eps.

All estimates hold for every admissible context and query. There is no conversion from a prior-averaged loss to uniform KL.

## 6. Prior work and boundaries

Bai et al., arXiv:2306.04637v2, Definition 1 (PDF page 5), supplies the architecture. Theorem 4 (PDF page 7) and Appendix D.1 supply known GD ridge point prediction with three heads and depth proportional to the condition number. Those facts are settled and are not claimed anew. The construction here combines classical Chebyshev iteration with exact attention operations to obtain simultaneous mean/variance and an explicit uniform KL budget. Novelty remains subject to literature and independent review.

The feature-input qualification is essential. A bounded finite-rank kernel on a compact set alone imposes no continuous or efficiently computable feature map on the raw inputs. A raw-input theorem needs additional regularity and an explicit feature-computation cost. The dossier's feature-map formulation motivates the feature-input reading used here; the reviewer must decide whether it closes Target 1 as intended.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:d607636f8bb63d92aae86ebe87bc095c863378e40c7757b232a3caebfaf4f168","revision_digest":"sha256:c83f32d096597a983c216b5023e30dce732c0e384663e77937b4e82999fca6e8","source_id":"owner:T336-w727-C002-v1","source_revision":"C002-v1-2026-10-20T20:00:48.215724+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

STATUS: independently checked proof; reviewer claude-738954b6 PASS on the exact claim version, recorded in w691/T244/AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. For n>=2, exact one-step extinction-or-zero-angle probability is p_n(theta)=2^(1-n)+(n-1)*((pi-theta)/(2*pi))^n. The killed true angle chain and its per-step nondegeneracy-conditioned kernel can be coupled through L layers with path total variation at most min(1,L*(n+1)*2^-n), uniformly in the initial angle in (0,pi). Scope limitation: A technical localization step only. Does not establish stopped generator convergence or entrance control; no new full angle law claimed.
Zero biases; independent Gaussian weight rows; width n>=2; nonzero initial inputs with angle in (0,pi).

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6dc21933118a9f085b795fb1aaf07524e88fe68721ab07b9b0e6059ed44e0498","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6dc21933118a9f085b795fb1aaf07524e88fe68721ab07b9b0e6059ed44e0498.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b2fa73d41571c00ac5d443608fd5c336e6ecfcc2e13b6fdb1cf832b84a68b5bc","bundle_entry_key":"relu-degeneracy","bundle_id":"population.t244-relu-angle-localization-001","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:gaussian-relu-atomic-degeneracy-path-coupling","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Exact atomic degeneracy and coupling over linearly many layers

Status: independently checked proof; reviewer PASS on the listed claim version. Target 1, technical support: removes the atomic degeneracy obstacle to a stopped/conditioned-kernel diffusion argument. This is one technical step, not a proof of the proposed SDE.

Assume a zero-bias width-n network with independent Gaussian weight matrices and ReLU, n>=2. Initial inputs are nonzero with angle theta_0 in (0,pi). Given nonzero nonproportional inputs with angle theta, define q=(pi-theta)/(2*pi). Let D be the event that one output vector is zero, or both output vectors are nonzero and have zero angle.

**One-step identity.**

    p_n(theta) = P(D|theta) = 2^(1-n) + (n-1) q^n <= (n+1) 2^-n.

Proof. P(X=0)=P(Y=0)=2^-n, and their intersection has probability q^n. Thus extinction contributes 2^(1-n)-q^n. Conditional on any fixed pattern of strict signs, the positive coordinates have an absolutely continuous density. Two nonzero nonnegative vectors can be proportional only if their positive supports agree. If that common support has size >=2, proportionality is a nontrivial polynomial equality (for two coordinates, X_i Y_j-X_j Y_i=0) and has probability zero. If the support is a singleton, proportionality is automatic. There are n such sign patterns, each with probability q^n. Add these disjoint probabilities. The bound uses q<=1/2. After the first surviving layer the angle is in (0,pi/2].

**Conditioned-kernel coupling.** Let P_n(theta,.) be the exact kernel, sending D to an absorbing cemetery state. Let Q_n(theta,.) be P_n conditioned on D not occurring, well-defined for n>=2 and theta in (0,pi). For any integer L, the path laws of P_n and Q_n started at the same angle satisfy, in the convention d_TV=sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|,

    d_TV(path_0:L(P_n), path_0:L(Q_n)) <= min(1, L (n+1) 2^-n).

Construct a step coupling while the chains agree: sample the P_n step. If it survives, use the same value for Q_n. If it dies, draw Q_n independently from its conditioned kernel and count a disagreement. The Q_n marginal is correct since its law is (1-p)Q_n+pQ_n. Each agreeing step disagrees with conditional probability at most (n+1)2^-n. The union bound proves the assertion. This is a per-step conditioned chain; it is not asserted to equal the original path law conditional on survival through L.

For L<=Tn the bound is T n(n+1)2^-n. Thus proving a weak path limit for Q_n is sufficient to prove the same weak path limit for the killed P_n chain (with any common embedding of its cemetery state).

**Limit of this repair.** Removing the atom does not ensure inverse-angle integrability. On the positive-probability event that both vectors have exactly the same two-coordinate support, the continuous angle density is positive near zero, and E[1/theta' | D^c] is still infinite. A proof must use bounded test functions or a further truncation. In particular, this coupling theorem is not permission to reuse the dossier's untruncated inverse-angle generator estimates.

Independent finite check: scripts/localization_check.py enumerates all sign patterns at theta=pi/2 for n=1,...,7, using integer counts. logs/localization_exact.txt records agreement with the formula. The proof above covers every theta, without numerics.

[Theorem 1 (Duflo (1997), Theorem 1.3.15) of arXiv:2606.21111, 'On Elephant Random Walk with Delayed Amnesia'] Let $\{M_n, \mathcal{F}_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a square-integrable martingale with predictable quadratic variation $\{\langle M\rangle_n\}_{n\ge 0}$. Also, let $\langle M\rangle_\infty=\lim_{n\to\infty}\langle M\rangle_n$. Then,\vspace{.1cm}\\
\noindent{(i)}  $\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n=M_\infty$ a.s. on $\{\langle M\rangle_\infty < \infty\}$, where $M_\infty$ is a finite random variable, and\vspace{.1cm}\\		
\noindent{(ii)}  $\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n/\langle M\rangle_n=0$ a.s. on $\{\langle M\rangle_\infty = \infty\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Convention $\hat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\xi}dx$. (a) (Always, as an $L^1$ identity) If $f\in L^1(\mathbb R)$, the periodization $Pf(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)$ converges absolutely for a.e. $x$, $Pf\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ with $\|Pf\|_{L^1(\mathbb T)}\le\|f\|_1$, and $\widehat{Pf}(k)=\hat f(k)$ for all $k\in\mathbb Z$. (b) (Pointwise identity) If in addition $\sum_nf(x+n)$ converges for every $x$ to a continuous function and $\sum_k|\hat f(k)|<\infty$, then $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i kx}$ for every $x$; taking $x=0$, $\sum_nf(n)=\sum_k\hat f(k)$. (c) (Convenient sufficient condition) If $f$ is continuous and there are $C,\delta>0$ with $|f(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ and $|\hat f(\xi)|\le C(1+|\xi|)^{-1-\delta}$, then (b) applies and both series converge absolutely; this holds for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. (d) Scaled and multidimensional forms: for $T>0$, $\sum_nf(nT)=T^{-1}\sum_k\hat f(k/T)$; for $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ and the lattice $\mathbb Z^d$, $\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^d}f(x+n)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\hat f(k)e^{2\pi i k\cdot x}$; more generally for a full-rank lattice $\Lambda$ with dual $\Lambda^*$ and covolume $|\Lambda|$, $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(\lambda)=|\Lambda|^{-1}\sum_{\mu\in\Lambda^*}\hat f(\mu)$. Classic application (Jacobi theta transformation): $\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2t}=t^{-1/2}\sum_ne^{-\pi n^2/t}$ for $t>0$.
(a): f integrable on R
(b): the periodization converges everywhere to a continuous function AND the Fourier transform is absolutely summable over the integers
(c): f continuous with (1+|x|)^{-1-delta} decay of both f and its transform
integrability alone does NOT give the pointwise identity

Let T be a triangulation of an n-dimensional simplex Delta^n with vertices v_0, ..., v_n. Suppose the vertices of T are colored with {0, 1, ..., n} such that each vertex of T lying on a face of Delta^n is colored with the index of one of the vertices spanning that face. Then T contains an odd number of fully colored n-simplices (simplices whose vertices receive all n+1 colors).
T is a simplicial triangulation of Delta^n
Coloring satisfies Sperner boundary condition

[Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ be two finite sets, $\rho$ and $\gamma$ be probability measures on $\Omega$ and $\Sigma$ respectively, and $f: \Omega \to 2^{\Sigma}$ be a function\footnote{Here, $2^{\Sigma}$ is the power set of $\Sigma$.}. For each $\eta \in \Sigma$, let
    $f^{-1}(\eta):=\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \eta \in f(\omega)\}.$
     Suppose that $ \sum_{\omega \in \Omega, \eta \in \Sigma} \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)] > 0$ and then define a coupling probability measure on $\Omega\times\Sigma$ by
	\[\mathscr{P}[\omega,\eta]\propto \rho[\omega] \gamma[\eta] 1\! \!1[\eta \in f(\omega)],~\forall (\omega, \eta)\in\Omega\times\Sigma. \] 

	\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$, denoted by  $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]  \propto \gamma[f(\omega)]\rho[\omega]$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. 
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$, denoted by $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}$, satisfies $ \mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta] \propto  \rho[f^{-1}(\eta)] \gamma[\eta] $ for each $\eta \in \Sigma$.   

\item[(c)] For each $\omega\in\Omega$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Omega}[\omega]\neq 0$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot | \omega]$ on $\Sigma$ is $\gamma[\cdot \mid f(\omega)]$.
        \item[(d)]   For each $\eta\in\Sigma$ with $\mathscr{P}_{\Sigma}[\eta]\neq 0$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\cdot|\eta] $ on $\Omega$ is $\rho[\cdot \mid f^{-1}(\eta)]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:generalcoupling of arXiv:2506.10765

body: Every square complex n by n matrix A can be written as A = U T U*, where U is unitary (U* U = I) and T is upper triangular. body: Z^2 bond FPP with iid weights in [a, b], 0 < a <= b. Let T_+ denote the passage time between two wall points confined to the upper half-plane H. Then for every r >= 1, P(T_+ - E T_+ >= t sqrt(r)) <= exp(-a t^2 / (8 b^3)) for t in (0, 4 b^2 sqrt(r)/a). Derivation: modified log-Sobolev tensorization over the edge weights (BLM Theorem 6.15 applied conditionally), the deterministic bound #G_+ <= (b/a) r on the number of edges lying in every H-geodesic (from subpath optimality and the weight band), and Herbst-Chernoff with lambda in (0, 1/b]. The deterministic edge-count bound makes any variational choice of an auxiliary parameter redundant; the earlier form of this lemma carried such a parameter and a constant of a/(16 b^3), and an independent referee (2026-08-10) confirmed all constants and derived this two-fold improvement by removing the parameter outright. The lower tail is NOT covered by this route.

body: For a real parameter delta >= 0 the SQUARED BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta started at y >= 0, written BESQ^delta, is the unique strong solution of dY_t = 2 sqrt( |Y_t| ) dW_t + delta dt with Y_0 = y; the solution is nonnegative, and pathwise uniqueness holds despite the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient by the Yamada-Watanabe criterion, which requires only Holder continuity of exponent 1/2. The BESSEL PROCESS of dimension delta, BES^delta, is X_t = sqrt(Y_t); for X > 0 it solves dX_t = dW_t + ((delta - 1)/(2 X_t)) dt. When delta = d is a positive INTEGER, BES^d started at |x| has the law of the radial part |B_t| of a d-dimensional Brownian motion started at x - a fact that makes the family the natural interpolation of radial Brownian motion to non-integer dimension. ADDITIVITY: BESQ^delta started at y and an independent BESQ^{delta'} started at y' add to a BESQ^{delta + delta'} started at y + y'; this holds for the SQUARED process and is false for the Bessel process itself. The index nu = delta/2 - 1 is the other common parameterisation and is the one that appears in the modified Bessel functions of the transition density; delta and nu must not be confused. For delta < 2 the boundary point 0 is reached and a boundary convention (absorbing or instantaneously reflecting) must be specified; for delta >= 2 the point 0 is never reached from y > 0 and no convention is needed. [standard; e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed., Chapter XI]

body:
Fix finitely many inputs x^1,...,x^m in R^n_in and a finite T>0. For clarity restrict to a positive definite input Gram matrix V_0^{alpha beta}=<x^alpha,x^beta>/n_in. All layers have width n, zero biases, and mutually independent standard Gaussian weight entries. Equivalently, start from this deterministic V_0 and, conditional on V_l, draw n independent Gaussian m-vectors G_i with covariance V_l; update V_{l+1}^{alpha beta}=(c_n/n) sum_i phi_n(G_i^alpha)phi_n(G_i^beta). This is the covariance Markov chain of the Gaussian network, up to the harmless first-layer index shift. Let d_n/n tend to T. Choose fixed real c_+,c_-, slopes s_+=1+c_+/sqrt(n), s_-=1+c_-/sqrt(n), phi_n(x)=s_+ max(x,0)+s_- min(x,0), and c_n=(E[phi_n(g)^2])^(-1) for standard Gaussian g. Then V_{floor(nt)}, with upper-triangular entries viewed as a vector, converges in distribution on finite time intervals in the Skorohod topology to the covariance diffusion dV=b(V)dt+Sigma(V)^(1/2)dB, started at V_0. For alpha<=beta and gamma<=delta, Sigma_{alpha beta,gamma delta}(V)=V^{alpha gamma}V^{beta delta}+V^{alpha delta}V^{beta gamma}. Set rho_{alpha beta}=V^{alpha beta}/sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta}), nu(rho)=(c_+-c_-)^2/(2pi) [sqrt(1-rho^2)-rho arccos(rho)], and b_{alpha beta}(V)=sqrt(V^{alpha alpha}V^{beta beta})nu(rho_{alpha beta}). The limiting scalar outputs at time T, conditional on V_T, form a centered Gaussian vector with covariance V_T; their unconditional law is the resulting Gaussian mixture. This result concerns width-dependent shaped activations and does not assert the same covariance diffusion for ordinary fixed ReLU.
A fixed finite collection of inputs with positive definite normalized Gram matrix (explicit restriction of the source)
Independent iid N(0,1) weights, no biases, constant width n
Fixed c_+,c_-; slopes 1+c_+/sqrt(n),1+c_-/sqrt(n)
Exact Gaussian variance normalization c_n; depth/width tends to finite T

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d746d249960c14956818a55178d85e8db1a9f5857398be1c88ff6d492fee9a04","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d7/d746d249960c14956818a55178d85e8db1a9f5857398be1c88ff6d492fee9a04.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:339799091c17839dc5d1953fd814cba3d617e59c555d1e94c18b84b63beddef7","bundle_entry_key":"weighted-stiefel-capture-growth","bundle_id":"population.t419-weighted-stiefel-capture-delay-022","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Weighted Stiefel gradient flow and Gaussian random subspaces","draft":"w705/bundle_022.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.riemannian:weighted-stiefel-captured-energy-growth-and-gaussian-entry-delay","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C036 v1: a necessary reduced-flow entry time

Kind: bound. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim.
This is a diagnostic for C029's reduced-flow entry quantile, not an
original-GD hitting-time theorem or a scored frontier move. The hardest
open piece remains an upper bound on Gaussian basin-entry time that can
be transferred to original GD with useful constants.

Let H be a fixed real PSD p-by-p matrix of positive trace h and largest
eigenvalue L>0. Let M be SPD r-by-r, 1<=r<=p, and let Y(t) solve

    Y'=M^(-1)YH(I-P), P=Y^T Y, YY^T=I_r.

Write m=lambda_min(M)>0, a(t)=tr(HP(t)), q(t)=h-a(t).
For t>=0, the deterministic captured-energy bound is

    a(t)<=a(0) exp(2Lt/m),
    q(t)>=max{0,h-a(0) exp(2Lt/m)}.

Indeed X=YH(I-P) gives a'=2 tr(M^(-1)XX^T). Since P is an orthogonal
projector, XX^T<=YH^2Y^T in PSD order. Also H^2<=LH, hence

    0<=a'<=2/m tr(YH^2Y^T)<=2L a/m.

Gronwall proves the assertion. In particular, if a(0)>0 and a trajectory
reaches q<=b with 0<=b<h and a(0)<h-b, its hitting time is at least

    (m/(2L)) log((h-b)/a(0)).

If a(0)=0, the same differential inequality makes a stay zero, so the
positive-capture threshold is never reached. No division by a(0) is
used in that case. When a(0)>=h-b the lower bound is simply zero.

## Gaussian initialization, without multiplying event probabilities

Let G be r-by-p iid standard normal, M=GG^T and
Y(0)=M^(-1/2)G; full row rank holds almost surely. For any
delta_G,delta_O>0 with delta_G+delta_O<1, suppose

    p>=4r(r+1)/delta_G.

Then with probability at least 1-delta_G-delta_O, simultaneously

    m>=p/2,  a(0)<=r h/(p delta_O).

To verify the first event, the diagonal Gram entries have variance 2p,
and its r(r-1) off-diagonal entries have variance p and mean zero.
Thus E||GG^T-pI||_F^2=p r(r+1). Markov gives
P[||GG^T-pI||_op>p/2]<=4r(r+1)/p<=delta_G.
The norm event implies m>=p/2.

For the second event, G has a right-orthogonally invariant law. Its
rank-r row projector P(0) consequently has mean (r/p)I: invariance
makes the expectation scalar, and its trace is r. Therefore
E a(0)=(r/p)h, and Markov yields the asserted upper-tail bound.
These two events need not be independent; their intersection is
bounded by a union bound. On it, for every t>=0,

    q(t)>=h [1-r exp(4Lt/p)/(p delta_O)]_+.

This gives both a simultaneous-in-time probabilistic lower envelope
and the unconditional expectation bound

    E q(t)>=(1-delta_G-delta_O) h
             [1-r exp(4Lt/p)/(p delta_O)]_+.

The discarded event contributes a nonnegative residual; no conditional
expectation is replaced by an unconditional product.

## Consequence for C029's particular quantile

Take delta_G=delta_O=1/4 and p>=16r(r+1). Normalize the singular values
of the exact rank-r target to lie in [mu,1], 0<mu<=1, so H has
eigenvalues lambda_i^2 and zeros, h>=r mu^2 and L<=1. Put

    t0=(p/4) log(p/(8r))>0.

For every t<=t0 the preceding expectation bound gives
E q(t)>=h/4>=r mu^2/4. For any 0<rho<1, C029's integer T satisfying
sup_lambda E q(T)<=rho mu^2/64 must therefore obey T>t0, because
r mu^2/4>rho mu^2/64. This lower bound is uniform over the normalized
spectral box, including repeated and unequal positive eigenvalues.

This shows an intrinsic dimension-dependent delay in that *reduced*
entry quantile. It does not identify its optimal order, supply the
missing upper bound, or lower-bound original GD: translating a reduced
lower bound requires separate tracking and error-margin estimates.

Sources: C029 reduced equation and quantile definition; direct
Gaussian second moments (also used in C032), projector invariance,
PSD trace inequalities and Gronwall. Prior-art status and independent
audit are unresolved; the flat-spectrum special case is not claimed
as new.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7e53973b7646342ce69fff35bbd9fbecd9bafebd0aa1ecb1c07691eed626ae95","revision_digest":"sha256:c8a0a3f38e88cff19ec66fb9e1edada064b5d69bbff2244522162e44e193b645","source_id":"owner-own-work:T419-C036:v1","source_revision":"v1-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Since for each $g\in G$, the measure $\bar\mathbb{P}_g$ is $\sigma$-finite, so is $\mathbb{Q}$.

We will now show $G$-invariance of $\mathbb{Q}$. Since for $A\subset G^{\mathbb{Z}}_x$ and $g \in G$ we have $gA\subset G^{\mathbb{Z}}_{gx}$, it suffices to show the invariance for a set $A \subset G^{\mathbb{Z}}_x$ for some $x\in G$. Then, for $g \in G$

    \be   (\partial _{x_j } + i \partial _{\xi_j }) 
    (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A) (X , Y) = 0 ,\quad
     (\partial _{y_j } - i \partial _{\eta_j })
       (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A)    (X , Y) = 0.\ee

       \forall\,X\in\R^{2n},\  (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A)  (X , X) = 
    \sigma _h^{\rm Wick} (A) (X).$$
      
      iii) If  $A\in C_h$ then we have,
      
      $$ \forall\, (X,Y)\in\R^{4n},\ | (\sigma_h^{\rm ext}A) (X , Y)   | \leq d_hA (X-Y) 
      e^{ \frac { 1 }  { 4h } |X-Y|^2  } .$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] For the standard cohomogeneity-one adjoint action of \(SU(3)\) on \(S^7\),
there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isometric smooth invariant Einstein
metrics.  They may be normalized by
\[
 \Ric(g_n)=6g_n,
\]
and have principal orbit \(SU(3)/T^2\) and two singular orbits
\(\mathbb{CP}^2\).

More precisely, the metrics can be chosen so that, if \(b_n\) denotes the
scale of the initial singular orbit and \(\beta_n\) its anisotropy parameter,
then
\[
 b_n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \beta_n\longrightarrow c_*<0,
\]
where \(c_*\) is the Ricci-flat threshold of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  Moreover, the sequence may be indexed so that, for some phase constant
\(\theta_*\in\mathbb R/\pi\mathbb Z\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{15}}2\log\frac1{b_n}
 =n\pi+\theta_*+o(1),
\]
and consequently
\[
 \frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}\longrightarrow e^{-2\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
\]
Let \(h_2\) denote the nonnormal Einstein metric on \(SU(3)/T^2\)
whose Ricci-flat cone is
\[
 dr^2+r^2h_2,
 \qquad
 f_1=f_2=\frac r{\sqrt5},\quad
 f_3=\sqrt{\frac25}\,r,
\]
and let \(g_{\RF,*}\) be the complete Ricci-flat threshold metric of
Proposition~\ref{prop:threshold}.  If \(p_n^\pm\) are points on the two
singular orbits, then
\[
 (S^7,b_n^{-2}g_n,p_n^\pm)
 \longrightarrow (M_*,g_{\RF,*},p_*)
\]
in pointed smooth Cheeger--Gromov sense.  On the complementary scale,
\[
 g_n\longrightarrow dt^2+\sin^2t\,h_2
\]
smoothly locally on \((0,\pi)\times SU(3)/T^2\).  Finally, there are
constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
 c b_n^{-2}\le \sup_{S^7}|\Rm(g_n)|\le C b_n^{-2}.
\]
Let \(K_{02}^{(n)}\) denotes the sectional curvature of \(g_n\) in the
two-plane spanned by the radial direction and a unit vector tangent to
the third isotropy summand. At eithe singular orbit,
$$
 b_n^2K_{02}^{(n)}\longrightarrow-\frac{1+2c_*^2}{2}.
$$
Consequently,
$$
 \frac{|K_{02}^{(n+1)}|}{|K_{02}^{(n)}|}
 \longrightarrow e^{4\pi/\sqrt{15}}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main theorem

body:
[Lem 32 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} of Remark~\ref{r:fp.cases} does not hold, then in any local
   maximizer $(\vvvv,\xxxx,\vwww)$ of the function $F_\diamond$ defined by \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, the vector $\vwww$ must be entrywise positive.
\begin{proof}
    If case \eqref{i:fp-case1} does not hold, we have $\hv_1 > 0$, $\hx > 0$, or $\mu_1 < \alpha$. We assume for contradiction that $\vwww$ is not entrywise positive, and divide the analysis into a few cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 1:} $\hv_1 > 0$ or $\hx > 0$. In this case, let  $\www_{j_1}$ be a positive entry of $\vwww$, which must exist due to the constraint $(\mu,\vwww) = 1$. Now suppose for contradiction that we have $\www_{j_2} = 0$. For small positive $\delta$, the replacement
\[(\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2})
\mapsto \bigg(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta
    \bigg)\]
increases the value of the budget
    \[\frac1\alpha
    \bigg( \sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\]
by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$. It follows that we may replace $\vvv_1$ with $\vvv_1 + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, or $\xxxx$ with $\xxxx + \Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, while remaining inside the set $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$. Recalling
\eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}, we can do this in a way which increases the value of $F_\diamond$ by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$, contradicting the assumption that we were at a local maximizer.

\item \emph{Case 2:} $\hv_1 < 0$, $\hx \le 0$, and $\mu_1 < \alpha$.
We divide further into two cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item     \emph{Case 2a:} $\vvvv$ is not identically zero.
    As above, let $\www_{j_1} > 0$ and $\www_{j_2} = 0$.
    Further let $\vvv_{j_3} > 0$, and note that $\hv_{j_3} \le \hv_1 < 0$.
    Therefore the replacement
    \[
        (\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2},\vvv_{j_3}) \mapsto
        \lt(\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta,
        \vvv_{j_3} - \Theta(\delta^{1/2})\rt)
    \]
    improves \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{1/2})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$.
    This gives a contradiction.

\item     \emph{Case 2b:} $\vvvv$ is identically zero. Then the constraints defining $S_\diamond(\lambda,\mu)$ reduce to
 \beq
        
        1 + \xxxx \le \frac1\alpha \bigg(\sum_{j=1}^s \mu_j (\www_j)^{1/2}\bigg)^2\,, \quad
        (\mu,\vwww) = 1\,.\eeq
    Since $\mu_1 < \alpha$, we have $\vwww \neq (1/\mu_1, 0, \ldots, 0)$.
   Thus there must exist at least one index $j_1\ge2$ for which $\www_{j_1}$ is positive.
    If $\www_1 = 0$, then the replacement
    \[(\www_1,\www_{j_1}) \mapsto
        \bigg(\delta,\www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta\bigg)\] improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam}
while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
    Therefore we must have $\www_1 > 0$.
    Finally, if $\www_{j_2} = 0$ for any $j_2 \ge 2$, the replacement
    \[
        (\www_1,\www_{j_1},\www_{j_2}) \rightarrow
        \lt(\www_1 + \delta^{2/3}, \www_{j_1} - \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta^{2/3} - \frac{\mu_{j_2}}{\mu_{j_1}} \delta, \delta \rt)
    \]
    improves the value of \eqref{e:fp-Fdiam} by $\Theta(\delta^{2/3})$ while remaining inside $S_\diamond$.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
This concludes the proof.
\end{proof}

body: Let H be an inner product space with norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x,x>). If H is real, the inner product is recovered from the norm by <x,y> = (||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) / 4 for all x, y in H. If H is complex, <x,y> = (1/4) sum_{k=0}^3 i^k ||x + i^k y||^2, equivalently <x,y> = (1/4)[(||x+y||^2 - ||x-y||^2) + i(||x+iy||^2 - ||x-iy||^2)]. Combined with the parallelogram-law characterization, this shows a norm comes from an inner product exactly when it satisfies the parallelogram law, and in that case the identity above is the only possible inner product inducing it. [standard, e.g. Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Polarization Identity for Inner Product Spaces

[Theorem thm:exist of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] {\rm[Jan-Ras-20-aop]} There exists a probability space $(\widehat\Omega,\widehat{\mathfrak{S}},\widehat\mathbb{P})$,  equipped with an additive group of continuous bijections $\widehat{T}=\{\widehat{T}_x:x\in\mathbb{Z}^2\}$ and satisfying the hypotheses of Section (sec:probsp of the paper), on which there exists a stochastic process
\begin{align}    
    \bigl({\widehat B}^{h{\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}}}(x,y) : x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^2, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),\, {\scaleobj{0.9}{\boxempty}} \in \{+,-\}\bigr)
\end{align}
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}  [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}]   \itemsep=3pt
\item \textup{(}No $\pm$ distinction at fixed $h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$, 
\[
\widehat\mathbb{P}\bigl\{{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,y)\bigr\}=1.
\]
When ${\widehat B}^{h-}({\widehat\omega},x,y) = {\widehat B}^{h+}({\widehat\omega},x,y)$, call the common value ${\widehat B}^h({\widehat\omega}, x,y)$.
\item \textup{(}Generalized Busemann function\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U), {\widehat B}^h \in \widehat{\mathcal{K}}$.  

\item \textup{(}Mean $-h$\textup{)} For each $h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U),$ $\widehat\mathbb{E}[{\widehat B}^h(0,e_i)] = -h \cdot e_i.$
\item \textup{(}Monotonicity\textup{)} For $h,h'\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$ with $h \cdot e_1 \leq h' \cdot e_1$, all $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, and $\widehat\mathbb{P}$-almost every ${\widehat\omega}$
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1) \geq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_1)  
\]
and
\[ 
    {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h+}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2) \leq  {\widehat B}^{h'-}(x,x+e_2).
\]
\item \textup{(}Left-/right-continuity\textup{)} For $\widehat\mathbb{P}$ almost all ${\widehat\omega}$, for all $h\in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{aligned}
{\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \nearrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) \qquad \text{ and } {\widehat B}^{h-}(x,y) = \lim_{\substack{-\partial \textup{g} (\mathcal U)\hspace{0.5pt}\ni\hspace{0.5pt}  h' \to h\\ h'\cdot e_1 \searrow h \cdot e_1}} {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y).
\end{aligned}\end{equation*}
\item \textup{(}Backward independence\textup{)} For any $I \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the random variables $\{\omega_x, {\widehat B}^{h\pm}(x,y) : y \geq x,\, x \in I,\, h \in -\partial \textup{g}(\mathcal U)\}$ are independent of the  weights  $\{\omega_x : \forall z\in I , \, x  \not\geq z \}$ behind $I$.\qedhere
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Suppose that we have a family $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ of resistance metrics coupled with $\Gamma$ where $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}\colon (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \times (\ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma) \to [0,\infty)$. Then it is associated with a weak \clekp{} resistance form if and only if the following hold.
 \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item The metric $\rmetres{C}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ is continuous with respect to $\dpathY$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. The conditional law of the collection $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U]}$ given $\Gamma\setminus\Gamma_{U^*}$ and $(\rmetres{V'}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V' \in \metregions[\C\setminus\ol{U}]}$ is almost surely measurable with respect to~$U^*$.

  \item Let $U \subseteq \C$ be open, simply connected. There exists a probability kernel $\mu^{U^*}$ such that for each $z \in \C$, the conditional law of $(\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions[U+z]}$ given $(U+z)^*$ is $(T_z)_* \mu^{U^*}(\cdot -z)$ where $T_z \FR(x,y) = \FR(x-z,y-z)$ denotes translation by $z$.

  \item Let $V,V' \in \metregions$, $V \subseteq V'$, and $x,y \in \ol{V} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$ such that for every $u \in V' \setminus V$ there is a point $z \in \ol{V}$ that separates $u$ from $x,y$ in $\ol{V'} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$. Then
  \[ \rmetres{V}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V'}{x}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item Suppose that $V_1,V_2 \in \metregions$ with $\ol{V_1} \cap \ol{V_2} = \{z\}$ (where the closure is taken with respect to $d_{\ol{V}}$, see Section~\ref{subsec:main_results}). If $x \in \ol{V_1} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, $y \in \ol{V_2} \cap \Upsilon_\Gamma$, then
  \[ \rmetres{V_1 \cup V_2}{x}{y}{\Gamma} = \rmetres{V_1}{x}{z}{\Gamma} + \rmetres{V_2}{z}{y}{\Gamma} . \]

  \item There exists a countable set $\{z_m\}_{m \in \N} \subseteq \Upsilon_\Gamma$ that is dense with respect to $\dpathY$ and such that the following holds. Suppose that $V \in \metregions$ consists of a single connected component and let $\CL \in \Gamma$ be a loop contained in $\ol{V}$ and intersecting $\partial V$. Then there exist two distinct points $a,b \in \CL \cap \partial V$ such that the following holds for sufficiently large $m \in \N$. Let $V_{a,b}$ (resp.\ $V_{b,a}$) be the collection of components of $V \setminus \CL$ that are connected to the counterclockwise arc of $\partial V$ from $a$ to $b$ (resp.\ from $b$ to $a$) by an admissible path within $V$. Let $A = \{z_1,\ldots,z_m\}$, $A_{a,b} = A \cap \ol{V_{a,b}}$, $A_{b,a} = A \cap \ol{V_{b,a}}$, and let $w, w_{a,b}, w_{b,a}$ be the weight functions associated with $\rmetres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A}$, $\rmetres{V_{a,b}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{a,b}}$, $\rmetres{V_{b,a}}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}|_{A_{b,a}}$, respectively. Then
  \[
   w(x,y) =
   \begin{cases}
    w_{a,b}(a,b)+w_{b,a}(a,b) ,& \{x,y\} = \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{a,b}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{a,b} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\
    w_{b,a}(x,y) ,& x,y \in A_{b,a} ,\, \{x,y\} \neq \{a,b\} ,\\
    0 ,& \text{otherwise.}
   \end{cases}
  \]
 \end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 25 of arXiv:2512.04807

[1 6 (\cite{HX24a}) of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] If the chain $X$ is ergodic, then its mean first passage times are all finite and satisfy 
\be

\mu_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}=1+\sum_{j \in S, j \ne i_1}\mu_{i_1ji_2\ldots i_{m-1}}p_{ji_2\ldots i_m}
\ee
for any $i_1, i_2, \ldots, i_m \in S$. In tensor form, (\ref{mfpteqn}) can be written as 
$$\mu={\cal E}+(\mu-\mu_d)\boxtimes {\cal P},$$
where $\cal E$ is the tensor of all ones and of the same size as $\cal P$, and where $\mu_d$ is the diagonal tensor obtained from $\mu$. Moreover, as a linear system, (\ref{mfpteqn}) is nonsingular if and only if the chain $X$ is ergodic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let g be a norm on R^2 that is even in the first coordinate (g(-h, m) = g(h, m)), as every lattice-symmetric FPP limit-shape norm is. For fixed m, the map h -> g((h, m)) is even and convex, hence minimized at h = 0, so g((h, m)) >= g((0, m)) = |m| g(e_2). Consequently, for a dogleg from (0,0) through v = (h, j) to (0, r) with j = r + m, m > 0 (longitudinal overshoot past the far endpoint): g(v) + g((0,r) - v) - g((0,r)) >= (r + m) g(e_2) + m g(e_2) - r g(e_2) = 2 m g(e_2), and symmetrically for j = -m < 0. The dogleg excess grows at least LINEARLY in the overshoot, with the explicit constant 2 g(e_2), using convexity and symmetry alone - no curvature hypothesis of any kind. The bound is tight as h -> 0. Use: in localization arguments it kills union sites with longitudinal overshoot at a rate no curvature assumption needs to fund, letting curvature windows be quoted only where they are literally assumed. Numerical attack: 0 violations in 300,000 trials on an anisotropic convex norm, worst ratio 1.000019.

body: Let w_j >= 0 with w_0 > 0 and let the generating function Phi(z) = sum_j w_j z^j have radius of convergence zero (limsup w_j^{1/j} = infinity), with no ratio or support hypothesis, and let Y_(1) be the largest box of the random allocation of m balls into n boxes with probability proportional to prod_v w_{y_v}. For every epsilon in (0,1) and 0 < alpha < beta there are delta > 0 and supported integers k_r -> infinity with P(Y_(1) <= (1 - epsilon) m) -> 0 uniformly over admissible (m, n) with (1 + 3 delta) k_r <= m <= (1 + 5 delta) k_r and alpha <= m/n <= beta. Hence every eventually admissible path with m_n/n -> lambda > 0 has a subsequence on which Y_(1)/m -> 1 in probability: the largest box cannot hold a vanishing fraction of the balls along the whole sequence (Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability fails), and Janson's Problem 19.41 is answered No; the same holds along a sampled index set exactly when successive indices have ratio tending to 1. The conclusion is subsequential, and the stronger P(Y_(1) = m) -> 1 is false (w_k = k!: the limit is e^{-1/lambda}).

v\neq0.
\]
Choose $\ell\in V^*$ such that $\ell(v)=1$, put $W=\ker\ell$, and write
\[
\gamma_t-\gamma_0=x_t v+X_t,
\qquad
x_t=\ell(\gamma_t-\gamma_0),
\qquad
X_t\in W.
\]

Let $\Lambda\subset2\pi\Q$ be finite and symmetric, so that
$\Lambda=-\Lambda$. Give $W$ an auxiliary Euclidean norm, let $W_{\C}$
be its complexification, and define the real Hilbert space
\[
E_\Lambda
=
\set{(z_\omega)_{\omega\in\Lambda}
\in\prod_{\omega\in\Lambda}W_{\C}:
 z_{-\omega}=\overline{z_\omega}}
\]
with the norm inherited from the Hilbert direct sum. Define the decorated
transverse path
\[
B_t^\Lambda(\gamma)
=
\left(
\int_0^t \e^{i\omega x_s}\dd X_s
\right)_{\omega\in\Lambda},
\qquad 0\leq t\leq T,
\]
and the orthogonal map
\[
T_\Lambda\colon E_\Lambda\to E_\Lambda,
\qquad
(T_\Lambda z)_\omega=\e^{i\omega}z_\omega.
\]
Denote by the same symbol the induced graded automorphism of tensor
series, and set
\[
r_t^\Lambda
=S\bigl(B^\Lambda(\gamma)|_{[0,t]}\bigr),
\qquad
h_\Lambda=r_T^\Lambda.
\]

Then there exists $t_\Lambda\in[0,T]$ such that
\begin{equation}
r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda
=h_\Lambda T_\Lambda\bigl(r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda\bigr).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, with
\[
a_\Lambda=r_{t_\Lambda}^\Lambda,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
h_\Lambda
=a_\Lambda T_\Lambda(a_\Lambda)^{-1}.
\end{equation}

For probability measures P and Q with densities p and q with respect to a sigma-finite measure lambda dominating both, the squared Hellinger distance is H^2(P, Q) = (1/2) integral (sqrt p - sqrt q)^2 d lambda = 1 - integral sqrt(pq) d lambda, where integral sqrt(pq) d lambda is the Hellinger affinity (Bhattacharyya coefficient), and H = sqrt(H^2). The value does not depend on the dominating measure (take lambda = P + Q) and lies in [0, 1]. Some texts omit the factor 1/2, which doubles H^2.

Refuted auxiliary bridge, not a statement of P0309: a finite-temperature ordinary grand-canonical Gibbs law with finite activity and measurable nonnegative pair interaction is supported on configurations admitting a globally bounded displacement bijection from a full-rank lattice. Under the explicitly stated ordinary-DLR assumptions this assertion contradicts the uniform conditional void bound and arbitrarily large holes. It is stronger than lattice periodicity of a probability law, which is not refuted. A fixed-count or renormalized long-range specification is outside this obstruction. Independent referee w536 checked the counterargument.
Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Finite activity 0<z<infinity and finite 0<beta<infinity
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count
title: Refuted global lattice-displacement bridge for ordinary DLR gases

model, defined via the transition rates given in equation (\ref{eq:c_BT}).

body: P (polynomial time) is the class of languages (decision problems, sets of finite strings over a finite alphabet) decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time: L is in P if there exist a deterministic Turing machine M deciding L and constants c and k such that M halts within c n^k + c steps on every input of length n. The class is robust: it is unchanged under standard variations of the machine model (multiple tapes, larger alphabets, random-access machines), since these simulate one another with polynomial overhead. P is closed under complement, union, intersection, and polynomial-time many-one reductions. P is standardly identified with the class of efficiently solvable decision problems. Examples: linear programming, primality testing, graph reachability, 2-SAT.
title: Complexity class P

[Corollary 5 (\textsf{Brownian Busemann process}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] Fix $n\geq1$ and $\be>0$, and define the anchored horizontal
  stationary free-energy profile by
  \begin{align}
    \cB^{\be}(x)
    =
    F_x^{\rstat,\be}-F_0^{\rstat,\be},
    \qquad x\in\R.
  \end{align}
  Then $(\cB^{\be}(x))_{x\in\R}$ is a two-sided standard Brownian
  motion.  More precisely, for every $m\geq1$ and every
  $x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_m$, the increments
   $\widehat\Delta_k
    =
    \cB^{\be}(x_k)-\cB^{\be}(x_{k-1})$,
  $1\leq k\leq m$,
  are independent with
    $\widehat\Delta_k\sim \text{Normal}(0,x_k-x_{k-1}).$
  Equivalently,
   $ x\in\R\mapsto
    \log Z_x^{\rstat,\be}-\log Z_0^{\rstat,\be}$
  is a two-sided Brownian motion with variance parameter $\be^2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Solving a finite two-player zero-sum game with m x n payoff matrix A (row player maximizing, column player minimizing the same quantity) is equivalent to solving a pair of dual linear programs. The row player's LP is: maximize v subject to sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i * A_{ij} >= v for all j=1,...,n, x_i >= 0, sum_i x_i = 1. The column player's LP, minimize w subject to sum_{j=1}^{n} A_{ij} * y_j <= w for all i=1,...,m, y_j >= 0, sum_j y_j = 1, is exactly the LP dual of the row player's program. Because both programs are feasible and bounded, strong LP duality guarantees their optimal values agree (v* = w*), recovering von Neumann's minimax theorem as a consequence of linear programming duality; standard LP algorithms, such as the simplex method or interior-point methods, applied to either program simultaneously compute the game's value and both players' optimal mixed strategies.
title: Zero-Sum Games and Linear Programming Duality

Let gamma be the oscillating spiral curve and let gamma_n be random curves satisfying d_P(gamma, gamma_n) < 1/n almost surely. Then gamma_n converges almost surely and hence weakly to gamma, but for any N in N there exists R > 0 such that lim_{n -> infinity} P(N_{r, R}^0(gamma_n) >= N) = 1 for any r in (0, R). Consequently, the Aizenman-Burchard power bound fails while the sequence is precompact.

Independent review pending. The proposed implication 'finite common-edge ray energy on a host graph implies that a surviving critical component inherits finite ray energy at some thinning retention r<1' is false without an additional structural premise. For two independent rays from a Borel ray measure mu write I_r(mu)=E[r^(-K)], where K counts common undirected edges. On the dyadic-burst tree, the uniform-child host measure has I_(1/2)=5/4 and critical root survival probability is at least 4/5. Nevertheless almost surely every infinite critical component C has p_c(C)=1. Such C admits no ray measure with finite I_r for r<1: the open-prefix second-moment argument would give positive percolation probability at r, a contradiction. The host is not quasi-transitive; this refutes unconditional inheritance and leaves a quasi-transitive structural premise unproved.

Since $\|X-Y\|_\alpha \leq \|X\|_\alpha + \|Y\|_\alpha$ (Minkowski),
and $t \mapsto t^\alpha$ is convex for $\alpha \geq 1$,
\[
\|X-Y\|_\alpha^\alpha \leq (\|X\|_\alpha + \|Y\|_\alpha)^\alpha
\leq 2^{\alpha-1}(\|X\|_\alpha^\alpha + \|Y\|_\alpha^\alpha).
\]
Hence $\tau(X,Y) \geq (2-2^{\alpha-1})(\|X\|_\alpha^\alpha+\|Y\|_\alpha^\alpha) \geq 0$.

\textbf{(i) Upper bound.}
For jointly S$\alpha$S random variables, there exists a spectral representation
[StoevTaqqu2004]:
\[
\|X\|_\alpha^\alpha = \int_E |f_1|^\alpha dm,\quad
\|Y\|_\alpha^\alpha = \int_E |f_2|^\alpha dm,\quad
\|X-Y\|_\alpha^\alpha = \int_E |f_1-f_2|^\alpha dm.
\]
