{"artifact_digest":"sha256:84c9b60155af6907a3fecadf669c0ae2002cb0a5ecf3bfea857c31c9207a7993","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/84/84c9b60155af6907a3fecadf669c0ae2002cb0a5ecf3bfea857c31c9207a7993.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c9a10610d8353387b8cecd233c37cc801eef07691001cce1b9911eb9daedfde8","bundle_entry_key":"small-floor-nontracking","bundle_id":"population.adam-singular-compactification-fullrank-small-floor-nontracking-009","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-fullrank-small-floor-uniform-active-threshold-nontracking-p-greater-than-one","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-021 v5; target1; kind narrowed; proof (unaudited).

STATEMENT
Fix 0<l<=L<infinity and 0<rho_max<rho_star=358811/13673160.
There exists delta(l,L,rho_max)>0 such that for every
lambda1,lambda2 in[l,L], eta>0 and
 0<epsilon/eta<=rho_max*min(lambda1,lambda2), ordinary
time0 separately bias-corrected Adam with b=9/10,d=999/1000, epsilon
outside sqrt and standard m0=v0=0, on H=diag(lambda1,lambda2), satisfies

 limsup_t |eta*C_active,t-38| >= delta(l,L,rho_max)        (1)

for Lebesgue-almost every initial position in R^2. Distinct eigenvalues
are allowed; no independence of the initialization coordinates is assumed.
The constant is existential, not a computer-evaluated bound.

For epsilon=eta^p and ANY fixed p>1 and fixed positive eigenvalues,
epsilon/eta eventually satisfies this condition. For any specified
countable eta_n->0 and any absolutely continuous initialization law,
(1) therefore holds simultaneously almost surely for all sufficiently
large n. This refutes eventual o(1/eta) active-threshold tracking on this
whole positive-definite two-coordinate small-floor range. It does not
identify the attracting dynamics, a limiting average, or a limit for
the curvature itself.

P=1 CONSEQUENCE
When epsilon=eta, rho_i=1/lambda_i. If BOTH eigenvalues are strictly
larger than lambda_star=13673160/358811, choose
 max_i(1/lambda_i)<rho_max<rho_star.
The theorem applies and gives generic full-dimensional nontracking.
Thus it covers the entire open p=1 range in which both scalar cycles
are hyperbolic with two unstable directions. The neutral endpoint and
mixed stable/unstable cycle ranges are not asserted. The p>1 consequence
above is unchanged and holds for every fixed positive eigenvalue pair.

AUDIT / DEPENDENCIES
This is an UNAUDITED candidate. It depends on015v3's corrected scalar
countable cycle basin and uniform capture, and019v1/020v1's extraction of
strictness from Fong--Yang's primary H.5 proof. The new work is a compact
closed-relation lift through the singular epsilon/eta=0 limit, relation
chain compression, and the origin margin. Each is supplied below. The
source H.5 inequalities have not been formally verified here. A reviewer
failure of one of these steps invalidates the global claim; origin
algebra alone does not prove it. No source-priority claim is made.

1. UNIFORM COMPACT LIFT
Put c=1/19,nu=1/1000,gamma=9/19,r=epsilon/eta. In coordinate i set

 y=x/(c eta), mu=m/(c eta lambda), V=v/(c eta lambda)^2,
 e=r/(c lambda), z=y_previous, s=sqrt(V)+e.

Use the compact parameter domain lambda_i in[l,L],0<=r<=rho_max*L,
with r<=rho_max*lambda_i for both coordinates. Then
0<=rho_i=r/lambda_i<=rho_max and 0<=e_i<=19*rho_max<1/2. Parameter r=0
will be used only as a compactification, not as an actual Adam run.
For actual r>0 define q=z/s. The raw variance history gives
V>=nu*z^2, and therefore |q|<=1/sqrt(nu)<32.

The absorbing argument of023 Section1 works without a subcritical
assumption and uniformly in r: in X=x/eta coordinates increments are
bounded by80, the corrected first-moment lag bound is720, every X enters
[-801,801], and raw moments have limsup bounds801 and801^2. Let
R=19*802. Every lifted actual tail lies in the fixed compact domain

 |y|,|z|<=R, 0<=V<=R^2, |q|<=32,
 V>=nu*z^2, q*(sqrt(V)+e)=z.                              (2)

Add a discrete branch label ell in{low,high}; low requires s>=1 and
high requires s<=1. At s=1 these are TWO distinct lifted states. This
keeps the potential continuous on the lifted domain instead of asserting
the false continuity recorded in018. Define the continuous functions

 Gamma(V,e)=8*gamma/3*min(sqrt(V),1-e)^3,
 phi_low=-c/2*(y-z)^2-Gamma,
 phi_high=(y^2-b*z^2)/(1+b)-(y+q-z)^2/2-Gamma.             (3)

Continuity is on the compact labeled domain (2); both formulas are
polynomials in y,z,q plus a continuous Gamma. The label copies need
not agree at s=1. Positions and q bounds make phi uniformly bounded.

2. A CLOSED COMPACT EDGE RELATION
For each coordinate an edge from a lifted state to a primed state has
an auxiliary number u satisfying

 V'=dV+nu*y^2, z'=y,
 u*s'=s, u>=0, d*u^2<=1,
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.                               (4)

Both endpoints satisfy(2), so q'*s'=y. On a high-labeled source also
require s'<=31/5. For regular s,s'>0, these are exactly source equations
105/118 and F1/F2/F3, with p=1/s,w=1/s',u=w/p. The F3 bound is stronger
than w>c since31/5<19. It follows for every bounded full physical orbit
by unrolling its history, as019 Section1 shows:

 s' <=(1+b)*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e <3*(1+b)+1/2=31/5

when p>=1. The disappearing initial-momentum term is taken to zero
along a bounded full history, not estimated using 1/e uniformly in time.

Let
 W_i=(q_i')^2-2*y_i*q_i',
 Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i,
 D=sum_i lambda_i*y_i*q_i'.
Require Psi_i>=0 for each i, and the active-band condition

 |sum_i lambda_i*W_i| <= c*delta*D.                       (5)

D>=0 follows from q_i'*s_i'=y_i and s_i'>=0. These constraints define
a closed relation R_(lambda,r,delta) on the product compact lift.
The existential u variables range in a compact interval, so projection
preserves closedness. The family is jointly closed in lambda in[l,L]^2,
r in[0,rho_max*L] with r<=rho_max*lambda_i, and bounded delta>=0. The source potential inequality
is included as Psi_i>=0; its applicability to actual limiting edges
is proved next, and its equality cases on all allowed regular edges
are checked in Section4.

The work expression has no singular denominator. In ordinary states
q_i'=w_i,next*y_i, so W_i=y_i^2*w_i,next*(w_i,next-2), and

 eta*C_active=(1/c)*sum_i lambda_i*(q_i')^2 / D.

Thus(5) is exactly the multiplied width-delta threshold inequality,
extended as0<=0 if the full gradient vanishes.

3. FIXED-POSITIVE-r CORRECTED OMEGA SETS ARE CONTAINED AND CHAIN TRANSITIVE
Here r>0 is fixed FIRST. On the physical absorbing box, the corrected
maps converge uniformly to uncorrected maps because denominators have
the fixed positive floor r/lambda_i. No uniform clock bound as r->0
is needed. We take an omega limit for each fixed r, and only THEN
allow a sequence of r values to approach zero.

Lift the actual tail using its current and previous positions, raw V,
q=z/(sqrt(V)+e), and the actual branch label (low at equality).
Every limit of adjacent lifted pairs satisfies(4): the source two-step
recursion is the uniform fixed-r limit after the clocks vanish. Extract
a bounded full physical orbit through such a pair from shifted original
histories. Its F3 bound is uniform as in Section2. The actual labels may
limit to either copy at s=1, but the closed-branch source inequalities
still give Psi_i>=0: the finite-curvature boundary checks in020 Section2
apply to each of the four branch closures. All other identities are
continuous. If the corrected active curvature eventually lies in the
width-delta band, (5) holds on every adjacent-pair limit as well.

Let K be the nonempty compact omega-limit of this lifted sequence.
Every adjacent-pair limit lies in R intersect(K x K). Every point of K
has both an incoming and outgoing edge there (extract preceding/following
states); by compact diagonal extraction it lies on a full path in K.
The distance of adjacent late pairs to this compact restricted relation
tends to zero, since any counterexample subsequence has a limit there.

K is internally chain transitive for this RESTRICTED CLOSED RELATION.
An epsilon-chain consists of true edges(a_j,b_j) in the relation, first
source a_0=x, jumps d(b_j,a_(j+1))<epsilon and final jump d(b_last,y)<epsilon.
For x,y in K choose late visits near x with their following states
converging to some v in R(x) intersect K. Use (x,v) as first edge. Follow
the actual late segment until a later visit near y, replacing each
adjacent pair by a nearby true restricted edge. All gaps are small and
all edges have endpoints in K. The last target jumps to y. This proves
internal chain transitivity without assuming a discontinuous label lift
preserves a single-valued continuous map.

4. ZERO-MARGIN FULL PATHS, INCLUDING THE SINGULAR ORIGIN
At regular scalar states s>0, the next s' is also positive: if e=0,V>0,
then V'>=dV>0. Source H.5's six-case algebra and the strict boundary
checks of019/020 apply. They use only(2),(4),F3 and e>=0; for finite
p,w the inequalities extend to e=0. In particular the smallest cubic
contribution was already bounded by its e=0 value in source Eq126.
The speed endpoint u=d^(-1/2) is treated by the y=0 case; if y!=0 it
is strict. Zero margin can therefore occur only at a scalar cycle,
at a regular origin (e>0), or on the pure-variance axis y=z=q=0
with p,w<=1. All the rational strictness gaps are those checked in
logs/stationary_margin_exact.json. At p or w equal1, use the labeled
closed-branch expressions checked in020, not continuity between copies.

The new singular case is s=0. It forces e=V=z=0, but y may initially
be nonzero (a spike following an origin). First take y=0. Then V'=0,
s'=0 and the high label is forced at both endpoints. Put h=q'. Equation
(4) gives y'=-(1+b)*h. Equations(3) yield exactly

 phi=-q^2/2,
 phi'=(1+b-b^2/2)*h^2,
 W=h^2,
 Psi=(b-b^2/2)*h^2+q^2/2=99*h^2/200+q^2/2.              (6)

Thus a zero-margin origin edge has q=h=0 and y'=0. This calculation
uses no floating-point estimate; check_origin_margin.py verifies it.

A scalar state with V=0,y!=0 cannot occur on a full zero-margin path.
Its predecessor has V_previous=0 and y_previous=0 by the nonnegative
variance recursion. That predecessor is an origin edge of(6), and zero
margin would prohibit the nonzero next position. Likewise a positive
pure-variance axis state leaves the zero-margin set in finite time:
V decreases geometrically until w crosses1, when the Gamma decrease or
the above-one case is strict. At e=0 it also crosses1 in finite time.

Consequently the only FULL scalar paths with Psi=0 at every edge are
the origin and exact two-cycle. In the lift the cycle phases are

 y=+/-a, z=-y, V=a^2, q=-2*y, ell=high,
 a=1/2-e,

and the origin has y=z=V=q=0,ell=high. The two-coordinate full
zero-margin paths are their nine product states. These statements apply
to every edge allowed by the broad relation, not only actual Adam paths.

5. EXACT-BAND FULL PATHS HAVE FINITELY MANY ACYCLIC CRITICAL ENDS
Now set delta=0. On every allowed product edge, (5) gives sum lambda_i W_i=0,
and therefore for the CONTINUOUS lifted function H=sum_i lambda_i*phi_i,

 H'-H=sum_i lambda_i*Psi_i>=0.                            (7)

Take any full path in a compact restricted relation with incoming and
outgoing edges at every point. Boundedness of H gives limits at both
time ends and Psi_i->0 there. Shift along any convergent subsequence
at either end and extract a full limiting path. Continuity of H and
closedness of the relation force Psi_i=0 on all its edges. Section4
therefore puts both end-limit sets among the nine critical product states.

At a critical product state its exact-band outgoing edge is unique.
A regular cycling coordinate has its usual next cycle phase and work0.
Each origin coordinate could algebraically have a singular h=q' at r=0,
but its work is h^2. The total exact work constraint forces every such
h to vanish. Thus critical product edges are precisely the fixed-origin
and the four period-two groups. Compactness/closedness then prevents a
tail approaching this finite set from jumping between different groups.
The full path approaches one critical orbit at each end.

H has one value at both phases of each critical orbit. At the scalar
cycle it is c*a^2-(8*gamma/3)*a^3, and at the origin it is0. There are
only finitely many product values. If a full path is not itself a
critical orbit, some Psi_i is positive at some edge by Section4, so(7)
implies STRICT increase between its two critical end values. Hence the
possible connecting paths are acyclic in a finite ordering.

6. CONTINUOUS SUPERLEVEL SETS GIVE A RELATIVE ATTRACTOR
Let K be compact, every point admitting incoming/outgoing restricted
edges, and internally chain transitive for the exact-band relation.
Choose h_max, the largest H value among critical periodic orbits in K.
At least one exists by Section5. Choose h<h_max above every smaller
critical value (if there is no smaller value, any h<h_max works).
The closed set
 U={z in K:H(z)>=h}
is positively invariant by(7). Let A be its maximal invariant subset,
 A=intersection_(n>=0) R^n(U).
The sets R^n(U) are nested nonempty compact sets. A is fully invariant;
compact diagonal extraction supplies a full path in U through each of
its points (also Akin2307.03815v1 Corollary2.6).

Every full path in A has both critical ends in U. The only critical
orbits in U have value h_max, so a noncritical such path would violate
the strict end ordering in Section5. Therefore A is exactly the finite
union of critical orbits of value h_max. In particular A subset int_K(U).
Nested compactness implies that for some finite N,
 R^N(U) subset int_K(U): otherwise select a point of each nested image
outside int(U) and obtain a point of A there, contradiction.

If K is not A, it has a point x outside U. Indeed if U=K, full invariance
would give A=K. Construct a one-step trapping neighborhood W containing U
and excluding x as follows. Put W0=U. Work backwards from N-1 to1,
choosing compact neighborhoods W_j of R^j(U), all excluding x, with
 R(W_(N-1)) subset int(W0),
 R(W_j) subset int(W_(j+1)) for 1<=j<N-1.
These choices follow from compactness/closedness of R: if R(C) is inside
an open set, a sufficiently small closed neighborhood of the compact C
has its R-image inside that open set. Each R^j(U) is a subset of U,
which is separated from x. Also R(W0)=R(U) subset int(W1).
For N=1 simply use W=U. Otherwise W=union_(j=0)^(N-1) W_j satisfies
 R(W) subset int(W), contains A and excludes x. All interiors are relative

Supplement to T421-W706-021 v5 Section6. Kind:special; target1.
Status: proof (unaudited). This verifies an abstract implication, conditional

It is not an independent proof of those source-dependent inputs.

HYPOTHESES. K is a nonempty compact metric space, R a closed subset of K times K,
and every point has at least one incoming and outgoing R-edge in K.
A continuous H:K->R is nondecreasing on edges. There are finitely many
critical periodic orbits. Every full doubly infinite path approaches one
such orbit at each time end. If a full path is not itself critical, its
forward critical end has STRICTLY larger H value than its backward end.
Each critical state has a unique outgoing edge, its ordinary successor.
The R-chain convention is true edges followed by small jumps, including
a final small jump to the desired endpoint, as in021 Section3.

CONCLUSION. If K is internally chain transitive, it is one critical orbit.

1. Closed relations and nested images.
For compact C subset K, R(C) is compact as the projection of the compact
set R intersect (C times K). Moreover for nested nonempty compact C_n,
 R(intersection_n C_n)=intersection_n R(C_n).
The forward inclusion is immediate. For the reverse, fix y in every
R(C_n). Its possible predecessors in C_n form nested nonempty compact
sets. Their intersection supplies a predecessor in intersection C_n.
No lower semicontinuity or continuous selection is used.

Choose h_max, the largest critical H value in K, and h<h_max above all
smaller critical values. At least one critical orbit exists by taking a
full path through any point; compactness supplies the stated end orbits
in K. Set U={H>=h}, with interiors always relative to K. It is nonempty,
compact and positively invariant. C_n=R^n(U), n>=0, are nested nonempty
compact sets: R(U) subset U by monotonicity, and every point has an outgoing
edge. Their intersection A satisfies R(A)=A by the preceding identity.
In particular each point of A has incoming and outgoing edges in A, and
one can recursively choose a full path in A through it. Positive-time
choices remain in A; predecessor choices use R(A)=A.

Every such full path has both end orbits in U, necessarily at level
h_max. Strict end ordering excludes every noncritical full path. Thus
A consists exactly of the union of critical orbits at level h_max.
Conversely each such orbit is contained in every R^n(U), because it has
arbitrarily long predecessors in that orbit. Therefore A subset int_K U,
since its H value is strictly greater than h.

2. Finite entry into the interior and one-step trapping.
Some N>=1 satisfies C_N subset int_K U. Otherwise the nested nonempty
compact sets C_n intersect (K minus int_K U) have a common point, which
would belong to A outside int_K U. If K!=A then some x in K lies outside
U: if U=K, seriality in both directions gives R(K)=K and A=K. Since U
is compact and x is outside, its distance from x is positive.

We use the following upper-neighborhood fact: if C is compact and
R(C) subset O for an open O, then a sufficiently small closed metric
neighborhood N_eta(C) in K satisfies R(N_eta(C)) subset O. Otherwise
choose eta_n->0 and edges with source tending to C and target outside O.
A convergent subsequence and closedness give an edge from C to K minus O,
contradiction. Closed metric neighborhoods are compact here.

If N=1 use W=U. If N>1, work backward j=N-1,...,1. Given an open
neighborhood O of C_(j+1), the upper-neighborhood fact permits a compact
neighborhood W_j of C_j with R(W_j) subset O and excluding x. Start
with O=int_K U and subsequently use O=int_K W_(j+1). Each C_j is a
subset of U, so x can always be excluded. Taking W_0=U gives
 R(W_(N-1)) subset int_K U,
 R(W_j) subset int_K W_(j+1), 1<=j<N-1,
 R(U)=C_1 subset int_K W_1.
Thus W=union_(j=0)^(N-1) W_j is compact, contains A, excludes x, and
 R(W) subset int_K W.
U itself need not be a neighborhood of all of U; only its interior
containing C_N and A is used. This avoids a hidden openness assumption.

3. Chains cannot escape.
R(W) and K minus int_K W are disjoint compact sets and both are
nonempty when needed; their distance gamma is positive. A relation
chain whose first source is in A remains in W when every jump is less
than gamma: an edge with source in W has target in R(W), and any such
jump lands in int_K W. The same gap prevents its final jump from reaching
x outside W. This contradicts internal chain transitivity. Hence K=A.
On A, true edges follow the unique critical successors. The finite set
of distinct critical orbits has positive separation; chains with smaller
jumps cannot switch orbits. Internal chain transitivity leaves one orbit.

contain a state (y,z,V,q)=(0,0,V0,0) with V0>0. Branch labels are arbitrary
subject to their own restrictions; the argument uses neither label.

a positive pure-variance state, with variance V0/d. Iterating this argument
backwards yields V_(-k)=V0*d^(-k) for every integer k>=0.

boundedness. This is a full-history obstruction, not a claim about a
one-sided orbit: positive pure variance has a perfectly valid forward
orbit with V_k=d^k*V0 and y=z=q=0.

All canceled quantities have now been accounted for: d>0; s,s'>0 follow
from positive variances; u>0 follows from u*s'=s; and b>0 is a hypothesis.
The growth conclusion uses d<1 and V0>0. If d=1 there is no growth and
constant positive pure variance is a bounded full path. If boundedness
or full negative-time history is removed, the forward orbit above is
not excluded. The lemma does not exclude limit states reached by
one-sided paths unless a full bounded limiting history has been obtained.

2. UNIFORM FINITE-WINDOW PAYMENT.

(z_n) for -N<=n<=N+1 whose central edge lies in C_sigma satisfies
 sum_{n=-N}^N D(z_n,z_(n+1))>=epsilon.                    (1)

# Corrected lifted edge limits and omega-set chains
Kind: special; target:1. Status: proof (unaudited).
Supporting argument for056 Section3, with a direct F3 derivation.
It does not independently audit the source potential inequalities or021.

1. The exact corrected recurrence and its limiting edge.
Fix eta>0, positive lambda_i and r=epsilon/eta>0. In one coordinate
use056's normalization c=1/19,b=9/10,d=999/1000,nu=1-d,
 y_t=x_t/(c eta), mu_t=m_t/(c eta lambda),
 V_t=v_t/(c eta lambda)^2, e=r/(c lambda)>0,
 z_t=y_(t-1), s_t=sqrt(V_t)+e, q_t=z_t/s_t.
Assume the actual tail and raw moments lie in a fixed bounded box;
this note does not re-prove the absorbing box. For t>=1 put
 kappa_t=(1-b^t)*(sqrt(V_t/(1-d^t))+e).
The position update at the PREVIOUS step gives exactly
 mu_t=-c*kappa_t*(y_t-z_t).
The raw recurrences mu_(t+1)=b*mu_t+(1-b)*y_t and
 V_(t+1)=d*V_t+nu*y_t^2 therefore imply
 y_(t+1)=y_t+b*(kappa_t/kappa_(t+1))*(y_t-z_t)
              -(1+b)*y_t/kappa_(t+1).                 (1)
Here (1-b)/c=1+b exactly; the clocks in kappa_(t+1) have index t+1.
On the bounded box kappa_t-s_t tends uniformly to zero at fixed e>0.
Indeed the sqrt clock factor tends to1, and its uncorrected argument
is uniformly bounded. For all sufficiently large t, kappa_t>=e/2.
All divisions in (1) thus pass to adjacent-pair limits. Every limiting
edge satisfies
 V'=dV+nu*y^2, z'=y, q'*s'=y, u=s/s',
 y'=y+b*u*(y-z)-(1+b)*q'.                             (2)
Also V>=nu*z^2, qs=z, u>=0 and d*u^2<=1, since
 s'>=sqrt(d)*sqrt(V)+e>=sqrt(d)*s.
Labels are part of a finite discrete coordinate: low at s>=1, high at
s<=1. At s=1 the two copies remain distinct. Label limits satisfy
these closed constraints; continuity of a single-valued label map is
neither asserted nor needed.

2. F3 from the bounded full gradient history.
Through any adjacent-pair limit, diagonal extraction of shifted raw
(y,mu,V) histories supplies a bounded doubly infinite uncorrected path.
Its moment recurrences unroll to the absolutely convergent formulas
 mu_t=(1-b)*sum_(j>=0) b^j*y_(t-1-j),
 V_t=nu*sum_(j>=0) d^j*y_(t-1-j)^2.                   (3)
Boundedness makes the discarded remainders b^n*mu_(t-n) and
d^n*V_(t-n) tend to zero. The past-step position equation is
 y_t=y_(t-1)-mu_t/(c*s_t).
Write B=1+b, s=s_t, V=V_t. In this linear functional of the past
positions the coefficient for j=0 is 1-B/s and for j>=1 is
 -B*b^j/s. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, with positive weights d^j and
b^2<d, gives
 nu*y_t^2 <= V*[1-2B/s+B^2*d/(s^2*(d-b^2))].          (4)
The bracket is the sum of squared functional coefficients divided
by d^j; in particular it is nonnegative. This is a deterministic
Hilbert-space inequality, not a concentration or independence argument.
The geometric series used is sum_(j>=1)(b^2/d)^j=b^2/(d-b^2).
Adding dV to (4), using V=(s-e)^2<=s^2 and positivity of the
resulting coefficient, yields
 V_(t+1) <= (1+d)*s^2-2B*s+B^2*d/(d-b^2).
For a high source 0<s<=1 and 1+d<2B, so its first two terms have
nonpositive sum. Consequently
 s'<=B*sqrt(d/(d-b^2))+e <3B+1/2=31/5                 (5)
whenever e<1/2. The square-root comparison uses d/(d-b^2)<9.
All constants in (5) are independent of the positive lower bound on e.
At e=0 singular source states are not derived by dividing by s here:
when parameters later tend to that boundary, the closed bound s'<=31/5
is inherited from these fixed-positive-e limiting edges instead.

3. Passing the active band without dividing at zero gradient.
With the post-variance-update convention in056, define
 qbar_i=y_i/(sqrt(V_i'/(1-d^(t+1)))+e_i),
 Dbar=sum_i lambda_i*y_i*qbar_i.
When the active quotient is defined its width-delta inequality is
 |sum_i lambda_i*(qbar_i^2-2*y_i*qbar_i)|<=c*delta*Dbar.
At fixed positive e_i, qbar_i-q_i' tends uniformly to zero on the
bounded box. Thus adjacent-pair limits obey the same multiplied band
with q_i'. This passage remains valid when the limiting gradient is
zero: no division by a limiting D is made. The statement here uses
exactly this timing convention; a different preconditioner timing
requires its own identification before applying this formula.

4. A compact-sequence lemma: restricted edge limits are chain transitive.
Let a_n be ANY sequence in a compact metric space, K its nonempty omega
set and G the set of all limits of pairs (a_n,a_(n+1)) as n->infinity.
Then G is compact and contained in K times K. Every point of K has an
incoming and an outgoing G-edge, by extraction of its predecessor or
successor along a subsequence. Also dist((a_n,a_(n+1)),G)->0; otherwise
a counterexample subsequence has a convergent pair limit belonging to G.

Fix x,y in K and epsilon>0. Choose h>0 with 2h<epsilon. Along a
subsequence a_n->x also extract a_(n+1)->v, giving the TRUE edge (x,v).
Choose n sufficiently late that dist(a_(n+1),v)<h and every later pair
is within h of G in the max product metric. Choose a later m>=n+2
with dist(a_m,y)<h. For j=n+1,...,m-1 replace the pair
(a_j,a_(j+1)) by an edge (A_j,B_j) of G within h.
Begin with (x,v). Its jump to A_(n+1) is <2h. Consecutive replacement
edges have jumps dist(B_j,A_(j+1))<2h, as does the last target's jump
to y. Thus this is an epsilon-chain with first source EXACTLY x,
all true edges and endpoints in K, and an allowed final jump to y.
There is no accumulated error and no uniform bound on m-n is required.
Therefore K is internally chain transitive for G and for every closed
relation restricted to K that contains G. This does not require
continuity of the label lift or of an underlying map.

5. Application boundary: what is CLEAN and what remains separate.
CLEAN for the compact-sequence lemma and the corrected algebra/F3
calculations above: their hypotheses, indices, inequality directions
and constants re-derive. For the actual lifted sequence, Sections1-3
place G in the physical and band constraints of056, assuming its
bounded box and its stated active-curvature timing convention.
The FIRST additional assertion not re-derived in this note is
 Psi_i=phi_i'-phi_i-W_i>=0 for every limiting labeled branch edge.
That is the source-potential inequality and all branch-closure cases;
it is not supplied by chain transitivity or Cauchy-Schwarz. Assuming
that inequality, G lies in056's restricted relation, and Section4 gives
all of056 Section3's seriality, full-path extraction, pair approach
and internal chain transitivity conclusions. The potential claims

[Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] There exist constants $C_1,C_2<\infty$, depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists 1\le j\le M:
\max_{u_{j-1}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]> C_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\right)
\le C_2(\log n)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, outside an event of probability $O((\log n)^{-1})$,
\begin{equation}

\max_{u_{j-3}\le r\le s\le u_j}X[r,s]
\le C'_1\mathbb{E}[\Delta_n]
\qquad\text{for all }3\le j\le M.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if we fix $l,q>0$,  
then for every $p>0$ there is
$K=K(p,l,q,\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{P}\left(
\exists r\le M:
\max_{u_r- l a_n^{(q)} \le s\le t\le u_r+{ la_n^{(q)}}}
X[s,t]
> K\mathbb{E}[X_{l a_n^{(q)}}]
\right)
\le (\log n)^{-p}.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma lem:local-max of arXiv:2608.23135

[Lemma 47 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \((U,h)\) be a smooth Riemannian manifold, and let
\(H_i,H:U\to\R^k\) be smooth maps with
\(H_i\to H\) in \(C^\infty_{\rm loc}\).  Suppose that \(0\) is a regular
value of \(H\), and set \(S=H^{-1}(0)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}K^+\Subset S\) are compact
domains, then, for all large \(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\) contains a small
normal graph \(K_i\) over \(K\), and \(K_i\to K\) smoothly.
\item If \(S\) is compact and is the entire zero set of \(H\) in a
precompact tubular neighbourhood \(U_0\Subset U\), then, for all large
\(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\cap U_0\) contains a compact boundaryless normal
graph \(S_i\) over \(S\).  Moreover, \(S_i\to S\) smoothly and
\(S_i\cong S\).
\end{enumerate}
If Riemannian metrics \(h_i\) on \(U\) converge smoothly to \(h\), the
induced metrics and volume forms on these graphs converge smoothly. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Sgn of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $g\ge 2$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathcal S_{g,n}=\emptyset$ for $n>2g+2$.
\item For $g+2<n\le 2g+2$, the locus $\mathcal S_{g,n}$ is empty unless $n\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$, and then it consists of the single point $y^n=x^2-1$, which lies in the hyperelliptic locus.
\item Let $3\le n\le g+2$ and $\mathcal S_{g,n}\ne\emptyset$. Then the datum $\mathbf C_{g,n}$ has $m\ge 3$. If $3\mid g+2$, then $\mathcal S_{g,g+2}$ contains the non-hyperelliptic curve $y^{g+2}=x^3-x$.
\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Asymptotic total length of finite SIRSN samples structural attempt Result: A local truncation argument gives the lower bound liminf E length/k>=ell. Tile the bulk of the large square by unit cells. For fixed R and M, retain in each cell only the length, truncated at M, of routes between sampled endpoints within distance R of that cell. Its local binomial point configuration converges in total variation to the corresponding rate1 Poisson configuration. The retained length is bounded by M, so its expectation converges. Summing disjoint unit-cell contributions and then taking k to infinity gives the Poisson local truncated expectation as a lower bound. Let M and then R increase: monotone convergence recovers the full sampled-network intensity ell. Check: Only a bounded endpoint region is used before taking k to infinity; its binomial count tends to a Poisson count and conditional positions have the same uniform law. Truncation avoids any unproved uniform-integrability step. Boundary cells are an asymptotically negligible fraction for fixed R. Obstruction: This proves no upper bound on total length. Rare paths can leave the sampling square by a large distance, and their exterior contribution is absent from the local lower-bound argument. Controlling those excursions remains necessary for equality.

\end{align}

body:
Let n>=2, K>0, and let x=(x_1,...,x_n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) be real random vectors whose 2n coordinates are mutually independent, each with a Lebesgue density bounded almost everywhere by K. Let Z be a deterministic real n by n matrix, u,v deterministic real n-vectors, and w a deterministic real scalar. Write sigma_1(Z)>=...>=sigma_n(Z)>=0 for its singular values, and assume r=rank(Z)>=2. Then Q=x^T Z y+x^T u+v^T y+w has a Lebesgue density satisfying ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2(C_RV K)^2 sqrt(2e*pi) min_{2<=j<=r} [j^(-1/2) (product_{i=1}^j sigma_i(Z))^(-1/j)], where C_RV is the universal constant in the Rudelson-Vershynin bounded-density projection theorem. Equivalently one may minimize over 2<=j<=n, interpreting terms with zero singular-value product as infinity. This is the k=1 corollary of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava, arXiv:2005.08930. No bounded-density bound is available in general at rank one: if U,V are independent uniform(0,1), UV has density -log(t) on 0<t<1, which is unbounded near zero. Independence only between the two vectors is insufficient even at rank two: x=(U,U), y=(V,V), Z=diag(1,-1) gives Q=0 almost surely. A quadratic-form application must independently verify the coordinate independence and rank hypotheses.
n>=2 and K>0
All 2n coordinates of x and y are mutually independent and each has a Lebesgue density bounded a.e. by K
Z,u,v,w are deterministic real coefficients
rank(Z)>=2

\[
\begin{aligned}
d_0&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_2), & d_1&=e_1,\ d_2=e_2,\\
d_3&=-\varepsilon(e_3+e_4), & d_4&=e_3,\ d_5=e_4,\\
d_6&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3), & d_7&=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
with masses $s_0=s_3=s_6=s_7=\frac1{4(1+2\varepsilon)}$ and
$s_1=s_2=s_4=s_5=\frac{\varepsilon}{2(1+2\varepsilon)}$, realized as a
whitened system through Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper). Exactly the four points
$d_0,d_3,d_6,d_7$ are strictly $4$-generated, and the four side points
$d_1,d_2,d_4,d_5$ are not generated by the other rays at all. The exact
Mahalanobis norms are
\[
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{2\varepsilon(3\varepsilon+2)}{\varepsilon+1}
\ \text{(generated points)},\qquad
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon+2}{\varepsilon(\varepsilon+1)}
\ \text{(side points)} .
\]
For $0<\varepsilon<\frac{\sqrt{33}-3}{12}\approx0.2287$, all generated
points have $t=1/\lVert v\rVert^2>1$ and all side points have $t<1$: no point is
simultaneously cheap and generated. At $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ the values
are exactly $t=\frac{5050}{203}$ and $t=\frac{101}{20401}$.

title: Rice's theorem

body: In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item. For example, of three gloves, at least two must be right-handed or at least two must be left-handed, because there are three objects but only two categories of handedness to put them into. This seemingly obvious statement, a type of counting argument, can be used to demonstrate possibly unexpected results. For example, given that the population of London is more than one unit greater than the maximum number of hairs that can be on a human head, the principle requires that there must be at least two people in London who have the same number of hairs on their heads.
title: Pigeonhole principle

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cd/cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:8fa1a006ec51c6fad47bb921cdb11f4678bf39fef10fc5ba1168b152a20f4745","bundle_entry_key":"instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","bundle_id":"population.t410-oracle-sampling-barriers-protected-blocks-003","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"computational complexity; conditional sampling; relative entropy; autoregressive scoring","draft":"w739/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Instance-uniform sampling is incompatible with Target 2 circuit hardness

Claim C005 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target: 2.
No novelty priority is claimed. This is an elementary necessary restriction
on an oracle construction, not a separation or an impossibility of C003 A.

## Exact hypothesis

Fix an oracle O. Suppose there is one randomized oracle algorithm U which,
given an explicit description of any deterministic oracle circuit C on m bits,
with output in {0,1,4} and positive total weight, samples a distribution within
total variation 1/10 of the law assigning probability C(z)/sum C to z.
Its time and randomness are bounded by one polynomial in the description
length and m. The quantifier includes circuits containing a fixed input x as
constants. Ordinary polynomial-size circuits may use O gates, in the usual
bit-query model. This is an INSTANCE-UNIFORM sampler interface.

Then NP^O is contained in RP^O, and consequently NP^O is contained in P^O/poly.
It is therefore incompatible with the circuit-hardness requirement of Target 2.

## Verifier reduction

Let A be any NP^O language, with a polynomial-time oracle verifier V(x,w)
and exactly p(|x|) witness bits after padding. Given x, construct in polynomial
time a circuit C_x with m=1+p(|x|) input bits. It assigns weight 1 to 0^m,
weight 4 to 1w when V(x,w) accepts, and zero to all other strings. The circuit
is polynomial-size: unroll the bounded verifier, with oracle gates for its
queries, and hardwire x. Its normalizer is 1+4 Z_x, where Z_x counts witnesses.
No normalizer computation is used by the reduction.

Run U on C_x. Accept only if the sampled word is 1w and V(x,w) actually
accepts. On a no input this never accepts. On a yes input the target event has
mass 4Z_x/(1+4Z_x)>=4/5. Total variation at most 1/10 leaves acceptance
probability at least 7/10. This proves A is in RP^O. The running time is
polynomial in |x| because U has one polynomial bound uniform over descriptions.

## Relativized randomized-to-advice step

For each input length n, repeat the preceding test independently k=n+2 times
and accept if any run accepts. A yes input is rejected with probability at
most (3/10)^k; a no input is never accepted. The union bound over all 2^n
inputs of length n gives probability of any mistake at most

    2^n (3/10)^(n+2) = (9/100)(3/5)^n < 1.

Thus there is one fixed polynomial-length collection of k random tapes that
works simultaneously for EVERY length-n input. Hardwire those tapes as advice
and unroll the oracle computation into a polynomial-size oracle circuit.
Only the independent repetitions on a single input were multiplied; inputs
need no independence. This proves A is in P^O/poly. The tape collection may
depend on n and O, exactly as the circuit model permits.

## Why this does not contradict C003

C003 A has quantifier form: for every fixed uniform weighted family W, there
exists a uniform polynomial-time sampler S_W. It supplies neither a computable
compiler W to S_W nor a polynomial bound uniform over weight descriptions.
In the reduction above x varies with the INSTANCE, not just with the length.
Replacing the family-specific samplers by a single sampler accepting C_x would
be an extra assumption, which is precisely what the theorem rules out.

C004 encoded a unary input into a polynomially related output length and so
did not require this additional uniformity. Encoding every binary x into its
own length requires exponentially many lengths; it does not yield a polynomial
time reduction and cannot silently convert C003 A into this stronger property.

Therefore an oracle construction for C003 must achieve family-specific
sampling without a polynomial-time instance-uniform weight-circuit interface.
It must also preserve hardness after all sampling/inversion interfaces are
available. Neither this proof nor C004 proves such a construction exists.
The joint oracle consistency problem for binary NP circuit hardness is OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a709e45865929b025dd7f8ab22e9a633f013cb492fed61e532bf39a91f8c0201","revision_digest":"sha256:d9fe42072d4cba052697690bd26cd19d3d236739c096685e652aa411c85317b6","source_id":"owner-own-work:T410-w739-C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T21:39:37.775816+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let n>=2, D be a real (n-1)-by-n matrix, X in R^n, A=[D;X^T], and r>=0. If the least of the n-1 singular values of D is <=r, then s_min(A)<=r. Otherwise let v span ker(D) with norm one, and let (v_i,s_i), i=1,...,n-1, be right singular vectors and positive singular values of D. Then s_min(A)<=r exactly when |<v,X>|^2 <= r^2(1+sum_i |<v_i,X>|^2/(s_i^2-r^2)).

body: Let (X, Sigma_X, mu) and (Y, Sigma_Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces and let f be measurable on the product sigma-algebra of X times Y, with values in R or C. If the double integral of |f| over X times Y with respect to mu times nu is finite (f is integrable), then for a.e. x the slice y -> f(x,y) is integrable, for a.e. y the slice x -> f(x,y) is integrable, and integral_X integral_Y f dnu dmu = integral_Y integral_X f dmu dnu = integral over X times Y of f d(mu times nu). Tonelli's theorem gives the same conclusion for f merely nonnegative and measurable, integrals allowed to be +infinity.

 b(s,q,e)=[A(s)+e*c]/[m(s)+K*q].                         (2)

For a fixed collection of cell signatures, rearrangement assigns the
largest high false counts to the largest b values, each with capacity q.
Hence after ordering cells by decreasing b, each cell receives a
contiguous block of the sorted high list. Equal b cell types can be put
in any fixed order: the variable-count contribution is unchanged.

Enumerate all signatures (s,q,e), sort by decreasing b, then run an
unbounded knapsack DP in that order. State: used native count vector,
number of high whole objects consumed and whether the donor is marked.
Choosing a cell consumes s,q and adds (2), using the next q false counts.
At a given signature, repeated choices are allowed; every choice consumes
at least one resource, so increasing total-resource order is acyclic.
A marked signature can only be used while the flag is0 and sets it1.
Skipping to the next signature is allowed. End with all resources used
and one mark. All finite partitions have a sorted representation by
rearrangement, and every DP path is a valid partition, proving equality.

There are at most2*(H+1)*product_t(v_t+1) signatures and at most
2*(H+1)*product_t(v_t+1) states per signature. Including prefix selections
gives a polynomial in d for each FIXED K0, of degree depending on K0.
Posterior rationals have bit length polynomial in explicit sample size;
sorting, benefits and DP sums use exact rational arithmetic. Backpointers
recover the actual partition; C026 supplies the robust generator and
finite-group policy symmetrization (efficient random permutations).

## Proof details, exact evidence and limits

Low-context removal can be performed in increasing risk order: the
smallest low object in a cell has risk no larger than the mean of the
remaining components. Removing it increases the remaining mean risk
and leaves deficit A fixed. The isolated low object has deficit0.
Repeating yields all lows isolated. If a remaining pool is nonempty,
its components all have risk>=F/(2K), so the maximum risk is attained
among nonlow cells. A whole branch always supplies a high counterpart.
Thus low cells need not be marked even at positive c.

For the prefix exchange keep the old high object's pool assignment:
increasing its expected false count increases both its nonnegative
deficit benefit and its risk. Only an isolated low count decreases.
The multiset of unselected native components is identical for equal h,
including the F-unit saturated branch. Therefore neither budget nor
baseline invalidates the exchange.

For rearrangement, expand each cell coefficient b into q identical
slots. Swapping inverted high counts x>=y between coefficients b>=a
changes benefit by(x-y)*(b-a)>=0. This elementary identity proves the
needed assignment step without trusting an external formula. It also
applies to the single marked coefficient. Exactly one cell is marked;
optimizing its identity is equivalent to c*maximum risk. Native-only
cells have q0 and do not constrain the high order. Whole-only cells
have s0,q>0 and remain allowed.

For repeated knapsack choices, each step strictly increases
sum_t used_v_t+used_high. Processing resource states in that order
permits all repetitions of the current signature. Moving to the next
signature prevents decreasing coefficient order. Equal-coefficient
types may be canonically grouped because their total high contribution
does not depend on which of their equal-b slots receive particular
counts. This proves both directions of the DP correspondence.

The fixed-K type bound and polynomial cardinalities above concern
explicit data and rational c. Posterior numerators/denominators have
O(n log K+K) bits before common reductions. Rational DP path sums have
at most O(Kd) summands of polynomial bit size; exact comparisons and
sorting therefore preserve polynomial bit complexity. Uniform draws
of context swaps and atom permutations implement C026 policy
symmetrization in polynomial time. Backpointers reconstruct native
components, high-count slots and the marked cell; low whole objects
are isolated. C026 supplies the actual robust generator.

scripts/posterior_prefix_dp.py is a guarded exact prototype:
before resource allocation it bounds signature-times-state work by
two million per prefix choice. Reconstruction of the resource path
checks counts, contiguous high slots, single donor mark and benefit.
These box limits are not an asymptotic algorithm restriction.

C026's UNRESTRICTED branch and multiset partition solver in1933 games,
including1340 below-half,529 saturated and1679 mixed-h cases.
It checks5510 prefix choices and200384 bounded state/signature products.
Cases include the C025 unit-splitting and internal budget-crossing

This is a cross-check of different optimizations; it is not an

logs/posterior_prefix_controls_check.json uses genuine K3,r2,N7 data:

TECHNIQUE CARD. Exponential approximation by Stein's method: couple a non-negative variable with a variable having its equilibrium law; when the two are close, the variable is close to the exponential law. Ross, Definition 5.2: for W ≥ 0 with E[W] = μ, W^e has the equilibrium distribution with respect to W if E[f(W)] − f(0) = μE[f'(W^e)] for all Lipschitz f. Theorem 5.4: if W ≥ 0 with E[W] = 1 and E[W²] < ∞, and W^e has the equilibrium distribution with respect to W and is coupled to W, then for Z ~ Exp(1), d_W(W, Z) ≤ 2E|W^e − W|. Proposition 5.5 builds W^e from the size-bias law: if W ≥ 0 with E[W] = μ, W^s has the size-bias distribution of W, and U is uniform on (0,1) and independent of W^s, then UW^s has the equilibrium distribution of W.
W ≥ 0 with E[W] = 1 and E[W²] < ∞ (Theorem 5.4)

[Definition 249 (Half-spectral curve) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Given $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$ non-zero with bipartite $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit, we define $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\textnormal{half}}$ to be the image in the quotient $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ (\textit{cf.} Definition~\ref{def:spcurv1}) of
\[
\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}.
\]
where $\epsilon$ is the unique bipartition of $\mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ such that $\epsilon(\boldsymbol{v}) = 1$. This is a bordered Riemann surface, whose boundary is the closure of the set of real points, that is the image in $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ of
\[
\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \big(\widehat{\amsmathbb{R}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}\big).
\]
See Figure~\ref{Fig:Half5} and \ref{Fig:Half7} for an example.

Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. For a known integer horizon k>=3, choose lambda_t=lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1)>0 and keep it fixed for all k rounds. Then E L(w_k)<=5*D2*R^2*ln(k)/k. Thus the coefficient is constant within a run and changes with the chosen horizon.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
Known horizon k>=3; lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1) used throughout the run.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Estimate the number of near-maximal configurations and compare with the connectivity threshold of the level set on the hypercube. Result: In the NK model with K = O(1) the fitness is a sum of n local terms each depending on K + 1 bits, so the field is a sum of n independent contributions (for the standard model with random neighbourhoods) and the level set at height M_n - delta_n with delta_n = o(n) but delta_n >> sqrt n contains exp(c delta_n^2/n)... the number of configurations within delta of the maximum is, by a large-deviation count, about exp(n I(delta/n)) for a rate I; bridges exist if this level set percolates on the hypercube, and a level set of density rho on the n-cube contains a giant connected component when the local structure allows, roughly when each configuration in the set has on average more than one neighbour in the set: the expected number of neighbours in the level set of a typical level-set point is n times the conditional probability that flipping one bit stays within delta of the maximum, which is n times (probability that the change of the K+1 affected local terms is at most delta), of order n delta/n = delta when delta is small compared to the local term scale... so bridges exist (heuristically) when delta_n >> 1, i.e. the level set within a constant deficit of the maximum is connected in the giant-component sense for deficits growing to infinity, while for bounded deficits the peaks are isolated. This suggests the answer depends on the deficit scale: bridges at deficit delta_n -> infinity, islands at bounded deficit. The argument is a branching heuristic (neighbour counts) without control of dependencies; making it rigorous would need a second-moment argument on the number of level-set paths, which I did not carry out. Key identity: Expected number of level-set neighbours of a level-set point is of order delta (the deficit); bridges expected iff the deficit tends to infinity. Obstruction: Second moment for level-set paths on the hypercube not done.

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] For $d$ odd there is an isomorphism of graded $S_n$-modules
	$$ 
H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)_d)\cong \bigoplus_{a+b=d-1} u_{(a,b)}\Sigma^{d}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast],
	$$
where
	$$u_{(a,b)} =
	\begin{cases}
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		\delta_{a,b} & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 0 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 
		& \\
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		1 & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 1 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 	
		& \\
		0 & \text{ else.}
	\end{cases}
	$$
title: Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Aldous and Fill, Open Problem 4.30 (p. 137) asks whether there is an explicit function psi(b,s) tending to 0 as s tends to infinity, not depending on the chain, with sup_x |P(S_t/(sigma sqrt t) <= x) - P(Z <= x)| <= psi(||g||_inf, t/tau2) for standardized g and continuous-time reversible chains. Our result (id P0209, 2026-09-08): NO such psi exists. Take two independent reversible chains: Y two-state with rates epsilon and 1 - epsilon (spectral gap exactly 1) and Z a fair sign flip at rate R/2; set epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4, A = 2 epsilon + sqrt((1-epsilon)(1-4 epsilon)), B = (2-A)/(1-epsilon) and g = A Z + B (Y - epsilon). Then exactly, at every s: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, ||g||_inf = 2 and tau2 = 1. Taking t = s sends t/tau2 to infinity with the sup norm pinned at 2, yet normality fails: S_t is compound Poisson with vanishing intensity (the mean number of visits to the rare state is epsilon t = 1/s, tending to 0), so with probability 1 - O(1/s) no visit occurs and S_t sits near the deterministic value -B epsilon t while the whole variance is carried by one rare excursion. Verification as the source words it: the identities were checked to seven decimals at every s, and the measured Kolmogorov distance to N(0,1) is 0.478, 0.505, 0.509, 0.506 at s = 30, 100, 300, 1000 - flat at about 1/2, not decreasing, while t/tau2 rises from 30 to 1000. Prior art not cleared. two independent reversible chains as specified (four states in total) g standardized: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, sup norm 2, tau2 = 1 t = s, epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4

    \[ x_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} p(n, i)x_i \ \text{ for $n > k$}. \]
    Suppose that $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} p(n,i) = 1$ and $\frac{p(n,i)}{p(n+1, i)}$ is increasing in $i$ for every $n$. Then $x_{n+1} < x_n$ for all $n \geq k$. In particular, $\lim_{n \to \infty} x_n$ exists. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota \colon X \to S\) be a morphism of $\F_p$-stacks.
Let
\[
X^{(1)} \defeq X\times_{S,F_S}S
\]
be the relative Frobenius twist, and let
\[
F_{X/S}\colon X \to  X^{(1)}
\]
be the relative Frobenius.
  \begin{itemize}
      \item   The \emph{(absolute) de Rham stack} of \(X\) is defined as a functor
  \begin{equation*}
    X^{\dR} \colon \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p} \to \Ani; \  R \mapsto X(W(R)/^L p),
  \end{equation*}
  where \(W(R)\) is the ring of Witt vectors of \(R\), \(-/^L p\) is the derived quotient by \(p\), and \(X(W(R)/^L p)\) is the mapping space \(\Map_{\dSch_{\setF_p}}(\Spec(W(R)/^L p), X)\) in the \(\infty\)-category of derived schemes over \(\setF_p\).
  Since this is isomorphic to the relative Hodge--Tate stack \((X/\setZ_p)^{\HT}\) of \(X\) relative to the crystalline prism \((\setZ_p, (p))\) introduced in \cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Construction 7.1}, this is a stack on \(\CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\) (\cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Lemma 7.3}).

  This is equipped with natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X} \colon X \to X^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_X \colon X^{\dR} \to X
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks: For each \(R \in \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\), each morphism is given by precomposition of morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    R \xrightarrow{\Phi_R} W(R)/^L p \quad \text{and} \quad W(R)/^L p \xrightarrow{\res} R,
  \end{equation*}
  where \(\Phi_R\) is the animation of the morphism \(a \mapsto [a^p] \bmod p\) and \(\res\) is the restriction morphism.
  Note that the composition \(\nu_X \circ \pi_X\) is the absolute Frobenius morphism \(F_X \colon X \to X\) of \(X\).
\item The \emph{de Rham stack} of $X$ over $S$ is defined by
\[
(X/S)^{\dR} \defeq X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR},\pi_S} S.
\]
We define natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X/S} \colon X \to (X/S)^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks as follows:
The morphism $\pi_{X/S}$ is defined by
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X \arrow[r,"\pi_{X/S}"'] \arrow[rd,bend right,"\iota"] \arrow[rr,bend left,"\pi_X"] & X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \\
& S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] & S^{\dR}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The morphism $\nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}$ is induced by the following commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \arrow[r,"\nu_X"] & X \arrow[d,"\iota"] \\
S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] \arrow[rr,bend right,"F"] & S^{\dR} \arrow[r,"\nu_S"] & S.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\item We assume that $\iota$ is smooth representable.
Then the cotangent complex \(L_{X/S}\) is a locally free \(\cO_X\)-module concentrated in degree \(0\).  
We set
\[
\Omega^1_{X/S} \defeq L_{X/S},
\qquad
\Omega^i_{X/S} \defeq 
\bigwedge_{\cO_X}^i\Omega^1_{X/S}.
\]
The universal \(S\)-derivation
\[
d_{X/S}\colon \cO_X \to  \Omega^1_{X/S}
\]
extends uniquely to the relative de Rham complex
\[
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
=
\left[
\cO_X
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^1_{X/S}
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^2_{X/S}
 \to \cdots
\right].
\]

We define a morphism of complexes of $\cO_{X^{(1)}}$-modules
\[
F^{\dR}_{X/S} \colon \cO_{X^{(1)}} \to F_{X/S,*}\Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}
\]
as follows:
We have
\[
d_{X/S}\circ F_{X/S}^{\sharp}=0
\]
by checking smooth locally on \(X\).  
Therefore, the morphism
\[
F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}} \to  F_{X/S,*}\cO_X
\]
defines a morphism of complexes
\[
F_{X/S}^{\dR}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}}
 \to 
F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S},
\]
whose degree \(0\) component is \(F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\) and whose
positive-degree components are zero.
\end{itemize}

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C006 v1). For d>=1, the signed radial line law on [-1,1] with density f_d(t)=(d/2)|t|^(d-1) can be (2k+1)-CM only if (k/(k+1))^d>=1/(2k+1). A zero-sum tuple cannot have every |t_i|>k/(k+1), since at least k+1 share a sign and cannot be canceled by k bounded terms. Thus F_2 is not 3-CM (1/4<1/3) and F_4 is not 5-CM (16/81<1/5). These are the uniform disk/four-ball conditional laws on unoriented lines through the center. The full balls are mixable, so this refutes componentwise centered radial-needle mixing, not the convex-body conjecture. Projection onto a fixed line has a different marginal.

body: In mathematical analysis, the alternating series test proves that an alternating series is convergent when its terms decrease monotonically in absolute value and approach zero in the limit. The test was devised by Gottfried Leibniz and is sometimes known as Leibniz's test, Leibniz's rule, or the Leibniz criterion. The test is only sufficient, not necessary, so some convergent alternating series may fail the first part of the test.
title: Alternating series test

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: Omega bounded. The proofs use boundedness twice - the auxiliary function exp(gamma x_1) must be bounded on Omega, and the maximum must be attained on a compact set. On unbounded domains the conclusion is false even for harmonic functions with zero boundary data. Unbounded counterexample: on the half-space {x_n > 0} the function u(x) = x_n is harmonic and vanishes on the whole boundary, yet u > 0 inside; sup u = infinity while sup over the boundary of u = 0. Bounded counterexample (so boundedness of u does not rescue the statement in general): for n >= 3 let Omega = {|x| > 1} and u(x) = 1 - |x|^{2-n}. Then u is harmonic in Omega, continuous up to the boundary, bounded with 0 <= u < 1, u = 0 on the boundary sphere, and sup over Omega of u = 1 > 0 = sup over the boundary of u^+. In the plane, u(x) = log|x| on {|x| > 1} is an unbounded version of the same phenomenon. What restores the principle: treat infinity as a boundary point, i.e. assume limsup of u(x) as |x| tends to infinity is <= 0 (then the principle holds on any unbounded Omega, by exhausting with large balls), or impose a Phragmen-Lindeloef growth restriction adapted to the geometry. The admissible growth is set by the opening of the domain, and a thinner domain permits faster growth, not slower: in a plane sector of opening pi/a the threshold is exp(|x|^a), so a narrow sector allows faster growth than a half-plane, and in a strip of width d the threshold is exp(pi|x|/d), the extremal being exp(pi x_1/d) cos(pi x_2/d). The same caution applies to the H^1 weak maximum principle: its proof uses the Sobolev inequality together with the fact that the level sets have finite measure.
title: Pitfall: The Weak Maximum Principle Needs a Bounded Domain (or Control at Infinity)

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent Bernoulli random variables with \mathbb{P}(X_k = 1) = p_k = 1 - \mathbb{P}(X_k = 0). Let S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k and \lambda = \sum_{k=1}^n p_k. Let Y \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda). Then the total variation distance between the distribution of S_n and Y satisfies d_{TV}(\mathcal{L}(S_n), \text{Poisson}(\lambda)) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^\infty |\mathbb{P}(S_n = k) - \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}| \le \sum_{k=1}^n p_k^2.

[Lemma lem:moving-bump of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let
\[
u:=\left(\frac1{2^n}\right)_{n=1}^\infty\in S_{\ell_1},
\qquad
b_n:=\frac12(e_{n+1}-e_{n+2})\in S_{\ell_1},
\]
where $(e_n)$ denotes the standard coordinate basis for $\ell_1$. 
Let $0<\kappa<1$, and let $S\in\mathcal L(\ell_1,\ell_1)$.
Suppose that there exist a set $A\subset\mathbb N$, a mapping
$\nu\colon A\to\mathbb N$, and scalars $(\lambda_j)_{j\in A}$ such that

\begin{enumerate}
\itemsep0.25em
\item  $Se_j=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j b_{\nu(j)}$ for every $j \in A$, and $|\lambda_j|\leqslant 1$ for every $j \in A$;

\item there exist $(j_n)\subset A$ and a sequence $(s_n)$ tending to
infinity such that
\[
Se_{j_n}=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)b_{s_n};
\]

\item $\sup_{j\notin A}\|Se_j\|<1$.
\end{enumerate}

Then $\|S\|=1$ and $S^*$ does not attain its norm.

Method: Zero speed on every bounded-degree subexponential-growth subgraph Result: Let H be a connected subgraph of a bounded-degree graph G with |B_G(x,n)|=exp(o(n)). The Carne-Varopoulos bound gives P_x(X_n=y)<=2 sqrt(deg_H(y)/deg_H(x)) exp(-d_H(x,y)^2/(2n)). Summing over reachable vertices yields P(d_H(x,X_n)>=epsilon n)<=C exp(o(n)-epsilon^2 n/2), which is summable. Thus the intrinsic speed on H is zero almost surely. Check: Reachability in H implies membership in B_G(x,n), but distances in the exponential bound remain intrinsic to H. Bounded degrees control the prefactor. This is a consequence of the classical heat-kernel bound, not a novelty claim. Obstruction: It settles the zero-speed equivalence for subexponential-growth Cayley graphs and their clusters only. For every k>=1, the prepared aligned finite scale law supported on 1,...,k+1, with zero output weights and biases and exp activation, has a positive risk threshold whose first hitting time for the normalized degree-k sphere harmonic tends to infinity with d. Thus k+1 occupied scales with fixed positive separation do not alone imply O(1)-in-d small-risk learning. For k=1 and scales 1,2 the Gaussian squared approximation floor exceeds 2/5, so risk 1/4 cannot be attained in dimension-uniform bounded time. For any fixed finite horizon T and positive minimum atom mass, d/dt E a^2<=1/2 implies pointwise bounded output coefficients and O(1/d) aligned-scale drift; the actual nonlinear output remains O(1/d) from its initial exponential span. The degree-k sphere harmonic has a strictly positive limiting Gaussian projection distance from the span at scales 1,...,k+1. For scales 1,2 and target Z the squared distance is 1-(1-4 exp(-2)+4 exp(-3))/(exp(1)-1)>2/5. This is a full-risk obstruction; no claim is made about a single harmonic projection hitting time. No novelty claim or independent certification.

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. By Aizenman's random-current identity the four-point Ursell function is expressed through the probability that the currents from x_1 to x_2 and from x_3 to x_4 share a cluster; non-triviality (nonvanishing renormalised coupling) is equivalent to inf over scales L of P(two independent random-current clusters at scale L intersect) > 0. The 4D case is now trivial (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin 2021); in 3D the heuristic is favourable because the current-cluster dimension (5 - eta)/2 = 2.48 exceeds 3/2, so independent fractals of that dimension would intersect with positive probability. A second-moment argument on the number of intersection points reduces the uniform lower bound to (a) a two-point function lower bound with exponent 2 - eps in d = 3 (Duminil-Copin's Conjecture 5, PIMS lectures) and (b) a variance bound on the intersection count, which involves six-point correlations beyond the Lebowitz inequality. Both inputs are open; (b) is the genuinely new obligation.

[Defin 55 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\op{s}_{\rho}$ be the dilation with scale $\rho > 0$: $\op{s}_{\rho}(x)=\rho x$. Given $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$, its pushforward by $\op{s}_{\rho}$
is the unique probability measure $\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu$  such that

$$\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(x) \, \mathrm{d}\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu( x)  \, =  \, \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(\rho  x) \,  \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, .$$

Note that $\mathrm{supp} \big[ \op{s}_{\rho \#} \mu \big] \,  =  \,  \rho \, \mathrm{supp} [ \mu ]$. For a probability measure $\mu$ and $\tau>0$, we denote by $\mu_\tau$
the probability measure obtained by the convolution

\begin{equation}

\mu_\tau=\frac{1}{2\tau} \mathbbm{1}_{[-\tau;\tau]} \ast \mu\,.

\end{equation}
title: Definition 55 of arXiv:2604.00635

body: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over an algebraically closed field, equivalently a compact Riemann surface, and let D be a divisor on X. Write l(D) for the dimension of the space of meromorphic functions on X whose poles are bounded by D and which have no other poles, and let K be a canonical divisor of X. The Riemann-Roch theorem states l(D) - l(K - D) = deg(D) + 1 - g, where deg(D) is the sum of the coefficients of D. Once deg(D) > 2g - 2 this gives l(D) = deg(D) + 1 - g exactly, since l(K-D) then vanishes. Proved by Riemann and Roch in the 1850s-60s; vastly generalized by Hirzebruch and Grothendieck.
title: Riemann-Roch theorem

[Lemma main_lemma of arXiv:2604.05921, 'Simplicity of random hypergraphs'] Let $\delta_1,\delta_2 \in \mathds{N}$. Given (possibly non-unique) vertices $v_1,v_2,\hdots,v_{\delta_1} \in V$, let the unique vertices be denoted by $v'_1,v'_2,\hdots,v'_{u(\vb*{v})}$, for some $u(\vb*{v}) \in \mathds{N}$. Similarly, let the unique vertices in $w_1,w_2,\hdots,w_{\delta_2}$ be denoted by $w'_1,w'_2,\hdots,w'_{u(\vb*{w})}$. Let $D(\vb*{v})=\frac{\delta_1!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v})!}$ and $D(\vb*{w})=\frac{\delta_2!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} m_{w'_i}(\vb*{w})!}$. Let $\hat{R}(\cdot)$ be as in (equation def:B_hat of the paper) and let $U$ denote a uniformly chosen vertex in $V$. For any functions $f_1^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$, $f_2^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$ and $w \in \mathds{N}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        &\sum_{\vb*{v} \in V^{\delta_1}}  \sum_{\vb*{w} \in (V\backslash\{v_1,\hdots,v_{\delta_1}\})^{\delta_2}} (D(\vb*{v})D(\vb*{w}))^w \prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} f_1^{(m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v}))}(v'_i) \prod_{j=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} f_2^{(m_{w'_j}(\vb*{w}))}(w'_j) \nonumber \\
        &=\sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} ia_i = \delta_1}}  \frac{\delta_1!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_1} k!^{(1+w)a_k}} \sum_{\substack{\vb*{b} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_2} ib_i = \delta_2}}  \frac{\delta_2!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_2} k!^{(1+w)b_k} } \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times \sum_{\gamma(\cdot) \in \hat{R}(\vb*{a},\vb*{b})} (-1)^{\sum{\vb*{g} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}, \vb*{h} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}( \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} g_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} h_j -1) \gamma(\vb*{g},\vb*{h})} \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times  \prod_{\substack{\vb*{y} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}\\ \vb*{z} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E} \big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} (f_1^{(i)}(U))^{y_i} \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} (f_2^{(j)}(U))^{z_j} \big] \big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i! \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j!} \Big)^{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})} \Bigg).
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:class-number-reduction of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $P\nmid N$, with $P$ odd, $N$ squarefree, and $PN>4$.  For $m\geq1$, whenever the arguments are discriminants, one has
\[
h(-P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-P^2N),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-4P^2N),
\]
and
\[
h(-P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-PN),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-4PN).
\]

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2604.00642, 'Quantitative central limit theorem for an integrated periodogram via the fourth moment the'] Let
\[
f_\alpha(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{-\alpha}L(\lambda),
\qquad \lambda\in(-\pi,\pi),\quad \alpha\in\mathcal A,
\]
where $\mathcal A=[a,b]\subset[0,1)$, and assume that the true parameter value $\alpha_0$ belongs to $\mathcal A$. Suppose that $L\in \mathcal C^1([-\pi,\pi]\setminus\{0\})$ is positive on $[-\pi,\pi]$ and slowly varying at $0$.

Define the Whittle contrast by
\[
Q_n(\alpha)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
\left[
\log f_\alpha(\lambda)+\frac{I_n(\lambda)}{f_\alpha(\lambda)}
\right]\dd\lambda,
\qquad \alpha\in\mathcal A.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\alpha_n\in \arg\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal A} Q_n(\alpha)
\]
be any measurable minimizer of $Q_n$ over $\mathcal A$. Then
\[
\widehat\alpha_n \xrightarrow{\mathbb P} \alpha_0,
\]
and
\[
\sqrt n\,(\widehat\alpha_n-\alpha_0)
\;\Rightarrow\;
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{4}{\sigma_0^2}\right),
\]
where
\[
\sigma_0^2
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \bigl(\log|\lambda|\bigr)^2\,\dd\lambda.
\]

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2604.18871, 'Quantitative approximation of the Vlasov(--Fokker--Planck)--Navier--Stokes system by stoch'] Let $(u, F)$ be any bounded weak solution of \eqref{eq:PDE}.
If for some $k\geq 3$ there is $M_k(F^\circ)< +\infty $, then there
exists a constant $C>0$ such that for all $t\in[0,T]$, we have
\begin{align*}
& M_k(F_t)  \\
& \leq \exp\Bigl(C (\|F^\circ\|_{L^\infty_{x,v}} +\sigma +1)\int_0^t \|u_s\|_{L^{k+d}_x} \dd s \Bigr)

Let A be an N-by-n real random matrix whose rows a_i^T are independent, with integers N,n>=2, common uncentered second-moment matrix Sigma=E[a_i a_i^T], and Gamma=E max_i||a_i||_2^2<infinity. Put r=min(N,n). There is an absolute C such that, for delta=C sqrt(Gamma log(r)/N), E||A^T A/N-Sigma||_op<=max(||Sigma||_op^(1/2)delta,delta^2). With an absolute constant C, enlarged if necessary, the same hypotheses give (E||A||_op^2)^(1/2)<=sqrt(N||Sigma||_op)+C sqrt(Gamma log(r)). These are both conclusions of Vershynin1011.3027v7 Theorem5.48 p30. Sigma may be singular; zero row means, identical row laws and independence of coordinates are not assumed. The dimension restriction excludes the literal zero-log singleton endpoint.

independent real rows sharing the uncentered second-moment matrix Sigma

body: [Definition 3.2 (δ-hyperbolic (Gromov, 1987) of arXiv:2606.10238, 'Hyperbolic Neural Population Geometry Benefits Computation'] ). A geodesic metric space (X , d) is δ-hyperbolic if every geodesic triangle in X is δ-thin. Equivalently for all x, y, z, w ∈X , d(x, z) + d(y, w) ≤ (3.1) max {d(x, y) + d(z, w), d(y, z) + d(x, w)} + 2δ, which is called the 4-point condition. In general, low δ means the geodesic metric space is more tree-like, as tree triangles (Chiswell, 2001) are 0-hyperbolic.

[Prop 12 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] Let $(x^{[n]}_{k})_{0\leq k\leq n}$ be a mesh.
Define
\[
\mu_{n}:=F(a)\delta_{a}+\sum^{n}_{k=1}\big(F(x_{k})-F(x_{k-1})\big)\delta_{x_{k}},
\]
and let $q_{n}$ be the quantile function of $\mu_{n}$. Then for
any $p\ge1$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\max_{1\le k\le n}(x_{k}-x_{k-1}).
\]
In particular, for the uniform mesh $x_{k}=a+\frac{b-a}{n}k$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\frac{b-a}{n}.
\]

[Lem 237 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,L,\epsilon,K>0$ and any sequence of $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_N)_{N\ge 1}$,
	\[
		\lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big) 
		= \lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu_{\sym}(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big)
		= 0\,.
	\]

\begin{proof}
	We only prove that the first limit is zero, as the second limit is proved analogously.
	Suppose for contradiction that there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta$ for infinitely many $N$.
	By \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4} from Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound}, there exists $C = C(\alpha,L,K) > 0 $ such that for sufficiently large $N$, $\mu(\cA_{N[K]}) \in \cP_4(\R,C)$.
Then, for infinitely many $N$, we have
	\[\mu(\cA_{N[K]})\in
		S_\delta 
		\equiv \Big\{ \mu \in \cP_4(\R,C) : \bbW_2(\mu, \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta 
		\Big\}\,.
	\]
	By Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq}, the space $\cP_4(\R,C)$ endowed with the $\bbW_2$ metric is compact.
	The set $S_\delta$ is closed with respect to the $\bbW_2$ metric, hence also compact. Therefore
 we may find $\mu \in S_\delta$ and a subsequence $(N_j)_{j\ge 1}$ such that
	\[
		\lim_{j\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big) = 0\,.
	\]
	As noted in Definition~\ref{d:truncated.lip.alg}, we have $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j[K]}) = \mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j})$: thus, since each $\cA_{N_j}$ is an $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithm, so is each $\cA_{N_j[K]}$. It follows by omitting finitely many $j$'s that we have
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_{N_j[K]},\mu)
	=\max\bigg\{
	\bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big),
	\bbW_2\Big(
		\mu^\Ising(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\cP(\{\pm1\})
		\Big)
	\bigg\}\le\epsilon
	\]
for all $j$. Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip} of  $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$, this implies
	\[
		\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\,,
	\]
	which contradicts that $\mu \in S_\delta$.
\end{proof}
title: Lem 237 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Defn of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,T]\rightarrow V$ be a continuous path with bounded
variation. The \textit{signature transform} of $\gamma$ (or simply
the signature) is the formal tensor series defined by 
\[
S(\gamma)\triangleq\big(1,\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{0},\int_{0<s<t<T}d\gamma_{s}\otimes d\gamma_{t},\cdots,\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<T}d\gamma_{t_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes d\gamma_{t_{n}},\cdots\big),
\]
where the path integrals are defined in the Lebesgue-Stieltjes sense.
The tensor series $\log S(\gamma)$ is known as the \textit{logarithmic
signature} of $\gamma$.

Every unbounded open convex set in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains an infinite straight ray starting at each of its points. If such a set is a mirror-complement component, that ray never collides with a mirror and is an escaping launch direction. The assertion needs convexity and does not settle the general all-reflected-rays trapping problem.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Status: proofs written; w346 KEEP pending. Neither result constructs an all-ray trapping mirror configuration.

Lemma 1. Every unbounded open convex set C in R^d contains an unbounded straight ray starting at each x in C. Therefore, if a mirror-complement component is unbounded, open and convex, an origin in it has an unobstructed escaping launch direction and cannot have every reflected ray bounded.

Proof: choose r>0 with B(x,r) contained in C and y_k in C with |y_k-x| tending to infinity. A subsequence of d_k=(y_k-x)/|y_k-x| tends to a unit direction d. For fixed t>=0 and sufficiently large k, convexity gives a ball centered at x+t*d_k with radius (1-t/|y_k-x|)*r contained in C. Eventually this radius exceeds 3r/4 and the center is within r/4 of x+t*d, so B(x+t*d,r/2) is in C. This holds for every fixed t with the same subsequential direction d, proving the entire ray stays inside C. No collision occurs along it.

Lemma 2. C={(x,y): x>0 and |y-x^2|<1} is open, connected and unbounded but contains no unbounded straight ray.

Proof: (x,u)->(x,x^2+u) is a homeomorphism from (0,infinity) times (-1,1), proving the first three properties. For a ray (a+bt,c+dt), t>=0, with nonzero direction: b<0 eventually violates x>0; b=0 and d!=0 eventually violates the strip condition; b>0 makes y-x^2 a quadratic with leading coefficient -b^2, whose magnitude diverges. Thus all possible directions leave C in finite time.

This gives an explicit algebraic version of the previous spiral-corridor obstruction: unbounded connected vacancy alone does not supply a straight ray. The corridor is not represented as a permitted mirror arrangement, and absence of straight rays does not establish trapping of reflected rays. Convexity is a sufficient special-case condition, not a necessary one.

[Definition def:fk_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $U\in C^1_b(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a bounded, continuously
differentiable vector field with bounded derivatives, and $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
The \emph{Feynman-Kac semigroup} associated with $U$ is the family
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t\geq 0}$ on $L^2(\mu)$ defined by
\begin{align}
  \bigl(P_t^{k,J} f\bigr)(x)
  \equiv
  \E^x\left[
    f(X_t)\exp\left(k \int_0^t U(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X_s\right)
  \right],
  
\end{align}
for $f \in L^2(\mu)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $t \geq 0$, where $\circ$ denotes
Stratonovich integration and $U(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X_\tau=\sum_i U_i(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X^i_\tau$.
title: Feynman-Kac semigroup for current observables

there is a non-empty, closed subset $S$ of $G$ of positive Haar

for any constant $C\geq 4$,
\begin{equation} 
\dR(U_S, Y) \leq (C+2)\dR(X, Y) + H_2(1 - 2/C), 
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\log \frac{\mu(S-S)}{\mu(S)} \leq (2C+4)\dR(X, Y) + 2H_2(1 - 2/C).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $\sigma=1+2d\zeta$, where $(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}\zeta(0)=0$ and $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$. In parts~\textup{(i)}, \textup{(ii)}, and~\textup{(iii)(a)--(b)}, assume additionally that
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\zeta(0)|}<\infty$ for some $\theta_0>0$.

\item \underline{\textup{Dimensions one, two, and three.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The rescaled mean converges:

$\mathcal W$ be white noise on $\mathbb{R}^d$, let

\]

\[
    \mathcal U(T,x)\coloneqq
    \sup_{\tau\leq T}\mathbf E_x^{\rm BM}
    \bigl[Z(T,x)-Z(T-\tau,B_\tau)\bigr]\, ,
\]
where the supremum is over stopping times for Brownian motion. Then, for every $T>0$,
\[
    R^{-(2-d/2)}\,u^{(R)}_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}
    \Longrightarrow

\]

$\bigl(u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}-\mathbb{E} u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}(0)\bigr)^{(R)}$ for

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]

[Lemma lem:delta of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Under any coupling between $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, we have
\begin{align}
    \mleft|
        \operatorname{Cov}[X^i(0), X^j(t)]
    \mright|
    &\leqslant
    2 \sqrt{
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) \mright] \cdot
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
    } \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ Y^i(0) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
        + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) Y^j(t) \mright] \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E}\mleft[Y^i(0)\mright] \mathbb{E}\mleft[ X^j(t) - Y^j(t) \mright]
    + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) \mright] \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) - Y^i(0) \mright].
\end{align}
Moreover, both factors appearing under the square root in (equation decom4631 of the paper) are nonnegative.
