body:
[Prop CLEcoupling1 of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Consider a zero boundary GFF $\Phi_D$ on $D$ and the nested CLE$_4$ determined by exploring consecutively two-valued sets $A_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. Then, for all boundary conditions $v \in 2\lambda \mathbb{Z}$, we have the following properties in coupling with $\Phi_D + v$: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item The labels $s_\ell \in \{-2\lambda, 2\lambda\}$ attached to each loop $\ell \in \text{CLE}_4^{n}$ are i.i.d. symmetric conditionally on the loops, 
and in terms of distributions,
$$\sum_{\Gamma \in \text{CLE}^{\rm nest}_4}(v1_{\Gamma \text{ outermost}}+s_\Gamma)
\1_{\operatorname{Int}(\Gamma)} = \Phi_D +v.$$
\item 
We assign the height $v$ to the boundary of the domain. Thereby, each gasket in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ can be uniquely attached a height corresponding to the sum of labels of loops $s_\ell$ in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ strictly surrounding this gasket, including the boundary of the domain. If this sum equals $h$, then we say that the gasket is at height $h$. Equivalently we can attach a height to each loop in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ by considering the sum of labels of loops surrounding and including this loop and the boundary. This way the height of the gasket corresponds to the height of its outermost loop.   
\item In this coupling, conditionally on the loops, for each $z \in D$, the heights $h$ of the gaskets in 
CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ surrounding $z$ form a simple symmetric random walk $S^z(m)$ with step-size $2\lambda$ and starting point $v$. 
\item For $v \neq 0$, consider $A_0$, the first passage set of $\Phi_D + v$ with boundary values $0$. Then $A_0$ is almost surely equal to taking the connected component of the boundary of the closed union of all gaskets of non-zero height. In particular, for each $z \in D \cap \mathbb{Q}^2$, the boundary of the connected component of 
$D \setminus A_0$ containing $z$ is constructed as follows: we consider the nested loop sequence surrounding $z$ until the first time that a loop of height $0$ appears and that is the boundary. 
\item Further, the sign excursion sets of $\Phi_D + v$ have the following description using nested CLE$_4$: we consider the closed union of all the gaskets in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ of height different than zero. The connected components have then the law of sign excursion sets.
\item Finally, the dual of the excursion sets, i.e. the complement of the excursion sets in $D$, is given by the disjoint union of all the gaskets of height $0$ in the nested CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop CLEcoupling1 of arXiv:2604.15146

[Theorem 5 (Chebotarev density theorem) of arXiv:2609.02444, 'The Hasse norm principle for $A_4$-quartic extensions of global function fields'] Let \(G\) be a finite group, \(\phi \colon X \to Y\) a \(G\)-torsor defined over \(\FF_q\), and \(\Phi \subset G\) a conjugacy class.
  \begin{enumerate}
      \item  Suppose that \(X\) is geometrically connected.
  Then
  \[ \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{|\{y \in Y(\FF_{q^m}) \mid \varphi(y) = \Phi\}|}{|Y(\FF_{q^m})|} = \frac{|\Phi|}{|G|}. \]
  \item More generally, suppose that \(Y\) is geometrically connected and \(X\) has \(r\) geometric components, all defined over \(\FF_q\).
  Then
  \[ \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{|\{y \in Y(\FF_{q^{m}}) \mid \varphi(y) = \Phi\}|}{|Y(\FF_{q^{m}})|} \leq r\frac{|\Phi|}{|G|}, \]
  with equality if and only if $\Phi$ is contained in the stabiliser of a geometric component of $X$.
  \end{enumerate}

body: Let f be a continuous complex-valued function on an open connected subset U of C. If for every closed triangular path T whose closed solid triangle lies inside U, the contour integral of f around the boundary of T equals zero, then f is holomorphic on U. Morera's theorem is essentially the converse of the Cauchy-Goursat theorem, and it is commonly used to prove that a function built as a locally uniform limit, series, or integral of holomorphic functions is itself holomorphic.
title: Morera's theorem

Let U be an open subset of R^D and L be C^3 on a neighborhood of the gradient-flow trajectories in question. For every x in U suppose the solution phi_t(x) of d phi_t/dt=-grad L(phi_t), phi_0=x, exists for all t>=0 and converges to Phi(x). Assume the resulting endpoint map Phi:U->R^D is C^2. Then for every x in U, D Phi(x) grad L(x)=0 and D^2 Phi(x)[grad L(x),grad L(x)]=-D Phi(x) Hess L(x) grad L(x). Here the second derivative of the vector-valued map is a bilinear map. The identities hold on the domain of the endpoint map, not merely at its limiting minima. They assert annihilation of grad L; they do not assert annihilation of every individual noise direction in a multi-output loss. Source: Li, Wang and Arora, What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? -- A Mathematical Framework, Lemma C.2, PDF p29.

[Lem 64 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have
$\sM^{\si}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sii}(\alpha,q_0)$.

\begin{proof} We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} for this proof:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\FAIRdefn\\
	\TMPONEdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
We see that the $\si$ and $\sii$ classes differ only in the condition on the Ising initialization $Y(q_*)\sim\zeta^\Ising$: the $\si$ class satisfies the condition~\ref{it:7.1} (i.e., $\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP_2(\R)$), while the $\sii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:7.2} (i.e., $\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP([-1,1])$).

Therefore, let us suppose we have controls $(q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the $(\alpha,q_0,L,\epsilon)$-$\si$ conditions, which drive processes $X,Y$ as in \eqref{e:formal.sde.main}, \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising}. We will construct controls $(\tilde q_*,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde w,\tilde p,\tilde \zeta,\tilde \zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the $(\alpha,q_0,L,\tilde{\epsilon})$-$\sii$ conditions, for some $\tilde{\epsilon}$ that will tend to zero as $\epsilon\to0$. The latter controls will drive processes $\tilde X, \tilde Y$ that will approximate $X,Y$.

Let $(\tilde q_*,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde p,\tilde \zeta) = (q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)$.
    We then take 
    \[\tilde\zeta^{\Ising}
    =f_\# \zeta^{\Ising},\quad
        f(x) = \begin{cases}
            1 - \epsilon/x
            & 
            \textup{for $x \in (1,+\infty)$,} \\
            (1-\epsilon) x &
            \textup{for $[-1,1]$,} \\
            -1 + \epsilon/x &
            \textup{for $x \in (-\infty,1)$.}
        \end{cases}
    \]
Thus $\tilde\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP([-1,1])$, so it satisfies condition~\ref{it:7.2}. We couple the initializations $Y(q_*)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ and 
	\[
	\tilde{Y}(q_*)
	=f(Y(q_*))
	\sim \tilde{\zeta}^\Ising\,.
	\]
Note that for $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, the function $f$ is an invertible mapping from $\bbR$ to $(-1,1)$.
    Recall from the definition \eqref{e:filt.X.Y} of $\cF_Y$ that we can write
    \[
        w_t = w_t\Big((W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},U',Y(q_*)\Big)\,,
    \]
where the $w_t$ on the right-hand side is a measurable function. We then define $\tilde w$ by setting
    \[
        \tilde w_t\Big((W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},U',\tilde Y(q_*)\Big)
        = w_t\Big(
        (W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},
        U',
        f^{-1}(\tilde Y(q_*))
        = Y(q_*) 
        \Big)\,.
    \]
Therefore $w=\tilde{w}$ as processes.
We let $\tilde X, \tilde Y$ be defined by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main} and \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} with $(\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde w)$ in place of $(b,\sigma,w)$; and we couple them to
$X,Y$ by taking the initializations $\tilde X(q_*) = X(q_*)$ and $\tilde Y(q_*) = f(Y(q_*))$, as well as the same

body: The axiom of choice (AC) states: for every family {A_i : i in I} of nonempty sets, indexed by any set I, there exists a choice function c defined on I with c(i) in A_i for every i. Equivalently: every Cartesian product of nonempty sets is nonempty; every surjection has a right inverse; every set of nonempty pairwise disjoint sets has a transversal selecting one element from each. Over the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms ZF, the axiom of choice is equivalent to Zorn's lemma and to the well-ordering theorem, and also to Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary compact spaces. AC is independent of ZF: Godel (1938) showed ZF plus AC is consistent if ZF is (constructible universe), and Cohen (1963) showed ZF plus the negation of AC is consistent if ZF is (forcing). Countable and finite choices do not follow from ZF alone in general, but AC is provable in ZF for finite index sets I by induction.

[Theorem Thm-long-time-Appendix of arXiv:2605.16963, 'Stochastic Euler Equations with Pseudo-differential Noise: Continuous and Discontinuous Pe'] Let the conditions of Theorem (Thm-local-Appendix of the paper) hold. Let  
		$\frac{d}{2}+p<\theta<s-\max \{3(\alpha\lor \beta\lor \varsigma),\ell\mathbf{1}_{\{\epsilon>0\}},1\}$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label={\bf{(\arabic*)}},leftmargin=0.79cm]\setlength\itemsep{0.2em}
			\item  Under (Hypo-DNI-1 F-h of the paper), the system (equation SPDE-general of the paper) with initial data $u(0)=u_0$ admits a global $H^s$ solution satisfying
			\begin{equation*}
				\mathbb{E} \left[V(\|u(t)\|_{H^s}^2)\Big|\mathcal{F}_0\right]  
				\leq \Big(V(\|u_0\|^2_{H^s})+\mathscr{G}_2t\Big) {\rm e}^{\mathscr{G}_1t},
				\quad t>0.
			\end{equation*}
			Moreover, the solution map $H^{s,\theta}\ni u_0\mapsto u(t)\in H^{s,\theta}$ is continuous, where $H^{s,\theta}$ denotes the space $H^s$ equipped with the $H^{\theta}$-topology.
			
			\item   If (Hypo-DNI-1 F-h of the paper) is strengthened to (Hypo-DNI-2 F-h of the paper), then $u$ satisfies 
			\begin{equation*} 
				\mathbb{E}\left[V(\|u(t)\|_{H^s}^2) \Big| \mathcal{F}_0\right]  
				\leq V(\|u_0\|^2_{H^s}), \qquad t\ge0.
			\end{equation*}
			Moreover, the problem (equation SPDE-general of the paper) on $\mathbb T^d$ admits an invariant measure $\mu$ in the sense of Definition (IM definition of the paper) with $E=H^s$. 
			
			\item  If (Hypo-DNI-3 F-h of the paper) holds, then  
			\begin{equation*} 
				\int_0^t\mathbb{E}  \left[V\left(\frac{\|u(t')\|^2_{W^{p,\infty}}}{M^2}\right)\Bigg|\mathcal{F}_0\right]{\,\rm{d}} t'
				\leq  \frac{V(\| u_0\|^2_{H^\theta})}{\mathscr{G}_3}\left(1-{\rm e}^{-\mathscr{G}_3t}\right),
				\quad t>0.
			\end{equation*}
			As a result, the Dirac measure centered at $0$ is the \textbf{unique invariant probability measure} on both $\mathbb T^d$ and $\mathbb R^d$ when $h(0)=0$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X be a square-integrable function of independent coordinates and let X^L denote X with the coordinates in a block L replaced by an independent copy. Then (X, X^L) is an exchangeable pair, and E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 Var(X) - 2 Cov(X, X^L). Consequently E[(X - X^L)^2] <= 4 Var(X) always, and E[(X - X^L)^2] <= 2 Var(X) whenever Cov(X, X^L) >= 0. The identity requires no independence beyond that of the resampled block and no structure on X beyond square-integrability.

In the width-one strip of the exact-variance lemma, perturb all Gaussian vertex weights by g^s=e^(-s)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2s))g' with independent copy g'. The number B_r(s) of diamonds where the maximizing choice differs has Binomial(r,q(s)) law, q(s)=arccos(e^(-s))/pi. The probability of identical maximizing paths is (1-q(s))^r, and their expected shared-vertex fraction is 1-rq(s)/(2r+1). For s=r^(-alpha) with fixed 0<alpha<2, the path-equality probability tends to zero, shared fraction tends to one, and Var(M_r) remains linear in r. This refutes only the unqualified path-change auxiliary bridge.

Let n,d>=1 and T>=2 be integers, and m>=1 an integer factor width. Fix tokens x_it in R^d, queries z_i in R^d, labels Y_i in {-1,+1}, and a linear head v in R^d. Select opt_i in argmax_t Y_i v^T x_it. Let C be the set of real d-by-d matrices satisfying (x_i,opt_i-x_it)^T W z_i>=1 for all i and t!=opt_i. Consider (Att-SVM), minimizing ||W||_F over C, and (Att-SVM-star), minimizing ||W||_* over C subject to rank(W)<=m. The nuclear norm ||W||_* is the sum of singular values. For each problem separately assume its feasible set is nonempty. Every global optimizer W of either problem has row(W) contained in S=span{z_1,...,z_n}. Consequently rank(W)<=dim(S)<=min(n,d), with the additional rank cap m in the nuclear problem. No uniqueness is asserted for nuclear-norm optimizers. The conclusion concerns global solutions of these margin problems, not arbitrary KKT points or gradient-descent limits.
finite real dataset and fixed linear head; opt_i chosen by token scores
nonempty feasible set for the particular stated optimization problem
global optimum, not merely a stationary point; nuclear problem retains rank cap m

[Theorem 1 (EPI on compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Assume that $G$ has no open subgroups except $G$ itself and possibly $\{0\}$. Let $X,Y$ be independent random variables on $G$ with finite entropies. Then
$$h(X+Y)-\frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y) \geq 0.$$
Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(i)$]
If $G$ is connected, then there is equality if and only 
if $X$ and $Y$ are both uniform on $G$.
\item[$(ii)$]
If $G$ is finite, then there is equality if and only if 
either both $X$ and $Y$ are uniform on the whole group $G$ 
or both $X$ and $Y$ are deterministic.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: EPI on compact groups

Let Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n (the centred cube of volume 1), n >= 2. For every unit vector a in R^n, 1 <= vol_{n-1}(Q_n \cap a^perp) <= sqrt(2). The upper bound is attained exactly when a = (+-e_i +- e_j)/sqrt(2) (for example the hyperplane orthogonal to (1,1,0,...,0)); the lower bound 1 (Hadwiger, Hensley; Ball gives a simpler proof) exactly when a = +-e_j. Probabilistic form: if U_1,...,U_n are independent and uniform on [-1/2,1/2] and a_1^2 + ... + a_n^2 = 1, the density of a_1U_1 + ... + a_nU_n is largest at 0, where it equals vol_{n-1}(Q_n \cap a^perp); so this density is at most sqrt(2), with equality for (U_1 + U_2)/sqrt(2).

Assumes: central sections (hyperplanes through the centre of the cube); cube normalised to volume 1: Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n; the density statement is for independent uniform inputs

theorem for \(\varphi(t)=t^2\) cannot additionally assert \(L^2\) convergence
or convergence of the prelimit variance to the finite Wigner-profile
covariance.

body: Coarea bound for a definite rank-two core. If (Y_1, Y_2) has density rho on R^2 and lambda_1, lambda_2 > 0, then S = lambda_1 Y_1^2 + lambda_2 Y_2^2 has density p_S(s) = (2 sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2))^{-1} int_0^{2 pi} rho(sqrt(s/lambda_1) cos th, sqrt(s/lambda_2) sin th) d th <= pi ||rho||_inf/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2) (substitute u = sqrt(lambda_1) y_1, v = sqrt(lambda_2) y_2 and use polar coordinates; in two dimensions the length of the level curve and the gradient cancel, which is why ||rho||_inf suffices, and in three dimensions this fails). For an orthonormal two-dimensional projection of independent coordinates with densities <= 1, ||rho||_inf <= 2 (Livshyts-Paouris-Pivovarov), attained by ((X_1 + X_2)/sqrt2, (X_3 + X_4)/sqrt2) with uniform laws on unit intervals, so a definite rank-two core has density <= 2 pi/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2). Passing from the core to the full form Q = core + R, with R depending on the same coordinates, is where the conjecture is hard.

Claim GO (proved special-case obstruction by w447; awaiting review).

Fix 0<kappa<1/4. On Z^2 consider the homogeneous kernel

p(+e_1)=1/4+delta, p(-e_1)=1/4-delta,
p(+e_2)=p(-e_2)=1/4,

where 0<delta<=1/4-kappa. Its environment law is a Dirac mass at that row at each site, hence is spatially iid and kappa-uniformly elliptic. Its increments are iid. The strong law gives X_n/n -> (2delta,0), so it is directionally transient and ballistic in e_1. Nevertheless

sup_{0<delta<=1/4-kappa} E_0[sum_{n>=0} 1_{X_n=0}] = infinity,

while first exit from the singleton {0} takes exactly one step for every delta. Thus no law-independent upper bound for total occupation can follow from kappa, dimension, directional transience and the singleton residence bound alone. Every individual law in this example has finite Green function: it is not a counterexample to C0041 or to finiteness under a fixed iid law.

Proof of the divergence with explicit constants. At delta=0 the transformed coordinates Y=X^(1)+X^(2), Z=X^(1)-X^(2) are independent simple symmetric walks. Consequently

P_0(X_{2n}=0) = [binom(2n,n)/4^n]^2 >= 1/(4n), n>=1.

The elementary central-binomial lower bound binom(2n,n)>=4^n/(2sqrt(n)) follows by induction from n=1, since

binom(2n+2,n+1)/binom(2n,n)=4(1-1/(2n+2))
and (1-1/(2n+2))^2 >= n/(n+1).

Every path of length 2n under p_delta has probability at least (1-4delta)^(2n) times its p_0 probability. If delta<=1/(16N) and n<=N, Bernoulli's inequality gives (1-4delta)^(2n)>=1-8delta n>=1/2. Therefore its Green function is at least

1 + (1/8) sum_{n=1}^N 1/n.

Choose delta_N=min((1/4-kappa)/2,1/(16N)); these are positive, preserve the same ellipticity lower bound, and give the divergent harmonic lower bound.

Proof of finiteness for fixed delta. For theta=(1/2)log((1/4+delta)/(1/4-delta))>0,

P_delta(X_n=0) <= E_delta exp(-theta X_n^(1))
 = [1/2+2sqrt(1/16-delta^2)]^n.

The base is strictly below one, so the Green series is finite. The obstruction is to a uniform or purely local inference, not to each law separately.

Let (X,d) be a compact metric space of diameter at most one, with covering numbers N(X,epsilon)<=epsilon^(-d_x) for 0<epsilon<=1, where d_x>0. Let P be a Borel probability measure, and W:X x X->[0,cmax] a measurable symmetric kernel with 0<cmin<=d_P(x)=integral W(x,y)dP(y) and cmax<=1. Assume there is ONE partition X=X_1 union ... union X_q into q>=1 measurable pieces such that |W(x,y)-W(xprime,y)|<=cLip d(x,xprime) for every y and every x,xprime in the same piece. Let x_1,...,x_n be independent samples from P, and fix 0<rho<=1/2. For any fixed bounded Borel f:X->R, define T_X f(x)=n^(-1)sum_i W(x,x_i)f(x_i) and T_P f(x)=integral W(x,y)f(y)dP(y). There is a universal C such that, with probability at least 1-rho, sup_x |T_X f(x)-T_P f(x)| <= C ||f||_sup [cLip sqrt(d_x)+(cmax+cLip)sqrt(log(q/rho))]/sqrt(n). The card uses a common partition explicitly; it does not assert this bound merely from separate, y-dependent partitions. The confidence range rho<=1/2 is retained to absorb the standard two-sided tail constants.

Method: Explicit model calculation or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: Linear Debye screening gives the formal structure factor S(k)=|k|^2/(|k|^2+m^2), with m^2 proportional to beta times the background density. Its truncated-correlation Fourier transform is proportional to -m^2/(|k|^2+m^2). In two dimensions the inverse transform is a multiple of the modified Bessel function K0(m*r), whose large-distance behavior is proportional to exp(-m*r)/sqrt(m*r). Check: The resolvent of -Delta+m^2 has Fourier multiplier1/(|k|^2+m^2); its heat-kernel integral yields the positive radial K0 kernel. Thus screening formally creates an exponential length m^-1 rather than a Riesz power tail. Obstruction: The linear-response closure is not proved for the interacting Gibbs law. A rigorous result needs a uniform control of nonlinear correlations and error terms at distances beyond the screening length. The calculation identifies a mechanism, not a clustering theorem.

body: In combinatorial mathematics and extremal set theory, the Sauer–Shelah lemma states that every family of sets with small VC dimension consists of a small number of sets. Here, the VC dimension is the largest size $k$ of a set with the property that all of its subsets can be formed by intersecting it with a member of the family. If the family has $n$ elements in its union, then the Sauer–Shelah lemma states that its number of sets is at most proportional to $n^{k}$.

[Lemma lem:singleton-order-sum of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathsf M_j$ be any typed passive copy of the coordinate pure-Weyl
multiplier in (lem:singleton-renewal of the paper), with arbitrary passive
Hilbert-space amplification.  Put
\[
 \mathsf V_j=\mathsf Q\mathsf M_j\mathsf Q,
 \qquad A_j=\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr T,
 \qquad \mathfrak H_a=\mathscr G\mathcal K^a\mathscr G^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M_j\mathscr T
 =\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr E^*=0,
 \qquad
 \mathscr G^*\mathsf V_j\mathscr G
 =-\mathcal KA_j-A_j^*\mathcal K.
\tag{3.2.10q$_1$}
\]
There is a numerical $C$ such that
\[
 \sum_{a,b\ge0}
 \|\mathfrak H_a\mathsf V_j\mathfrak H_b\|
 \le C\frac{\log(n+2)}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_2$}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $L<\infty$ there is $A_L<\infty$ such
that a passive-singleton component with $2\le s\le L\log n$ labelled
vertices satisfies, after summing every strict chronological order and
every allowed finite-gap simplex,
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\in S_s}
 \|\mathcal X_{s,\sigma}\|
 \le \frac{A_L^s}{N}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_3$}
\]
After the proved circuit-anchored root/pass rewrite, its one free
translation, and a fixed terminal ribbon gluing, its scalar contribution is at most
$A_L^s(m/N)\mathfrak a_\Gamma$, where
$\mathfrak a_\Gamma$ is the positive projective majorant of the already
normalized non-temporal atom.
The same conclusion holds for several Haar-separated passive-singleton
components after their labelled vertex sets have been fixed, with one
factor $m/N$ per component and no interleaving multinomial.  This last
sentence does not sum over varying component-label decompositions; the
physical maximal passive-only components are instead annihilated exactly

body: Publication record. In the critical beta-splitting random tree a clade of m leaves splits into clades of i and m - i leaves with probability proportional to 1/(i(m - i)); the drawn length of a binary tree is the total length of the vertical lines of its cladogram, each vertex drawn at the level of its height. Open Problem 14 of D. J. Aldous and S. Janson, The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, asks for a proof that the expected drawn length L_n grows roughly like n log^4 n. Y. Shmalo, The drawn length of the critical beta-splitting tree grows linearly (2026) shows instead that L_n/n converges to a finite constant lambda with 4.800 < lambda < 5.372 (lambda ≈ 4.88 numerically). Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-drawn-length (commit 536da55fafcf). Not refereed; an independent read is owed.
title: Aldous-Janson Open Problem 14 (critical beta-splitting tree) answered: the expected drawn length grows linearly, L_n/n -> lambda with 4.800 < lambda < 5.372, not like n log^4 n (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/beta-splitting-drawn-length)

Owner-own-work auxiliary proof draft (unaudited); no novelty priority claimed. Fix any oracle O. Let P_L be given by a uniform polynomial-time O-relative evaluator of nonnegative rational weights with polynomial numerator/denominator bit bounds and positive normalizer. Suppose a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR proposal R_L has polynomial next-bit precision and P_L(x)<=D(L)R_L(x) pointwise, for an integer-valued polynomial D>=1. For every fixed positive integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR Q_L with KL(P_L||Q_L)<L^(-c). Conditional importance sampling with K=(1024 D L^(2c+2))^2 samples per position, globally shared random tapes, and one dyadic normalizer-scale exponent suffices; smoothing and output rounding bound KL by (47/120)L^(-c). Exact normalization, a sampler for P and distributional inversion are not assumed. The domination premise itself also yields nonuniform inverse-polynomial-TV sampling by bounded rejection. No common oracle with NP circuit hardness and domination proposals for all efficiently weighted laws has been constructed. This does not settle Target 2 or assert that the premise follows from IR2.
Uniform polynomial-time O-relative rational weight evaluator; known polynomial numerator/denominator bit bound; Z_L>0

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7f/7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c09df2b09707d05f05fb2f6dbb0380264179e71202c00d2d2f47ca7cd469954d","bundle_entry_key":"importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","bundle_id":"population.t410-importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"autoregressive distributions; importance sampling; oracle computational complexity; forward KL; nonuniform circuits","draft":"w739/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Polynomial domination by an AR proposal suffices for forward-KL approximation

T410-w739-C012 v1. Kind: auxiliary sufficient-condition lemma. Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). Owner-own-work draft; no novelty priority claimed.
This is an alternative sufficient condition, not a construction of the target oracle.

## Statement and unpaid obligation

Fix an oracle O. For each integer L>=1 let P_L(x)=w_L(x)/Z_L on
{0,1}^L. The nonnegative rational weights w_L are uniformly polynomial-time
computable relative to O, not all zero, and their numerator and positive
denominator have bit lengths at most a known polynomial b(L).

Assume a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive proposal R_L:
its next-bit probabilities are exactly evaluable dyadics with common
precision B(L), a polynomial. Assume further that

    P_L(x) <= D(L) R_L(x) for every x,                         (1)

where D>=1 is an integer-valued polynomial. Then for each fixed positive
integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive Q_L
whose next-bit probabilities are dyadic and

    KL(P_L || Q_L) <= (47/120) L^(-c) < L^(-c).              (2)

Natural logarithms are used. All circuits use the same oracle O. Their
size exponent may depend on c and on the polynomial bounds. The uniform
weight evaluator is a single algorithm; the proposal and resulting Q may
have length-dependent advice. For any fixed positive real requested
exponent one can instead use its integer ceiling.

The hardest unpaid step for Target 2 is to construct ONE oracle with
NP^O not contained in P^O/poly and, for EVERY efficient-weight law, a
proposal satisfying (1). This proof supplies no such oracle or universal
proposal. It does not derive (1) from the reported IR2 result, assert
equivalence with C003's sampler/inverter criterion, or settle Target 2.

## 1. Only a short scale advice is needed

The weight representation implies 2^(-b)<=Z_L<=2^(b+L). Choose the
integer a=ceil(log_2 Z_L) as nonuniform advice and set A=2^a. Then

    Z_L <= A <= 2 Z_L,       z:=Z_L/A belongs to [1/2,1].

The signed exponent a uses O(log(b+L+1)) bits; the rational A itself has
polynomial representation length. We do NOT assume the exact rational Z
has polynomial bit length: arbitrary rational weight denominators need
not share a small common denominator.

For R(x)>0 put h(x)=w(x)/(A R(x)); set h=0 when R(x)=0. Domination
ensures P(x)=w(x)=0 on the latter set. Consequently

    0 <= h(x) <= D,          E_R h = z.

Computing h takes polynomial-size exact rational arithmetic: R(x) is a
product of L polynomial-bit dyadics, and w,A have polynomial bit length.
Hereafter L subscripts are omitted.

## 2. Conditional importance estimates and change of measure

For a prefix s of length i<L with R(s)>0, define

    a_s=E_R[h(X)|s],    b_s=E_R[h(X) 1{X_(i+1)=1}|s].

Then P(s)=R(s)a_s/z. When P(s)>0 the true next-bit probability is
p_s=b_s/a_s. Draw K independent suffix samples from R(.|s). This is an
exact ancestral sampler: each next-bit dyadic of precision B uses B fair
bits, so at most LB random bits per sample. Let ahat_s,bhat_s be the
sample means of h and h times the next-bit indicator. Define

    g_s=bhat_s/ahat_s if ahat_s>0; otherwise g_s=1/2.

We always have 0<=g_s<=1 and ahat_s*g_s=bhat_s, including the zero
denominator case because nonnegative h forces bhat_s=0 there. Thus

    a_s |g_s-p_s| <= |a_s-ahat_s|+|b_s-bhat_s|.             (3)

This follows by writing a_s*g_s-b_s as
(a_s-ahat_s)*g_s+(bhat_s-b_s). Each sample variable lies in [0,D], so
variance of each mean is at most D^2/K. By Cauchy-Schwarz its mean
absolute error is at most D/sqrt(K). Multiply (3) by R(s)/z and sum over
prefixes with P(s)>0. Since their R masses sum to at most one and z>=1/2,

    sum_s P(s) E |g_s-p_s| <= 4D/sqrt(K)                   (4)

at every position. Prefixes of zero P mass contribute zero. At an
R-null prefix output 1/2 directly; it is P-null by (1).

No sample from P, normalizer computation, or distributional inversion
was used. In particular we did not require an accuracy guarantee at
each one of exponentially many prefixes.

## 3. One polynomial table of shared tapes

At each position select K independent tapes of length LB. Use these
SAME tapes to evaluate the conditional sampler at every prefix of that
length. For each FIXED prefix its K samples have exactly the independent
law used above. Evaluations at different prefixes may be correlated;
only linearity of expectation over prefixes is used in (4).

There are L*K*L*B advice bits, not a tape table indexed by all prefixes.
For any fixed advice table, evaluation runs K ancestral samplers and
computes their exact rational sample means. Adding K polynomial-bit
rationals can increase bit length by at most a polynomial factor K;
division and the other arithmetic therefore have polynomial circuits.
This remains true when the proposal itself has nonuniform advice.

## 4. Smoothing, KL, and explicit sample count

Write eta=L^(-c), epsilon=eta/(16L), and choose the perfect square

    K = (1024 D L^(2c+2))^2.

This is polynomial for fixed c. Let q_s=epsilon+(1-2epsilon)g_s at
R-positive prefixes, so q_s is in [epsilon,1-epsilon]. Also

    |p_s-q_s| <= |p_s-g_s|+epsilon,
    (p_s-q_s)^2 <= 2|p_s-g_s|+2epsilon^2.

For Bernoulli parameters p in [0,1], q in (0,1), the inequality
log t<=t-1, applied to each nonzero P term, gives

    kl(p||q) <= (p-q)^2/[q(1-q)].                          (5)

The same formula holds at p=0,1 by the zero-mass convention. Chain rule
for forward KL, (4), and (5) yield

    E KL(P||Q) <= [8DL/sqrt(K)+2L epsilon^2]
                         /[epsilon(1-epsilon)].          (6)

Here sqrt(K)=64DL/(eta epsilon). Each of the two terms in (6) equals
eta/[8(1-epsilon)]. Since epsilon<=1/16, their sum is at most
(4/15)eta. This calculation averages over a finite, polynomial-length
random table, not over independent conditional errors along a P path.

## 5. Polynomial-bit dyadic outputs

Choose an integer t with Delta=2^(-t)<=eta epsilon/(16L), for example
t=ceil(log_2(256 L^(2c+2))). Replace q_s by

    qhat_s = floor(2^t q_s)/2^t.

Then |qhat_s-q_s|<=Delta and qhat_s>=epsilon/2, while both complementary
probabilities are at least epsilon/2. The derivative of log on this
range is at most 2/epsilon. For every fixed random table, each next-bit
log probability changes in absolute value by at most 2Delta/epsilon.
The chain rule therefore gives

    KL(P||Qhat) <= KL(P||Q)+2L Delta/epsilon
                <= KL(P||Q)+eta/8.

Use qhat=1/2 at R-null prefixes. Averaging shows

    E KL(P||Qhat) <= (4/15+1/8)eta = (47/120)eta.

Some single finite table has loss at most this average. Fix it as advice.
The resulting Qhat is a normalized AR law with polynomial-size oracle
circuits and t-bit dyadic next probabilities. This proves (2).

## Scope and validation

The proposal premise already implies NONUNIFORM approximate sampling of
P, although the proof above does not invoke such a sampler. Indeed draw
X from R and accept it with probability h(X)/D, using a fresh uniform
number in [0,1]. The acceptance probability is z/D>=1/(2D), and the
accepted law is exactly P. Rational acceptance probabilities can instead
be rounded DOWN to dyadics of mesh delta. The acceptance probability
decreases by at most delta and the accepted law changes in total
variation by at most 2D delta, provided delta<=1/(4D): if v(x) is the
unnormalized accepted mass and v'(x)<=v(x), their missing total mass e
is at most delta, and TV(v/alpha,v'/(alpha-e))<=e/alpha<=2D delta.
The rounded success probability is at least 1/(4D). Truncating after
T independent proposals adds at most (1-1/(4D))^T to the TV error.
For a requested inverse-polynomial error rho, choose dyadic
delta<=rho/(4D) and T>=4D ln(2/rho). Thus a strict polynomial-time
NONUNIFORM dyadic sampler with TV error at most rho follows. Its
normalizer-scale advice and the proposal advice need not be uniform.
This implication is an explicit limitation of the sufficient condition,
not a contradiction to it or a uniform sampling theorem for the oracle.

This proof is a sufficient-condition derivation, not a novelty claim or
an independently checked proof. Finite rational diagnostics check (3),
the prefix change-of-measure identity, and the constants, with an omitted-
denominator negative control. They do not prove the asymptotic theorem
by enumeration. No enormous K sample run is proposed or performed.
The condition (1) must be established before applying this to any
particular oracle or weight family. Target 1 C001 v2 remains subject to
independent review; Target 2 remains OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:cd6159c155b54a445d85ded8bfe2169b8fbff887b41d8a66fa0cb61f5b912613","revision_digest":"sha256:f19892a156489aea3c44cdeab77ef7112d4b9e56b7b483fe2d21b6bdf47d45f1","source_id":"owner-own-work:T410-w739-C012-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T22:53:13.841333+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

For each epsilon in (0,1), delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon) is the largest delta in (0,1] such that the following implication holds for every finite forest G, independent Bernoulli edge probabilities in [0,1], vertices o,b and nonempty relay set A: if P(o connects to A)>1-delta and P(a connects to b)>1-delta for all a in A, then P(o connects to b)>1-epsilon. A two-edge path rules out every larger delta, so delta_star is also a necessary upper bound on any proposed all-finite-graph modulus. Its sufficiency for arbitrary cyclic graphs is not asserted.

Let G be a countable simple graph with uniformly bounded degree. In independent Bernoulli bond percolation at p in [0,1], tau_p(x,y)=P_p(x is connected to y by a finite open path), allowing the path of length zero. T_p has matrix tau_p and initially acts on finitely supported functions on V. Boundedness means extension to a bounded operator on l2(V) with counting measure. Let p_2->2=sup{p:T_p is bounded}; for infinite connected vertex-transitive G, pc=inf{p:P_p(|C(o)|=infinity)>0} and pu=inf{p:P_p(exactly one infinite cluster)=1}.

body:
Let Z be a random finite measure on D with total mass T>0 almost surely and 0<E[T]<infinity. Put U_A=Z(A)/T. Then E[Z(A)]/E[T]-E[U_A]=Cov(T,U_A)/E[T] for each measurable A. Consequently mean normalized measure equals normalized mean measure exactly when Cov(T,U_A)=0 for every A. Independence of total mass and normalized measure is sufficient but unnecessary: three equally likely outcomes T=(1,2,3), U_first=(1,0,1) on two sites give both averages (2/3,1/3), yet T and the normalized measure are dependent. No integrability or independence claim for DGFF extremal mass is inferred from this finite example.
Positive total mass
Finite positive mean total mass
0<=U_A<=1

[Lemma 25 (Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] There are constants
\[
        K_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,\qquad \Lambda_*<\infty,
        \qquad \beta_{\mathrm{reg}}>0,\qquad C_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,
\]
depending only on \(K,N,\sigma\), with the following property.  For every
\(0<\beta_*\leq\beta_{\mathrm{reg}}\), there is a constant
\(\eta_{\mathrm{st}}>0\), depending only on \(K,N,\sigma,\beta_*\), such that the following holds.
Let \(p(\tau)\) be any parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block, for
some \(\delta_0\geq c_0\), under the standing fixed-threshold application.
Fix the torus structure used during this
stage and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Put
\[
        b:=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))}.
\]
Assume that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian,
\(\BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds, and \(b<\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).  These are
exactly the analytic start conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with
\(\Lambda=\Lambda_*\) and \(\eta=\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r(\tau)\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow
\(q(\tau)\) relative to it exist on \([1,100]\), and
\begin{align}
        |\sec_{r(\tau)}|&\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}/\tau,
                &&1\leq\tau\leq100,                               \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &<\beta_*,                                         \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.                                 
\end{align}
If
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian, \(\BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds,
\(|\sec_{r^+(1)}|\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}\), and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\|q^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
 +\|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}\\
 &\qquad\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
        \|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
        \leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart

body:
Abel's theorem (the Abelian direction): if the series sum a_n converges to s, then the power series f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1 and f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below. The converse is false in general: f(x) = sum (-1)^n x^n = 1/(1 + x) tends to 1/2 while sum (-1)^n diverges. Tauber's theorem (the Tauberian direction): if f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1, f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below, and n a_n -> 0, then sum a_n converges to s. Littlewood strengthened the condition to a_n = O(1/n) (Littlewood's Tauberian theorem, 1911), and Hardy and Littlewood showed that a one-sided bound n a_n >= -C also suffices. 'Abelian' theorems pass from a summability method's convergence to a weaker one; 'Tauberian' theorems go back under an extra growth condition on the terms.
Abel: sum a_n converges
Tauber: f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below and n a_n -> 0 (Littlewood: a_n = O(1/n) suffices, with a harder proof)

On the benchmark corpora the two orderings part on pkanrtm (24,000 calibration rows, a near-zero-target tail): the squared-loss criterion picks the simplex, the worst vertex, on every cell. The same criterion written in the score's own metric, R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), repairs it. Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, q>=2 an integer, K>=0, u the uniform independent q-color law, and gamma_K the free ferromagnetic Potts law proportional to exp(K times the number of agreeing edges). Then D(u||gamma_K)>=|E|[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]. Equality holds on forests; for K>0 and a graph with a cycle it is strict. Thus on growing Z^d boxes at any fixed K>0, liminf D(u||gamma_K)/|V|>=d[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]>0. This is a product-law obstruction and does not establish critical discontinuity.

Owner-own-work research draft; status proof (unaudited), independent review and priority assessment pending. Fix k>=1 and D>=k+1. In R^(k+1) let M0 be the smooth closed surface z^2+Phi(|x|^2)=1, where Phi(s)=0 for s<=1 and Phi(s)=(s-1)exp(-1/(s-1)) for s>1. Let V0 be its surface volume. Put ell=1/(2sqrt(k)), A=1/12, Q=[-ell/2,ell/2]^k, and b(t)=64t^3(1-t)^3 on [0,1], zero outside. For n>=1 put h=ell/n and partition Q into n^k cells with lower corners c_i. For every sigma in {-1,+1}^(n^k), define f_sigma(x)=A h^2 sum_i sigma_i product_j b((x_j-c_ij)/h), T_sigma(x,z)=(x,z+f_sigma(x)), Vn=area(T_sigma(M0)), and t_n=(V0/Vn)^(1/k). Let mu_(sigma,n) be exactly uniform surface probability on t_n T_sigma(M0), isometrically embedded into R^D. There are constants C,W0 depending only on k,D and this fixed base such that, for W>=W0, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG architecture with at most W charged edge weights and biases has sup_(n,sigma) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],mu_(sigma,n))<=C W^(-4/k), with depth O(W). All fixed coefficients are charged; absent edges are absent; skip connections, unrestricted real weights and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed. The exact squared-gradient graph area density is C2 across every cell face with bounds independent of n; uniformly positive C2 chart densities have uniformly C2 inverse triangular transports. Apply Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk Theorem 3.3 (arXiv:1906.09477, p.5) at r=2,d=k, then a logarithmic-size tent-map scalar-source conversion and a fixed finite chart mixture with positive-time connectors. The source-conversion coupling uses the exact smooth map Lipschitz constant, not the coding network Lipschitz constant. This is a candidate theorem only for this entire explicit packing family, not all reach-bounded C2 surfaces. No bounded-bit, efficient weight-computation, complete T339 solution or novelty claim is made.
Exactly the explicit smooth base and signed cubic-endpoint bump family in the statement; k>=1, D>=k+1; scalar uniform latent source; unrestricted real-weight sparse feedforward DAG parameter count including fixed coefficients. Analytic proof unaudited, depending on unaudited T2-007 regularity and the known Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk theorem.

body:
For an integral operator T_k on L^2 with kernel k, the formula tr T_k = integral of k(x,x) dx is not a definition and not automatic. (1) An L^2 kernel is an equivalence class modulo null sets, and on a nonatomic space the diagonal is a null set, so k(x,x) has no meaning at all without choosing a distinguished representative; different representatives give different 'diagonal integrals'. (2) Continuity of the kernel is not enough for trace class. Carleman's example: there are continuous 2pi-periodic functions g whose Fourier coefficients are not absolutely summable. The convolution operator (T f)(x) = (1/(2 pi)) times the integral over the circle of g(x - y) f(y) dy has the continuous kernel k(x,y) = g(x - y)/(2 pi), is normal with eigenvalues the Fourier coefficients of g and eigenfunctions the exponentials, so its singular values are the moduli of those coefficients; hence T is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, while the naive diagonal integral is the finite number g(0). (3) What does hold: if T is trace class on L^2([a,b]) and has a continuous kernel on [a,b] x [a,b], then tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx; and by Mercer's theorem, if k is continuous, symmetric and positive semidefinite on a compact interval (more generally on a compact metric space with a finite Borel measure of full support), then the associated operator is trace class, the eigenfunction series converges absolutely and uniformly, and tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx = sum of the eigenvalues. So the safe routes are positivity plus continuity (Mercer), or an independent proof of trace class plus continuity; 'the kernel is nice' by itself is not a proof.
the operator is trace class, or the kernel is continuous and positive semidefinite (Mercer) on a compact space with a finite Borel measure of full support
the kernel is a continuous representative, so that its diagonal values are defined
an L^2 kernel alone determines only a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, whose diagonal is undefined

[Thm intro-coupling of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] Let  \(d=4,5\) and fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).  Let \(G_1\) be the
coarse-grained self-intersection graph of the simple random walk path $S[0,n]$ constructed
from the block length
\[
    a_n =
    \begin{cases}
    \varepsilon n(\log n)^{-1}, & d=4,\\
    \varepsilon n^{2/3}, & d=5,
    \end{cases}
\]
and let \(G_2\) be the corresponding long range percolation graph, with
nearest-neighbor edges present deterministically and with the dimension-dependent
connection probabilities specified below.  Then \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) can be
constructed on the same probability space so that
\[
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigl(G_1\neq G_2\bigr)=0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_k] = 0 and \text{Var}(X_k) = \sigma_k^2 < \infty. Let S_k = \sum_{j=1}^k X_j. Then for every \epsilon > 0, \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{1 \le k \le n} |S_k| \ge \epsilon \right) \le \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} \sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\text{Var}(S_n)}{\epsilon^2}.

Preserved duplicate statement and commentary:
Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables with E[X_i] = 0 and Var(X_i) < infinity for each i, and let S_k = X_1 + ... + X_k. Then for every lambda > 0, P(max_{1 <= k <= n} |S_k| >= lambda) <= Var(S_n) / lambda^2 = (sum_{i=1}^n Var(X_i)) / lambda^2. This strengthens Chebyshev's inequality applied to S_n alone into a bound on the whole running maximum. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a nonnegative random variable X, typically a count of some combinatorial structure written as X = sum_i X_i for indicator random variables X_i, the Paley-Zygmund inequality gives P(X > 0) >= (E[X])^2 / E[X^2]. Expanding E[X^2] = E[X] + sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j], the method succeeds in proving P(X>0) is bounded away from 0 exactly when the pair-correlation sum sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j] is of the same order as (E[X])^2, that is, when correlations between the indicators do not overwhelm the square of the mean. This is the standard route to existence results, such as an infinite cluster, a long crossing, or a large clique, once a first-moment computation has already established that E[X] is large or diverging, complementing the first-moment method, which by Markov's inequality only ever gives upper bounds on P(X>0). The method does not give any rate of convergence beyond the crude Paley-Zygmund ratio, gives no lower bound at all if the correlation structure is not controlled, and can produce a vacuous (near-0) bound whenever the variance is dominated by rare, strongly correlated configurations even though the mean itself is large. Typical failure: Computing a large or diverging first moment E[X] and declaring existence of the structure without bounding E[X^2]; if the indicators X_i are strongly positively correlated (a common situation for overlapping structures), the pair-correlation term can dominate (E[X])^2, making the Paley-Zygmund bound vacuous even as E[X] -> infinity, which is exactly the situation where a large first moment gives a false sense of near-certain existence. Canonical reference: Paley and Zygmund, 1932, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society; Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, fourth edition, Wiley.

the correlation sum not growing asymptotically faster than (E[X])^2

Let P be a locally finite poset, R a nonzero commutative ring with 1, and Q a subset with the induced order. Restricting an element of the incidence algebra I_R(P) to the comparable pairs of Q is a unital R-algebra homomorphism onto I_R(Q) if and only if Q is order-convex: x <= z <= y with x, y in Q forces z in Q. In that case mu_Q(x, y) = mu_P(x, y) for all x <= y in Q.

Finite-dimensional local corollary of van den Berg-Hetebrij-Rink parameterization theorem. Let F be a C^k map, integer k>=2, on a neighborhood of 0 in R^c x R^s, fixing 0, with DF(0)=diag(I_c,A_s) and spectral radius(A_s)<1. Then, after restricting to a neighborhood, there is a C^k center graph h with h(0)=0,Dh(0)=0 and a local C^k center map R, DR(0)=I_c, such that F(u,h(u))=(R(u),h(R(u))) wherever both sides remain local. The graph is parameterized by its center coordinate u. For k=3 this gives a C3 center graph. This assertion is a graph-existence and reduced-map theorem; it does not by itself assert a phase projection or stable foliation for nearby points.

Model: unit-rate rightward TASEP on Z; extra killing at0 at rate kappa>0.

Writing J_i=E[eta_i*(1-eta_(i+1))], stationarity of eta_i gives J_(i-1)-J_i=kappa*1_(i=0)*E eta_0. There is also an exact obstruction to any independent Bernoulli invariant law whose site densities r_i all lie strictly between0 and1. For adjacent sites, subtract the derivative of r_i*r_(i+1) from the generator derivative of E[eta_i*eta_(i+1)]. At a product law the covariance derivative equals J_i*(r_(i+1)-r_i), with killing terms cancelling. Stationarity therefore forces all adjacent densities equal. The one-site balance at0 then forces kappa*r_0=0, a contradiction.

The internal jump i to i+1 leaves eta_i*eta_(i+1) equal to0 both before and after, whereas it changes the two marginal means by -J_i and +J_i. Incoming and outgoing exterior jumps factor under the product law, giving the displayed covariance derivative. Independent killing at0 contributes the same product term in both expressions and cancels.

Strictly interior densities are essential: degenerate empty or blocked measures are not ruled out by dividing by J_i=r_i*(1-r_(i+1)). The invariant-law classification remains open here. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] For every pair of integers satisfying \eqref{eq:nk-range}, there is a compact
embedded rotational torus $\Sigma^n\subset\R^{n+1}$ whose homothetic
dilations form a shrinking solution of the unnormalised $\sigma_k$-curvature
flow \eqref{eq:sigma-k-flow} in the Sobolev almost-everywhere sense defined in
Section~\ref{sec:weak}.  More precisely, $\Sigma$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item The torus is smooth away from two rotational latitudes and satisfies
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S)$ there.
  \item If $\Omega$ is the bounded domain enclosed by $\Sigma$ and
  $S_{\mathrm w}$ is the weak shape operator of $\partial\Omega=\Sigma$, then
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w})$ almost everywhere with
  respect to the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal H^n$.
  \item Set $X_t=((k+1)(T-t))^{1/(k+1)}X$ and
  $\Sigma_t=X_t(M)$.  If $\nu_t$ and $S_{\mathrm w,t}$ are the outward unit
  normal and weak shape operator of $\Sigma_t$, respectively, then
  $\langle\partial X_t/\partial t,\nu_t\rangle
  =\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w,t})$ at $\mathcal H^n$-almost every point, for every
  $t<T$.
  \item Its profile curve has H\"older regularity $C^{1,1/k}$ and belongs
  to the Sobolev class $W^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<k/(k-1)$.
\end{enumerate}
If $s$ is arclength along the profile curve and $s_0$ is either singular
parameter, then the profile curve is
not $C^2$ at $s_0$, and the magnitude of its meridional principal curvature
is asymptotic to a positive multiple of $|s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346

Let k be Bin(n,1/2). On n/3<=k<=2n/3 let S and R be independent
chi-square variables with respectively k and k-1 degrees of freedom and
M=sqrt(S/R). Off this central-k event put M=1. For fixed 0<d<K and bounded
C^5 f with bounded derivatives through order five, uniformly for u in [d,K],

    n E[f(uM)-f(u)] = 2u f'(u)+u^2 f''(u)
        +(1/n)[10u f'(u)+11u^2 f''(u)+4u^3 f'''(u)
                            +(u^4/2)f''''(u)] + O_(f,d,K)(n^(-3/2)). (B)

The exact conditional raw moments, for k large enough, are

    E M     = (k-1)/(k-2),
    E M^2   = k/(k-3),
    E M^3   = (k^2-1)/[(k-2)(k-4)],
    E M^4   = k(k+2)/[(k-3)(k-5)].                  (G)

These follow from E(chi-square_r)^z=2^z Gamma(r/2+z)/Gamma(r/2),
independence, and Gamma(x+1)=x Gamma(x). In particular the first formula
is exact; approximating its two gamma ratios separately is unnecessary.
Expansion in 1/k gives

    E(M-1)   =1/k+2/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^2 =1/k+5/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^3 =6/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^4 =3/k^2+O(k^-3).

For central binomial k,

    E[1/k; central]=2/n+2/n^2+O(n^-3),
    E[1/k^2; central]=4/n^2+O(n^-3).

For example expand around mu=n/2 with k-mu, whose odd central moments
vanish and whose second moment is n/4. The fourth central moment is O(n^2);
central-k Taylor denominators are bounded below by n/3, and the remaining
binomial tails are exponential. Thus the four mixed moments are respectively

    2/n+10/n^2+O(n^-3),
    2/n+22/n^2+O(n^-3),
    24/n^2+O(n^-3),
    12/n^2+O(n^-3).

Also E|M-1|^5=O(n^(-5/2)). To verify this last bound, split on central
S/k and R/k. There, M-1 is Lipschitz in their centered deviations and has
fifth absolute moment of this order. The chi-square exponential tails,
Holder, and higher inverse moments on central k bound the omitted part
exponentially. This is possible for all sufficiently large n, since k
then exceeds every fixed inverse-moment threshold used.

Fourth-order Taylor expansion with fifth-derivative remainder now proves
(B), including the factors 1/2,1/6,1/24. The fourth-order term is of size
1/n in the scaled generator, exactly the same order as the signed third
moment term. Therefore a derivation using only a third-order Taylor term
cannot give the complete weak 1/n correction, even before ReLU flips.

This partial expansion does not upgrade C004's full O(n^-1/2) error to
O(1/n). The unresolved pieces are the mixed baseline/flip moments and
angular geometry terms, uniformly enough to match the singular entrance.
If such a complete expansion is obtained, a time-step weak-error formula
also needs the discrete-vs-continuous semigroup correction, not only the
coefficient displayed in the one-step generator.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3d7df9f2e51673034c933127493e891f934b33deb918593bd355f53d6e87ca80","revision_digest":"sha256:f282992730d5aa78d8c74a31004934b8f1d577dbbef911eb63487680c57725d0","source_id":"owner-own-work:T244-w691-C030:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma L:basis-for-comparison of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $y_1 \le y_2 \in \mathbb{Z}, t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_1,t]_{\textsf{L}}$ and $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_2,t]_{\textsf{L}}$, and take $f:\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Then for any $E:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \le E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \ge x\}$. Similarly, 
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \ge E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \le x\}$.

Let $X$ be $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\mathbb{R}^M$ with covariance $\Sigma$. Split the rows into two independent parts of sizes $m$ and $n - m$ with sample covariances $S_1 = V_1\Lambda_1 V_1^T$ and $S_2$. The nonparametric eigenvalue-regularised covariance estimator is $\hat\Sigma = V_1 \operatorname{diag}(V_1^T S_2 V_1)\, V_1^T$, averaged over $K$ random splits. Then: (i) $\mathbb{E}[V_1^T S_2 V_1 \mid V_1] = V_1^T \Sigma V_1$, so each diagonal entry $v_i^T S_2 v_i$ is an unbiased estimate of the population variance in the direction $v_i$ - the Ledoit-Peche oracle $d_i^* = v_i^T\Sigma v_i$ evaluated on independent data; (ii) as $M, n \to \infty$ with $M/n \to c > 0$ and $m/n \to r \in (0,1)$, $\hat\Sigma$ is asymptotically optimal in Frobenius loss among estimators of the form $V_1 D V_1^T$ with $D$ diagonal (Lam 2016, Theorem 1); (iii) $\hat\Sigma$ is positive semidefinite and carries no bandwidth, floor or shrinkage constant beyond the split fraction (Lam recommends choosing $m$ by minimising $\|\hat\Sigma_m - S\|_F$ over a grid; $m = n/2$ is the usual default). A population direction of genuinely small variance keeps a small estimate (its held-out variance is small too); a direction whose small sample variance was a finite-sample cancellation receives the variance it actually has out of sample.
rows i.i.d. with finite fourth moments
M/n -> c > 0, m/n -> r in (0,1)
the two parts of the split are disjoint (independence of V_1 and S_2 is what carries the argument)

Let X be a compact Hausdorff space and let A be a subalgebra of C(X, R), the continuous real functions with the supremum norm, such that A contains the constant functions and separates points (for x != y in X there is f in A with f(x) != f(y)). Then A is dense in C(X, R). Complex form: a subalgebra of C(X, C) that contains the constants, separates points, and is closed under complex conjugation is dense in C(X, C). The Weierstrass approximation theorem is the case X = [a, b] with A the polynomials: every continuous real function on [a, b] is a uniform limit of polynomials.

Fourth-power uniform integrability is unnecessary: the fourth bound gives second-power uniform integrability, and Portmanteau bounds the limiting fourth moment. This does not supply an Ising deficit or field tightness.

[Defi 34 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] Let $c\colon [t_0,t_1]\to A$ be a smooth admissible curve and set $\gamma:=\pi\circ c$. Let $b\in \Gamma(\gamma^*A)$ be a smooth section along $\gamma$. Then there is a well-defined section $\mathcal{T}_c(b)\in \Gamma(c^*TA)$ defined as follows: Let $A_U\cong U\times\mathbb{A}$ be a vector-bundle trivialization such that $\gamma(J)\subseteq U$ for a subinterval of $[t_0,t_1]$. Write $r_x\colon \mathbb{A}\to T_xM$ for the local representative of the anchor, \Cref{loctho}. In the trivialisation we identify
\begin{align} c(t)=(\gamma(t),a(t)),\quad b(t)=(\gamma(t),\beta(t)),  \text{ then define }  \notag\\ 
\mathcal{T}_c(b)(t) = \left( \gamma(t), a(t), r_{\gamma(t)}(\beta(t)), \frac{d\beta}{dt}(t)+C_{\gamma(t)}(a(t),\beta(t)) \right), 
\end{align} where $C$ is the local structure map from \Cref{locbrac} \eqref{loctrivrbracket}.

[Theorem KALOKAIRI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $\varrho (N)$ be a sequence of probability measures on
  $\hat{U} (N)$ such that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N} \log \text{} S_{\varrho (N)}^{U
    (N)} (u_1, \ldots, u_r, 1^{N - r}) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (u_i),
    
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is an analytic function in a complex neighborhood of $1$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $1^r$. Then the random measure
  $N^{- 1} \sum_{i = 1}^N \delta \left( \frac{\lambda_i + N - i}{N} \right)$, converges,
  as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in probability, in the sense of moments to a
  deterministic measure $\mathbf{m}$ on $\mathbb{R}$, whose moments are given
  by
  \begin{equation}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}} t^k \mathbf{m} (d \text{} t) = \sum_{m = 0}^k
    \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m) !}  \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} (x^k
    (\Psi' (x))^{k - m}) \right|_{x = 1} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let H be a Hilbert space. (a) If A and B in B(H) are Hilbert-Schmidt, then AB is trace class and ||AB||_1 <= ||A||_2 ||B||_2. (b) Conversely, every trace-class T factors as T = AB with A and B Hilbert-Schmidt: with the polar decomposition T = U|T| take A = U |T|^{1/2} and B = |T|^{1/2}, so that ||A||_2 ||B||_2 = ||T||_1. (c) More generally (Hoelder inequality for Schatten classes) if 1 <= p, q, r <= infinity with 1/r = 1/p + 1/q, and A is in S_p, B in S_q, then AB is in S_r with ||AB||_r <= ||A||_p ||B||_q, where ||X||_p = (sum_n s_n(X)^p)^{1/p} and S_infinity is the compact operators with the operator norm.

Bifurcations occur in both continuous systems and discrete systems.

Let $E$ be a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix with eigen-decomposition $E = \sum_k \lambda_k u_k u_k^T$ (for instance a sample covariance) and let $C$ be any symmetric $p \times p$ matrix (the population covariance). Among all estimators of the form $\Xi = \sum_k \xi_k u_k u_k^T$ - the same eigenvectors as $E$, free eigenvalues - the Frobenius loss $\|\Xi - C\|_F^2$ is minimized by the oracle choice $\xi_k^{\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$, the projection of the population matrix onto the $k$-th sample eigenvector, with minimal loss $\|C\|_F^2 - \sum_k (u_k^T C u_k)^2$. In particular the oracle eigenvalues are convex combinations of the population eigenvalues (they lie between the smallest and largest population eigenvalue) and their sum equals $\operatorname{tr} C$: a rotationally invariant estimator that is optimal in Frobenius loss never moves the trace and always shrinks the spread of the sample spectrum toward the population spread.
E and C symmetric p x p; the estimator class is restricted to the eigenvectors of E

[Thm 11 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Let $\alpha$ be a quadratic irrational, let $ax^2+bx+c$ be its minimal polynomial with $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{gcd}(a,b,c)=1$ and $a>0$, and let $Q(x,y)=ax^2+bxy+cy^2$ be the corresponding binary quadratic form. For any constant $\theta>1$ and any integer $M \ge 1$, we have
\[ \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{1}{m^{\theta} \| m \alpha \|^{\theta}} = c(\alpha, \theta) \log M +O(1) \]
with an implied constant depending only on $\alpha$ and $\theta$. The constant $c(\alpha, \theta)$ is given by
\[ c(\alpha, \theta) = \frac{D^{\theta/2}}{\log \varepsilon} \sum_{\substack{n \in \mathbb{Z} \\ n \neq 0}} \frac{R_Q(n)}{|n|^{\theta}}, \]
where $D=b^2-4ac>0$ is the discriminant, $R_Q(n)$ is the number of primary representations of $n$, and $\varepsilon=(t_0+u_0\sqrt{D})/2$ with the smallest positive solution $(t_0,u_0)$ of Pell's equation $t^2-Du^2=4$.

Fix theta in (0,pi/2] and unit probe q; teacher w=cos(theta)q+sin(theta)u, u uniform on S^(ell-1) in q-perp, ell=d-1>=2. An unlabeled isotropic Gaussian pool and independent seed select m indices without teacher labels. The learner sees only those m teacher labels, plus q, theta and the unlabeled pool, and outputs a unit linear normal. Conditional on the pool and seed, at most (e*max(1,m/ell))^ell selected-label patterns occur. The latitude cap argument gives expected error at least sin(theta)*(2*(e*max(1,m/ell))^ell)^(-1/(ell-1))/(2*pi). For a rotation-equivariant protocol this applies to each fixed teacher-probe pair. If m/ell->alpha>0 in probability, liminf expected error>=sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*max(1,alpha)), independent of source-pool size. Threshold max-margin is equivariant. The same bound applies to each fixed-fraction deterministic limit and their infimum at retained alpha, excluding an asymptotic exponential envelope at fixed theta>0. No extra unselected labels, label-adaptive selection, or teacher-dependent side information are allowed. No matching upper rate or actual crossover is proved.

For all b-Lipschitz maps F:[0,1]^k to R^D and probability densities p with lambda<=p<=Lambda and Lip(p)<=K, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG with at most W charged edge weights and biases achieves sup_(F,p) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],F#(p dx))<=C W^(-2/k) for W>=W0. [Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For a sequence $f=(f_r)_{r\ge0}$ with values in $\Bbbk=\Q(q)$, let
\[
 (Lf)_r=f_{r+1},\qquad (Mf)_r=q^rf_r;
\]
then $LM=qML$.  In one discrete variable, the standard
$q$-Weyl-algebra definition of $q$-holonomicity is equivalent to the
existence of a nonzero recurrence
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=0}^{d}p_a(q,q^r)f_{r+a}=0,
 \qquad p_a(q,M)\in\Q(q,M),
\end{equation}
after clearing denominators if necessary.  This equivalence and the
multivariate $q$-Weyl-algebra definition used below are recalled in
\cite[Section~3]{GLsurvey}.
title: Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585

[Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $f_n:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ be a sequence of functions satisfying (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper) which converge uniformly on compact sets to continuous limit $f:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ which also satisfies (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper). Suppose that additionally $f$ satisfies the following shape bound: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item For all $c_0 > 0$, there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all $u = (x, a, t; y, b; t + s) \in \mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$ with $s < c_0$ we have that
		$$
		\left|f(u) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{s} \right|\le C s^{1/3} \log^2\left(\frac{{2\|u\|_2}}{s}\right).
		$$
	\end{itemize}
	Suppose $\pi_n$ is a sequence of continuous geodesics for $f_n$ between points $(u_n, s)$ to $(v_n, t)$, where the sequence $(u_n, s; v_n, t)$ is precompact in $\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$.
	Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sequence $\pi_n$ is precompact in the uniform topology on functions from $[s, t] \to \Lambda$.
		\item If $\pi:[s, t] \to \Lambda$ is a subsequential limit of $\pi_n$, then $\pi$ satisfies (equation E:f-equality of the paper) for any finite set $\{s = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k = t\} \subset [s, t]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2609.02878 (conjecture environment labelled conj:intro-kpolystable-fibres).] Assume that every fibre \(F_y\) is K-polystable with respect to
\(-K_{F_y}\). Then the finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow is Type I:
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le t<T}\sup_{x\in X}
 (T-t)|\Rm(g(t))|_{g(t)}(x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Moreover, fix \(q\in Y\), and let
\(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}\in2\pi c_1(F_q)\) be a normalized
K\"ahler--Einstein metric,
\[
 \Ric(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}})=\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}.
\]
Write \(g_{q,{\rm KE}}=2g_{\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}}\), so that
\(\Ric(g_{q,{\rm KE}})=\tfrac12g_{q,{\rm KE}}\). After forgetting the
conjugate heat measures, every Type-I-scale blowup at \(\xi\) based at
\(F_q\) is isomorphic, as a K\"ahler metric flow, to
\begin{equation}
 \left(
 \C^m\times F_q,\,
 J_0\oplus J_{F_q},\,
 g_{\rm E}+(-s)g_{q,{\rm KE}}
 \right)_{s<0}.
\end{equation}
Thus the residual factor is the central fibre with its own complex
structure. (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: K-polystable smooth fibres

Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T in K(X,Y). If x_n -> x weakly in X, then ||T x_n - T x|| -> 0. Conversely, if X is reflexive and T in B(X,Y) maps every weakly convergent sequence to a norm convergent sequence, then T is compact. Without reflexivity the converse fails (the identity of l^1 maps weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent ones by Schur's property but is not compact).
X and Y are Banach spaces
T is bounded and linear

OWNER OWN WORK, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C005 v1. Exact obstruction reduction for Target 3, not an escape theorem; no novelty claimed for Gaussian conditioning. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, x_* a deterministic unit vector, A have iid N(0,1) entries, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). Use f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 and unmodified GD. Set e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0 e1||, e2=(x0-q0 e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=Ae1, h=Ae2, B=AE, z0=q0*g+rho0*h, v0=z0*(z0^2-g^2) coordinatewise, s=||v0||, u=v0/s, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, q1=q0-eta*g^T*v0/m, p1=rho0-eta*h^T*v0/m. Excluding null events rho0*s=0, conditional on F1=sigma(x0,g,h,w), z1=A*x1 has Gaussian law with mean mu=q1*g+p1*h-eta*||w||^2*v0/m and covariance tau^2*P, where tau=eta*s*||w||/m. Also w is standard Gaussian in dimension d-2, independently of sigma(x0,g,h). Consequently E[q2|F1]=q1-eta/m sum_i g_i*mu_i*(mu_i^2+3*tau^2*(1-u_i^2)-g_i^2). This retains the residual-direction memory term; centering at q1*g+p1*h with conditionally mean-zero error for the same F1 is false. No claim rules out a different conditioning history or center. At m=ceil(alpha*d), ||w||^2/m converges in probability to 1/alpha for fixed alpha>0. Growing-horizon response and overlap-noise control, and random-start escape, remain open.

 \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  The random field $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ with values in $\mathbb {M} $  
satisfies  {\em $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  if
there exists an increasing-decreasing family of 
 functions $\omega_k :  [0, \infty) \to [0,2]$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, 
(called correlation decay functions), such that $\lim_{s \to \infty}\omega_k(s) = 0$ for all $k \in\mathbb{N}$ and for all $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and all $f \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^p)$, and
  $g \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^q)$ we have

\begin{align} 
\left| \mathbb {E} [f(\bk {M(x_i)}1{p}) \, g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] - \mathbb {E} [f(\bk  {M(x_i)}1p)] \, \mathbb {E} [g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] \right| \le \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{align}

where $s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q})$ is at (equation defs of the paper).
\item  The random field $M$
satisfies {\em $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}  if~(equation e.field-mixing of the paper) holds when \textnormal{BL}\ is replaced by $\mathbb{B} $.
 \item  Under Item~(i)  (resp. Item (ii)), the random field  $M$  has  {\em fast $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  (resp.  {\em fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations})

Let (X_n)_{n >= 0} be a martingale for a filtration (F_n) and let F_infinity be the sigma-algebra generated by the union of the F_n. The following are equivalent: (i) the family {X_n} is uniformly integrable; (ii) X_n converges almost surely AND in L^1 to some X_infinity; (iii) there exists Y in L^1 with X_n = E[Y | F_n] almost surely for every n, that is the martingale is CLOSED. When these hold one may take Y = X_infinity, and X_infinity = E[Y | F_infinity]. Consequences: for a UI martingale, E[X_infinity] = E[X_0], and the optional stopping identity E[X_tau] = E[X_0] holds for EVERY almost surely finite stopping time tau, with no boundedness assumption on tau or on the martingale - this is a genuinely stronger conclusion than the standard three sufficient conditions (bounded tau, bounded martingale, or E[tau] finite with bounded increments). An L^1-bounded martingale need not be UI, and then only the almost sure half of (ii) survives. For p > 1, an L^p-bounded martingale is automatically UI by de la Vallee Poussin and converges in L^p as well; p = 1 is the exceptional case. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Theorems 13.3 and 14.1]

is satisfied then the discrete time Markov chain $\{K_n\}$ is positive recurrent 
and its stationary distribution $\pi$ has finite mean: 
$\sum_{k=1}^\infty k \pi_k < \infty$. Similarly, the sequence of service stages 
posesses a unique stationary distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^+$ which has finite mean 
$\int_0^\infty y dF(y)<\infty$. 

Further, if for some $m>1$ 
$\mathbb{E}[\sigma_1^m]= \int_0^\infty m t^{m-1} \big(1-G(t)\big) dt <\infty$, then 
$\int_0^\infty y^m dF(y)<\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let C be a convex subset of a real vector space X and f: C -> R. f is convex if f(lambda x + (1-lambda) y) <= lambda f(x) + (1-lambda) f(y) for all x, y in C and lambda in [0,1]. If X is a normed space with dual X*, the subdifferential of f at a point x_0 in C is the set partial f(x_0) = {v in X* : f(x) >= f(x_0) + v(x - x_0) for all x in C}, whose elements are called subgradients of f at x_0; partial f(x_0) may be empty, a single point, or contain more than one point. [standard, e.g. Rockafellar, Convex Analysis]

[Corollary 7 (\textsf{Law of small chaotic blocks}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix an order $r\geq1$.  For each $n$, let
$F_{n,1}$, $\ldots$, $F_{n,K_n}$ be independent centered variables in
order-$r$ chaoses
over mutually independent component spaces, 
and
suppose that

\noi
\begin{align}
 X_{n,k}:=F_{n,k}+\theta_{n,k}\in\N_0.
\notag
\end{align}
Put
$F_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n} F_{n,k}$,
$\theta_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\theta_{n,k}$, and
$X_n:=F_n+\theta_n$.
In the Poisson setting, assume

\noi
\begin{align}
 \theta_n\to\lambda,
 \quad
 \sum_km_2(F_{n,k})\to\lambda,
 \AND
 \sum_k\cP(F_{n,k})\to0.
\notag
\end{align}
Then $X_n$ converges to $\Pois(\lambda)$ in total variation.  In the
Rademacher setting, the same conclusion holds with $\cP$ replaced by
$\cR$, provided that the maximal coordinate influence $\cM(F_n)$ of $F_n$ tends
to zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 1.2 (Colorful Tverberg theorem) of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let $d,t\geq 1$, let $(X,\mathcal{C})$ satisfy $\textup{VC}(\mathcal{C})\leq d$, and let $S_{1},\ldots,S_{d+1}\subseteq X$ be pairwise disjoint finite sets. If $|S_{i}|\geq d(t-1)+1$ for every $i\in[d+1]$, then there exist pairwise disjoint transversals $T_{1},\ldots,T_{t}$ of the color classes whose convex hulls have a common point; that is, $\bigcap_{j=1}^{t}\operatorname{conv}(T_{j})\neq\varnothing.$

[Lemma lem:parameter-family of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] There is $s_0>0$ such that, for every $|s|<s_0$, the zeros of
$F_{z,s}$ admit an indexing
\[
    L_{z,s}
    =
    \{p_{\lambda,s}(z):\lambda\in\Lambda\}
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $L_{z,s}$ are real and uniformly Delone, with constants
independent of $z$ and $s$;

\item for all $z \in Z$, 
\[
    L_{Tz,s}=L_{z,s}-1;
\]

\item for all $z \in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{L_{z,s}}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1);
\]

\item
if $s\neq0$ and
\[
    L_{w,s}=L_{z,s}-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^uz;
\]

\item
for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $z\in Z$, the map
$s\mapsto p_{\lambda,s}(z)$ is real analytic and satisfies
\[
    p_{\lambda,0}(z)=\lambda,
    \qquad
    \left.
    \frac{d}{ds}p_{\lambda,s}(z)
    \right|_{s=0}
    =
    -\frac{H_z(\lambda)}{S'(\lambda)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

    Consider a continuous-time simple random walk on $G$. Let $K_1, K_2 > 1$.

    \vspace{2mm}

\begin{align} 
        \sum_{y \in D} \mathbb P_y \left( \tau_x \le a^2 \right) \ge c\cdot \theta(a) \, .
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Auffinger--Damron--Hanson Question 13 asks for chi<1/2 in d>=2 under suitable conditions on the iid lattice edge law F, and chi=1/3 in d=2. Their separate Question 15 asks for chi>0 in suitable dimensions; the canonical P0104 card combines them. The survey leaves both suitable conditions on F and the exact variance-scaling meaning of chi open. O(n/log n) variance gives a limiting logarithmic standard-deviation exponent of 1/2, so it is insufficient for strict subdiffusivity. A power saving in rotationally invariant Riemannian FPP and finite-size straight-path identities for lattice FPP do not establish a fixed-law lattice chi=1/3 result. Current October 2026 openness is not certified by this note.

[Theorem 10 (Oracle bound over the three fixed statistical comparators) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Let \(T\geq5\) and let \(\mathcal D_N=\{(\bm X^{(i)},Y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^N\) consist of independent copies of \((\bm X,Y)\). Before observing \(\mathcal D_N\), fix fully specified deterministic comparators \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\) of the forms introduced above. Their specifications include every threshold and calibration constant, the clipping radius, and the selected approximation networks. There exists a fixed CNN classifier class with parallel branches \(\mathcal H\), with the head specification fixed as in Definition~\ref{def:cnn}, such that \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\in\mathcal H\). Let \(d_{\mathcal H}=\operatorname{VCdim}(\mathcal H)\), where \(1\leq d_{\mathcal H}\leq N\), and let \(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}}\in\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal H}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb I\{h(\bm X^{(i)})\neq Y^{(i)}\}\). Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
\operatorname{err}(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}})
\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H}\operatorname{err}(h)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta)
\leq\min_{G\in\{S,V,AR\}}\operatorname{err}(\overline h_G)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Oracle bound over the three fixed statistical comparators

Status: proof (unaudited). Claim w730-T355-C005 v1. Novelty unestablished.

Let d,q be positive finite integers. Let H be a constant symmetric positive
definite q by q matrix with extreme eigenvalues 0<m<=M. Let
A:R^d -> R^{q x q} be C^1, A(u)^T A(u)=H, and

    sup_u sum_i ||partial_i A(u)||_op^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Let z_k be iid R^q-valued labels, independent of the past, with
E z_k=0 and E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No symmetry or higher moment is assumed.
Fix sigma>=0, 0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M, deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Consider label-noise SGD

    h_{k,i}:=u_{k+1,i}-u_{k,i}=-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k, B=I-eta H.       (1)

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}) define f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and

    F_2=sup_u ||D^2 f(u)||_op,
    F_vv=sup_{u,v} ||D_v^2 F(u,v)||_op,
    F_uv=sup_u ||D_u a(u)||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho),
    gamma=min{m, M(2-rho)/rho} > 0.

For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),               (2)

    C(T)=c [F_vv/2 + T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2
                       + F_uv sigma D/gamma].         (3)

Thus the slow-clock weak rate is a=1 with an explicit constant linear
in T, with only centered second-moment labels. Covariance proportionality
to the loss Hessian is asserted ON the minimizing manifold v=0, where
the noise covariance is sigma^2 diag(0,H). No off-manifold covariance
proportionality is asserted. The ambient loss is L=v^T H v/2.

The limiting constant tangential process is the known trace-Hessian
flow: Li-Wang-Arora, arXiv:2110.06914v4, Corollary 5.2, pp.8-9 and 33.
The quantitative estimate and removal of symmetry are candidate results,
not a verified priority claim. General T355 remains open.
