[Theorem 2 (Structural representation and exact extraction) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] For every represented subsequence of \eqref{overview:eq:packet}, the
following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Roman*)}]
 \item Labeled block evaluation extends uniquely, at every physical
 weight $q$, to a unitary
 \begin{equation}
 \mathbb U_q:
 \cW_q\!\left(\bigoplus_{s\le q}\cK_s\right)
 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\cH_q.
 
 \end{equation}
 This unitary gives the direct implication in
 \eqref{overview:eq:weak-closure}; collision-null replicas give the
 converse realization and the convergence of the finite contraction
 register.

 \item Put
 \begin{equation}
 a_Q=\sum_{r=1}^{Q-1}\binom{Q-1}{r}^2\binom{2r}{r},
 \qquad
 \mu_Q=\left\lfloor\frac{Q^2+Q+1}{3}\right\rfloor.
 
 \end{equation}
 There are nested common graded modules $M^{[J]}$ such that the separated
 feedback energy and the coherently aggregated Gaussian self-plus-interface
 defect satisfy
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_Q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le\frac{a_QR^4}{J},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\mathrm{res}}(r^{[J]})+\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}}(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})
 \le\frac{\mu_Qa_QR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 Consequently, along a further subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
 F_n\Longrightarrow A_*+G_C,
 \qquad G_C\indep A_*.
 
 \end{equation}
 This factorization is quantitative and unconditional, but the active
 factor $A_*$ need not be canonical.

 \item Suppose that the packet is carried by one chaos order $q$, and let
 $\xi_a=[f_{n,a}]_{\mathcal U}\in\cH_q$.  A Gram-reduced trajectory
 admits a sufficiently slow diagonal $J(n)\to\infty$ for which
 \begin{equation}
 (A_n^{[J(n)]},B_n^{[J(n)]})
 \Longrightarrow
 \left(
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cD_q}\xi,
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cK_q}\xi
 \right).
 
 \end{equation}
 The second component is Gaussian and independent of the first.  The
 reduced feedback may be stopped after fewer than $J$ promotions with
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le \frac{d\,a_qR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 If $\kappa_{n,a}$ denotes the fourth cumulant of the $a$th component,
 then, along the represented subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
  P_{\cD_q}\xi=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \lim_{\mathcal U}\sum_a\kappa_{n,a}=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  F_n\Longrightarrow_{\mathcal U}N_d(0,\Sigma),
  
 \end{equation}
 and the finite-level characteristic-function error is bounded by a
 constant times $|t|^2(\sum_a\kappa_{n,a})^{1/2}$.

 \item For a finite mixed-degree terminal $T$, let $\cN_s(T)$ be the
 closed span of the ranges of its nonlinear one-leg flattenings of
 primitive weight $s$.  Then
 \begin{equation}
 T=\mathsf A^{\can}+\mathsf G^{\can},
 \qquad \mathsf G^{\can}\indep\mathsf A^{\can},
 
 \end{equation}
 where the covariance of $\mathsf G^{\can}$ is maximal among graded
 Gaussian factors annihilated by the complete raw one-leg nonlinear
 register.  Simultaneous extraction can fail to reach this split; a
 lexicographic, weight-by-weight extraction does reach it.
\end{enumerate}
The $J^{-1/2}$ law-level bound derived from
\eqref{overview:eq:HS-rate} concerns only the noncanonical factorization
\eqref{overview:eq:noncanonical}; no quantitative rate toward
\eqref{overview:eq:canonical} is asserted. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Structural representation and exact extraction

[Proposition 242 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Let $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$ be non-zero and $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}} = (\boldsymbol{v} \otimes \boldsymbol{v}\,,\,0)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any $\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ we have $(\boldsymbol{w} \otimes \boldsymbol{w}\,,\,0) \in \mathfrak{G}^{[2]}.\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}$.
\item $\textnormal{Ker}(\pi^{\circ})$ is a torsion-free abelian group.
\item $\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is bijective if and only if $(\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}})^{-1}(\{\boldsymbol{v} \otimes \boldsymbol{v}\}) = \{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}\}$.
\item If $\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has finite $\mathfrak{G}^{[2]}$-orbit, then $\pi^{\circ}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is bijective.
\item If $-\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} \in \mathfrak{G}$, then $\textnormal{Ker}(\pi^{\bullet}) = \{(\tau \textnormal{\textbf{Id}},\tau \textnormal{\textbf{Id}})\,\,|\,\,\tau \in \{\pm 1\}\}$ and the maps $\pi_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\bullet}$ and $\mathfrak{p}^{\bullet}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ have degree $2$ (examples where this is realized will appear in Theorem~\ref{thm:spcurvenonbip}).
\item If $-\textnormal{\textbf{Id}} \notin \mathfrak{G}$, then $\pi^{\bullet}$, $\pi^{\bullet}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ and $\mathfrak{p}_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\bullet}$ are isomorphisms.
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 242 of arXiv:2601.16377

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6038d28eb971bf442bc01c3b4e93ee5444e37b0824f264f4f9c558155eaf4227","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/60/6038d28eb971bf442bc01c3b4e93ee5444e37b0824f264f4f9c558155eaf4227.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d573087f35a7b32ffd59589ea853e28d563fa1f54ff9ce13dc859d0863f48a69","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c22","bundle_id":"population.i0005-final-exploration-energy-and-charge-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and interacting particle systems","draft":"w661/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:parking-resampling-range-optimized-density-constant-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C22 v1: range-optimized resampling density constant

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis resampling
inequality and SRW range identity; UNCHECKED prior separate statement of
the optimized constant. This is a derived refinement, not a solution.

Let eta(x) be iid nonconstant integer-valued with mean zero and finite
first moment, in the source's parking model. Write S_t=E A_t(0), and
gamma=E|eta(0)-eta'(0)|>0 for an independent copy. Let R_n be the range
of full-space discrete-time nearest-neighbor SRW through time n. Whenever

    E|R_{2t}|-1 >= 1/gamma,

the source's resampling argument gives

    S_t >= 1/[8(E|R_{2t}|-1)].

For d>=3 only, if g=G(0) is the finite full-space SRW Green value, this
implies

    liminf_{t->infinity} t S_t >= g/16.

For the sparse critical law, S_t=h_t is also the unfilled-hole probability.
In d4 this improves the constant 1/16 displayed in the source's coarse
range estimate to G(0)/16. No recurrent-dimensional finite-Green formula
is asserted, and no upper density asymptotic follows.

## 1. Primary inequality and its optimization

Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis, arXiv:2609.02820v1, Lemma 5.1 proof Step 3,
pp.18-19, retains the exact range in its resampling/cancellation count:

    4S_t >= epsilon-(epsilon^2/2)(E|R_{2t}|-1),
                        for every 0<=epsilon<=gamma.

The two resampled systems have the same mean-zero law; the expected
number of surviving discrepancy labels is bounded by their combined
active/hole density 4S_t. The source derives the displayed inequality
before replacing E|R_{2t}|-1 by 2t. We use that already proved inequality,
not an independent claim that unmatched labels are independent.

Put L=E|R_{2t}|-1. It is positive for integer t>=1. If L>=1/gamma,
the maximizer epsilon=1/L belongs to the allowed interval. Substitution
gives 4S_t>=1/(2L), proving the finite-time bound. Since the expected
range tends to infinity, its condition holds eventually for each fixed
nonconstant initial law.

## 2. Exact transient range rate

For any finite K, summing a walk's unique last visit to K through time n
over starting points gives

    sum_y P_y(T_K<=n)
       =sum_{m=0}^n sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+>m).

For K={0}, the left side is E|R_n| by path translation. In d>=3 the
right summand tends to P_0(T_0^+=infinity)=1/g. Cesaro averaging yields
E|R_n|/(n+1)->1/g. Therefore

    t/[8(E|R_{2t}|-1)] --> g/16.

Combining with Step 1 gives the liminf. The source sparse law has
gamma=4p(1-p), if an explicit law-dependent threshold is desired.

## Scope

The source's 1/16 is a law- and dimension-independent coarse constant.
The refinement depends on the full-space transient Green value and uses
the exact walk range. It does not resolve closer-hole geometry, improve
the missing Palm bound in C9, or justify a fixed-p density limit.

Primary source: arXiv:2609.02820v1 Lemma 5.1 proof Step 3. Full-space
escape/capacity normalization: Sznitman arXiv:0704.2560v3 (1.5)-(1.7).

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space. For 0 < p < infinity, L^p(mu) is the set of equivalence classes, under equality mu-almost everywhere, of measurable f: X -> C (or R) with ||f||_p = (int_X |f|^p dmu)^{1/p} < infinity. L^infinity(mu) is the set of classes of measurable f with ||f||_infinity = ess sup |f| = inf{ M >= 0 : mu({|f| > M}) = 0 } < infinity (the infimum is attained, so |f| <= ||f||_infinity a.e.). For 1 <= p <= infinity, ||.||_p is a norm and L^p(mu) is a Banach space; for 0 < p < 1 it is only a quasi-norm (||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p)) and d(f,g) = ||f-g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric. l^p denotes L^p of the counting measure on N (or on a set I). The conjugate (dual) exponent p' of 1 <= p <= infinity is defined by 1/p + 1/p' = 1, with 1' = infinity and infinity' = 1.
(X, Sigma, mu) is a measure space
functions are Sigma-measurable and identified when equal mu-a.e.
0 < p <= infinity

[Proposition prop:multi_extention_Asmussen of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $g: [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be non-decreasing and absolutely continuous with $g(0)=0$ and a locally finite density $g'\geqslant 0$ satisfying $\int_0^y g'(x)x^{-2}\mathrm{d} x<\infty$ for some $y>0$. Let $\bm{X}$ be a $d$-dimensional L\'evy process with L\'evy measure $\nu$ such that $\mathds{E}[g(60|\bm{X}_1|)]<\infty$ and $\mathds{E}[\bm{X}_1]=0$. Then
\begin{equation}
    \lim_{n\to\infty}n
    \mathds{E}\big[g\big(\big|\bm{X}_{1/n}\big|\big)\big]
=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}g(|\bm{v}|)\nu(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:multi_extention_Asmussen of arXiv:2510.06891

[Theorem th:tail_stable of arXiv:2412.06374, 'Stable and tempered stable distributions and processes: an overview toward trajectory simu'] Let $X\sim S_\alpha(\sigma,\beta,\delta)$ with $\alpha \in (0,2), \sigma>0, \delta \in \mathbb{R}$. Let $f_X$ be the corresponding density.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $\beta \in (-1,1]$, $
\mathbb{P}(X>x) \underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\sim} c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha(1+\beta)x^{-\alpha},$ and $
f_X(x) \underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\sim} \alpha c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha (1+\beta) x^{-\alpha-1}$.

\item For $\beta \in [-1,1)$, $
\mathbb{P}(X<x) \underset{x\rightarrow -\infty}{\sim} c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha(1-\beta)x^{-\alpha},$ and $
f_X(x) \underset{x\rightarrow -\infty}{\sim} \alpha c_\alpha \sigma^\alpha (1-\beta) x^{-\alpha-1},$
\end{enumerate}
where $c_\alpha= \frac{1-\alpha}{2\Gamma(2-\alpha) \cos(\pi\alpha/2)}\mathbf{1}_{\alpha\neq 1} + 
\pi^{-1} \mathbf{1}_{ \alpha = 1}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1.2 \cite{nolan_univariate_2021}

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2511.09280, 'Random Walk conditioned to stay above a non-flat floor: curvature effects'] Let \(\beta>0\). Let \((X_k)_{k\in\Z}\) be an i.i.d.\ sequence of \(\calN(0,\beta)\) random variables and \(S\) the associated random walk. Let \(p\geq 1\), and let \(h:[-1,1]\to [0,1]\) and \(\alpha_p\geq 0\) be given by
    \[
    	h(x) = 1-\abs{x}^p,\; h_n(k) = nh(k/n), \text{ and }\alpha_p = \frac{p-1}{2p-1}.
	\]
    Let \(\{S\geq h_n\} = \{S_k\geq h_n(k)\ \forall k =-n,\dots,n\}\), \(P_{0}^{h_n} = P(\cdot \given S_{-n} = S_n = 0, S\geq h_n)\) and \(\rS_0 = n^{-\alpha_p}(S_0-n)\).
    There exist \(C,c,c_-,c_+\in (0,+\infty)\), \(n_0\geq 1\), such that, for any \(n\geq n_0\) and \(\lambda\geq 1\),
    \[
        C^{-1}e^{-c_- \lambda^{(2p-1)/p}}
        \leq P_{0}^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_0 \geq \lambda \bigr)
        \leq Ce^{-c_+ \lambda^{(2p-1)/p}}.
    \]
    In particular, for all \(p\geq 0\) and \(r\geq 0\), there exist \(K_-\) and \(K_+\) such that, for any \(n\geq n_0\),
    \begin{gather*}
        K_- \leq E_0^{h_n}\bigl(\rS_0^r\bigr) \leq K_+
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        K_- \leq \Var_{P_{0}^{h_n}}(\rS_0) \leq K_+.
    \end{gather*}

body:
[Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\hat{Y}$ the stopped martingale defined above, we can construct a deterministic time change $\tilde{Y}$ that can be expressed as the stochastic integral
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_0^t \tilde{w}_t\,d\tilde{W}(t)
    \]
for $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$,
where
$\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)=Y(q_0)$,
$\tilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion, and $\tilde{w}$ satisfies
the constraint $\E[(\tilde{w}_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$.

\begin{proof} We will construct a  martingale $\tilde{Y}$ to essentially be the deterministic time-change of $\hat{Y}$ such that $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2]=t$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$. Then, for $t\in[\gamma(1),1]$, we will take $\tilde{Y}$ to be any martingale ending at $\pm1$ almost surely, which exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} below. To formalize the time reparametrization, since $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,\gamma(1)]$ is nondecreasing, we can define its right-continuous generalized inverse 
\[\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,.\]
As a consequence of \eqref{e:gamma.prime} we must have $\gamma(t)-\gamma(s)\le t-s$ and $\lambda(t)-\lambda(s)\ge t-s$ for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$. It  follows by combining these inequalities with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} that
    \beq
    \begin{aligned}
    s &\ge \gamma(s) \ge \gamma(1)+s-1 \ge s-4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,\\
    t &\le \lambda(t) \le \lambda(\gamma(1)) + t-\gamma(1)
    =1+t-\gamma(1) \le t+4\epsilon^{1/2}
    \end{aligned}
    \eeq
for all $s\in [q_0,1]$, and $t\in [q_0,\gamma(1)]$. It is clear from this that we must define $\tilde{Y}(t) = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))$, so that
we will have $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2] = \E[\hat{Y}(\lambda(t))^2] = \gamma(\lambda(t))=t$. Since
    \[
    \hat{Y}(\lambda(t)) = Y(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)}
        w_u \ind\{u\le\tau\} \,dW(u)\,,
    \]
by considering the change of variables $u=\lambda(s)$ it is natural to define
    \beq
    \tilde{W}(t) = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)^{1/2} dW(u)\,.
    \eeq
Then $\tilde{W}$ is a local martingale with quadratic variation
    \[
    \langle \tilde{W}\rangle_t 
    = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)\,du
    = \gamma(\lambda(t))-\gamma(q_0) = t-q_0
    \]
for all $t\in[q_0,1]$, so by the L\'evy characterization it is a standard Brownian motion on $t\in[q_0,1]$, and is progressively measurable with respect to the time-changed filtration
$\tilde{\cF}_Y(t)\equiv\cF_Y(\lambda(t))$. We then define the modified control
    \[
    \tilde{w}_s
    \equiv
    \frac{w_{\lambda(s)}}{\gamma'(\lambda(s))^{1/2} }
      \ind\{\lambda(s)\le \tau\}\,,\]
where we define $\tilde{w}_s\equiv1$ in the case $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ --- by Lemma~\ref{l:generalized.inverse.fn}, the set of such times $s$ is of measure zero. If $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ then clearly we have $\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]=1$, and otherwise 
\eqref{e:gamma.prime} gives
	\[\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]
    =\frac{\E[(w_{\lambda(s)})^2 \ind\{
        \lambda(s)\le\tau\}]}
        {\gamma'(\lambda(s))}
    = 1\,.
    \]
We can then express the desired process as
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^t \tilde{w}_s\,d\tilde{W}(s)\,,
    \]
where $\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)= Y(q_0)$. This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416

body: Density of bilinear forms in independent vectors. If x, y in R^n are independent with coordinates of densities at most K, then x^T Z y + x^T u + v^T y + w has density at most 2 (C_RV K)^2 (2 e pi)^{1/2} min_{j >= 2} j^{-1/2} (sigma_1(Z) ... sigma_j(Z))^{-1/j} (J. Banks, J. Garza-Vargas, A. Kulkarni, N. Srivastava, Overlaps, eigenvalue gaps, and pseudospectrum under real Ginibre and absolutely continuous perturbations, arXiv:2005.08930, Corollary 2.4; Theorem 2.1 there treats matrices X, Y in R^{n x k}). The proof conditions on y: the form is linear in x with coefficient Z y + u, and E|Z y + u|^{-1} is finite once that vector has a bounded density in two or more dimensions. With rank one it fails, since E|t|^{-1} diverges for a scalar t with bounded density. In the bounded-density conjecture for x^T A x, a single hub coordinate X_h paired with its partner L = <w, X'> is exactly this rank-one bilinear case, which is why one hub needs a third large eigenvalue through a transverse square, while two hubs are the rank-two case and are bounded.

Let A be an m by n random matrix with independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian entries of proxy at most K. Then with probability at least 1 - 2 exp(-c t^2), the operator norm satisfies ||A|| <= C K (sqrt(m) + sqrt(n) + t), with absolute constants c, C. In particular ||A|| is of order sqrt(m) + sqrt(n) with high probability - the correct scale, matching the Bai-Yin limit for iid fourth-moment entries.

[Corollary 12 (Parametrization of the unique toroidal limit) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Assume the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:classification} and suppose that
$\Var_T\neq0$ and $\spt\Var_T$ has genus one.  Then there exists a
uniformly conformal bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism
\[
 f\in W^{2,2}(\Sigma,\R^4)\cap W^{1,\infty}(\Sigma,\R^4),
 \qquad
 f\colon\Sigma\longrightarrow M:=\spt\Var_T,
\]
and there are a smooth zero-scalar-curvature, unit-volume metric
$g_{\mathrm{poin}}$ on $\Sigma$ and a function $u\in L^\infty(\Sigma)$
such that
\begin{equation}
 
 f^*g_{\mathrm{euc}}=e^{2u}g_{\mathrm{poin}}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 
 \Var_T=v(M,1),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 
 \lVert\Var_T\rVert
 =f_\#\mu_{f^*g_{\mathrm{euc}}}
 =\mathcal H^2\llcorner M.
\end{equation}
In particular, formula \eqref{eq:limit-measure} is independent of the sequence
used to construct the parametrization $f$.

Let pi be a prior probability, let L(theta)=log p(D|theta) be finite pi-almost-surely, and let I be an open interval of positive inverse temperatures. Let q_lambda=e^(lambda L)pi/Z(lambda), with 0<Z(lambda)<infinity for lambda in I. Let f be a real measurable function independent of lambda. Explicit sufficient regularity for the source differentiation step is: for each compact K contained in I there is a pi-integrable H_K dominating e^(lambda L)(1+|f|)(1+|L|^2) for all lambda in K. Then d/dlambda E_q_lambda f=Cov_q_lambda(f,L). In particular the total-data Gibbs objective J(q_lambda)=-E_q_lambda L satisfies Jprime(lambda)=-Var_q_lambda(L)<=0. For the per-example objective Ghat=J/n, the derivative is -(1/n)Var_q_lambda(L). These two normalizations must not be interchanged. This is the AppendixA Eq14 quotient-rule identity with sufficient differentiation regularity made explicit; no globally strict decrease is asserted when the variance vanishes.

 |m_2(F)-\theta|
 +\frac{2q-1}{2q}\sqrt{\cP(F)}

 +\frac43\cP(F)
 \bigg].
\notag
\end{align}

[Corollary cor:contraction-with-cascade-coefficients-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let 
\(
q\in(1,2)
\),
\(r\ge2\), and let \(G\) be a finite set. Fix \(m\ge0\).
Suppose that the family
\[
(Z_u)_{\lvert u \rvert=m}
\]
is independent of \(\mathcal F^X_m\), that the vectors \(Z_u\) are independent
and coordinatewise mean zero, and that all \(Z_u\) have the same distribution
as a random vector \(Z\) with
\[
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q<\infty.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\left\|
\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u Z_u
\right\|_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\middle|\mathcal F^X_m
\right]
\le
C_q r^{q/2}
\left(\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u^q\right)
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\left\|
\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u Z_u
\right\|_{\ell^r(G)}^q
\right]
\le
C_q r^{q/2}\rho(q)^m
\mathbb{E}\lVert Z \rVert_{\ell^r(G)}^q.
\end{equation}

body:
OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Pair-balanced factual identities under partial verification

T379-C015 v2, proof (unaudited). Both exact verification suites PASS;
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending.
Targets 1 and 2. This is a conditional data-regime result, not a global
expected minimax claim. The unresolved unequal-sibling-count regime is
the hardest missing piece; C010 shows why its ordering cannot be assumed.

## Model and data region

Use the paired VC-d experiment: d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K integers;
one A and one S per pair, all remaining contexts known S. S has K true
candidates, A has an independent uniform r-subset. The source p chooses
contexts uniformly, then true candidates uniformly. Observe n>=0 iid
factual context/candidate samples without orientation tags. Independently
a perfect verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each
variable context, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Let C_x be the union of
distinct observed and verified candidate identities in context x.

Condition on any positive-probability data outcome for which every pair
has |C_left|=|C_right|=h_j<=r. The actual identities may differ. Thus no
orientation is logically excluded, and every one of 2^d orientations
is compatible. Counts and likelihoods of repeated observations can be
unequal: uniform orientation weights below are an ARTIFICIAL proof
distribution, not the actual Bayesian posterior. Under a chosen
orientation, the A support ranges uniformly over r-subsets containing
C_A. Put D_h=#{j:h_j=h}, ell<=h<=r.

Define

 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N),
 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)),
 M_h=(D_h/N)*(2-h/r-h/K),
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

Over ALL generators, with source Mis_infinity<=c required in every
compatible world (including every compatible A support), the proposed
exact conditional worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V_D(c)=tau_ell*(T_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h=ell+1}^r (tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.       (1)

All formulas allow missing D_h and c in [0,1]. Exact score bins define
source Mis_infinity=TV(g,p_Pi), with p uniformly coarsened in each bin.

## Lower bound across arbitrary mixed bins

Average orientations fairly and A supports uniformly conditional on
containing their known identities. Let mu be the resulting mean law.
Every known true atom in a variable context has density

 a=(1/r+1/K)/(2N).

The uncertified atoms of a pair at count h have density b_h and false
probability tau_h under this artificial prior. Their total mu mass is
M_h across the D_h pairs. Known S atoms have density 1/(NK).

As h increases, tau_h increases and b_h decreases: directly,
b_h-b_{h+1}=(K-r)/(2Nr(K-h)(K-h-1)) when h<r. All safe densities
are >=1/(NK)>=b_h. Thus E_h, the union of uncertified atoms in pairs
with count at least h, consists of lower-density atoms than its entire
complement. For ANY partition Pi, uniform coarsening increases its mass:

 mu_Pi(E_h)>=mu(E_h)=T_h.

Indeed in each cell the mean density over E_h is at most the mean over
its complement, so replacing both means by the cell mean transfers
mass into E_h. This proves the assertion per bin, not merely globally.

Robust feasibility and linearity/TV convexity give TV(mu_Pi(g),g)<=c.
Hence g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+. Layer-cake decomposition of the artificial
average false risk gives

 max_world H(g)>=tau_ell*g(E_ell)
                   +sum_{h>ell}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*g(E_h)
                >=V_D(c).

No joint-probability multiplication or actual-posterior identity is used.

## Matching construction

Start from mu. Remove mass min(c,T_ell) from uncertified groups in
decreasing h order, uniformly within each h group, and add it uniformly
to the fixed known S reservoir. All remaining g(E_h)=(T_h-c)_+.
Each pair's known-true group has h atoms from each sibling and invariant
source mass h*(1/r+1/K)/N. Its uncertified group has K-h atoms from
each sibling and invariant source mass (2-h/r-h/K)/N, regardless of
orientation or which residual truths occupy A. The constructed g is
constant on every such group. Exact score bins only merge invariant
groups, so p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world. Since g_Pi=g,
Mis_infinity<=TV(mu,g)<=c. The uncertified false-atom fraction in each
h group equals tau_h in every world. Thus actual H equals V_D(c)
worldwise, proving conditional sharpness of (1).

## Same-data oracle and exact estimation penalty

If the true partition is additionally supplied, let

 A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr), Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t,
 alpha_h=(K-r)/(K-h)=2tau_h.

The same-data known-partition frontier, by the ordered known-A groups,
is

 O_D(c)=alpha_ell*(Q_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h>ell}(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+.       (2)

Here A_h is the posterior mass of unknown true candidates of the actual
A contexts, and their densities decrease while their false risks rise.
The same mixed-bin tail proof and transfer-to-S construction apply.
Thus V_D(c)=O_D(c)+[V_D(c)-O_D(c)] is an exact matching decomposition,
with nonnegative difference because giving the partition enlarges
feasibility. At c=0 it simplifies to the explicit positive penalty

 V_D(0)-O_D(0)
   =sum_{h=ell}^r D_h*h*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h)).             (3)

The penalty is zero at h=0, and at h=r contributes kappa/(2N) per pair,
recovering C013's unresolved full-verifier value. In general it depends
on the factual-support histogram, not merely VC dimension or a single
unweighted classification-error scalar. A fair completion among the
2^d support-consistent ERM orientations has conditional expected
classification error 1/N per pair; (3) weights that error by
h*(K-r)^2/[2rK(K-h)]. This is a specified ERM, not an optimal posterior
classification claim. The conditional minimax lower bound is not
silently averaged into a global expected lower bound; C014 forbids
that shortcut at positive budgets.

## Scope

This removes supplied tags and retains actual factual identities for
every balanced outcome, all n,K,r,ell and all calibration budgets. It
allows different h across pairs, but does not cover unequal sibling
counts, already identified pairs, or an unconditional exact expected
frontier. Equal h in every pair reduces the conditional formula to the
corresponding earlier C008 experiment with that many known truths;
the histogram, actual untagged-data applicability and explicit oracle
penalty are the proposed extension, not a claim that C008 was unknown.
Primary basis: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9;
own earlier C008/C009 are unaudited drafts. No novelty or target score
is certified until independent mathematical and priority review.

## Extension: include identified pairs under a coverage ordering

The same theorem extends as follows. Partition the d pairs into resolved
and unresolved pairs. A resolved pair has a context with >r distinct
known truths, logically forcing S and identifying its sibling as A.
Let E_j count these known A contexts with j distinct known truths,
ell<=j<=r. Each unresolved pair still has balanced count h<=r; D_h
now counts just these unresolved pairs. Require

 j>=h_max for every resolved A, where
 h_max=max{h:D_h>0}.                                    (4)

If no unresolved pairs exist, condition (4) is vacuous. Known facts
in identified S and fixed S contexts are all safe and have density
1/(NK), irrespective of their observed identities or counts.

There are two positive-risk group types under the artificial compatible
prior (independent fair unresolved orientations and uniform compatible
A supports):

In the noiseless isotropic Gaussian teacher model with an independently specified probe at fixed theta in (0,pi/2], let E(alpha,theta) be the infimum of fixed-threshold max-margin limiting errors at retained aspect alpha, including no pruning f=1, with dimension limit first. For alpha>=1, sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*alpha)<=E(alpha,theta)<=1/alpha, so its large-alpha log-log exponent is -1. The lower bound is the retained-label latitude/counting argument C012, independent of original-pool size. For the upper bound keep all data: the classical Vapnik support-vector leave-one-out bound, reproduced in Burges 1998 Sec.7.4 Eq.(93), says expected risk of an m-point SVM is at most the expected support-vector fraction in m+1 iid points. Folded Gaussian rows have full density on the teacher half-space and affine general position, so a homogeneous minimum-norm hard-margin classifier has at most d active constraints almost surely, giving expected error<=d/(m+1). C007 and bounded convergence give unpruned limiting error<=1/alpha. The classical bound itself is not new; this is an unaudited application combined with C012. The constants leave a gap as theta->0. An exact crossover, initial exponential regime and optimal retained fraction are not established.

For compatible (y1, y2), the conditional law of X given Y1 = y1 and Y2 = y2 has mean m12 = m1 + D T^+ w and covariance K12 = K1 - D T^+ D^T, which coincide with the one-shot pseudoinverse formulas for the stacked observation (Y1, Y2). body:
Let X_1, ..., X_n be INDEPENDENT random variables with values in [0,1], let X = sum_i X_i and mu = E[X]. Then for every delta > 0, P(X >= (1 + delta) mu) <= ( e^{delta} / (1 + delta)^{1 + delta} )^{mu} <= exp( - delta^2 mu / (2 + delta) ), and for every delta in (0,1), P(X <= (1 - delta) mu) <= ( e^{-delta} / (1 - delta)^{1 - delta} )^{mu} <= exp( - delta^2 mu / 2 ). The two tails have DIFFERENT constants and the upper-tail exponent degrades from delta^2 mu/3 for delta <= 1 to roughly delta mu log delta for large delta; quoting the lower-tail constant 1/2 for the upper tail is a common error. The bounds hold with mu replaced by any upper bound on E[X] in the upper tail, and by any lower bound in the lower tail, which is how they are usually applied. The variables need only be independent and [0,1]-valued, not identically distributed and not Bernoulli. [standard; e.g. Mitzenmacher and Upfal, Probability and Computing, 2nd ed., Theorems 4.4 and 4.5]
X_1, ..., X_n independent with values in [0,1]
mu = E[X] (or an upper bound for the upper tail, a lower bound for the lower tail)
delta > 0 for the upper tail, delta in (0,1) for the lower tail

[Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Fix $n\in \Z_{\geq 1}$ and a set $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda_0(n)\subset \Lambda\subset \Lambda_1(n)$ (see Section \ref{subsection:coarsemapproper}). 
    Let $G$ be a closed subgroup of $\rmB(n)$.
    Then the composition $\mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G : G\to \R^{ \Lambda}$ is coarse.
    Here, $G$ is equipped with the LR-coarse structure, $\R^{\Lambda}$ is equipped with the bounded coarse structure (see Example \ref{example:coarse}) and $\iota_G$ is the inclusion map from $G$ to $\rmB(n)$.
    In particular, for closed subgroups $L,H$ of $G$, 
    if the pair $(\mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G(L), \mu_\Lambda\circ \iota_G(H))$ is asymptotically disjoint in $(\R^{ \Lambda},\mathcal{E}_d)$, 
    the natural $L$-action on $G/H$ is proper (see Corollary \ref{corollary:coarsemapproper}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 40 of arXiv:2608.25785

[Prop 24 (Tree-graph inequality) of arXiv:2510.23423, 'One-arm exponents of the high-dimensional Ising model'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a subgraph of $\mathbb Z^d$ and $\beta\geq 0$. Then, for every $x,y,z\in V$,
\begin{equation}
	\phi_{G,\beta}^0[x\connect{}y,z]\leq \sum_{u,u'\in V: \: u\sim u'}\phi_{G,\beta}^0[x\connect{}u']\phi_{G,\beta}^0[u'\connect{} z]\phi^0_{G,\beta}[u\connect{}y].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tree-graph inequality

body: [Definition 2.4 of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let G be a generator family of proper convex sets. The dual Radon number r⊤ G is the least integer m such that every m-element family F ⊆G has a nontrivial partition F = F1 ˙∪F2 satisfying conv \ F1 ∪ \ F2  ̸= X. If (X, C) is finite and G = B is its basis, then r⊤ B is exactly the Radon number of the dual convexity space.

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.20169, 'THEORY OF UNCERTAIN PROBABILITY:\\ CAN WE DERIVE THE PROBABILITY DENSITY FUNCTION OF UNCER'] If $\left(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U}\right)$ is an arbitrary measurable space, a function $\mathbb{X}$: $\Pi\rightarrow\mathcal{U}$ is a measurable map from $\left(\Pi, \mathbb{F}\right)$ to $\left(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U}\right)$ if 

$\mathbb{X}^{-1}(U)\equiv\left\{\boldsymbol{\pi}:\mathbb{X}(\boldsymbol{\pi})\in U\right\}\in\mathbb{F}$ for all $U\in\mathfrak{U}$.

If $(\mathcal{U},\mathfrak{U})=(\mathcal{R},\mathfrak{R})$, $\mathbb{X}$ is called an uncertain random variable.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.20169

[Lemma lem:HS-curvature-full of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] On a Riemann surface the Hitchin--Simpson curvature is of type $(1,1)$ and is
\begin{equation}
 R_{D_h}
 = R_h
  +[\theta,\theta_h^{*}].
\end{equation}
In particular,
\(
 \mathrm{tr}_E[\theta,\theta_h^{*}]=0
\), so
\(
 \mathrm{tr}_E R_{D_h}=\mathrm{tr}_E R_h
\).

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2606.15432, 'A Concavity Theorem for the Parisi PDE'] Let \(h_1,h_2\in \Hoelder{\alpha/2}([0,1])\).
Then, for all $(s,x)\in [0,1]\times \R$,
\begin{equation*}

D^2\Psi^\gamma[h_1,h_2](s,x)
=
-
\int_s^1
\iint_{[s,\sigma]^2}
h_1(\rho_1)h_2(\rho_2)
A^{\gamma,s,\sigma,x}(\rho_1\wedge\rho_2)
\dd\rho_1\dd\rho_2\dd{\sigma},
\end{equation*}
where
\begin{equation}
    
    A^{\gamma,s,\sigma,x}(\rho)
    =
    \frac12
    P_{s,\rho}^\gamma[L_\rho^\gamma w_{\rho,\sigma}^\gamma](x)
    +
    \frac{1}{4}
    \int_s^\rho
    P_{s,\tau}^\gamma
    \Bigl[
        \gamma(\tau)\tau 
        \partial_x P_{\tau,\rho}^\gamma[v^\gamma(\rho,\,\cdot\,)]
        \partial_x w_{\tau,\sigma}^\gamma
    \Bigr](x)
    \dd{\tau}
\end{equation}
with $\rho\in [s,\sigma]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2606.15432

body: In mathematical measure theory, for every positive integer n the ham sandwich theorem states that given n measurable "objects" in n-dimensional Euclidean space, it is possible to divide each one of them in half (with respect to their measure, e.g. volume) with a single (n − 1)-dimensional hyperplane. This is possible even if the objects overlap.
title: Ham sandwich theorem

For standard-zero-moment ordinary bias-corrected diagonal two-coordinate Adam with b=.9,d=.999,outside-sqrt epsilon and fixed positive eta,epsilon, suppose theta_h=eta*lambda_h/epsilon>38 and0<theta_l=eta*lambda_l/epsilon<=38. Active convergence to38 forces the low coordinate to its origin and the high coordinate to its origin or exact two-cycle, deriving both denominator limits. A persistent positive asymptotic top gap is equivalent to gradient norm tending to zero and squared high-gradient fraction tending to(38-theta_l)/(theta_h-theta_l). On the ENTIRE strict mixed range theta_h>38>theta_l>0, origin-rate separation makes this compensation impossible: active convergence to38 forces the high cycle and scaled top limit38. At theta_l=38, the top gap criterion remains vanishing gradient norm with high-gradient fraction tending to zero; the top limit is then theta_h. The gradient condition implies active convergence to38 and a positive top gap unconditionally under the stated assumptions; the reverse implication and orbit classification are conditional on012v2.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e934d48fb0362708de34878b61da317fd803f99e3874c114fa0e87beb2918f34","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e9/e934d48fb0362708de34878b61da317fd803f99e3874c114fa0e87beb2918f34.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a5c69602c4b73c6dc1a2e41bbfda398026619db98f1a1db0f8d6cf7c7297f00a","bundle_entry_key":"mixed-caps","bundle_id":"population.adam-zero-work-paths-mixed-cap-alignment-011","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"adaptive optimization and discrete dynamics","draft":"w706/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-mixed-cap-active-tracking-gradient-proportions-vanishing-gradient","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-024 v2; target2; kind narrowed; reviewer PASS conditional on012v2; B=>A unconditional.

STATEMENT
Fix eta,epsilon>0 and a positive diagonal quadratic in two coordinates.
Use ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam, b=.9,d=.999, outside-sqrt
epsilon and standard zero moments. Label the coordinates h,l so that

 theta_h=eta*lambda_h/epsilon>38,
 0<theta_l=eta*lambda_l/epsilon<=38.

Write g_i=lambda_i*x_i, P_i=sqrt(v_i,next/(1-d^(t+1)))+epsilon,
S_t=eta*max_i lambda_i/P_i, and A_t for scaled active sharpness.
All limits involving the active quotient or gradient proportion below
are along all their defined times, assumed to occur arbitrarily late.

If A_t->38, then the low-cap coordinate converges to its origin, and
the high-cap coordinate approaches either its origin or its exact
alternating cycle with position amplitude eta/38-epsilon/lambda_h.
In particular BOTH variance denominators converge automatically.

B=>A is unconditional; reverse implication and classification conditional on012v2. The conditions are:
 (A) A_t->38 and liminf S_t>38;
 (B) ||g_t||->0 and
       q_t=g_h,t^2/(g_h,t^2+g_l,t^2)
           -> q_star=(38-theta_l)/(theta_h-theta_l).       (1)
When these hold, S_t->theta_h. When A_t->38 through a nonzero high-cap
cycle instead, S_t->38. No convergence of denominators is assumed.

For theta_l=38, q_star=0: the gradient aligns with the CRITICAL low-cap
coordinate while its norm tends to zero. For theta_l<38, q_star lies
strictly between0 and1: (1) prescribes a nonzero relative contribution
from each vanishing gradient. This apparent strict-subcritical compensation is IMPOSSIBLE by025v1,
proofs/036_general_origin_rate_separation.md: an all-origin trajectory
has a subsequence of active sharpness tending to theta_l<38. If the low
initial position is zero, its coordinate is identically zero and the
all-origin active limit is instead theta_h>38. Consequently, whenever
theta_h>38>theta_l>0 and A_t->38, the high coordinate MUST cycle and
S_t->38. A persistent asymptotic top gap is impossible on the entire
strict mixed-cap range. The critical case theta_l=38 remains governed
by(1), with q_star=0 and both gradients vanishing.

For p=1, epsilon=eta, the conditions are lambda_h>38>=lambda_l>0;
q_star=(38-lambda_l)/(lambda_h-lambda_l), and the top limit is lambda_h.
This is a whole mixed-cap parameter-range classification conditional
on active tracking, not an additional isolated example.

AUDIT / HARDEST DEPENDENCY
Reviewer claude-738954b6 checked024v2 step by step, initially conditional
on012v2. The exact012v2 PASS (21 Oct01:4x) discharges that condition;
its reviewer row explicitly confirms024v2 now stands without conditions.
Claims023v1 and025v1 lemma are independently PASS as well. Both(A)=>(B)
and(B)=>(A), the tracking-forced orbit classification and strict mixed-cap
exclusion therefore stand under the displayed algorithm/parameter
assumptions. Tracking itself is still a hypothesis, not a typical-start
conclusion. This proof avoids source piecewise-potential strictness,
Conley trapping and scalar unstable-basin claims015/019/021.

1. DECAY OF THE LOW-CAP COORDINATE
Claim012v2, proofs/015_global_subcritical_critical.md, gives
x_l,m_l,v_l->0, including the critical cap theta_l=38. Thus
g_l->0 and P_l->epsilon. The absorbing argument in033 Section1 gives
boundedness of the high-cap physical state; it uses only the elementary
standard-moment Cauchy--Schwarz and bounded increments, not claim022.

2. TRACKING FORCES ZERO HIGH-COORDINATE WORK ON ITS OMEGA SET
The exact active identity is

 sum_i (g_i^2/P_i)*(eta*lambda_i/P_i-38)
    =(A_t-38)*sum_i g_i^2/P_i.                           (2)

The final sum is bounded because epsilon>0 and the physical trajectory
is bounded. At zero-gradient times extend both sides by zero. The
low-coordinate term tends to zero; hence the high-coordinate work
tends to zero along ALL times when A_t->38 along defined times.

For FIXED positive eta,epsilon, the corrected physical maps converge
uniformly on bounded states to the raw continuous Adam map. Thus the
high-coordinate omega set is compact, has incoming and outgoing raw
edges, and every point lies on a bounded full raw path in that set.
Passing (2) to each edge gives

 x_h^2*(eta*lambda_h/P_h-38)=0.

After normalizing X=x_h/eta,M=m_h/(eta*lambda_h),
V=v_h/(eta*lambda_h)^2,rho=epsilon/(eta*lambda_h), this is exactly
(ZW) of023, with D=1/38 and 0<rho<D. By023 every full path is an origin
or an exact cycle. Therefore the omega set is contained in these three
physical states. The actual tail approaches this finite set. Uniform
convergence of corrected maps and continuity of the raw map imply that
each sufficiently late step near a critical state goes near its unique
critical successor. Separation of the origin and the two cycle phases
therefore forces the tail to stay in ONE orbit group, with alternating
phases in the cycle case. This proves the asserted convergence and
does not invoke a global theorem about arbitrary omega-limit sets.

3. PROJECT THE TWO POSSIBLE LIMITS TO ACTIVE/TOP SHARPNESS
If the high coordinate cycles, P_h->eta*lambda_h/38, P_l->epsilon,
and |g_h| has positive limiting amplitude. Thus its active weight
dominates the vanishing low weight, A_t->38 and S_t->max(38,theta_l)=38.

If the high coordinate tends to its origin, both gradients and raw
variances tend to zero, so P_h,P_l->epsilon. Uniformly in the relative
gradient magnitudes, the weighted active formula gives

 A_t=theta_l+(theta_h-theta_l)*q_t+o(1).                 (3)

For example divide numerator and denominator by g_h^2+g_l^2: the two
coefficient arrays converge to fixed constants, and the denominator
is bounded away from zero since P_i->epsilon>0. Therefore A_t->38
if and only if q_t->q_star. Also S_t->theta_h>38.

Consequently(A) rules out the high cycle and implies(B). Conversely
(B), independently of any origin classification, implies v_i->0 by
the stable variance filters, hence P_i->epsilon. Formula(3) proves
A_t->38, while S_t->theta_h. This proves the equivalence and top limit.

LIMITS OF THE CLAIM
The theorem is a necessary-and-sufficient asymptotic GRADIENT condition;
it is not an existence claim or an initialization-basin classification.
By025, comparable vanishing gradients with the prescribed fraction
cannot actually occur under active tracking in the strict-subcritical case. Generalization beyond diagonal Adam,
outside-sqrt epsilon, fixed positive parameters or standard moments
requires another argument. Exact-version review is complete;012v2 dependency discharged.


FINITE-RUN DIAGNOSTIC (NOT AN ASYMPTOTIC THEOREM)
Tracking was not observed in the reviewer's three p=1 starts with cap
pairs(60,20),(45,37.9),(200,1): the reported A_t wandered about32--38.8
through t=18000 with intermittent high-coordinate bursts. See
logs/reviewer_c024_check_out.txt and reviewer_c024_trace_out.txt.
These finite deterministic traces do not prove asymptotic nontracking
or describe all generic starts. The classification assumes tracking;
it is not evidence that tracking is typical.

Pollett's Section 2 conjecture (ii) asks whether, for a lambda-transient irreducible countable transient class with almost sure absorption, every finite strictly positive limit of t^a e^{lambda t} p_t(i,j) must factor as A x_i m_j. Our result (id P0288, 2026-09-08): NO. Take the nearest-neighbour continuous-time walk on Z (rate 1 each side), killed at rate kappa everywhere plus an extra rate v at the origin. The class is lambda-transient with lambda = kappa, and t^{3/2} e^{kappa t} p_t(i,j) tends to [(|i| + 2/v)(|j| + 2/v) + i j] / (4 sqrt pi). The i j term makes the limit a rank-two form - its 2x2 minor on rows and columns {0,1} equals (2/v)^2/(16 pi) > 0 for every v - so no rank-one A x_i m_j factorisation exists; the reason is structural, a chain with two ends carries one degree of freedom per end. Verification as the source words it: the Feynman-Kac semigroup was solved directly at t = 100, 400, 1600, 6400, and against the claimed limits 0.141047, 0.282095, 0.705237, 0.423142 for (i,j) = (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,-1) at v = 2 the computed values converge monotonically to 0.141010, 0.282004, 0.705018, 0.422932, with the minor formed from the measured entries 0.019879 against the predicted 0.019894. PRIOR ART WARNING carried in the ledger row itself: Foley and McDonald published a discrete two-end construction from which the same continuous-time obstruction follows, so treat this as confirmed mathematics and probably known.

body: In mathematics, the gamma function is the most common extension of the factorial function to complex numbers. First studied by Daniel Bernoulli, the gamma function is defined for all complex numbers except non-positive integers, and for every positive integer ⁠⁠. The gamma function can be defined via a convergent improper integral for complex numbers with positive real part: The gamma function then is defined in the complex plane as the analytic continuation of this integral function: it is a meromorphic function which is holomorphic except at zero and the negative integers, where it has simple poles.

body: In linear algebra, the Cholesky decomposition or Cholesky factorization is a decomposition of a Hermitian, positive-definite matrix into the product of a lower triangular matrix and its conjugate transpose, which is useful for efficient numerical solutions, e.g., Monte Carlo simulations. It was discovered by André-Louis Cholesky for real matrices, and posthumously published in 1924. When it is applicable, the Cholesky decomposition is roughly twice as efficient as the LU decomposition for solving systems of linear equations.

[Lemma 45 (Watson's Lemma) of arXiv:2511.13559, 'Asymptotic analysis of rare events in high dimensions'] Let $f,h\in C^L([0,T])$ and suppose  $h(0)=0$ and $h'(t)>b>0$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. Define the operator $D_h$ by $(D_hf)(t):=\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{f(t)}{h'(t)}\right)$. Then
\be
\int_0^Tf(t)e^{-\la h(t)}\dd t=\frac{1}{h'(0)}\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}(D_h^{k-1}f)(0)\la^{-k}+\Rem_{L},
\ee where
\bs
|\Rem_{L}|\leq  b^{-1}\|D_h^{L-1}f\|_\infty\la^{-L} + b^{-1}e^{-\la b T}\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}\la^{-k}|(D_h^{k-1}f)(T)|.
\es Here, $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ denotes the sup norm over the interval $[0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 17 (Secant row-sum identity) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $X,Y\in \mathrm{St}(n,k)$ and set $K=Y-X$. Define
\[
q_{ij}=r_i(X)\cdot r_j(K)-r_j(X)\cdot r_i(K),\qquad 1\leq i<j\leq n.
\]
Then
\be
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}
=\|K\|_{F}^{2}-\mathrm{Tr}\bigl((K^{\top}X)^{2}\bigr).
\ee
Moreover,
\be
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}
\geq \|K\|_{F}^{2}-\frac14\|K\|_{F}^{4}.
\ee
In particular, if $\|K\|_{F}\leq 1$, then
\[
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}\geq \frac34\|K\|_{F}^{2}.
\]

    Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the family of self avoiding walk trees of graphs in $\mathcal{G}$.

    \begin{equation}
        | {F}_{T,n,\Vec{\lambda}}(r') -{F}_{T,n}(r)|\leq \eta_1.
    \end{equation}

body: In topology, a surface is a two-dimensional manifold. Some surfaces arise as the boundaries of three-dimensional solid figures; for example, the sphere is the boundary of the solid ball. Other surfaces arise as graphs of functions of two variables; see the figure at right. However, surfaces can also be defined abstractly, without reference to any ambient space. For example, the Klein bottle is a surface that cannot be embedded in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
title: Surface (topology)

[Theorem 6 (Matrix Freedman) of arXiv:2604.27119, '\Large Applied Random Matrix Theory\relatedversion'] Consider a finite matrix martingale sequence $(\mtx{S}_0, \dots, \mtx{S}_n)$
consisting of $d_1 \times d_2$ matrices, real or complex.

Suppose that the elements of the difference sequence 
$(\mtx{X}_1, \dots, \mtx{X}_n)$ are uniformly bounded:
$\norm{ \mtx{X}_k } \leq B$.

Introduce the \term{conditional quadratic variation} sequence:
\[
V_k \coloneqq
	\lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j \mtx{X}_j^* \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\vee \lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j^* \mtx{X}_j \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\quad\text{for $k = 1, \dots, n$.}
\]
For parameters $v, t \geq 0$, we have the probability inequalities
\begin{align}

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq \sqrt{2 v t} + Bt/3 \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \, \econst^{-t}; \\

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq t \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \exp\left( \frac{-t^2/2}{v + Bt/3} \right).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be bounded and open with $C^1$ boundary, $T>0$, and let $u,\tilde u$ be smooth on $\overline{U_T}$ and solve $u_t=\Delta u$ and $\tilde u_t=\Delta\tilde u$ in $U_T$ with the same values on $\partial U\times[0,T]$. If $u(\cdot,T)=\tilde u(\cdot,T)$ in $U$, then $u\equiv\tilde u$ in $\overline{U_T}$: two solutions that agree at one later time agreed all along. (Regularity up to the boundary is load-bearing only through what the proof uses: the difference must lie in $H^1_0(U)$ at each time and the integrations by parts below must be legitimate; mere continuity on $\overline{U_T}$ with no regularity of $\partial U$ does not supply this.) Quantitatively, for the difference $w$ the function $t\mapsto\log\|w(t)\|_{L^2(U)}^2$ is convex on $[0,T]$, so $\|w(t)\|_{L^2}\le\|w(0)\|_{L^2}^{1-t/T}\,\|w(T)\|_{L^2}^{t/T}$ (conditional stability of Holder type for $0<t<T$). The abstract form: if $A$ is a nonnegative self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $H$ and $v(t)=e^{-tA}v_0$, then $\|v(t)\|^2$ is log-convex and $v(T)=0$ forces $v_0=0$. Backward uniqueness must not be confused with backward stability or backward solvability, both of which fail.
U bounded open in R^n with C^1 boundary
u, tilde u smooth on the closure of U_T and solving the heat equation in U_T (enough regularity that the difference lies in H^1_0(U) at each time and the integrations by parts are valid)
u = tilde u on the lateral boundary partial U x [0,T]
u(.,T) = tilde u(.,T) on U
abstract version: A nonnegative self-adjoint on a Hilbert space, v(t) = e^{-tA} v_0

A function holomorphic on an open set U equals its Taylor series locally: around any z0 in U it has a power series expansion converging on every disk centered at z0 contained in U. In particular holomorphic functions are infinitely differentiable.

Assuming one-way functions, the GPX posterior-hard family admits positive smooth polynomial-LSI regularizations with bounded covariance, polynomial-time generative descriptions and polynomially accurate computable forward-score networks. Their actual LSI constants lie between D^100/96 and O(D^206(log D)^2); norm-one selector observations with noise Theta((log D)^-2) put their ratios between Omega(D^100(log D)^4) and O(D^206(log D)^6). A polynomial-time posterior sampler achieving TV 10^-6 for at least 1-10^-6 of observations would contradict GPX hardness. The computational interface is polynomial-accuracy score networks, not a unit-cost exact-score oracle. No novelty or independent-check claim.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:869d142b2cb0ffd730879486ba8359ad49b02ade4d4afdfee77a95ce06c53e74","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/86/869d142b2cb0ffd730879486ba8359ad49b02ade4d4afdfee77a95ce06c53e74.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:82be63b4d1a0152de4f95ca510e74289e5b6f6f317b225f3e19864a386ec4e40","bundle_entry_key":"draft-posterior-hardness-polynomial-lsi-regularization","bundle_id":"population.w740-t411-c007-v2-reviewed-supersede","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"posterior sampling and functional inequalities","draft":"w740/bundle_003_r1.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.sampling:draft-posterior-hardness-polynomial-lsi-regularization","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Posterior-sampling hardness with polynomial log-Sobolev priors — C007 v2

Status: proof (unaudited). Source/interface inspection, the 31 original checks, and constructive lemma C008 with 38 additional exact coefficient checks recorded; independent review remains required. This is a proposed proof of T411 Target 2. It makes no novelty claim. Target 1 remains open.

## Computational scope and statement

Use the computational model of Gupta, Jalal, Parulekar, Price and Xun, arXiv:2402.12727v2: a diffusion prior is supplied through polynomial-size, polynomially bounded, effectively constructible approximate forward-score networks. Gaussian sampling primitives and polynomial-precision computations are understood as in that source. This is not a lower bound against a unit-cost oracle for exact prior scores.

Assume one-way functions exist. For all sufficiently large ambient dimensions D in the source's hard family, there are positive smooth priors M_D, coordinate-selector matrices A_D of norm one, and Gaussian observation standard deviations sigma_D=Theta((log D)^(-2)), with the following properties.

* The priors have explicit polynomial-time generative descriptions, bounded covariance operator, and polynomially accurate forward scores witnessed by polynomial-size ReLU networks (specifically 8-well-modeled in Definition 1.1).
* Their actual optimal LSI constants satisfy

  D^100/96 <= C_LS(M_D) <= C D^206 (log D)^2.

* Therefore their actual observation ratios satisfy

  c D^100 (log D)^4 <= ||A_D||^2 C_LS(M_D)/sigma_D^2
       <= C' D^206 (log D)^6.

* There is no polynomial-time sampler which, with probability at least 1-10^(-6) over observations, outputs a law within TV 10^(-6) of the posterior, using the stated computable score interface and the generative description. Such a sampler would invert a one-way function.

Constants may depend on the fixed source construction, not on D. The polynomial exponents are chosen to keep the approximation budget explicit; no optimal exponent or matching boundary is asserted.

The LSI convention is Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E||grad f||^2. The final priors contain nondegenerate Gaussian noise: the finite-coin approximation below is of the center sampler, not a claim that a discrete finite-grid output approximates a continuous law in TV.

## 1. Primary-source input

Take the hard family P_D from Theorem 1.8 / Lemma 3.5 of Gupta et al. The construction is Definition 3.2, scaled in Definition 3.3; its well-modeled score networks are Corollary 3.6, with their construction completed in Appendix C.8. It has these properties:

1. A_D selects the encoded last coordinates, so A_D A_D^T=I and ||A_D||=1. Observation noise is beta_D=Theta((log D)^(-2)). A (1/10,1/10) posterior sampler, in Definitions 1.2 and 1.5, would contradict one-way-function hardness. The success probability is over the observation.
2. P_D is 10-well-modeled: at every D^(-10)<=v<=D^10 its smoothed score has squared L2 approximation error less than D^(-10)/v^2, by a polynomial-size network with polynomially bounded weights. These are the source's effective constructions from the forward one-way-function circuit; no preimage is supplied.
3. Each seed is uniform fair bits. Given the seed, the first coordinates are independent N(seed_i,1/R_D^2). Each remaining coordinate is an independent phase-0 or phase-half discretized centered Gaussian, divided by R_D, where R_D=Theta(log D), and its phase is specified by the forward function of the seed. The unscaled grid spacing and its reciprocal are polynomially bounded.

C008 supplies an explicit polynomial-time construction for the scalar phase-lattice score networks. Its exact assumptions, normalized summation algorithm, truncation bounds, finite-precision error budget, rational ReLU interpolation and Gaussian tail proof are in proofs/C008_uniform_phase_lattice_scores.md. This replaces the sketch of effective scalar-network generation in C007 v1; it does not assume that network existence alone implies an algorithm.

Choose a fixed K large enough to include the source scalar grid spacings, smoothing scales and rescalings by R_D. C008 gives squared scalar score error at most 3D^(-2q), and output magnitude O((q+K)log D/u), for any fixed sufficiently large q. Taking q>K+1 gives precisely the bounded-output form needed by the source's scalar primitive construction in Lemma C.11. The source's polynomial-size, constant-depth network compositions have polynomial sensitivity to inverse-polynomial coefficient rounding; enlarge q by that fixed sensitivity exponent and by the coordinate-summation budget. The construction constant in the source can be fixed sufficiently large once to accommodate these error budgets. All exponents are fixed before D varies.

Lemma C.15 (PDF p.32) explicitly composes a vertex decoder, the forward circuit, these scalar score primitives, and ReLU switches. At large scales Lemmas C.19/C.20 (PDF p.38) use product two-Gaussian-mixture scores; those are finite Gaussian sums with explicitly evaluable coefficients and the same polynomial-window interpolation argument. Ordinary conditional Gaussian scores are linear. Consequently the forward networks used below are generated with polynomial work and polynomial precision. No conditional seed probability or circuit inverse is computed. The model remains polynomial-accuracy Gaussian primitives, not an exact-real score oracle.

Both phase lattices are symmetric about zero. Therefore E P_D=0; its raw second-moment operator is bounded by an absolute constant, also stated in the well-modeled condition. The first coordinate is exactly

(1/2)N(1,1/R_D^2)+(1/2)N(-1,1/R_D^2).

The conditional lattice Gaussian has uniform Gaussian-type tails for the source spacings <=1: its normalizer is bounded below by c/epsilon, and its tail sums are bounded above by C exp(-T^2/4)/epsilon. These bounds follow by counting grid points in [-1,1] and comparing the tails with the Gaussian integral. In particular all coordinate fourth moments are uniformly bounded and E||X||^4=O(D^2). No independence between the different encoded phase choices is needed for this fourth-moment conclusion.

## 2. A finite-coin center sampler

There is a polynomial-coin deterministic map S_D:{-1,1}^k->R^D, k=O(D log D), such that

W2(P_D,Law(S_D)) <= D^(-130),
||S_D(b)|| <= B_D:=4D^2 for all b,
E[S_D S_D^T] <= K I

for an absolute K and all sufficiently large D. Here is a finite algorithmic construction, not an enumeration of the exponentially many seeds.

Sample the seed with its exact fair bits and evaluate its forward circuit. For each scalar Gaussian or phase-lattice Gaussian primitive, truncate the unscaled variable at absolute value D. The tail second-moment contribution is exponentially small in D^2, uniformly in the two lattice phases; this uses the preceding elementary tail-sum comparison. For a continuous Gaussian, quantize its truncated value to mesh D^(-300). For a lattice primitive retain the actual grid points in [-D,D]. There are polynomially many points because the grid reciprocal is polynomially bounded.

For each of the Gaussian and two lattice-phase tables, approximate its finite probabilities by nonnegative dyadic probabilities, of common denominator 2^b, with total mass one and total variation error at most D^(-1000). One can round all but one weight down and assign the remaining mass to the last cell; use b large enough that the number of cells times 2^(-b) is below the requested error, and compute each weight to a further fixed number of guard bits. Thus b=O(log D), with a sufficiently large fixed constant. The Gaussian bin probabilities and lattice weights are computable to this precision in polynomial time, for example by Taylor approximation and integration on the bounded interval; their arguments have polynomial size. Standard elementary series likewise approximate R_D and the grid spacing to the finer mesh precision. No inversion of the forward circuit occurs.

Use b fresh fair bits and the dyadic CDF to choose a cell exactly, independently for each primitive. Couple this with the ideal primitive by a common-part coupling on the finite cells. On a table mismatch the squared unscaled error is at most O(D^2); the total mismatch probability over O(D) coordinates is O(D^(-999)). On a match, continuous quantization contributes at most D^(-300) per coordinate, and parameter rounding can be made smaller. Gaussian and lattice tail second moments contribute exp(-cD^2) times a polynomial. Summing the squared errors proves the stated global W2 bound for sufficiently large D. All values after division by R_D>=1 have absolute value at most 3D, so the norm bound 4D^2 is valid. The tables and the circuit have polynomial descriptions and are built in polynomial time. The number of random bits is O(D log D), even if a deliberately inefficient polynomial-size table is used.

Finally, for each unit vector v, this coupling gives

E(v.S_D)^2 <=2E(v.X)^2+2E||S_D-X||^2 <=K.

Thus bounded covariance is preserved without multiplying a tiny TV error by the square of an unnecessarily enormous output cutoff.

## 3. Regularize to polynomial LSI

Put r=D^(-20), a=D^(-100), h=a/k. Apply C006 to S_D, using fresh standard Gaussians Z in R^k and W in R^D:

c(z)=min(1,min_i |z_i|/h),
F(z)=c(z)S_D(sign z),
M_D=Law(F(Z)+rW).

It has a positive smooth density, bounded covariance operator, and

C_LS(M_D)<=B_D^2 k^2/a^2+r^2
 <=16 k^2 D^204+r^2 <=C D^206(log D)^2.

It is explicitly samplable using the given forward circuit and Gaussian randomness.

Let P_r=P_D*N(0,r^2 I). Gaussian translation gives

TV(Law(S_D+rW),P_r) <=W2(P_D,Law(S_D))/r <=D^(-110).

For clarity, the translation estimate follows by integrating the absolute directional derivative of the Gaussian density: TV(N(x,r^2I),N(x',r^2I))<=||x-x'||/r. Integrate this over the displayed coupling and use Cauchy--Schwarz. No density of the unsmoothed P_D is required.

C006 and the triangle inequality therefore give TV(M_D,P_r)<=a+D^(-110)<=2a.

The prior score is also globally Lipschitz with a polynomial bound: if V=F(Z), then ||V||<=B_D, and Gaussian convolution gives Hess log p(x)=-I/r^2+Cov(V|V+rW=x)/r^4. Its operator norm is at most r^(-2)+B_D^2 r^(-4)=poly(D). This is a regularity statement, not a polynomial exact-score evaluation algorithm.

## 4. Preserve effective forward-score networks

For D^(-8)<=u<=D^8 put v=sqrt(u^2+r^2). For large D, D^(-10)<=v<=D^10. The u-smoothed score of P_r equals the v-smoothed score of P_D. Use its source network and clip each output to [-D/u,D/u]. The clipping is an explicit ReLU operation with coefficients polynomially bounded on the scale interval.

Apply C005 with P=P_r, Q=M_D, L=D and TV distance at most 2a. The squared score error under (M_D)_u is at most

[2D^(-10)+12D exp(-D^2/2)+16aD(D^2+1)]/u^2 <=D^(-8)/u^2

for all sufficiently large D. This estimate is uniform over the full scale interval. For an explicit eventual bound, the degree-nine Taylor term gives exp(D^2/2)>12D^11 once D>=32; the remaining polynomial terms are smaller than D^(-10) for sufficiently large D. Hence the numerator is at most 4D^(-10), below D^(-8).

Together with bounded covariance, these clipped networks witness 8-well-modeledness. Their descriptions are computed by taking the source network at v and adding the clipping layer. The construction uses only the forward circuit and polynomial-precision scalar parameters. It does not approximate exact prior scores to arbitrarily requested accuracy and does not furnish unit-cost exact-score access.

## 5. The actual optimal LSI lies in a polynomial regime

The first marginal of P_r is the symmetric mixture of N(+1,t^2) and N(-1,t^2), where t^2=R_D^(-2)+r^2. Its probability in [-1/4,1/4] is at most 2 exp(-9/(32t^2)). Since R_D=Theta(log D) and r=D^(-20), this is at most a=D^(-100) for sufficiently large D. The symmetry makes each outside plateau have mass at least (1-a)/2.

The TV bound to M_D gives belt mass at most 3a and each outside plateau mass at least (1-5a)/2>=2/5. Let f be zero for x_1<=-1/4, one for x_1>=1/4, and linear between. Its squared gradient is 4 in the belt and zero outside, so its energy is at most 12a. Two independent copies show Var(f)>=4/25>1/8. Therefore

C_P(M_D)>=1/(96a)=D^100/96,
C_LS(M_D)>=C_P(M_D).

This is a lower bound on the actual optimal LSI constant. No irrelevant dummy coordinate or inflated LSI certificate is used to obtain a large observation ratio.

## 6. Transfer a posterior sampler back to the hard source

Write beta=beta_D, A=A_D, and choose sigma=sqrt(beta^2-r^2)>0. Positivity and sigma=Theta(beta) hold for sufficiently large D. Under the common coupling

X~P_D,  X_r=X+rW,  Y=A X_r+sigma E,

the joint law of (X,Y) is exactly the source model with noise beta: A A^T=I, so rAW+sigma E is N(0,beta^2 I), independent of X. The marginal law of (X_r,Y) is the P_r prior with independent observation noise sigma. This equality is before conditioning; W need not be independent of Y afterward.

For tau=1/100 let e_y be the conditional probability that ||X_r-X||>tau in this coupling. Since E||rW||^2=D^(-39),

E_Y e_y <=10^4 D^(-39).

Markov's inequality implies e_y<=1/100 outside an observation set of probability at most 10^6 D^(-39).

Suppose a polynomial-time M_D posterior sampler has TV error <=epsilon_0=10^(-6) with probability at least 1-epsilon_0 over its observations. Denote its output law at y by Q_y and let q(y)=TV(Q_y,M_D(.|y)). Since TV is at most one, E_{(M_D)_Y}q<=2epsilon_0. Observation marginalization contracts TV, so changing the Y law to that of P_r costs at most 2a. The conditional-TV averaging inequality proved in C002 gives

E_{(P_r)_Y} TV(M_D(.|Y),P_r(.|Y)) <=2TV(M_D,P_r)<=4a.

Consequently

E_{(P_r)_Y} TV(Q_Y,P_r(.|Y)) <=2epsilon_0+6a.

Markov at 1/100 makes the bad-observation probability at most 200epsilon_0+600a=0.0002+600a. On the remaining observations, couple Q_y to P_r(.|y) with failure at most 1/100, and then use the conditional coupling of X_r to X, with norm error at most 1/100 except on probability 1/100. The gluing lemma for couplings and a union bound give (1/100,2/100)-closeness to P_D(.|y).

The total bad-observation probability is at most

0.0002+600D^(-100)+10^6 D^(-39),

which is below 1/10 for sufficiently large D. This is stronger than the forbidden (1/10,1/10) source posterior guarantee. All wrapper computations, forward-score network calls and generative descriptions are polynomial, so the hypothetical sampler contradicts the source's one-way-function lower bound.

## 7. Observation ratio and conclusion

The same selector A has norm one and sigma^2=Theta((log D)^(-4)). Combining the two-sided prior LSI bounds with this noise scale gives exactly the two-sided polynomial bounds in the statement. Thus the construction lies in the polynomial-LSI class and the polynomial observation-ratio regime of Target 2, in the stated approximate-score interface.

This proof neither resolves Target 1 nor establishes a sharp transition. Its cryptographic assumption and hardness source are Gupta et al.; the proposed extension consists of the explicit polynomial-LSI regularization and preservation of their computable score interface. body: The union-closed sets conjecture, also known as Frankl’s conjecture, is an open problem in combinatorics posed by Péter Frankl in 1979. A family of sets is said to be union-closed if the union of any two sets from the family belongs to the family. The conjecture states: For every finite union-closed family of sets, other than the empty family, there exists an element that belongs to at least half of the sets in the family.

[Lemma Analogue of lemma 3.9 of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $u_0\in L^\infty(M)\cap L^r(M)$, $1\leq r\leq +\infty$.
    Let $b=b(r)=\frac{(n-1)^2}{2\max(2,r)}K_1$ (it is 0 if $r=+\infty$). There exist three functions $F_1,F_2,F_3:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ such that for every $t>0$, $x\in M$, the following holds for $\alpha>\frac{n-2}{4}$ and $\rho >0$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $\frac{n-2}{4}<\alpha<\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_1(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha=\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_2(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha>\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_3(\rho)^k.$$
    \end{enumerate}
    Here $C>0$ depends on $\alpha,K_1,n,$ and $r$. 
    The functions $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to \mathbb{R}_+$ are differentiable and satisfy the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For $i\in \set{1,2,3}$, and $K_1>0$ we have  
        \[ \dv{F_i}{\rho}<0,\quad\sup_{\rho\in\mathbb{R}_+}F_i(\rho)=F_i(0)<\infty,\text{ and }\lim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty}F_i(\rho)=0.\]
        
        Note that this implies $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to (0,F_i(0)]$ is invertible.
        \item For $K_1>0$, we have the asymptotics \begin{equation}
        F_i(\rho)\sim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty} \begin{cases}
            \left(\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^{2\alpha-\frac{n}{2}+1}& i=1,\\
                \frac{(\ln \rho)^2}{\rho}& i=2,\\

[Theorem thm:cycle of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] Let $\a_2, \ldots, \a_K : {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be differentiable functions with bounded derivatives, where $K \geq 2$ is an integer independent of $N$, and fix $y_0 > 0$. Let $\phi : {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ be the test function
	\[ \phi(x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y)\, f_k^N(x)\,, \]
and let $\varphi(x,y) \coloneqq \phi(x, y/a_N)$ on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} _N \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $. Then with $T = N \lfloor y_0 a_N \rfloor$,
	\[ \frac{1}{N} \langle \! \langle D_T,\, \varphi \rangle \! \rangle
	\Rightarrow \ensuremath{\mathcal N}\!\left( 0\,, \sum_{k=2}^K \a_k(y_0)^2\, \frac{1 - e^{-2\g_k y_0}}{2 \g_k} \right) \]
as $N \to \infty$, where $\g_k = \sqrt{2}\,\pi\,\lfloor k/2 \rfloor$.

body: Let (X, ||.||) be a normed vector space over R or C. There exists an inner product <.,.> on X with ||x||^2 = <x,x> for every x in X if and only if the norm satisfies the parallelogram law: ||x+y||^2 + ||x-y||^2 = 2||x||^2 + 2||y||^2 for all x, y in X. When this holds, the inner product is recovered from the norm by the polarization identity. [Jordan and von Neumann (1935); see Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Parallelogram-Law Characterization of Inner-Product Norms

[Lemma 37 (Ergodicity of the Palm version) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group and $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. Let $\mathbf Y$ be a Poisson point process on $X$ with intensity $c \, {\rm vol}$ for some $c>0$ and with iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$-marks. Let $\mathbf Y_0=\mathbf Y \cup \{\mathbf o\}$, where $\mathbf o$ is equipped with an independent ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$-mark. Then the following hold:
\begin{itemize} 
\item[{\rm(1)}] Let $A$ be a $G$-invariant event and let $A_0$ be the restriction of $A$ to configurations containing the origin. Then $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in A_0)=\mathbb P(\mathbf Y\in A)\in \{0,1\}$.
\item[{\rm(2)}] Let $B_0$ be an event such that $B_0=B'$, where $B'$ is the restriction of the event $B:=GB_0$ to configurations that contain the origin.
Then $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in B_0)=\mathbb P(\mathbf Y\in B)$. In particular, $\mathbb P(\mathbf Y_0\in B_0)\in\{0,1\}$.
\end{itemize}
The same conclusions hold when $\mathbf Y$ is replaced with the unmarked Poisson point process $Y$ and $\mathbf Y_0$ is replaced with $Y_0=Y\cup\{o\}$.

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the combinatorial identities (layer = second-largest branch height, maximum layer = floor(diam/2) <= height) were verified by brute-force leaf stripping on 40 random recursive trees of sizes 6 to 120 (480 vertices), with the 5-vertex path as a control] This is the layer part of the campaign answer to Conjecture 2 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. For each integer n>=3, let T_n be a random recursive tree on vertices 1,...,n, in which each vertex j>=2 chooses its parent independently and uniformly from 1,...,j-1. Repeatedly remove all vertices of degree at most one, assigning layer zero to the first removed set and successively increasing the layer. Let L_n be the maximum layer. As n tends to infinity, L_n=e log n-(3/2)log log n+O_P(1), where logarithms are natural and O_P(1) means that the centered sequence is bounded in probability. Under this removal rule, L_n=floor(diameter(T_n)/2); other conventions for the last vertex left standing change the maximum by at most one. The proof uses the recursive-tree height estimate of Addario-Berry and Ford (Corollary 1.3) and the fact that the root's normalized subtree sizes have a stick-breaking limit whose second-largest term is positive almost surely. The maximum-rank part of Conjecture 2 is not addressed. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

[Proposition prop:seven of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] For fixed atoms $(t_i,z_i)$, the admissible weight vectors $p$ form a
polytope cut out by at most $7$ linear equalities, and the worst weight
vector (minimizing $E$) may be taken at a basic feasible solution, of support
at most $7$. Consequently each inequality of Conjecture~(conj:CE of the paper) holds
for all finite systems if and only if it holds for all systems with at most
seven atoms; and, since atoms may be split into identically placed copies
without changing anything, it suffices to treat systems with \emph{exactly}
seven labelled atoms.

there is an invertible matrix $\Lambda$ such that $\sete\bracmid{Y'-Y}{Y} =-\Lambda Y$ and a 
random matrix $E$ such that $\sete\bracmid{E}{Y} =\sete\bracmid{(Y'-Y)(Y'-Y)^T-2\Lambda}{Y}$.
Then for $g\in C^3(\setr^d)$,
\[
\abs[\big]{\sete[g(Y)] - \sete[g(Z)]} \leq \Abs{\Lambda^{-1}}_\mathrm{op} \paren*{\frac{\sqrt{d}}{4}M_2(g) \sete\brac[\big]{\Abs{E}_\mathrm{HS}} + \frac{1}{9}M_3(g)\sete\brac[\big]{\abs{Y'-Y}^3}},
\]
where $Z$ is a standard multivariate normal on $\setr^d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let F(x)=Qx+b be a Euclidean isometry preserving a bounded connected smooth domain D. Suppose normal reflected Brownian motion X in D almost surely visits every nonempty interior open set infinitely often. Then Y=F(X) is a reflected-Brownian coupling, and it is shy if and only if min_{closure D}|x-F(x)|>0. A bounded convex preserving domain has a fixed centroid and therefore no shy isometry coupling. A planar annulus with inner radius R>0 and nontrivial rotation theta has separation at least 2R*|sin(theta/2)|. No claim about arbitrary nondeterministic shy couplings is made.
Euclidean isometry preserving D
Normal reflection
Recurrence to every nonempty interior open set
Compact domain closure

    min_{x in closure D} |x-F(x)| > 0.

Applying this to epsilon=1/k shows inf_t |X_t-F(X_t)|=0 almost surely, ruling out shyness.

If D is convex, its volume centroid c lies in D. Any preserving Euclidean isometry fixes c: change variables in its centroid integral to obtain Qc+b=c. body: Let X be a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space and let K be a nonempty compact convex subset of X. Then K equals the closed convex hull of its extreme points, ext(K), where x in K is an extreme point if it cannot be written as t y + (1 - t) z for distinct y, z in K and t in (0,1); that is, x = ty + (1-t)z with t in (0,1) forces y = z = x. In particular ext(K) is nonempty whenever K is nonempty, compact, and convex, and every such K is recovered as the closure of the convex hull of ext(K).

body: Method (campaign status: proved): Take a maximum matching $P_1,\dots,P_N$ in $\Gamma$. Greedily choose a remaining pair, a witness row $E_s$ containing it, and remove the batch $B_s$ of all remaining matching pairs meeting $E_s$; put $a_s=|B_s|$. Batches partition the matching. With $V_s$ the endpoints of $B_s$ and $U_s=E_s\cap V_s$: $|U_s|\ge a_s+1$ (tag 14), the $U_s$ are disjoint, and $E_s$ avoids every later $U_t$. Condition outside $\bigcup_s U_s$ and peel $U_k,\dots,U_1$ in reverse exposure order. Notes: Key independence bookkeeping: earlier selected row indicators are independent of the set being peeled, and variables in earlier $U_t$'s are held as arbitrary parameters. This is exactly why the Littlewood-Offord input must be TARGET-UNIFORM (two-point form).

[Lem backprop of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $d$ be a positive integer and $D,\varepsilon$ be positive reals.
    There exists a positive integer $\ell$ depending only on
    $d,D,\varepsilon,C,V,\delta,t$ such that for all $k<t/\delta$ and
    polynomials $P:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d$ with
    $\|P\|_1\le DN$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
 \left|\mathbb{E}[ P(\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k+1)}) ] - \mathbb{E}\left[ P\left( \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -
 \beta\delta \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -\delta
 \text{\boldmath $P$}_\ell(\text{\boldmath $h$},\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)}) + \sqrt{2\delta}\text{\boldmath $\eta$}^{(k)} \right) \right]
 \right| \le \varepsilon N.
\end{align*}

    for all $\text{\boldmath $h$}$ with $\|\text{\boldmath $h$}\|_\infty\le C$. Furthermore, there exist
    a positive integer $d'$ and a positive real $D'$ depending only
    $d,D,\varepsilon,C,V,\delta,t$ such that for all polynomials
     $P:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d$ with
    $\|P\|_1\le DN$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
 \mathbb{E}\left[ P\left( \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} - \beta\delta\text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} -
 \delta\text{\boldmath $P$}_\ell(\text{\boldmath $h$},\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)}) + \sqrt{2\delta}\text{\boldmath $\eta$}^{(k)}
 \right) \Big| \text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)} \right] = Q(\text{\boldmath $\tau$}^{(k)})
\end{align*}

    for some polynomial $Q:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of degree at most $d'$
    with $\|Q\|_1\le D'N$.

[Lemma delta_x cyclic of arXiv:2609.02213, 'Invariant subspaces for free linearizations of Lipschitz maps'] Let $x$ be an element of a pointed metric space $(M,e)$, and let $f\in \Lip(M,M)$. Then the following assertions are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[$(i)$]
			\item $\delta(x)$ is not a cyclic vector for $T_{f,e}$;
			\item there exists $\varphi\in \Lip_0(M,e)\setminus\{0\}$ such that
			$$
			\langle \varphi,\gamma\rangle=0,
			\qquad \forall \gamma\in \lspan\mathrm{Orb}(\delta(x),T_{f,e});
			$$
			\item there exists $\varphi\in \Lip_0(M,e)\setminus\{0\}$ such that
			$$
			\varphi(f^n(x))=\varphi(f^n(e)),
			\qquad \forall n\in \mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}.
			$$
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
