body: Lebesgue measure on R^n is the complete translation-invariant measure obtained by applying Caratheodory's construction to the outer measure m*(A) = inf of sum of volumes of countable covers of A by open boxes. It assigns each box its elementary volume, is defined on the Lebesgue sigma-algebra (Borel sets completed by null sets), and is the unique (up to scale) translation-invariant Borel measure finite on bounded sets. Non-measurable sets exist (Vitali) assuming the axiom of choice.

For every integer n >= 1 there is a prime p with n < p <= 2n. Conjectured by Bertrand (1845, verified to 3 million), proved by Chebyshev (1852); the proof below is Erdos's (1932), from the prime factorisation of the central binomial coefficient. Refinements: for n >= 25 there is a prime in (n, 6n/5) (Nagura); the prime number theorem gives a prime in (n, (1 + eps) n) for every eps > 0 and n large; Ramanujan primes generalise the statement to k primes in (n/2, n].

In addition, for every integer n > 3 there is a prime p satisfying n < p < 2n-2. This sharpened form complements, and does not replace, the original assertion for all integers n >= 1.
n a positive integer
the elementary product bound prod_{p <= x} p < 4^x is used for real x >= 2 (Erdos)

[Defi construction of nu of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Suppose $t\in\mathbb{Z}$. Set $t':=t-\lfloor\frac{n\log n}{2}\rfloor$, and $\gamma_t:=\exp(-2t'/n)$. Let $\nu_n^t$ denote the measure on $\mathfrak{S}_n$ defined by the following sampling process: first, sample $M_t\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ according to the distribution 
$$\mathbf{P}[M_t=k]=\mathbf{P}(\Pois(\gamma_t)=k)/\mathbf{P}(\Pois(\gamma_t)\le n),$$ 
then sample a uniformly random subset $S_t$ of size $M_t$ in $[n]$. Finally, sample a uniformly random element of $\mathfrak{S}_{[n]\backslash S_t}$ and view it as an element of $\mathfrak{S}_n$ by fixing all of the elements in $S_t$.

body: Method (campaign status: exact-certificate): Checker using ONLY integer arithmetic and fractions.Fraction (no floating point). construction(n) builds A = e_0, B_i, C_i, the residuals {A+B_u : u in starts} and the S12 gap-wise basis. structural_check(n) asserts: |starts| = d = (n+2)//3; gaps in {2,3}; |basis| = r = n+1 and rank(basis) = r; |residuals| = d and rank(residuals) = d; and that EVERY form of D_n is 'covered', i.e. there is a basis element b and a sign in {-1,+1} with rank(residuals + [form - sign*b]) = d (the selector residual lies in R). activation_check(n) enumerates all independent sets of C_n, groups them by z = restriction to starts, and asserts count <= 2^{n-d-|z|} and 2*count <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}. Defaults: structural n = 4..30, activation n = 4..16. [Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'] Given an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ and a set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Lim}(\kappa)$, a\linebreak \emph{$(\kappa, S)$-quagmire} is a quadruple $(T, {<}, {\lhd}, Q)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(Q\arabic*)},  start=0]
\item 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(T, <)$ is a $\kappa$-Kurepa tree,
\item $\lhd$ is a binary relation on $T$ whose restriction to each level of $T$ is a strict linear order; nodes of distinct heights are $\lhd$-incomparable,
\item the function $Q$ is a partial function from $T^2$ to $T$ whose domain consists of the pairs $(x, y) \in T^2$ such that $\mathrm{ht}(x) < \mathrm{ht}(y)$ and $x \lhd \pi_{\mathrm{ht}(x)}(y)$,
\end{enumerate}

\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$, then $x < Q(x, y) \lhd y$,
\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $y < z$, then $Q(Q(x, y), z) = Q(x,z)$,
\item if $(y, z) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $x \lhd y$, then $Q(x, Q(y, z)) = Q(x, z)$,
\item if $x \lhd y$ and $\mathrm{ht}(x) \in S \cup \{\kappa\}$, then there exists $\alpha < \mathrm{ht}(x)$ such that $\pi_\alpha(x) \lhd \pi_\alpha(y)$ and $x = Q(\pi_\alpha(x), y)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505

body: An arithmetic function f (defined on positive integers) is multiplicative if f(1) = 1 and f(mn) = f(m) f(n) whenever gcd(m, n) = 1; completely multiplicative drops the coprimality condition. Multiplicative functions are determined by their values on prime powers. Examples: Euler's phi, the divisor count and divisor sum, the Mobius function mu. The Dirichlet convolution of two multiplicative functions is multiplicative, and Mobius inversion recovers f from its summatory function.
title: Multiplicative Arithmetic Function

[Definition defi_solution_approx of arXiv:2603.26307, '\LARGE The incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with thermal noise'] A  \emph{weak martingale solution 
		to (equation Eq_approx of the paper)} 
	consists of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathfrak{A},\mathbb{P})$, a filtration $\mathscr{F}$ satisfying the usual conditions, independent $3$-dimensional standard $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(W_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ and $3\times 3$-matrix valued $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(B_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ with covariance structure (equation Eq_noise_matrix_covariation of the paper), a weakly continuous and adapted  $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$-valued process
	$u_{\delta,\epsilon}$, and $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3)$-valued  $\psi_{\delta,\epsilon}$, such that the following holds:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item  We have the additional regularity  $ u_{\delta,\epsilon}\in L^{2}(0,T;H^2( \mathbb{T}^3 ;\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ and $\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} \in  L^{2}(0,T;H^2( \mathbb{T}^3))$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  For every divergence-free $\varphi\in C^{{\infty}}(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				& \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}  u_{\delta,\epsilon}(t)\cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x \,-\, 
				\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_0 \cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,+\,\epsilon\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_{\delta,\epsilon}\Delta^2 \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} -  \Bigl(\frac{1}{2}+ \frac{F_1}{4}\Bigr) \nabla u_{\delta,\epsilon}: \nabla  \varphi \,+\, u_{\delta,\epsilon}\otimes u_{\delta,\epsilon}:\nabla \varphi \,\mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} s \,+\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} f_n \nabla \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x :\mathrm{d} B_{n,s},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
		and $\nabla \cdot u_t = 0$ for all $t\in [0,T]$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  
		For every $\zeta\in C_c^{{\infty}}([0,T) \times \mathbb{T}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				&-\,
				\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}  \partial_t \zeta  \, \mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} t \,-\, \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}
				\psi_0 \zeta
				\,\mathrm{d} x+\,\epsilon\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi_{\delta,\epsilon}\Delta^2\zeta\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s 
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} - \bigl(1+ {F_1}/2 +G_1/2\bigr) \nabla \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}\cdot \nabla  \zeta \,+\,\psi_{\delta,\epsilon} u_{\delta,\epsilon}\cdot \nabla \zeta   \,-\, (F_2/2+G_2/8) \psi_{\delta,\epsilon} \zeta \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t \\
				&\qquad+\, \int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \zeta\, h_\delta(\psi_{\delta,\epsilon})\bigl(
				|\nabla \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}|^2 \,+\, |\nabla_\mathrm{sym} u_{\delta,\epsilon}|^2 + \epsilon
				\bigr)\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t
				\\&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3
				\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon} g_n \partial_i \zeta  + \frac{1}{2} \psi_{\delta,\epsilon}  \zeta \partial_ig_n \,\mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} W_{n,t}^i
				\, +\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j =1}^3\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}u_{\delta,\epsilon,j}\partial_i (\zeta f_n) \,\mathrm{d} x \,\mathrm{d} B_{n,t}^{ji},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}  $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.	
	\end{enumerate}
title: Weak martingale solution to \eqref{Eq_approx}

body: [Corollary 3.8 (Recovery of Hoeffding’s Inequality) of arXiv:2603.10190, 'Hoeffding-Type Concentration Bounds for Exchangeable Random Variable'] Let $(X_{m})_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of $[0,1]$ -valued random variables, and set $\mu\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[X_{1}]$. Then, for every $M\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(\bar{X}_{M}-\mu\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}},\qquad\mathbb{P}\left(\mu-\bar{X}_{M}\geq t\right)\leq e^{-2Mt^{2}}.$

[Proposition prop:mean of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold and consider
additive functionals of density-type $\overline{\rho}_t$ (Definition~(def:empirical_density of the paper))
and current-type $\overline{J}_t$ (Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)).
For every $t>0$ the stationary (time-independent) means
are given by  
\begin{align}
\E^\mu\bigl[\overline{\rho}_t(V)\bigr] &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V \mathrm{d} \mu = \E^\mu[V],
\\
\E^\mu\bigl[\overline{J}_t(U)\bigr] &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} v_{\textrm{s}} \cdot U \mathrm{d}\mu = \E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}} \cdot U ] =\E^\mu[W],
\end{align}
with local mean velocity $v_{\textrm{s}}$ from Eq.~(equation eq:drift_split of the paper)
and $W\equiv v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U$.
title: Stationary expectation values

[Theorem thm:REA of arXiv:2604.23981, 'Accelerating sampling via asymptotic relaxation enhancing flows'] Consider a given flow $v$. Let
$\sigma:=\liminf_{A\to\infty}\Psi_A$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $v$ is relaxation enhancing (or $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)=\emptyset$)
if and only if $\sigma=\infty$, and also if and only if $\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=\infty$.

\item  If $\sigma<\infty$, then $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)$
is nonempty and 
\begin{gather}
\sigma=\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=r(v).
\end{gather}
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, suppose $\sigma<\infty$ and $q_0$ satisfies Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper) with $q_0-1\in \mathcal{Y}$. Then, for any $\delta>0$, there is some $A_0$ such that whenever $A>A_0$, one has
\[
\mathcal{H}(\rho(t)| \pi)=\int q \log q \pi dx \le C\int |h|^2\pi \,dx \le C_1\exp(-(\sigma-\delta) t),
\]
where $C_1$ depends only on the two constants in Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper).

body: [Lemma geometric lemma of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] Let $ x \in \{ 0, 1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^d} $ be an $ m$-net configuration for some $ m \in \mathbb{N}$. Then for all $ c> 0$ and $v\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ there exists $D$ which depends only on $c$ and $d$ such that for any $ m \geq 2$, $\mathbf{B}(v, \lfloor cm \rfloor)$ intersects at most $ D$ Voronoi cells in the Voronoi covering around the set $ \{ w \in \mathbb{Z}^d~:~ x_{w} =1\}$.

For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph G with p_c(G)<1, the historical Benjamini-Schramm question asks whether at p=p_c(G) there is almost surely no infinite open cluster. The p_c<1 hypothesis is essential: on the two-sided line p_c=1 and all edges are open at that parameter. This card records the precise question, not a present-day open-status verdict.

[Lemma 21 (Localized martingale property) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] For each fixed $\delta\ge2$, $\eps\in(0,1)$ and $n\ge1$, define
\[
M_t^{W,n}:=\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}u'_{\delta,\eps}(Y_s)
\bigl(a(s,X_s)-\wt a(s,\wt X_s)\bigr)\dd W_s
\]
and
\[
M_t^{Z,n}:=\int_0^{t\wedge\tau_n}\int_{\R\setminus\{0\}}
\{u_{\delta,\eps}(Y_{s-}+\gamma_s z)-u_{\delta,\eps}(Y_{s-})\}\,\wt N(\md s,\md z),
\]
where $\gamma_s:=\sigma(s,X_{s-})-\wt\sigma(s,\wt X_{s-})$. Then $M^{W,n}$ and $M^{Z,n}$ are true martingales.

[Definition def-quantum-cone of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $W > 0$ and let $\alpha = Q - \frac{W}{2\gamma}$. Sample independent standard Brownian motions $(B_t)_{t \geq 0}, (\tilde B_t)_{t \geq 0}$ conditioned on $\tilde B_{t} - (Q-\alpha) < 0$ for all $t>0$. Let
	\[Y_t := \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} 
				B_{t}+(Q-\alpha) t & \mbox{for} & t\ge 0\\
				\tilde{B}_{-t} -(Q-\alpha) |t| & \mbox{for} & t<0
			\end{array} 
			\right. \]
	Let $\hat \psi = \psi_1 + \psi_2$ where $\psi_1$ is the distribution on $\mathcal{C}$ which is constant on each line segment $\{t\} \times [0,2\pi]$ satisfying $\psi_1(z) = Y_{\mathrm{Re}(z)}$, and $\psi_2$ is an independent copy of $h_\mathcal{C}^2$. The \emph{weight $W$ quantum cone} is $(\mathcal{C}, \hat \psi, -\infty, +\infty)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and we define the probability measure $\mathcal{M}^\mathrm{cone}(W)$ to be its law.
title: Definition def-quantum-cone of arXiv:2411.19810

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] Let $Z\subset\Sn^1$ be the two singular parameter values of the closed profile
curve constructed above.  The quantity
\[
 \chi=\cos^{k-1}\theta\,\frac{d\theta}{ds}
\]
has a continuous extension through every $s_0\in Z$, with
\begin{equation}
 \chi(s_0)=\frac{r(s_0)^{k-1}x(s_0)\sin\theta_0}{A}.
\end{equation}
Consequently the formula
\begin{equation}
 d\mathcal K_k[X]
 =
 \left[
 -A r^{n-k}\chi+B r^{n-k-1}\cos^k\theta
 \right]\,ds\,d\omega
\end{equation}
defines a finite signed Radon measure on the fixed parameter manifold
$M=\Sn^1\times\Sn^{n-1}$, where $d\omega$ is the standard volume measure on
$\Sn^{n-1}$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}
 =
 -A\frac{\chi}{r^{k-1}}
 +B\left(\frac{\cos\theta}{r}\right)^k
\end{equation}
is continuous on $M$ and satisfies
\[
 \sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}=-\langle X,\nu\rangle,
 \qquad
 \mathcal K_k[X]=\sigma_k^{\mathrm{ren}}\,d\mu_X.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \mathcal K_k[X](\{s_0\}\times\Sn^{n-1})=0
 \qquad (s_0\in Z).
\]

[Defn 38 (Markov operator, canonical process, and canonical measure) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] Let $\br \in \Ek$ be an SRI chain with base measure $\nu$ and decay function $F$. Define the associated \textbf{Markov operator} $P_{\br}$ to act on functions $f$ by the formula $$(P_{\br} f)(\mathbf x) := \int_{I^k} f(\y) \br ( \mathbf x,\dr \y),$$ defined for all Borel-measurable functions $f:I^k\to\mathbb R$ for which the integral converges absolutely for all $\x\in I^k.$

    We also denote by $(\mathbf R_r)_{r\ge 0} = (   R^1_r,...,   R^k_r)_{r\ge 0}$ the \textbf{canonical coordinate process} on $(I^k)^{\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}},$ and we denote by $\Pbb$ the \textbf{canonical probability measure} on $(I^k)^{\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}}$ under which the canonical coordinate process is distributed as the Markov chain with transition kernel $\br$ started from initial state $\x$. We also denote by $\Ebb$ the associated \textbf{expectation operator.}
title: Markov operator, canonical process, and canonical measure

body:
Let Omega be a bounded domain in R^n with C^1 boundary and outward unit normal nu, and let u be a sufficiently regular solution of -Laplacian u = f(u) in Omega with u = 0 on the boundary. Write F for the primitive of f with F(0) = 0. Then n times the integral over Omega of F(u) minus ((n-2)/2) times the integral over Omega of u f(u) equals (1/2) times the boundary integral of (x dotted with nu) times |partial u / partial nu|^2. Taking f(u) = |u|^{p-1} u with the critical exponent p = (n+2)/(n-2) makes the left side vanish identically, so on a STAR-SHAPED domain, where x dotted with nu >= 0 with strict positivity somewhere, the boundary term forces the normal derivative to vanish and hence u = 0: the critical Dirichlet problem has no nontrivial regular solution on a star-shaped domain.
Enough regularity to justify the integrations by parts (u in C^2 up to the boundary, or in H^2 with the boundary terms interpreted by trace theory), the Dirichlet condition, and C^1 boundary.
The non-existence conclusion needs star-shapedness;
on an annulus the identity holds but proves nothing, and indeed nontrivial critical solutions exist there.

body:
[Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let $\chi$ be a Navier--Stokes potential on an open fiber domain  \(\mathscr F\subset\mathscr E\) (containing its zero section) of a relaxation bundle \(\mathscr E\subseteq\Sym^2T^*\Mcal\). Then, a \textbf{relaxation rate map} consists of a smooth fiberwise map $\mathscr B=\mathscr B(\beta,\zeta)\in\mathscr E^*$ defined for all future timelike $\beta$ and all $\zeta \in \mathscr F$, satisfying the following conditions.

\bei 

\item \emph{Stable equilibrium property:}
\bel{eq:pot-relax-map}
\mathscr B(\beta,0)=0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)\geq0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\zeta=0.
\ee

\item \emph{Positivity property:}  Its linearization along the equilibrium manifold $\mathbb M$ given by 
\bel{eq:pot-relax-linearization}
\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)
\coloneqq
\frac{\del\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}}{\del\zeta_{\gamma\delta}}(\beta,0)
\ee
must be symmetric under interchange of the two index pairs and positive definite on~$\mathscr E$, namely
\be
\eta_{\alpha\beta}\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)\eta_{\gamma\delta}>0
\qquad
\text{for every nonzero }\eta\in\mathscr E.
\ee
\eei
Furthermore, the associated \textbf{production term} is
\bel{production-term-value}
\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}
\coloneqq
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}
\geq0.
\ee
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.31171

[Definition 59 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] For a function $f : \amsmathbb{R} \rightarrow \amsmathbb{R}$, the Lipschitz norm is
\[
|\!| f |\!|_{\textnormal{Lip}} = \sup_{x \neq y} \bigg|\frac{f(x) - f(y)}{x - y}\bigg|.
\]
For $f \in \mathscr{L}^1(\amsmathbb{R})$ with Fourier transform $\widehat f$ --- \textit{cf.} our convention in Section~\ref{Notasec} --- we will make use of the norm
\[
|\!|f|\!|_{\frac{1}{2}}=\bigg(\int_{\amsmathbb{R}} |s| |\widehat f(s)|^2 \dd s\bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\]
We also introduce the space $\mathscr{H}_{\textnormal{Lip},\frac{1}{2}}$ of bounded real-valued functions on $\amsmathbb{R}$ with finite norms
 $|\!|f|\!|_{\textnormal{Lip}}$, and $|\!|f|\!|_{\frac{1}{2}}$.

Let n>=1, L_n=beta_n=n and M_n=2^(n^2). Take M_n distinct singleton paths, each with deterministic zero Gaussian field and positive weight exp(n), and one long path of M_n independent N(0,n) coordinates, each of weight 1/M_n. The covariance is PSD and its maximum diagonal is n. Put S_n(xi)=M_n^(-1) sum_i exp(xi X_i), H_n(xi)=min(n,log S_n(xi)), and F_n(xi)=-(1/n)log(exp[-n^2(1-log 2)]+exp[-n log S_n(xi)]). Then E[H_n(2)-H_n(0)]/n -> 1 whereas E[F_n(2)-F_n(0)]/n -> 1-log 2. Hard-min median exponents converge, beta_n->infinity and maximum variance is O(L_n), but normalized integrated soft-min response has the wrong endpoint limit when uniform smoothing error is omitted. This is a finite Gaussian counterexample, not planar LFPP.

One long path with M_n independent centered N(0,n) coordinates of weight 1/M_n

Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. Every infinite connected nearest-neighbor tree T embedded in Z^d has p_c(T)=1: at most (2n+1)^d simple root paths have length n, so their q-open union has probability at most (2n+1)^d q^n. In Z^2 the connected acyclic graph retaining all vertical edges and only the horizontal row y=0 spans every vertex and has density one, yet has p_c=1. This comb is not quasi-transitive and is not an iid lattice cluster; it refutes density-only robustness and does not refute the critical quasi-transitive target.

[Lemma lem:fixed-interrupted-renewal of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a spatial ribbon map $\Gamma$, one labelled residual
component $\mathcal C$ with $r_{\mathcal C}\le L\log n$ nonconstant
slots, one physical anchor, and its complete packet/root channel.
A hard ordinary supernode is one fused physical time containing either a
nonsingleton packet resource or the time-indexed linear Jacobi child
$-2N^{-1}W_i$.  The coupled pure-Weyl root is a special hard symbol; the
total number of special root symbols is bounded by an absolute constant
$B_0$.  Aggregate Ricci is not present in this ported theorem and is
treated separately in the aggregate-Ricci synthesis below.

For every fixed $L$ there are $A_L<\infty$ and a numerical exponent
$B<\infty$ for which the estimate below holds.

Suppose $\mathcal C$ contains a hard resource and reserve its
chronologically earliest resource-bearing hard supernode as the endpoint,
breaking a same-node tie by the fixed ribbon-slot order.  Let
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{surplus ordinary hard supernodes}\},\\
 o_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{all }\mathsf S^\pm
                         \text{ singleton supernodes}\},\\
 v_{\mathcal C}&=\#\{\text{all }\mathsf V
                         \text{ singleton supernodes}\},\\
 t_{\mathcal C}&=b_{\mathcal C}+o_{\mathcal C}+v_{\mathcal C}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3.4.1x}
\]
If $\mathfrak e_{\mathcal C}$ is the selected endpoint resource and
$\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}$ is the remaining normalized terminal
amplitude, then, for $\delta=1/16$,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{\substack{\text{weak orders, equality blocks, finite gaps,}\\
                  \text{and typed states on }\mathcal C}}
 |\operatorname{Contr}_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}|
 \le A_L^{r_{\mathcal C}}(r_{\mathcal C}+1)^B
 \mathfrak e_{\mathcal C}\mathfrak a_{\Gamma,\mathcal C}
 n^{-\delta t_{\mathcal C}}.}
\tag{3.4.1x$_1$}
\]
The estimate holds at the application horizon $m=cN$ for each fixed
$c\ge1$, uniformly in every finite remaining-time constraint; its
constant is independent of $c$, while the threshold in $n$ may depend on
$c$.  Summing the one anchor costs at most $m$.

[Proposition 19 (Algebraic prefactor) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $\lambda=\alpha/\mu\to\infty$ (small noise), with the safe boundary nearby and the threshold $\theta$ at distance $h_\theta$ uphill, so that $\Lambda:=\lambda h_\theta^2=\alpha h_\theta^2/\mu\to\infty$. Then
\[
p^{\ex}_{uv}\sim\frac12\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\pi\alpha}}\,\frac{1}{h_\theta}\,e^{-\Lambda}\cdot\frac{1}{W(z;h_{\mathrm{safe}})}\asymp\Lambda^{-1/2}e^{-\Lambda},
\]
an exponential rate $e^{-\Lambda}$ times an algebraic factor $\Lambda^{-1/2}$, not a multiplicative $(1+o(1))$.

DRAFT: proof (unaudited), w726-T332-C2 v1. Let n>=1 and 0<=c<=n. Let G be G(n,c/n), with independent edges and iid standard-Borel vertex marks independent of its edges, with numerical labels forgotten; let T be an identically marked Poisson(c) Galton-Watson tree. Root G at a fixed vertex independently of graph and marks. For these graph and tree laws, let states lie in a bounded Borel subset K of a separable Banach space, diameter D, invariant under all updates on locally finite graphs and induced subgraphs. Initial states depend only on own iid marks. Each measurable isomorphism-invariant layer rule depends only on the mark, own state and the unordered neighbor-state list, is the same on graph and tree independently of graph size, and is rho-Lipschitz in the maximum norm of the entire input list, uniformly over degrees, marks and layers, with 0<rho<1. Define delta_1(r)=min(1,4(1+c)^(2r+2)/(3n)). For every depth L and radius r>=0, root-law W1 is at most 2D rho^r+D delta_1(r). For a scalar 1-Lipschitz readout bounded by B, pooled variance is at most 34 B^2 (1+c)^(2r+2)/n+2D^2 rho^(2r), uniformly in L. Optimizing r gives polynomial n-rates for fixed c and rho. This does not assert a depth-uniform TV bound or an expected empirical bounded-Lipschitz supremum. Independent review is pending.

Let n_1, ..., n_k be pairwise coprime positive integers and N = n_1 n_2 ... n_k. For any integers a_1, ..., a_k there exists an integer x with x = a_i (mod n_i) for every i, and x is unique modulo N. Equivalently, the ring map Z/NZ -> Z/n_1Z x ... x Z/n_kZ, x -> (x mod n_1, ..., x mod n_k), is an isomorphism of rings. The same holds in any commutative ring for pairwise comaximal ideals I_1, ..., I_k: R/(I_1 ... I_k) is isomorphic to the product of the R/I_j.

Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be real numbers which are CONVEX, meaning the second differences D2 a_n := a_n - 2 a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are >= 0 for every n >= 0, and which tend to 0. (These two hypotheses already force a_n >= 0 and a_n nonincreasing: the first differences a_{n+1} - a_n are nondecreasing, so if one of them were positive the sequence would tend to +infinity. They also force n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, since the differences are monotone.) THEOREM (Young; Zygmund, Trigonometric Series, Ch. V). Put S(x) = a_0/2 + sum_{n >= 1} a_n cos(nx). Then: (1) the series converges for every x not in 2 pi Z, uniformly on every compact subset of (0, 2 pi); (2) S(x) >= 0 for all such x; (3) S is Lebesgue integrable on (-pi, pi), with (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of S over (-pi,pi) equal to a_0/2; (4) the series IS the Fourier series of S, that is a_n = (1/pi) times the integral over (-pi,pi) of S(x) cos(nx) dx for every n >= 0. The whole theorem rests on one identity: with K_n(x) = (1/(n+1)) (sin((n+1)x/2) / sin(x/2))^2 >= 0 the Fejer kernel, normalised so that (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of K_n over (-pi,pi) is 1, double summation by parts gives S(x) = sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) (D2 a_n) (1/2) K_n(x), with sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) D2 a_n = a_0 < infinity. Nonnegativity is then read off from D2 a_n >= 0 and K_n >= 0, and integrability from the normalisation. SHARP EDGES. (a) It is CONVEXITY, not monotone decrease, that does the work: monotone decrease to zero gives convergence off the origin by Dirichlet's test, but it does not produce the Fejer representation and therefore gives neither nonnegativity nor integrability of the sum. (b) The SINE analogue is false in this form. If (b_n) is convex and decreases to 0, then sum b_n sin(nx) still converges pointwise off 2 pi Z, but its sum is Lebesgue integrable if and only if sum b_n / n converges. The classical counterexample is b_n = 1/log n for n >= 2, which is convex and decreases to 0 while sum 1/(n log n) diverges: the resulting series converges everywhere but is not the Fourier series of any Lebesgue integrable function. Never transport the cosine statement to the sine case. (c) 'Integrable' cannot be improved to 'bounded': for a_n of order 1/n the sum behaves like log(1/|x|) near 0, which is integrable and unbounded. (d) The conclusion S >= 0 is on (0, 2 pi); nothing is claimed at x in 2 pi Z, where the series may diverge (it diverges precisely when sum a_n = infinity). (e) Convexity is only assumed for n >= 0 on the given sequence; a sequence that is eventually convex gives the same conclusions after subtracting a trigonometric polynomial, but then nonnegativity of the sum is lost.
(a_n)_{n >= 0} is a real sequence
the second differences a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are nonnegative for every n >= 0 (convexity)
a_n -> 0 as n -> infinity
consequences used and derived from these: a_n >= 0, a_n nonincreasing, n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, sum (n+1)(a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2}) = a_0
integrability is with respect to Lebesgue measure on the circle

Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assume1},~\ref{assume:global2} are satisfied and there is some $R \geq 12/\cmin+2(1+2M)(\log\la)/d$ and a constant $\CL$ such that $\z\in C^4(\us(R\e)\times[0,(R\e)^2])$,~\eqref{A} is satisfied, and

&R\e(\omega_{1,1}+\omega_{0,2}(R\e,R\e)) + (R\e)^2\omega_{2,1}(R\e,0)\leq1/2,\\
&\left(\omega_{3,0}^2 +\omega_{4,0}(R\e,0)\right)\frac{d^2}{\la}  \leq \CL.

\es
Then
\begingroup
\addtolength{\jot}{0.7em}
\be
\int_{D}e^{-\la z(u)}\dd u =  \frac{(2\pi/\la)^{d/2}e^{-\la z(0_{d+1})}}{\la\sqrt{\det H}}\left(1+ \Rem_1\right),
\ee \endgroup where

|\Rem_1| \les_{R,\CL} &\left(\omega_{3,0}^2+\omega_{4,0}(R\e,0)\right)\frac{d^2}{\la} + \left(\omega_{1,1}^2+\omega_{2,1}(R\e,0)\right)\frac{d}{\la}+ \omega_{0,2}(R\e,(R\e)^2)\frac{1}{\la}  + \frac{1}{\la^M}.

Let X be a {0,1}-valued field on Z^d, d>=2, such that sigma-fields on sets at sup-norm distance greater than integer r>=0 are independent. Suppose P(X_x=0)<=delta for every vertex. Put K=(r+1)^2. If delta<=64^(-K), then the good sites have an infinite nearest-neighbor component with positive probability; no stationarity or FKG assumption is needed.

Proof: restrict to the coordinate Z^2 plane. Color it by its two coordinates modulo r+1. Sites of any one color are mutually independent: successive use of the sigma-field range assumption is valid since every remaining site is farther than r from the previously selected set. Any specified set of m bad sites contains at least ceil(m/K) sites of one color, so its all-bad probability is at most delta^(m/K). No product over dependent sites is used.

If the origin is good but its good component in this plane is finite, its exterior vertex boundary contains a simple star-connected circuit of bad sites enclosing the origin. The elementary square-lattice contour fact follows by tracing the outer polygonal boundary of the union of unit squares of the finite component; successive exterior squares touch at sides or corners, and loops can be erased while preserving an enclosing circuit. For a circuit of m vertices, its intersection with the positive horizontal ray supplies a starting vertex (j,0), 1<=j<=m: enclosing the origin forces a crossing of that ray and of the opposite half-plane, and its diameter is at most m in the sup norm. For each of at most m starts there are at most 8^m star-step sequences. Thus the number of such circuits is at most m*8^m.

Set alpha=8*delta^(1/K)<=1/8. A union bound over the enclosing circuits gives

    P(origin belongs to an infinite good component)
      >= 1-delta-sum_{m>=1} m*alpha^m
      = 1-delta-alpha/(1-alpha)^2
      >= 1-1/64-8/49 = 2575/3136 > 0.

The sum includes impossible short circuits and is therefore a conservative bound. Delta=0 is immediate. An infinite component in the plane is also one in the full lattice. Let (M,g) be a complete connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n >= 2, and suppose there is a constant k > 0 such that Ric(v,v) >= (n-1) k g(v,v) for every tangent vector v (Ricci curvature bounded below by that of the round sphere of constant sectional curvature k). Then M is compact, diam(M) <= pi/sqrt(k), and the fundamental group of M is finite. The dimension condition is needed: for n = 1 the Ricci tensor vanishes and the hypothesis reads 0 >= 0, so the real line is complete, connected and not compact.

[Definition 56 (Villain model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{Villain model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \begin{multline}
         e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)}
         =
         \Big(\prod_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\sigma_y)\Big)
            \Big(\prod_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\zeta_y)\Big);
            \\
         p_\beta(z,z'):=\sum_{m\in\Z} e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\big(\arg(z)-\arg(z')+2\pi m\big)^2}.
    \end{multline}
    Notice that the Hamiltonian is defined somewhat atypically and incorporates
    the dependency on $\beta$; more on this later.
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c^{\Villain}=\beta_c^{\Villain}(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c^{\Villain})$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\Villain, \beta}$.
    The label $\Villain$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.
title: Villain model

[Lemma lem:joint-reflected-ricci-root of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let
\[
 \mathcal R^{\rm in}=W_+^{\rm in}\otimes W_-^{\rm out},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R^{\rm out}=W_+^{\rm out}\otimes W_-^{\rm in}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12a}$}
\]
be the physical doubled-reversal boundary.  Let
$B,B'\in\operatorname{Sym}_0(H)$ and
$|\alpha|,|\beta|,|\alpha'|,|\beta'|\le1$.  The complete distinct-time
aggregate-Ricci sources, with these statuses, and every finite or
unit-circle literal-$W$ Green kernel define an operator
\[
 \mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B'):
 \mathcal R^{\rm in}\longrightarrow\mathcal R^{\rm out}
\]
satisfying
\[
 \boxed{
 \|\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B')\|_\mathrm{op}
 \le \frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F,
 \qquad |z|=1,}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12b}$}
\]
with the same bound for every finite Green kernel.  At coincident
reflected root times the complete shared-plane source defines an operator
$\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},=}(B,B')$ obeying the same bound.  Consequently
every physically typed joint complement
\[
 K\in\mathcal S_1(\mathcal R^{\rm in},\mathcal R^{\rm out})
\]
obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 |\operatorname{Tr}(K^*\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}(B,B'))|
 \le\frac Cn\|B\|_F\|B'\|_F\|K\|_1.}
\tag{3.3.1w$_{12c}$}
\]
At coincident times replace $\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},z}$ in this display
by $\mathscr A_{{\rm Ric},=}$. 
The assertion is joint: no replica-projective factorization of $K$ is
assumed.  It remains true after tensoring the root operator by an
ancillary identity which lies outside the literal-$W$ Green rail.

A proof for the critical variable-length boundary-to-boundary SAW law does not by itself prove convergence for the uniform n-step honeycomb walk rooted at the origin with a free endpoint. In a fixed finite path collection, conditioning fugacity weights x^L on L=n gives uniform n-step weights, but a shrinking conditioning probability can invalidate transfer from a weak mixture limit. A conditional local limit with relative error, as well as endpoint and domain transfer, is an additional premise. This campaign concept is a draft; it is not an SLE convergence proof.

body: Publication record. Krauth and Mézard predicted in 1989 that the storage capacity of the Ising perceptron at zero margin is an explicit constant alpha* ≈ 0.8330786. With M_N the largest number of random patterns an N-dimensional Ising perceptron can store, Y. Shmalo, The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron: verification of the outstanding numerical conditions (arXiv:2607.11010, July 2026) gives a computer-assisted proof that M_N/N -> alpha* in probability, alpha* in [0.833078599, 0.833078600]: earlier work gave matching lower and upper bounds conditional on a one-variable global sign condition of Ding and Sun and a two-variable global sign condition of Huang, and the paper verifies both rigorously in Arb ball arithmetic. Nonzero margin and the general free-energy/TAP problem are not addressed. Certificates and verifiers: https://github.com/yspennstate/ising-perceptron-capacity (commit 072cdc2c624b); ResearchGate record 409127298. Not refereed. Item T069 of the owner's list of 200 famous open problems in probability.
title: Krauth-Mezard capacity conjecture for the Ising perceptron at zero margin proved by computer-assisted verification of the Ding-Sun and Huang conditions, alpha* in [0.833078599, 0.833078600] (Shmalo 2026, arXiv:2607.11010, repository yspennstate/ising-perceptron-capacity)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: In a finite killed domain V, let J(x) count departures from x during stabilization of n particles at 0, and let h be the final sleeper indicator. Conservation and the fresh uniform jump choice give $\mathbb E h(x)=n1_{x=0}+\Delta\mathbb E J(x)$, where $\Delta f(x)=(2d)^{-1}\sum_{y\sim x}f(y)-f(x)$ with zero extension outside V. This follows by stopping after K departures, taking expectations of arrivals, and then passing to the finite-domain absorption limit. It identifies the candidate continuum Poisson equation, but not its unknown density or free boundary. Check: The finite process has finite expected absorption time: from every reachable state there is a finite positive-probability sequence moving all particles to sinks, and the state space for fixed n,V is finite. Summing the identity over V gives final mass = initial mass minus expected boundary flux, independently checking the sign. Obstruction: A limit of the expected odometer is insufficient: concentration, a uniform bulk sleeper density, and inner/outer control of the visited region are all still required.

[Theorem 11 (Averaged macroscopic-loop criterion) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(G_n\) be a random simple graph on \([n]\). Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).
Assume that \((G_n)_n\) satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:sparse-random-graph}, with limiting
edge density \(\alpha\), and that
\[
\alpha>c_{\theta,u}.
\]
Then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Averaged macroscopic-loop criterion

OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; F0124_C16 version 3; status: independently checked proof. For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with p in [37/39,1] and independent iid fair sign scenery, every exterior configuration is good. At theta=(1-p)/p=2/37 the constant-word WHOLE no-cut coefficients h_l have an exponentially decaying bound h_l<=C(1001/1000)^(-l) for some finite C. Confined-path resolvents give the full path partitions E,J,Q; exact renewal yields H=Q-1-(J-1)^2/E. Its ballistic pole cancels. Writing lambda=(1+sqrt(1-16theta z^2))/2 and r=(1-lambda)/lambda gives uniformly convergent meromorphic series. Along 0<=z<=1001/1000, lambda>=682/1000 and r<=318/682; the regular series is bounded by six exact rational terms plus an analytic bound on its ENTIRE infinite tail, giving a strictly positive denominator G. H continues analytically along that interval. Its coefficients are nonnegative, so the proved Vivanti-Pringsheim argument gives a Taylor radius greater than 1001/1000 and summability. Monotonicity of raw coefficients in theta extends the result to all p>=37/39; p=1 is iid. Real-axis analyticity alone would be insufficient without nonnegative coefficients. This is a restricted high-drift result, not the full p>4/5 classification, and no novelty is asserted.

body: Setting: online SGD for a soft committee machine with K students w_1..w_K in R^N and M = K orthonormal teachers v_1..v_K, activation g(x) = erf(x/sqrt 2), output sum_i g(w_i . x), Gaussian inputs, no noise, step eta/N. As N -> infinity the overlaps Q_ij = w_i . w_j and R_in = w_i . v_n follow a deterministic ODE in time t = steps/N (the Saad-Solla equations, including the eta^2 term). From a symmetric start (Q = q0 I, R = 0) the ODE enters the symmetric plateau, where all students have equal overlap with every teacher; the plateau is a saddle whose one unstable direction is the antisymmetric mode, with rate lambda(eta) > 0. Open (top-400 row T240): for K = 2, prove that the plateau exit time tau_N of SGD at dimension N satisfies tau_N / log N -> 1/(2 lambda(eta)) in probability, for small eta or an explicit eta interval. This requires deterministic entry into the plateau, positive transverse noise there, and recovery after the exit.
title: Open problem: escape time from the symmetric plateau of a teacher-student soft committee machine

body:
[Theorem eq:counter-match of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:counterexample}
Fix \(p\ge3\) and \(\sigma>1\).  There exists a symmetric probability law \(\mu=\mu_{p,\sigma}\) on \(\mathbb R\) with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item \(\mu\) has a strictly positive \(C^\infty\) density and is sub-Gaussian.
\item If \(\xi\sim\mu\) and \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\xi^r=\mathbb E G^r,
 \qquad r=1,\ldots,2p.
\end{equation}
\item There is a compact interval \(B\subset(0,\infty)\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 >\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\end{equation}
Moreover, the same interval satisfies
\begin{align}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^J(B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^G(B),
 \\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\min}^J(-B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\min}^G(-B).
 
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
In particular, sub-Gaussianity together with Gaussian moment matching
through order \(2p\) does not force the Gaussian rate of unregularized
critical-point counts in a compact energy window when no spatial
localization restriction is imposed. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:gaussian-coordinate-orbit-calibration of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $A\in W^{1,1}(0,T;\mathsf{S}^d)$ satisfy
(equation eq:pure-time-covariance-class of the paper), and let $\omega_{A,K}$ be any
correction constructed in (equation eq:pure-time-correction of the paper) with
$K\geq K_{\mathrm{hom}}$.  Suppose that a reference pair
$(b^{\mathrm{orig}},a^{\mathrm{orig}})$, started from
$x_{\mathrm{orig}}$ and satisfying
Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper), has reference process
$X^{\mathrm{orig}}$ and admits mutually inverse space--time
maps $\Phi,\Psi$ with the regularity required in
Theorem~(thm:coordinate-naturality of the paper).  Put
$y_0=\Phi_0(x_{\mathrm{orig}})$, let the model $(0,A)$ start from $y_0$, and
suppose, for every $(t,x)\in(0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, that
\begin{equation*}
 \begin{aligned}
  A(t)&=D_x\Phi_t(x)a^{\mathrm{orig}}(t,x)D_x\Phi_t(x)^\top,\qquad
  0=\partial_t\Phi_t(x)+D_x\Phi_t(x)b^{\mathrm{orig}}(t,x)
      +\tfrac12a^{\mathrm{orig}}(t,x):D_x^2\Phi_t(x).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
The sharp calibration is then
\begin{equation*}
 C_{t^\alpha\omega_{A,K}}(X^{\mathrm{orig}})=C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}}
 \qquad\text{for every }\alpha\geq0.
\end{equation*}

Let Omega in R^n be open, 1 < p < infinity, and Lu = sum a^{ij}D_{ij}u + sum b^i D_i u + c u with a^{ij} = a^{ji} continuous on Omega, b^i, c in L^infinity(Omega), sum a^{ij}(x) xi_i xi_j >= lambda|xi|^2 (lambda > 0) and |a^{ij}|, |b^i|, |c| <= Lambda. Let u in W^{2,p}_loc(Omega) intersect L^p(Omega) satisfy Lu = f a.e. in Omega with f in L^p(Omega). Then for every open Omega' with compact closure in Omega, ||u||_{W^{2,p}(Omega')} <= C ( ||u||_{L^p(Omega)} + ||f||_{L^p(Omega)} ), where C depends only on n, p, lambda, Lambda, Omega', Omega and the moduli of continuity of the a^{ij} on the closure of Omega'. Global version and solvability: if in addition Omega is a bounded C^{1,1} domain, a^{ij} in C^0(closure of Omega), c <= 0, g in W^{2,p}(Omega) and f in L^p(Omega), then there is exactly one u in W^{2,p}(Omega) with Lu = f a.e. and u - g in W^{1,p}_0(Omega), and ||u||_{W^{2,p}(Omega)} <= C ( ||f||_{L^p(Omega)} + ||g||_{W^{2,p}(Omega)} ). Continuity (or VMO) of the leading coefficients is essential; the estimate also fails at p = 1 and p = infinity.

body: In mathematical analysis and in probability theory, a σ-algebra is part of the formalism for defining sets that can be measured. In calculus and analysis, for example, σ-algebras are used to define the concept of sets with area or volume. In probability theory, they are used to define events for which a probability can be defined. In this way, σ-algebras help to formalize the notion of size.

body: In combinatorics, the inclusion–exclusion principle (commonly referred to as PIE) is a counting technique which generalizes the familiar method of obtaining the number of elements in the union of two finite sets; symbolically expressed as $|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|$ where A and B are two finite sets and |S| indicates the cardinality of a set S (which may be considered as the number of elements of the set, if the set is finite). The formula expresses the fact that the sum of the sizes of the two sets may be too large since some elements may be counted twice. The double-counted elements are those in the intersection of the two sets and the count is corrected by subtracting the size of the intersection.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] A \emph{limiting point} at time \(T\) is an element
\(\xi\in M_T\) of Bamler's metric-flow slice at the limiting time
\cite[Definition~2.32 and the paragraph following
equation~(2.34)]{BamlerStructure}.  We represent it by a probability
conjugate heat flow
\[
 \xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T},\qquad d\mu_t=v_t\,dV_{g(t)},
\]
where
\[
 \partial_tv_t=-\Delta_{g(t)}v_t+R_{g(t)}v_t,
 \qquad v_t>0,
 \qquad \int_Xv_t\,dV_{g(t)}=1.
\]
The representation has the following two properties of the limiting slice:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \(\xi\) is a subsequential limit of point conjugate heat flows
whose pole times increase to \(T\);
\item for \(D=2n\),
\begin{equation}
 \Var_{g(t)}(\mu_t)
 :=\iint_{X\times X}d_{g(t)}(x,y)^2\,d\mu_t(x)d\mu_t(y)
 \le H_{2n}(T-t).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The limiting point is called \emph{fixed} when it is chosen before any
sequence of blow-up scales.  Every tangent argument below keeps this
same limiting point while the scales vary.
title: Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02878

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For random walk in a random environment on Z^d satisfying a directional transience condition, such as Sznitman's condition (T) or the stronger (T') in a direction l, or a simpler ballisticity/non-nestling condition, one constructs regeneration times tau_1 < tau_2 < ... at which the walk achieves a new running maximum in direction l and never backtracks below that level afterward. Under condition (T'), or the weaker (T), the increments (X_{tau_{k+1}} - X_{tau_k}, tau_{k+1} - tau_k), for k >= 1, form an i.i.d. sequence, reducing the walk, which is not itself Markovian once the environment is averaged out, to a genuine i.i.d.-increment structure from which a law of large numbers (a deterministic limiting velocity) follows directly, and, with additional finite-moment control on the regeneration increments, a central limit theorem follows via classical tools for sums of i.i.d. variables. This does not establish the directional transience condition itself, verifying (T) or (T') for a given environment law is typically the hard remaining step; it does not directly give a central limit theorem without separately checking finite second moments of the regeneration increments, which can genuinely fail in slow or near-critical regimes; and it is specific to the static, fixed-in-time environment model. Typical failure: Assuming the regeneration increments automatically have finite variance, and hence a central limit theorem follows, once ballisticity or condition (T') has been established; ballisticity under (T') only guarantees a finite mean regeneration time, and a genuine central limit theorem requires an additional, often delicate, verification of finite second moments, a point on which the Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer branching-with-migration machinery exists precisely because these moments can fail. Canonical reference: Sznitman and Zerner, 1999, Annals of Probability; Sznitman, 2002, Ecole d'Ete de Probabilites de Saint-Flour, Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics.
an i.i.d., or ergodic and suitably mixing, random environment
a directional transience condition, typically Sznitman's (T) or (T'), or an equivalent ballisticity condition, in some direction l
uniform ellipticity of the transition probabilities, standard though sometimes relaxed in specific results
existence of well-defined regeneration times with positive probability of never backtracking, verified from the environment's independence or mixing structure
title: Technique: Sznitman-Zerner Regeneration Structure for RWRE

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Every geodesic spanning tree of a Cayley graph has branching number equal to the growth rate (October 2026), proves that if T is a spanning tree of an infinite, connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph G, rooted at o and geodesic (every vertex is at the same distance from o in T as in G), then the branching number of T equals the growth rate of G. For Cayley graphs this answers Question 3.12 of Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks, where it was known for lexicographically constructed trees (Lyons and Peres; Liu and Xiang, arXiv:2010.01530). As a consequence, Bernoulli percolation on any such tree has critical probability equal to one over the growth rate. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/geodesic-tree-branching (commit c8e96497f0ad). Not refereed.
title: Every geodesic spanning tree of a quasi-transitive graph has branching number equal to the growth rate, answering Lyons-Peres Question 3.12 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/geodesic-tree-branching)

Therefore no graph- and scale-uniform c>0 gives original_probability>=c*sprinkled_probability. The four source distances are comparable to m. This refutes a quantitative reverse bridge only; both probabilities vanish at fixed beta, and the full critical Z^3 conjecture is untouched.

[Lemma lem:order-preservation of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] Let $T$ be an IYT and let $\mathbf{p}^T_a, \mathbf{p}^T_b$ be the lazy
	trajectories starting at boxes $a, b \in \mathbb{N}_0^2$. If
	$\mathbf{p}^T_a[s_0] \preceq \mathbf{p}^T_b[s_0]$ for some integer
	$s_0 \geq 0$, then
	\[
		\mathbf{p}^T_a[t] \preceq \mathbf{p}^T_b[t]
		\qquad \text{for all } t \geq s_0 .
	\]
	Moreover, once the two positions coincide they remain equal at all

Unreviewed bridge checklist. For a finite nonempty family of real path log costs f_p(y), beta>0 and K paths, define H(y)=min_p f_p(y) and F_beta(y)=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp(-beta f_p(y)). Then 0<=H(y)-F_beta(y)<=log K/beta for every y. For growing families, L_n->infinity and log K_n/(beta_n L_n)->0 therefore suffice for normalized expected endpoint differences to agree whenever the hard endpoint limits exist and the costs are integrable. A sharper effective-entropy estimate may replace this sufficient condition. The finite Gaussian response identity also requires retaining the negative beta times covariance of path gradients; its two nonnegative pieces cannot be separated or discarded just because one route wins almost surely. Neither the entropy bound nor concentration evaluates the actual planar-LFPP normalization exponent.

Positive beta and normalization L_n
Integrable endpoint log costs

body:
OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; proof (unaudited); D0007-C007 v1; audits w667:PASS. Let r>=1 be finite, p_j>0 with sum p_j=1, and a_j<b_j finite. Then F=sum p_j Uniform[a_j,b_j] is n-CM for every sufficiently large integer n, with overlapping or disconnected intervals and arbitrary centers. Put ell_j=b_j-a_j, c_j=(a_j+b_j)/2, mu=sum p_j c_j, D=sum |c_j-mu|, ell_max=max ell_j, ell_bar=sum p_j ell_j. A sufficient threshold is ceil(max(2, max_j[(1+6D/(r*ell_j))/p_j], [2D+2*ell_max+sum ell_j]/ell_bar)). Rounded counts K_j have mean np_j and discrepancy at most one; conditional tilt slopes 6*delta/(r*K_j*ell_j), delta=n*mu-sum K_j*c_j, share a sign and restore exact uniform marginals because E[delta]=0. The established joint monotone-density criterion applies in each state. The threshold may diverge along approximations to a general density; no full D0007 solution is claimed.
r finite >=1
p_j>0 and sum p_j=1
a_j<b_j finite
Wang-Wang joint monotone-density criterion

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c91af946a7143d6a981511609cc357ed9da62d3a4dd33fc2af6b91f8db024f23","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c9/c91af946a7143d6a981511609cc357ed9da62d3a4dd33fc2af6b91f8db024f23.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:331277ca8184ad2063d12d899b833e486f4487b68e909379aea2bd454ca9e246","bundle_entry_key":"finite-uniform","bundle_id":"population.finite-uniform-mixtures-counted-monotone-tilts-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; constant-sum couplings","draft":"w662/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.complete_mixability:finite-uniform-mixtures-eventual-complete-mixability-w662","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# D0007-C007 v1: Every finite mixture of nondegenerate bounded uniform laws is eventually CM
Status: proof (unaudited). Special case of D0007 using the established Wang-Wang joint monotone-density criterion. Novelty not asserted.

Statement. Let r>=1 be finite, p_j>0 with sum p_j=1, and a_j<b_j finite. Then F=sum_{j=1}^r p_j Uniform[a_j,b_j] is n-CM for every sufficiently large integer n. The intervals may overlap or be disconnected; their centers need not agree.

An explicit sufficient threshold is as follows. Put ell_j=b_j-a_j>0, c_j=(a_j+b_j)/2, mu=sum p_j c_j, D=sum |c_j-mu|, ell_max=max ell_j, and ell_bar=sum p_j ell_j. Every integer n at least

 N=ceil(max(2, max_j[(1+6D/(r ell_j))/p_j],
                   [2D+2 ell_max+sum ell_j]/ell_bar))

is an admissible complete-mixability order.

External theorem used: If all n univariate laws have increasing densities (or all have decreasing densities) on finite essential intervals [A_i,B_i], then they are jointly mixable iff sum A_i+max(B_i-A_i)<=sum means<=sum B_i-max(B_i-A_i). Source: Wang-Wang, Joint Mixability, doi:10.1287/moor.2015.0755, as stated in Wang arXiv:1411.6190v3 Section 2.2(e), equation (7), p.9. This theorem is cited, not reproved.

1. Random counts. There is a finite random vector K=(K_1,...,K_r) of integers satisfying sum K_j=n, E[K_j]=n p_j, and |K_j-np_j|<=1, with each K_j either floor(np_j) or ceil(np_j). Here is a direct construction. Let z_j be the fractional parts of np_j. Their sum s=n-sum floor(np_j) is an integer. If two z coordinates are strictly between zero and one, move along the direction e_i-e_j to the first boundary in each direction, and choose between those two endpoint vectors with probabilities making their expectation the original vector. Every such step preserves the sum s and each conditional coordinate expectation and reduces the number of fractional coordinates by at least one. A vector with exactly one fractional coordinate cannot have integer sum. After finitely many steps all coordinates are zero or one. The resulting random Z has sum s and E Z_j=z_j. Put K_j=floor(np_j)+Z_j. Only finitely many count states occur.

The threshold on n ensures K_j>=np_j-1>=6D/(r ell_j), and also K_j>=1: when D>0 the first bound is strictly positive, while when D=0 the threshold gives np_j>=1 and floor(np_j)>=1.

2. Center discrepancies. For a count state K define

 delta(K)=n mu-sum_j K_j c_j.

Its expectation is zero. Since sum (np_j-K_j)=0,

 delta=sum_j (np_j-K_j)(c_j-mu),

so |delta|<=D.

3. Conditional tilted marginals. For each component j and state K, put

 t_j(K)=6 delta(K)/(r K_j ell_j),
 q_{j,K}(x)=(1/ell_j)[1+t_j(K)*2(x-c_j)/ell_j]
           for a_j<=x<=b_j, and zero outside.

The positivity bound from Step 1 gives |t_j|<=1, so q is nonnegative and integrates to one. Its essential support is the whole [a_j,b_j], even when one endpoint density is zero. A direct affine integral gives mean c_j+t_j ell_j/6=c_j+delta/(r K_j). For any fixed K, all t_j have the same sign. Thus all q_{j,K} densities are increasing when delta>0, decreasing when delta<0, and constant when delta=0. Form a list of n conditional laws by taking K_j copies of each q_{j,K}. Their means sum to

 sum K_j c_j + sum_j K_j*delta/(r K_j)
       =sum K_j c_j+delta=n mu.

4. Check the monotone-density mean condition. Let W(K)=sum_j K_j ell_j. The sum of left endpoints is sum K_j c_j-W/2, and the sum of right endpoints is sum K_j c_j+W/2. Also max interval width is at most ell_max. Since K_j>=np_j-1,

 W>=n ell_bar-sum ell_j>=2D+2 ell_max.

Hence W/2-|delta|>=ell_max, which places n mu between the left-endpoint sum plus the maximal width and the right-endpoint sum minus it. All hypotheses of the cited theorem hold. Therefore the n conditional laws admit a joint coupling with sum exactly n mu for each count state K. Only finitely many states occur, so selecting one coupling for each requires no measurable-selection argument.

5. Restore the original full marginals. Select K according to Step 1, use its constant-sum coupling, and uniformly permute coordinates. A fixed coordinate has marginal density

 sum_j E[(K_j/n)q_{j,K}(x)].

For each j its constant part is (E K_j/n)/ell_j=p_j/ell_j. Its linear perturbation has coefficient E[K_j t_j]/(n ell_j), and

 E[K_j t_j]=6 E delta/(r ell_j)=0.

Thus the full density is exactly sum p_j 1_[a_j,b_j]/ell_j, the density of F. Overlapping component intervals do not affect this identity. The sum is n mu in every selected coupling and remains so after permutation. This proves the statement and threshold.

Hardest remaining D0007 piece: approximate a general density by such mixtures at one fixed sufficiently large n with thresholds controlled uniformly. The displayed N depends on the smallest component weights and widths. Along increasingly fine approximations it may diverge, so weak approximation alone does not extend this theorem to every absolutely continuous law. body:
[OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT: T407-GD-006 v2, proof (unaudited); independent audit pending; priority unestablished. Extends the continuous-flow result in bundle_003 to finite discrete updates.] Candidate finite joint-GD regime: the shared square CNN with h=p(p+1)/2 spanning filters and patch-specific trainable readout reaches any positive population squared error from n=k h noiseless Gaussian samples in finitely many simultaneous full-batch gradient updates almost surely. Both layer steps are explicit strictly positive functions of observed data and initialization. Together with the unit-sphere rank lower bound, this gives order kp^2 versus (kp)^2 sample separation at risk 1/4 and confidence 15/16 for local CNN versus equivariant learners. Moreover a finite dyadic rescaling W_0=s W_base, a_0=s^-2 a_base preserves the initial function and makes the proved filter/readout step ratio exactly one. Hence one common positive constant GD step suffices from this explicit data-dependent scaled initialization. Scope: p,k>=1; independent standard Gaussian patches; arbitrary symmetric local quadratic targets; spanning shared filter initialization (Gaussian almost surely), arbitrary finite readout; sample-dependent two-timescale steps; exact real arithmetic; no uniform runtime, finite-precision or equal-rate claim. Lower bounds use unit L2 target class. Equal-rate corollary changes initialization by a data-dependent scaling; it is not IID standard Gaussian initialization or a universal fixed scale.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:3a80596b772f05118f111ea7ea2d0bb9581b1cb3119aa85901a44e31fee559f2","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/3a/3a80596b772f05118f111ea7ea2d0bb9581b1cb3119aa85901a44e31fee559f2.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:bf98a7d6766c3a79c8cc643de3d5f16d76ea612299ca9ec0c3b9113bcde32d13","bundle_entry_key":"draft-discrete-shared-quadratic-cnn","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-discrete-joint-quadratic-cnn","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-finite-joint-gd-shared-quadratic-cnn-scaled-initialization","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 3: finite joint gradient descent for a shared quadratic CNN

Status: proof (unaudited), T407-GD-006 v2. This is a specified algorithm with sample-dependent positive step sizes. Priority is unestablished; the proof uses standard local conditioning and descent ideas. It extends the continuous-flow candidate T407-JOINT-005, without changing its version.

## Statement and model

Let p,k>=1, d=kp, h=p(p+1)/2, D=kh. For independent standard Gaussian patches x_j in R^p, targets are arbitrary f_star(X)=sum_j x_j^T M_j x_j, M_j symmetric. The shared-filter square CNN is
  f_(W,a)(X)=sum_j sum_r a_(r,j)(w_r^T x_j)^2,
with h shared filters and a separate trained coefficient for each filter/patch pair. Initialize with rank-one filter matrices spanning Sym(p), and any finite readout. Independent Gaussian filters have this spanning property almost surely, and Gaussian readout initialization is allowed.

From n>=D noiseless IID Gaussian examples, simultaneous full-batch gradient descent on BOTH parameter blocks with the explicit positive constant steps below attains any prescribed population squared error epsilon>0 after finitely many iterations almost surely. There is no target-coefficient oracle, continuous-flow computation, stochastic-gradient assumption, or claimed uniform running-time bound. The algorithm uses the empirical design and its singular values. This is not a theorem about fixed equal steps, noisy labels, or degree q>2.

The lower bounds from Section 5 of proofs/target3_joint_quadratic_flow.md apply unchanged: for the unit-L2 local target class at risk epsilon and confidence 1-delta, arbitrary local learners need n>=D(1-epsilon-4delta) when positive, while orthogonally equivariant learners need n>=[d(d+1)/2](1-epsilon-4delta). At epsilon=1/4, delta=1/16 these are D/2 and d(d+1)/4. Thus the discrete algorithm also yields the specified order kp^2 versus (kp)^2 separation. These are noiseless statistical sample bounds; computational constants can depend very badly on the realized sample.

## 1. Design and initialization

Use an orthonormal symmetric vectorization svec, Phi with rows concatenating svec(x_j x_j^T), and B(W) whose columns are svec(w_r w_r^T). Stack a by patch and put b(W)=I_k tensor B(W). Then theta=b(W)a and e=Phi theta-y. Gaussian full design rank for n>=D follows from a nonzero determinant polynomial: place e_i and e_i+e_l successively in one patch at a time, setting other patches zero. This gives a block-diagonal invertible evaluation witness. The same p(p+1)/2 witness vectors yield a spanning initial filter bank. Gaussian absolute continuity makes both rank failures null. Consequently sigma=sigma_min(Phi)>0, S=||Phi||op>0, gamma=sigma_min(B(W_0))>0.

Set M=||W_0||F, R=M+1, L=2M+1,
  rho=min(1,gamma/(2L)), beta=gamma/2, lambda=beta^2 sigma^2.
For ||W-W_0||F<=rho we have ||B(W)-B(W_0)||op<=L||W-W_0||F<=gamma/2; hence sigma_min(B(W))>=beta, ||B(W)||op<=R^2, and ||W||F<=R. These follow from ||ww^T-vv^T||F<=(||w||+||v||)||w-v||. In particular e always lies in range(Phi), because labels are realizable in this coefficient space.

Let E=||e_0||. If E=0, output the initialized function, which equals the target since Phi is injective. The gradients vanish, so any positive steps would preserve it. Assume E>0 henceforth. Define
  A=||a_0||+4 R^2 S E/lambda+1,
  eta=min(1, rho lambda/(16 S R A E)),
  Jbar=S(R^2+2 R A), Ebar=S R^2 A+||y||,
  H=Jbar^2+Ebar S(2 A+4 R),
  tau=min(1/H,1/(2lambda)).
All denominators are strictly positive. Fix these constants for the whole run. Write loss ell(W,a)=||e||^2/2. The simultaneous update is
  a_(t+1)=a_t-tau gradient_a ell(W_t,a_t),
  W_(t+1)=W_t-tau eta gradient_W ell(W_t,a_t).
Both gradients are evaluated at the same old iterate. Both learning rates are strictly positive and depend only on initialization and observed inputs/labels.

## 2. Derivative bounds on a convex safe set

Let K={||W-W_0||F<=rho, ||a||<=A}, a convex subset of Euclidean parameter space z=(W,a). Its output Jacobians obey
  ||J_a||op<=S R^2, ||J_W||op<=2 S R A,
so ||J_z||op<=Jbar. Indeed the coefficient derivative satisfies
  ||D_W theta[Delta W]||<=2||W||F ||a|| ||Delta W||F.
For two joint parameter perturbations u=(u_W,u_a), v=(v_W,v_a), expansion of theta, quadratic in W and linear in a, gives
  ||D^2 theta[u,v]||
  <=2 A ||u_W||F ||v_W||F
     +2R(||u_W||F ||v_a||+||v_W||F ||u_a||)
  <=(2 A+4R)||u|| ||v||.
This follows directly from Cauchy-Schwarz on the filter and patch indices; there is no dimension-dependent hidden constant. Since ||e||<=Ebar on K,
  ||D^2 ell||op <=||J_z||op^2+||e|| S(2 A+4R)<=H.
Also the readout block alone gives a local PL inequality on K:
  ||gradient_a ell||^2=||b(W)^T Phi^T e||^2
  >=beta^2||Phi^T e||^2>=lambda||e||^2.
The last inequality uses e in range(Phi), not an untrue minimum-singular-value inequality for arbitrary vectors in R^n.

## 3. Induction handles step segments before invoking descent

Put P=diag(eta I_W,I_a), so z_next=z-tau P gradient ell. As eta<=1, ||P g||^2<=g^T P g. On any update segment contained in K, Taylor's theorem with the Hessian bound yields
  ell(z_next)<=ell(z)-tau g^T P g+(H tau^2/2)||P g||^2
              <=ell(z)-(tau/2)g^T P g
              <=(1-tau lambda)ell(z).
This is not yet a justification that iterates stay in K. We prove both conclusions inductively.

Let q=sqrt(1-tau lambda), so 0<q<1 since 0<tau lambda<=1/2. Assume all iterates through t are in K and ||e_j||<=E q^j through t. Their update formulas and the derivative bounds give the CANDIDATE next iterate, before using any descent on its segment,
  ||a_(t+1)-a_0|| <=tau S R^2 E sum_(j=0)^t q^j
                  <=2 S R^2 E/lambda,
  ||W_(t+1)-W_0||F <=tau eta 2 S R A E sum_(j=0)^t q^j
                    <=4 eta S R A E/lambda<=rho/4.
Here tau/(1-q)=(1+q)/lambda<=2/lambda. In particular ||a_(t+1)||<A and the new filter bank is strictly inside the rho ball. The old and new iterates are both in the convex set K, so their entire segment lies in K. The preceding descent inequality is now justified, proving ||e_(t+1)||<=E q^(t+1). Initialization supplies the base case. This resolves the possible circularity in an informal discrete first-exit argument.

Thus all iterates stay bounded, B(W_t) stays invertible, and
  ||e_t||^2<=E^2(1-tau lambda)^t<=E^2 exp(-tau lambda t).
All updates are finite algebraic operations on real parameters at every finite t; this is a mathematical exact-arithmetic algorithm, not a finite-precision guarantee.

## 4. Population risk and finite stopping

For the block-diagonal symmetric coefficient error Delta M,
  R_pop=E(X^T Delta M X)^2=2||Delta M||F^2+(tr Delta M)^2
       <=(d+2)||Delta theta||^2<=(d+2)||e_t||^2/sigma^2.
Therefore stop when the computed residual squared is <=epsilon sigma^2/(d+2). A sufficient iteration count when E>0 is
  t>=max(0,ceil(log((d+2)E^2/(sigma^2 epsilon))/(tau lambda))).
The design is fixed and no new examples are used in these iterations. Although n=D suffices with probability one, the conditioning, steps and iteration count need not be uniform over samples or initializations. If the displayed logarithm is negative, t=0 suffices.

## Prior-art scope and hardest audit point

Primary sources checked: Li-Ma-Zhang arXiv:1712.09203v5, Theorem 1.2 and its teacher/factorization context (PSD quadratic teacher); Sarao Mannelli-Vanden-Eijnden-Zdeborova arXiv:2006.15459v3, Section 2 Equation (1) (fixed positive readout); Jin-Montufar arXiv:2006.07356v5, Theorem 1 (wide univariate ReLU implicit bias; all parameters trained). The last source is explicitly about joint gradient descent and illustrates that local conditioning/near-initialization analysis is established methodology. Its inspected theorem is not the finite shared quadratic bank and n=D statement here. These searches are incomplete and establish no novelty.

The hardest audit point is the combined uniform Hessian bound and the discrete induction: the candidate next iterate must be proved inside the safe set before invoking Taylor descent on its segment. The proof above orders these steps explicitly. No stochastic conditional bounds or floating-point estimates are used. The full discrete result is not Lean-certified.


## 5. Equal learning rates after an explicit initialization rescaling

This corollary removes the two-timescale UPDATE restriction by changing the initialization. It does not claim equal-rate convergence from every fixed initialization. Take any base spanning bank W_base and finite readout a_base. For s>=1 set
  W_(0,s)=s W_base, a_(0,s)=s^(-2) a_base.
Since B(s W_base)=s^2 B(W_base), the initial represented function and initial residual E are independent of s. The finite-design sigma and S are also independent of s. If E=0, the base function is already correct and no optimization is needed. Assume E>0.

Let M_base=||W_base||F, gamma_base=sigma_min B(W_base)>0,
  R_base=M_base+1, L_base=2M_base+1,
  lambda_base=gamma_base^2 sigma^2/4,
  A_bound=1+||a_base||+4 R_base^2 S E/lambda_base.
At scale s, gamma_s=s^2 gamma_base and lambda_s=s^4 lambda_base exactly, while R_s=s M_base+1<=s R_base and L_s<=s L_base. Therefore if
  s>=max(1,2 L_base/gamma_base),
the safe radius rho_s=min(1,gamma_s/(2L_s)) equals one. The Section 1 readout bound obeys
  A_s=||a_base||/s^2+4 R_s^2 S E/(s^4 lambda_base)+1<=A_bound.
Consequently
  rho_s lambda_s/(16 S R_s A_s E)
  >=s^3 lambda_base/(16 S R_base A_bound E).
Choose s by doubling 1,2,4,... until BOTH preceding radius condition and
  s^3 lambda_base>=16 S R_base A_bound E
hold. They hold at a finite scale because their right sides are finite constants. This is a terminating initialization procedure using only observed data and the base bank/readout; it never calls the unknown target coefficients. It can also be specified by choosing the first dyadic scale above the explicit maximum of the displayed thresholds.

For this chosen scaled initialization, Section 1's eta is exactly one. Thus the same proof gives ordinary simultaneous gradient descent
  (W_(t+1),a_(t+1))=(W_t,a_t)-tau gradient ell(W_t,a_t)
with ONE common strictly positive sample-dependent constant step tau. The n=D almost-sure sample guarantee and the finite stopping rule remain valid, as do the stated local-versus-equivariant lower bounds.

One may take the deterministic base bank e_i,e_i+e_l and a_base=0. Alternatively Gaussian base filters span almost surely. After data-dependent common rescaling their distribution is not IID standard Gaussian: do not present this corollary as a claim about standard Gaussian initialization or a universal sample-independent scale. Its statistical sample count is uniform over targets; its scale and running time are not bounded uniformly. No numerical simulation is used to choose the scale in this proof.


Supporting normalized rank lower proof:


For any finite-dimensional quadratic function space V of dimension q, equipped with its L2(Gaussian) inner product, choose an orthonormal basis psi_1,...,psi_q. For the local space q=D; for all homogeneous symmetric quadratics q=Q=d(d+1)/2. The covariance of the unwhitened symmetric coefficients is positive definite, because
  E (X^T M X)^2=2||M||_F^2+(tr M)^2>0 for M!=0,
so this orthonormal basis exists and all target coefficients below are valid quadratics.

Put a uniform prior on coefficient xi in the unit sphere S^(q-1). Every target f_xi=sum xi_i psi_i has L2 norm exactly one. Conditional on the input sample, its n noiseless labels reveal only the projection of xi on the row span of the evaluation matrix. That row span has rank r<=n and is independent of xi before seeing labels. By reflection symmetry on its orthogonal complement, the posterior mean is precisely the observed projection. Among arbitrary output functions, the posterior mean target minimizes squared prediction risk. Its Bayes risk, averaged over labels and inputs, is E||xi-P_row xi||^2=1-r/q>=1-n/q (and zero is the trivial bound for n>=q). This gives minimax expected squared risk >=(1-n/q)_+; it is a known spherical-prior dimension argument, not a new statistical principle.

For confidence bounds, postprocess any learner by projecting its output into V in L2 and then clipping its coefficient norm to the unit ball. This does not increase squared error against any unit-norm target and bounds that error by four. If an output is not in L2, map it to zero: it could not have finite error against a target in V on a successful event. A uniform guarantee risk<=epsilon with probability >=1-delta would thus imply average risk <=epsilon+4delta. Therefore n>=q(1-epsilon-4delta), whenever the factor is positive. This is an inequality for real n, so the actual integer sample requirement is its ceiling.

The local class includes all diagonal quadratics. Every full homogeneous quadratic is an orthogonal rotation of a diagonal one, and its L2 norm is preserved by Gaussian rotation. For an equivariant learner, a uniform guarantee on the normalized local class therefore implies the same guarantee on the entire normalized full quadratic class. Apply the preceding q=Q Bayes lower bound. For an arbitrary local learner use q=D. Conversely D or Q Gaussian observations give exact coefficient recovery by local or full least squares, respectively; full least squares with minimum Frobenius-norm tie-breaking is orthogonally equivariant even on singular datasets.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:4f385fe4de70e173b3af1296be5ed7dfb42883127e6ab928dadafe34fd1ac78d","revision_digest":"sha256:fa1288624c8d53976021dcdd6ed837364fee10a8c02fbb355b348b9f2a509f6e","source_id":"owner-own-work:w693:T407-GD-006:v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20T11:25:12.725984+03:00; v2; unaudited; supersedes discrete v1, continuous-flow argument remains separately recorded","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 19 (The models are EFIIDs) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] All three models alluded to above are EFIIDs.
    More precisely, we obtain the following results.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[\emph{\textbf{XY}}] Consider the XY model in dimension $d\in\Z_{\geq 2}$
        at inverse temperature $\beta\in[0,\beta_c(d))$.
        Then the infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu_{\XY,\beta}^{+1}$
        is an EFIID.
        \item[\emph{\textbf{SWM}}] Consider the SWM in dimension $d\in\Z_{\geq 2}$
        at inverse temperature $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
        Then the infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu_{\SWM,\beta}^0$
        is an EFIID.
        \item[\emph{\textbf{Coulomb}}] Consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas at $\beta\in[0,\beta_{\BKT}(\Villain))$.
        Then the sequence $(\mu_{\Coulomb,\Lambda_n,\beta}^\free)_n$
        tends to some infinite-volume measure $\mu_{\Coulomb,\beta}^\free$ on $\Z^{F(\Z^2)}$ as $n\to\infty$ in the local convergence topology,
        and this limit is an EFIID.
    \end{itemize}
    In the case of the Coulomb gas, we are careful not to call this measure a Gibbs measure, as the Hamiltonian of the model is non-local and therefore it is not so clear what it means exactly to be a Gibbs measure.

    In particular, these results imply that for any of the three models,
    correlations between bounded observables decay exponentially fast in the distance at which they are measured. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The models are EFIIDs

body: A random variable X with mean mu = E[X] is sub-exponential with parameters (nu, b), nu > 0 and b > 0, if E[exp(t(X - mu))] <= exp(nu^2 t^2 / 2) for all |t| < 1/b. Equivalently, up to absolute constants, the tails satisfy P(|X - mu| > s) <= 2 exp(-s^2 / (2 nu^2)) for 0 <= s <= nu^2/b and P(|X - mu| > s) <= 2 exp(-s/(2b)) for s > nu^2/b. Every sub-Gaussian random variable is sub-exponential, but sub-exponential variables such as squares of Gaussians or exponential random variables may have heavier tails than any sub-Gaussian. [standard, e.g. Wainwright, High-Dimensional Statistics]
title: Sub-Exponential Random Variable

body: [Definition 5 (Distances) of arXiv:1710.10644, 'Percolation without FKG'] Let Q be a quad, and let x and y be two vertices belonging to Q. (1) The ambient distance between x and y, denoted by d(x, y), is the graph distance in Λ between x and y, i.e. the length of the shortest path from x to y. It does not depend on Q. (2) The intrinsic distance between x and y in Qo ∪∂Q, denoted by dQ(x, y), is the length of the shortest path γ from x to y satisfying ˚γ ⊆Qo (or +∞if no such path exists).
title: Definition 5 (Distances) of arXiv:1710.10644: Percolation without FKG
