body: Question 5 of Hu and Sun's survey on Hunt's hypothesis (H) (arXiv:1908.06825) asks whether every pure-jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfies (H). The classical sufficient conditions bound Im psi by a multiple of 1 + Re psi; the oldest, Kanda-Forst, asks |Im psi(z)| <= M (1 + Re psi(z)) for all z. The driftless subordinator with Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}, x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}, has sum a_m x_m = 1 and sum a_m = infinity, and along z_m = 1/(m x_m) its exponent psi(z) = int (1 - e^{izx}) nu(dx) satisfies |Im psi(z_m)| / (1 + Re psi(z_m)) = 4m + O(1) (computed at high precision: 23.999 at m = 6, 32.000008 at m = 8), so the Kanda-Forst ratio is unbounded and the classical route to (H) is closed for it. It is not a counterexample to (H): an octave-by-octave estimate of the Kesten-Bretagnolle integral int Re(1/(1 + psi(z))) dz suggests the integral diverges, so points would be polar - a heuristic, not a proof. The example is atomic, outside the survey's type-(alpha, beta) density class, and the survey's Theorem 2.8 and Remark 2.21 anticipate processes of this kind, so it is an explicit witness with a computed rate rather than a new phenomenon.

[Theorem 5 (Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] For every \(C_0\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C=C(C_0)\) with the following property. Let
\[
A_i=B_i+L_i,
\qquad
i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
be self-adjoint matrices. Assume that \(B_i\in\mathcal A\) for a finite-dimensional \(C^*\)-algebra \(\mathcal A\) satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal A\le C_0n$, and assume $\|B_i\|\le 1$, $\|L_i\|\le 1$, and $\|L_i\|_F^2\le \frac{n}{\log^3(en)}$ for every \(i\in[n]\). Then, there exist signs \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\{\pm1\}\) such that
\[
\Bigl\|
\nlsum_{i=1}^n x_iA_i
\Bigr\|
\le
C(C_0)\sqrt n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matrix Spencer for rank-constrained perturbations of algebraic families

body:
[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $L\subset M_{n,m}(\R)$ and $K\subset \R^n$ be compact sets of positive volume whose convex hulls contain the (appropriate) origin in their interiors. Then, 
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n]((K^{\star,Q})_{\circ,Q})^m 
    \] 
    and 
    \[ 
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((L_{\circ,Q})^{\star,Q})\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m,
    \]
    with equality only for invariant sets (up to sets of Lebesgue measure zero). 
    
    In particular, the following two statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $K$ or $K^\circ$, has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m 
    \]
    with equality if and only if $K=E$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets; 
    \item  if $L_{\circ,Q}$ or $(L_{\circ,Q})^\circ$ has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m
    \]
    with equality if and only if $L=E^{\star,Q}$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset \R^n$ up to removal of null sets.
    \end{enumerate}

body: In probability theory and mathematical physics, a random matrix is a matrix-valued random variable—that is, a matrix in which some or all of its entries are sampled randomly from a probability distribution. Random matrix theory (RMT) is the study of properties of random matrices, often as they become large. RMT provides techniques like mean-field theory, diagrammatic methods, the cavity method, or the replica method to compute quantities like traces, spectral densities, or scalar products between eigenvectors. Many physical phenomena, such as the spectrum of nuclei of heavy atoms, the thermal conductivity of a lattice, or the emergence of quantum chaos, can be modeled mathematically as problems concerning large, random matrices.
title: Random matrix

Let $x\in\mbb R^2$ and $t>0$ be fixed,
and suppose that $Z$ is either $B^x$ or $B^{x,x}_t$.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item Let $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$.
There exists a random variable $\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)$ such that
\[\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)
\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
there exists a random variable $\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)$ such that
\[\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\Big(\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)-\mbf E\Big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)\Big]\Big)

\begin{equation}
 \eta^{(M-1)}_0 \succeq  \eta^{(M-2)}_0 \succeq \dots \succeq \eta^{(2)}_0 \succeq \eta^{(1)}_0 
\end{equation} according to the basic coupling $\mathbf{P}$. Then we define the \textbf{colored ASEP} $(\zeta_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for all $t \geq 0$ by
\begin{equation}
\zeta_t(i) := 1+\sum_{j=1}^{M-1} \big(1-\eta^{(j)}_t(i)\big)  
\end{equation}  for all $t \geq 0$ and $i \in  V$. We refer to the particles of colors $1,2,\dots,M-1$ as \textbf{first class particles}, \textbf{second class particles}, and so on, as well as to type $M$ particles as \textbf{empty sites}.

body:
Egorov's theorem states that on a FINITE measure space, almost everywhere convergence of measurable functions implies almost uniform convergence: for every eps > 0 there is a measurable E with mu(E) < eps such that the convergence is uniform on the complement of E. Finiteness cannot be dropped. On R with Lebesgue measure let f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}; then f_n -> 0 at every point, but for ANY set E of finite measure the complement meets [n, n+1] for infinitely many n, so sup over the complement of E of |f_n| equals 1 for infinitely many n and the convergence is not uniform off any set of small measure. What survives on a sigma-finite space is the LOCAL statement: for every measurable A with mu(A) < infinity and every eps > 0 there is E contained in A with mu(E) < eps and uniform convergence on A minus E; equivalently, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence on each set of finite measure. The converse implication holds in general: almost uniform convergence always implies convergence almost everywhere and in measure, on any measure space. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.33 and Exercise 2.39]
mu(Omega) < infinity for the global statement; a set of finite measure for the local statement
f_n measurable, f_n -> f mu-almost everywhere, all functions finite a.e.

body: Classical Schwarz lemma: if f maps the open unit disk holomorphically into itself and f(0)=0, then |f(z)|<=|z| and |f'(0)|<=1. Equality at a nonzero point or in the derivative bound forces f(z)=az with |a|=1. A distinct higher-dimensional result is Royden's Theorem1 (1980): let M be complete Kaehler with Ricci curvature at least k<=0, and N be Kaehler with holomorphic sectional curvature at most K<0. For a nonconstant holomorphic f:M->N, let nu be the maximal complex rank of df. In the paper's curvature convention, ||df||_op^2 <= Lambda(f) <= (2nu/(nu+1)) k/K, where Lambda(f)=trace_g(f*h) is the sum of squared singular values. Constant maps satisfy zero derivative directly. Trace energy and squared operator norm are distinct when rank exceeds one. This note does not assert the same conclusion for arbitrary Hermitian targets or remove the rank factor from the trace bound.
title: Schwarz lemma and Royden bound with hypotheses

body:
[Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}=\{R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $1$, with drift $-\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$, for each $i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$.
We consider the O'Connell-Yor polymer partition function (see [OYbb]) across $\{\mathcal{B}_i\}_{i=1}^{2k}$, defined as
\[
Z_{\mathcal{B}}(x,i;y,j) = \idotsint_{x=x_i\le \cdots \le x_j \le x_{j+1}=y} \exp\left( \sum_{i'=i}^j \mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'+1})-\mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'}) \right) dx_{i+1}\cdots dx_j,
\]
for any $1\le i \le j \le 2k$, and $0\le x \le y$.

Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j\in\llbracketi, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of inverse gamma random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal{B}$, satisfying 
\[X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
1 & j =i,\\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_j-\gamma_i), \qquad &j\in\llbracket i + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i- \gamma_{2k + 1 -j}), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i+\alpha), \qquad &j =  2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
\[
R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in P[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; x, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in P[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x\ge 0,\\
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; |x|, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x< 0,
\end{cases}
\]
where $P[i,\ell]$ is the collection of all up-right paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(-i,i)$ to $(-1,\ell)$, and  
$\hat{P}[i,\ell]$ is the subset of such paths that intersect $\{(x,x+2k+1): x\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020

STATUS: proof (unaudited). For the exact critical tanh infinitesimal-angle kernel of C050, n Cov(log M_q,log H_q) converges uniformly for 0<q<=C/n to [[2,-1],[-1,1]]. Conditional eigenvalue coupling preserves the joint norm/tangent law and compares it to independent chi-square variables with L2 log errors <=C*q*log(2n); covariance error is O_C(log(n)/sqrt(n)+log(n)^2/n). Reciprocal-angle logarithms reverse the off-diagonal signs. Assumptions: Fixed finite C; n->infinity; equal variances q in (0,C/n]; n>=2; angular derivative at zero taken before n limit. Scope: Leading centered one-step noise only, not drift, finite-angle evolution, entrance convergence, or all-order cumulant remainders; proof unaudited.
Fixed finite C; n->infinity; equal variances q in (0,C/n]; n>=2; angular derivative at zero taken before n limit.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/1a/1a086ad6a7ee1d1a40459d2a78d3b63dd7781ab3d438caac379eb986d3a8d885.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:77287f4d4792c9d694f179b6884ade1129b6f8376e899da074d1e85d979a5106","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","bundle_id":"population.t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise-017","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_017.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-tangent-shared-wishart-noise","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Critical tanh: exact tangent kernel and its shared Wishart noise

20 October 2026. C050/C051; Target 3. Proof drafts, unaudited.
These are infinitesimal-angle one-step results, not a two-input tanh
diffusion theorem or an all-order cumulant expansion. No novelty asserted.

## C050: exact positive-variance kernel

Fix n>=2 and q>0. Let g,h be independent N(0,I_n) vectors. For two inputs
with equal preactivation variance q and angle theta, the next activated
vectors are exactly distributed as

    x = tanh(sqrt(q) g),
    y(theta) = tanh(sqrt(q)(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h)).

The independent Gaussian weight rows give these conditional marginals
given the present Gram matrix. The tanh critical weight variance is 1/n;
thus the next diagonal variance is K'=||x||^2/n and the radial multiplier
is M_q=||x||^2/(nq). There is no width-dependent shaping normalizer.

Set D=diag(sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i)), P_x=I-xx^T/||x||^2. Then the right-hand
derivative H_q of the angle between x and y(theta) at theta=0 is

    H_q^2 = q h^T D P_x D h / ||x||^2.

Proof: y(0)=x and y'(0)=sqrt(q)Dh. The derivative of y/||y|| is
sqrt(q)P_x Dh/||x||, whose norm is the nonnegative angular speed.
Almost surely x is nonzero and this speed is positive for n>=2.

Conditionally on g, Q_q=h^T D P_x D h is a sum of n-1 independent
chi-square_1 variables with positive weights equal to the nonzero
eigenvalues lambda_j of D P_x D. These satisfy

    d_min^2 <= lambda_j <= 1,
    d_min = min_i sech^2(sqrt(q)g_i).

Indeed these nonzero eigenvalues equal those of P_x D^2 P_x restricted
to x-perp, whose Rayleigh quotients lie in that interval. Both M_q and
the conditional weights depend on the same g. In particular the exact
positive-q model must retain this conditioning; replacing Q_q by an
independent chi-square is a different kernel. Even the radial sum
||x||^2/q is bounded above by n/q, unlike a chi-square variable.

For fixed n, q decreases to zero gives jointly, almost surely under the
original (g,h) coupling,

    M_q -> S/n,      H_q -> sqrt(R/S),
    S=||g||^2 ~ chi-square_n,
    R=h^T P_g h ~ chi-square_(n-1),  R independent of g and hence of S.

The independence follows because the conditional law of R given g is
the same chi-square_(n-1) law for every nonzero g. The SAME S appears in
the radial multiplier and angular denominator. For n=1 the tangent
speed is zero, so logarithmic angular statements below exclude n=1.

## C051: uniform leading noise at the critical variance scale

For every fixed C<infinity, uniformly over 0<q<=C/n, define

    A_q=log M_q,       B_q=log H_q.

As n increases,

    n Cov((A_q,B_q)) -> [[2,-1],[-1,1]].

Here Cov is centered covariance. Equivalently, replacing B_q by the
logarithmic reciprocal-angle multiplier -B_q changes both off-diagonal
entries to +1. This only identifies one-step noise, not a drift limit.

### Coupling and quantitative error

Draw g and, independently, eta_1,...,eta_(n-1) iid standard normals.
Use a measurable ordering of the eigenvalues above and put

    Q_q^* = sum_j lambda_j(g) eta_j^2,
    R^* = sum_j eta_j^2,       S=||g||^2.

The pair (M_q, sqrt(q Q_q^*/||x||^2)) has EXACTLY the required joint
law (M_q,H_q), by the conditional quadratic-form law. Also S and R^*
are independent chi-squares with the stated degrees of freedom.
Thus this construction verifies both coupled marginals. No pointwise
comparison with the original h projection is being asserted.

For z>=0, sech^2(z) <= tanh(z)/z <= 1, with the continuous value at zero.
Consequently, with Z=max_i |g_i|,

    d_min^2 <= ||x||^2/(qS) <= 1,
    d_min^2 <= Q_q^*/R^* <= 1.

Since log(cosh z)<=z^2/2, this yields the deterministic coupling bounds

    |A_q-log(S/n)| <= 2q Z^2,
    |B_q-(1/2)log(R^*/S)| <= q Z^2.

A Gaussian union bound P(Z^2>r)<=min(1,2n exp(-r/2)), integrated as
E Z^4=integral_0^infinity 2r P(Z^2>r)dr, gives
||Z^2||_2 <= C_0 log(2n). Hence each logarithmic error has L2 norm at
most C_1 q log(2n), without deleting any event or inverse tail.

### Covariance calculation

Let A_0=log(S/n), B_0=(log R^*-log S)/2. Gamma integration gives

    Var A_0 = psi_1(n/2),
    Cov(A_0,B_0) = -(1/2)psi_1(n/2),
    Var B_0 = (psi_1((n-1)/2)+psi_1(n/2))/4.

The trigamma series psi_1(z)=sum_(k>=0)(z+k)^(-2) and integral comparison
give psi_1(z)=1/z+O(z^-2). These identities can alternatively be obtained
by differentiating E S^t=2^t Gamma(n/2+t)/Gamma(n/2) at t=0.
The displayed baseline covariance therefore has the claimed limit
after multiplying by n, and its centered L2 norms are O(n^-1/2).

For centered random variables, covariance perturbation by L2 errors e
has size at most C(n^-1/2 ||e||_2 + ||e||_2^2); centering an error costs
no more than its L2 norm. After multiplying by n, our bound is

    O(sqrt(n) q log(2n) + n q^2 log(2n)^2)
       = O_C(log(2n)/sqrt(n) + log(2n)^2/n),

uniformly over 0<q<=C/n. This tends to zero and proves C051.

## Scope left open

The limits are: first the angle derivative at zero for fixed n,q,
then n -> infinity with q<=C/n. C051 does not justify exchanging the
infinitesimal-angle limit with a finite-angle network evolution, does
not give the order-1/n drift, and does not establish that actual tanh
input correlations approach one. The scalar critical-tanh diffusion
and cumulant-rate work remain separate claims C026-C027 and C044-C047.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:22c6d532d863fd81ef53240a00570657817f6c17e8e5fb0515c76a33cfbda523","revision_digest":"sha256:fc88eab43dde02de84f288e293b9f37cf1114c075d6075db6c02f0a27cabfd4e","source_id":"owner-own-work:T244-w691-C051:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T13:53:12.705197","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: [Theorem 3.11 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,k,N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ be partial permutations, let $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, let $Y$ be the matrix resulting from the partial trace evaluation $(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{k}})(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})$, and let $q=\sum_{j=1}^{k}(m-|D(\sigma_{j})|)$ with $D(\sigma_{j})$ the domain of $\sigma_{j}$, so that $Y$ acts on a space of dimension $N^{q}$. For every $p\in\mathbb{N}$, $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\mathrm{Tr}((YY^{*})^{p})\leq N^{2pC(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}.$ (3.2) Moreover, for any configuration $\bm{\pi}_{0}$ with $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k};\bm{\pi}_{0})=M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$, it holds that $Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*}=N^{2M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}I_{N^{q}},\qquad\mathrm{Tr}((Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}Y_{\bm{\pi}_{0}}^{*})^{p})=N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}\quad(p\in\mathbb{N}).$ Thus, the tuple $(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m})=(E_{\pi_{1}},\ldots,E_{\pi_{m}})$, which is independent of $p$, attains every lower moment bound $N^{2pM(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})+q}$. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

[Lemma lem:complete-collision of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] In a fresh Kac frame put $\mathsf P_i=a_ia_i^*$ and
$W_i=\mathsf P_i-N^{-1}I_W$.  Before any ancillary boundary routing, the intact
coordinate-plane average obeys, for arbitrary real
$|\epsilon_i|\le1$,
\[
 \left\|\frac1N\sum_i\epsilon_iW_i\right\|_\mathrm{op}\le\frac2N.
\tag{3.2.10f}
\]
The exact scalar identities are
\[
 W_i^2=\left(1-\frac2N\right)W_i+\frac{N-1}{N^2}I,
 \qquad [A_i,\mathsf P_i]=0.
\tag{3.2.10g}
\]
If a passive map separates equal labels, then
\[
 \mathsf P_iT\mathsf P_i=\langle a_i,Ta_i\rangle \mathsf P_i;
\tag{3.2.10h}
\]
this expression remains in the intact collision block and is not replaced
by a scalar unless $T$ itself is scalar.  Relative to the Jacobi
coefficients $1,\gamma$, the only naked finite-$N$ residuals in (eq:3.2.10g of the paper)
are $-2N^{-1}W_i$ and $-\gamma N^{-1}I$.  The first child remains
time-indexed.  The second is formed only after the $m-1$ collision labels
have been summed; before residual temporal components are defined it is
removed from the temporal word, with $\gamma$ retained in the
monomer--dimer ledger and the remaining $N^{-1}$ kept as a favorable
scalar coefficient carrying no time, gap, anchor, or translation.

[Corollary cor: double well of arXiv:2503.24372, 'A criterion on the free energy for log-Sobolev inequalities in mean-field particle systems'] Under the same conditions as the previous theorem,
let $d=1$, and consider the choice of confinement potential of the form
\begin{equation}

 V(x)
 =
 \frac{x^4}{4} - \lambda\frac{x^2}{2}
 ,\qquad
 x,y,\lambda\in\R,
\end{equation}
or more generally suppose  that $V$ is in the GHS class, i.e.~satisfies Assumption~(ass_doublewell of the paper) below.
Then for any $T>T_c$ (defined in (equation eq_def_beta_c of the paper)), 
the measure $m^N_T$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with a constant independent of $N$.  
Moreover, the log-Sobolev constant vanishes  linearly at $T_c$: 
\begin{equation} 	
\limsup_{N\to\infty} \gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	
\leq 
c_1 (T-T_c)
,\qquad
\gamma^N_{\mathrm{LS}}(T)	\geq 
c_2 (T-T_c)
,\quad 
N\geq 1,
\end{equation}
for some  constants $c_1, c_2>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$\mathbb{E}\left[\abs{\xi(u)}^{2k}\right]\prec\psi^{2k}$$

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two.     \[
        \mathbb{E}^x\left[f(X_t);t\leq \sigma \right]=\int_E p^-_\sigma(t,x,y)f(y)\mu(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall t>0,x\in E, f\in \mathrm{b}\mathscr{B}(E).

In particular, 
\[
    p(t,x,y)=p^-_\sigma(t,x,y)+p^+_\sigma(t,x,y),\quad \forall t>0, x,y\in E 
\]
provides a decomposition of transition density function into the contributions before and after $\sigma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth exponents in the spatial city-formation model structural calculation Result: A rigorous one-sided bound supports the balanced exponent when0<alpha<1 and beta>2alpha. Write d=beta/2-alpha>0. A union bound over influence disks gives area{I(y,t)>u}<=pi*c0^(2/beta)*u^(-2/beta)*M_t^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta), using concavity of the population power. Thus the conditional founding probability is at least1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*M_t^d)], K=(2pi)^(beta/2)*c0. Put theta=(1-alpha)/(1+d) and m=floor(kappa*t^theta). Until M reaches m, each of the last floor(t/2) arrivals has founding chance at least p=1/[2*(1+K*t^alpha*m^d)]. Choose kappa small so this Bernoulli count has mean at least2m. A stopped coupling and Chernoff then give P(M_t<m)<=exp(-c*m) for large t. Check: The disk estimate is valid even at the square boundary because clipping only reduces area. Sum_i N_i^(2alpha/beta)<=M^(1-2alpha/beta)*t^(2alpha/beta). On the event M_t<m the threshold has never been reached, so domination by independent Bernoulli(p) increments throughout the half-interval is legitimate. The exponent identity theta*(1+d)=1-alpha makes the mean comparable to m. Obstruction: This proves a lower city-count growth bound in the balanced regime, not the matching upper bound, comparable populations, unbalanced regime, or alpha1 logarithmic law. The upper bound requires control of spatial clustering and influence overlap that the union bound does not supply.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0218-growth-exponents-in-the-spatial-city-formation-model

[Proposition 9 (Bounds on the error terms) of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] There exists an event \(\Omega\), measurable with respect to the Brownian paths
\(\{B_i(s)\}_{1\le i\le n,\ 0\le s\le \sfT}\), such that
\[
\mathbb P(\Omega)\ge 1-Ce^{-(\log n)^2},
\]
and the following holds on \(\Omega\).
For every \(t\in[0,\sfT]\), every \(x \in \cF_t\), every \(u\in \mathcal L\cap \mathcal D_0^{(t,x)}\), and every \(0\le s\le t\),
\begin{align}
|M_{s\wedge \sigma}(u)|
&\le \frac{C(\log n)^2}{n\sqrt{\eps\,\eta_*}},
\\
|R_{s\wedge \sigma}(u)|
&\le \frac{C\log n}{n\eps}.

\end{align}
title: Bounds on the error terms

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $d = o(\sqrt n)$. Suppose the exchangeable unconditional base vector $\mathbf X$ satisfies \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item  $\E X_1^2 = 1$,
        \item  $\frac{1}{n^{4d}}\E\nm{\mathbf X}_2^{8d} \to 1$, and 
        \item  there exists a sequence $L = L_n$ satisfying $Ld^2 / n \to 0$ such that $\E(X_1^8\dotsm X_r^8) \leq L^{2r}$ for all $1 \leq r\leq d$.
        
        
    \end{enumerate} then the three conditions in \cref{thm:main} are satisfied, and we have with probability $1$ that \[\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}.\]

    Alternatively, \cref{cond:8th-block-mmt} may be replaced by 
    \begin{enumerate}[resume,label=(iii')]
        \item  there exists a sequence $L = L_n$ satisfying $Ld^2 / n \to 0$ such that $\frac{1}{n^{2r}} \E\nm{\mathbf X}_4^{8r} \leq L^{2r}$ for all $1 \leq r \leq d$.\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 6 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Defn Infinitesimal holonomy of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a cooriented $C^0$-foliation on $M$, and $\gamma : S^1 \rightarrow L$ be a smooth closed curve tangent to a leaf $L$ of $\mathcal{F}$, inducing a holonomy map 
    $$h : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \rightarrow (-1,1)$$
    for some $\varepsilon > 0$. We say that $\mathcal{F}$ has \textbf{infinitesimal attracting holonomy} around $\gamma$ if for every open interval $\{0\} \subset I \subset (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$, there exists a smaller open interval $\{0\} \subset J \subset I$ such that 
    $$\overline{h(J)} \subset J.$$

[Theorem 4 (The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $u \in \R^n$. Let $f \in \mathcal{F}(\conbodI)$. Then, for every measurable function $g:\R^n\to\R_+$ and measurable, non-increasing function $\Omega : (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ such that 
    \[
    f(x)g(y) \leq \Omega^2(\langle x, y \rangle), \qquad \forall \,\,x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } \langle x,y \rangle>0,
    \] 
    it holds
    \begin{equation}
    
        \left(\int_{\R^n} f(x) \langle x,u \rangle^2 dx \right) \left(\int_{\R^n} g(y) \langle y,u \rangle^2 dy \right) \leq \left(\int_{\R^n} \Omega(|z|^2) \langle z,u \rangle^2 dz \right)^2.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Functional, isotropic Ball-Santal\'o inequality

Let n/(d-1)->alpha>0 and let the orthogonal block G have independent standard Gaussian entries, independent of iid T. Maximize min_i(a*T_i+(Gv)_i) on a^2+||v||^2<=1. The limiting margin and teacher coefficient are K and a*, the unique positive-margin optimizer of max k subject to k,a,s>=0, a^2+s^2<=1 and sqrt(alpha E[(k-aT-sH)_+^2])<=s, H independent standard Gaussian. In the isotropic Gaussian test model its limiting disagreement is acos(a*)/pi. This includes unpruned T=|Z|. Proof extends empirical envelopes and uses endpoint secants for uniform concave-profile convergence; it relies on the unaudited conditional-CGMT argument. [Lemma 16 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Let
\[     A^{(n)}_{ij}:=\Cov(\xi_{n,i},\xi_{n,j}),     \qquad 0\le i,j\le b^n-1.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}     b^{-2n}\sum_{i,j=0}^{b^n-1}\abs{A^{(n)}_{ij}}^2\le C     \qquad\text{for all }n.                                    
\end{equation}
Also,
\begin{equation}     \Var(\xi_{n,k})\le Cn     \qquad\text{for all }n\text{ and }0\le k\le b^n-1.          
\end{equation}

[Lemma eq:compact-support-joint-energy of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Suppose Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and
(ass:bochner-regularity of the paper) hold.  Let $w$ be a regular weight, let
$I=(r_0,r_1)$, and suppose
$h\in W_{p,\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(I\times\mathbb R^d)$ for some $p>d+2$.  If, for every compact
positive strip $J\Subset I$, there is a compact set $K_J\Subset\mathbb R^d$ such
that
$
 h=0\,\text{on }J\times(\mathbb R^d\setminus K_J),
$
then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak B_{J,w}(h)<\infty
 \qquad\text{for every compact positive strip }J\Subset I.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently, if, in addition, $h=S_IF$ for some $F\in L_w^2(I)$ and $h$ has
an upper terminal gap, then
\begin{equation}
 h\in\mathfrak C_{\rm B}(I,w).
 
\end{equation}

body:
Let γ : [α,β] → C be a closed piecewise C^1 curve and let a be a point not on the trace of γ. The winding number (index) of γ about a is n(γ,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ dz/(z - a). It is always an integer; as a function of a it is constant on each connected component of the complement of the trace of γ, and it is 0 on the unbounded component. The definition extends additively to cycles (finite formal integer combinations of closed curves) and, via continuous branches of the argument, to merely continuous closed curves. A cycle γ lying in an open set U is called null-homologous in U (homologous to zero) if n(γ,w) = 0 for every w in C minus U. An open connected U ⊂ C is simply connected if and only if every cycle in U is null-homologous in U, if and only if the complement of U in the Riemann sphere is connected. The homology form of Cauchy's theorem reads: if f is holomorphic on U and γ is a cycle null-homologous in U, then ∫_γ f(z) dz = 0 and n(γ,z) f(z) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ - z) dζ for every z in U off the trace of γ.

the point a does not lie on the trace of γ

For every pair of integers r,s>=2 there exists an integer R(r,s) such that every red-blue coloring of the edges of a complete graph on at least R(r,s) vertices contains either a red complete subgraph on r vertices or a blue complete subgraph on s vertices. In particular, R(3,3)<=6.

[Proposition prop:tilted_gen_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $k\in\mathbb{R}$ and let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold, in particular, 
assume additive noise $D=\sigma\sigma^\top/2$. The semigroup
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t \geq 0}$ is a strongly continuous semigroup on $L^2(\mu)$ whose
infinitesimal generator acts on $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ as
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J
  &=
  b \cdot (\nabla + kU)
  +
  (\nabla + kU) \cdot D(\nabla + kU),
  
\end{align}
or equivalently, expanding for $f \in D(\mathcal{L})$ yields
\begin{align}
  \mathcal{L}_k^J f
  &=
  \mathcal{L}f
  +
  k\bigl(b \cdot U + \nabla \cdot DU\bigr) f + 2kU \cdot D \nabla f
  +
  k^2(U \cdot DU)f.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tilted generator for current observables

Let f: U -> R^n be C^1 on an open set U containing an equilibrium x* of y' = f(y) (f(x*) = 0), and suppose x* is hyperbolic: A = Df(x*) has no eigenvalue with zero real part. Then there are a neighborhood V of x* and a homeomorphism h: V -> h(V) in R^n with h(x*) = 0 that conjugates the nonlinear flow phi_t near x* to the linear flow exp(tA): h(phi_t(x)) = exp(tA) h(x) for x in V and every t with phi_s(x) in V for s between 0 and t, so orbits go to orbits with the direction of time kept. The discrete-time analogue holds for a diffeomorphism g with a hyperbolic fixed point x* (Dg(x*) has no eigenvalue of modulus 1): g is locally topologically conjugate near x* to Dg(x*).
f is C^1 near the equilibrium x*
x* is hyperbolic: Df(x*) has no purely imaginary eigenvalue (resp. Dg(x*) has no eigenvalue of modulus 1 in the discrete-time case)

body: Seifert-Van Kampen theorem: Let X be a topological space written as X = U union V, where U and V are open and path-connected and the intersection U intersect V is nonempty and path-connected, and choose a basepoint x_0 in U intersect V. Let i and j denote the homomorphisms pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(U, x_0) and pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(V, x_0) induced by inclusion. Then pi_1(X, x_0) is the pushout of i and j, i.e. the free product with amalgamation pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0) modulo the normal subgroup generated by all elements i(g) j(g)^{-1} with g in pi_1(U intersect V, x_0). In particular, if U intersect V is simply connected then pi_1(X, x_0) is the free product pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0). This lets one compute fundamental groups of spaces built from simpler pieces.
title: Seifert–Van Kampen theorem

Let k be an algebraically closed field and R = k[x_1, ..., x_n]. Weak form: every proper ideal I of R has a common zero, that is, V(I) = {a in k^n : f(a) = 0 for all f in I} is nonempty; equivalently every maximal ideal of R has the form (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n). Strong form: for every ideal I, the ideal of polynomials vanishing on V(I) is the radical of I: if g in R vanishes on V(I) then g^m in I for some m >= 1. Hence V and I give an inclusion-reversing bijection between radical ideals of R and algebraic subsets of k^n.
k algebraically closed (over R, for example, x^2 + 1 has no zero and the weak form fails)

[Definition def:cone of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] For any $u_1>1$, we choose a small constant $d_0>0$ and a large constant $n_1>64\, d_0^2$ such that the following construction is possible for all $n>n_1$ and $1\le m\le n$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$]
        \item On the unit sphere, we pick $n$ unit vectors $(v_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ such that $|v_i-v_{i'}|>12\,d_0\,n^{-1/2}$ for any $1\le i<i'\le n$. Let $S_i:=\mathsf{C}(v_i,d_0/\sqrt n)$, $1\le i\le n$, be $n$ disjoint cones.
        \item On each surface $S_i\cap\partial \mathcal{B}_0$, we further pick $m$ points $v_{i,j}$ along an arc such that the following properties hold.
        Let $c_0$ and $c_1$ be two small positive constants. Consider two smaller cones
        \[
        T_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},u_1^{-n}) \quad \text{and} \quad V_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},c_0m^{-1}n^{-1/2}).
        \]
        For any $i,j$, we have $T_{i,j}\subseteq V_{i,j}\subseteq S_i$, $\mathrm{dist}(v_{i,j},\partial S_i)\ge c_1\, n^{-1/2}$, and $V_{i,j}\cap V_{i,l}=\varnothing$ if $j\neq l$. Moreover, if $1\le j<l\le m$, then $ |z/|z|-v_{i,l}|\geq c_1|j-l|/(m\sqrt n)$  for every $z\in V_{i,j}$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:ub of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] In the setting of (thm:1 of the paper), fix $n\geq 1$ and $K>0$, let $\rho_n(x)$ be the maximum vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ above $x+(\frac{L}2,0)$ for $-N_n^{2/3} \leq x\leq N_n^{2/3}$,
and set $\sigma^2>0$ as per (def:sigma of the paper). 
Then every weak limit point $\mathbf{Y}_n(t)$ of the process $Y_n(t):=N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$ ($t\in[-K,K]$), as $L\to\infty$, satisfies
\[ \mathbf{Y}_n \preceq \mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,. \]
Moreover, for every fixed $m$, every weak limit point $({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ of the processes $(Y_n(t))_{n\leq m}$ satisfies
\[ ({\ensuremath{\mathbf Y}}_n)_{n\leq m} \preceq \bigotimes_{n\leq m}\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}\,.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:ub of arXiv:2509.04333

An elementary probability control, not an FPP counterexample. If J is uniform on {1,...,m} and A_i={J=i}, each deterministic event has probability 1/m, while P(union_i A_i)=1. Equivalently, each threshold indicator has mean 1/m and their maximum is always one. Therefore an estimate for every deterministic pair of endpoints does not automatically control a pair chosen after observing the environment. For the square boundary S_n in Z^2 there are 8n sites and at most 64n^2 ordered endpoint pairs; a raw union bound needs a per-pair bound o(n^-2) to vanish. Qualitative midpoint decay supplies no such conclusion. Independence of the resampled edge from its outside environment is valid; multiplying success probabilities for correlated endpoint capacities or selected corridors needs an additional justified filtration or independence argument.
uniform m-point toy probability space for the control
square lattice boundary for the endpoint count
title: DRAFT proof guard: deterministic endpoints and adaptive maxima

[Proposition prop:Lambda_variational of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] With the Dirichlet form $\mathcal{E}(f,f)=-\langle\mathcal{L}_S f,f\rangle_\mu$,
\begin{align}
  &\Lambda^\rho(k)
  =
  \sup\left\{k\langle V,f^2\rangle_\mu-\mathcal{E}(f,f)
    \mathrel{\Big|} f \in D(\mathcal{L}_k^\rho),\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)} = 1
  \right\},
  
  \\
  &\Lambda^J(k)
  =
  \sup\left\{k\langle v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U,f^2\rangle_\mu
        + k^2\langle U\cdot DU,f^2\rangle_\mu-\mathcal{E}(f,f)
    \mathrel{\Big|} f \in D(\mathcal{L}_k^J),\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)} = 1
  \right\}.
  
\end{align}

body:
[Proposition pro: Wasserstein-$p$ bound without exchangeability final version of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Let $X\in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a random vector, and $T: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function. Suppose $T(X)$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[|T(X)|^p] < \infty$ for some $p > 1$. We assume Assumptions (assumption: Stein identity final version of the paper), (assumption: Kramers-Moyal expansion final version of the paper) and (assumption: integrability of Kramers-Moyal coefficients final version of the paper)
     hold for $X$ with operator $\mathcal{A}$ and mapping $T$. Then for any $t_0 > 0$, we have the following upper bound for Wasserstein-$p$ distance between $\mathcal{L}(T(X))$ and $\mathcal{L}(Z')$, 
    \begin{align}
        W_p(\mathcal{L}(T(X)), \mathcal{L}(Z')) &\leq g_0(t_0,p) + \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - a_{k}^{\mathcal{L}_{OU}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &= g_0(t_0,p) + g_1(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[| a_{1}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) + T(X)|^p]^{1/p} \notag\\
        &+ g_2(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{2}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X) - 1|^p]^{1/p} + \sum_{k=3}^{\infty} g_k(t_0,p) \mathbb{E}[|a_{k}^{\mathcal{A}, T}(X)|^p]^{1/p}, 
    \end{align}
    where $Z'\sim N(0,1)$ and the coefficients $g_k(t_0,p)$ for $k\ge 0$
are continuous in $(t_0,p)$ and are given explicitly in (equation eq: W-p bound final of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wasserstein-$p$ bound via generator comparison

[Thm 43 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $M$ be a matroid. Suppose $F$ is a flat of $M$ minimal for the property that $M$ is a non-trivial modular join over $F$. Choose flats $F_0, F_1$ with $F = F_0 \cap F_1$ such that $M = P_F(F_0, F_1)$. 
Then $M$ is supersolvable if and only if $M_0 \deq M|_{F_0}$ and $M_1 \deq M|_{F_1}$ are both supersolvable and at least one of them has a full modular flag passing through $F$.

[Lemma cutoff of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] Let $\tau,j_0,\alpha$ be as above. Let $U=\frac{\mathcal{L}^n}{\mathcal{L}^n(Q_{j_0,\alpha})}\in {\mathcal M}_+(\mathbb{R}^n)$
     be the Lebesgue measure normalized by the volume of $Q_{j_0,\alpha}$.  Then for any $\delta>0$ there is a cutoff function $\eta\in C_c^\infty(Q_{j_0,\alpha};[0,1])$ such that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\eta(x) =1 $ whenever $x\in  Q_{j_0,\alpha}$ with $\dist(x,\partial Q_{j_0,\alpha}) \geq \delta$ 
        \item $\| \dive \left(j_0 \left(\eta \tau + (1-\eta)U\right)\right) \|_{\mathrm{KR}} \leq C|j_0|\alpha$,
    \end{enumerate}
where $C$ depends only on $R$ and $n$.

body: Let mu and nu be probability measures on a measurable space (S, S), and let (X, Y) be any coupling of mu and nu, meaning X and Y are random variables defined on a common probability space with X distributed as mu and Y distributed as nu. DRAFT proof-audit material, independent referee check pending. On the path o--a2--b--a1 with three independent Bernoulli(1/2) bonds, order A=(a1,a2). Let F2 mean that a2 is the first member of A connected to o in this order. Then P(F2)=3/8 and P(F2 and a2 connects to b)=1/8, so P(a2 connects to b | F2)=1/3, whereas min_(a in A)P(a connects to b)=1/2. The first-reached event contains a decreasing exclusion, so FKG does not justify the pointwise conditional lower bound. The Kozma--Nitzan global inequality P(o connects to b)>=P(o connects to A)min_(a in A)P(a connects to b) is nevertheless an equality here (both sides 1/4). This refutes the conditional proof premise, not the global conjecture.

body: Let (mu_n) be a sequence of probability measures and mu a probability measure on a metric space S with its Borel sigma-algebra. The following are equivalent: (i) mu_n converges weakly to mu, meaning integral of f d mu_n converges to integral of f d mu for every bounded continuous f: S -> R; (ii) limsup_n mu_n(F) <= mu(F) for every closed set F; (iii) liminf_n mu_n(G) >= mu(G) for every open set G; (iv) mu_n(A) converges to mu(A) for every Borel set A with mu(boundary of A) = 0. [standard, e.g. Billingsley, Convergence of Probability Measures]
title: Portmanteau Characterization of Weak Convergence

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \((T_L)_{L\geq1}\) be positive trace-class contractions on a Hilbert space. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \(\sup_{L\geq1}L^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(T_L)<\infty\);
\item there is a measurable \(r:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) with \(r\in L^1(0,\infty)\) such that, for every \(m\geq1\),
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{tr}(T_L^m)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_0^\infty r(\xi)^m\,\mathrm{d}\xi.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then, for each \(t>-1\),
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{1}{L}\log\det(\operatorname{Id}+tT_L)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}
\int_0^\infty \log\bigl(1+t\,r(\xi)\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\xi,
\]
locally uniformly for \(t\) in compact subsets of \((-1,\infty)\).

  We call $\tau$ a \textit{functor} on $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ if it satisfies the following.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      For every $ (S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$,
      one has a metric space $(\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}), d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}})$
      where $\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$ is a set and $d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}}$ is a metric on it.
      We simply write $\tau(S) \coloneqq \tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$.
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      one has a distance-preserving map $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$.
    \item 
      For any two root-and-distance-preserving maps $f :S_{1} \to S_{2},\, g : S_{2} \to S_{3}$,
      it holds that $\tau_{g \circ f} = \tau_{g} \circ \tau_{f}$.
    \item 
      For any $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$, 
      it holds that $\tau_{\id_{S}} = \id_{\tau(S)}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Similarly, we call $\tau$ a functor on $\mathfrak{M}$ if it satisfies the same conditions 
  not for $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ but for $\mathfrak{M}$.

Every set can be well-ordered: for every set X there exists a total (linear) order on X in which every nonempty subset of X has a least element. Over ZF the well-ordering theorem is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to Zorn's lemma.

P is nonempty (the empty set with the empty order, or any singleton). Every chain in P has an upper bound: take the union of the domains with the union of the orders; end-extension makes this a well-defined linear order, and it is a well-order because any nonempty subset meets some member W of the chain, and its least element within that W remains least overall, since later members of the chain only add elements above all of W. [Dfn 37 (Sub-exponential class) of arXiv:2609.02398, '\textbf{Convex Order Comparisons for Sub-Gamma Random Variables}'] Let $\sigma, \alpha > 0$. A random variable $X$ belongs to the class
$\SE(\sigma^2, \alpha)$ if
\begin{align}
    \E\left[e^{\lambda X}\right]
    \leq \exp\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2}{2}\right)
    \qquad \text{for all } |\lambda| \leq \frac{1}{\alpha} \, .
    
\end{align}
title: Sub-exponential class

body:
[Prop discretize of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Given a strong solution $t\mapsto \text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}\in\mathbb{R}^N$ to the SDE

    \begin{align*}
{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}=\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(t)}){\rm d} t+\sigma{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(t)}
\end{align*}

    on $\mathbb{R}^N$ for some function $\text{\boldmath $a$}:\mathbb{R}^N\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^N$ and constant diffusion coefficient $\sigma$, along with a step
    size $\delta\in(0,1)$, consider the Euler-Maruyama scheme
    $\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(0)},\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(1)},\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(2)},\ldots$ defined recursively by
    $\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(0)}=\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(0)}$ and

    \begin{align*}
\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n+1)}=\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n)}+\delta
\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(n)})+\sigma(\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(\delta(n+1))}-\text{\boldmath $w$}^{(\delta n)}).
\end{align*}

    Suppose that, for some positive constants $K_1,K_2,K_3$, we have that
    $\mathbb{E}[\|\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(0)}\|^2]\le K_1N$, $\| \text{\boldmath $a$}({\boldsymbol 0})\|^2\le K_2N$, and
    $\| \text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $u$})-\text{\boldmath $a$}(\text{\boldmath $v$})\|\le K_3\|\text{\boldmath $u$}-\text{\boldmath $v$}\|$ for all $\text{\boldmath $u$},\text{\boldmath $v$}\in\mathbb{R}^N$,
    i.e. the initial condition is bounded in $L^2$ and the drift
    coefficient is Lipschitz and bounded at the origin. Then there
    exists a constant $L$ depending only on $K_1,K_2,K_3$ such that
    for all $\delta>0$ and $T\in\delta\mathbb{N}$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[\|\text{\boldmath $x$}^{(T)}-\text{\boldmath $y$}^{(T/\delta)}\|^2]\le Le^{LT}\delta N.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop discretize of arXiv:2608.06500

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Let $t>0$ and $x_1,x_2\in\mbb R^2$ be fixed.
Suppose that the pair $(Z_1,Z_2)$ is either $({_1}B^{x_1},{_2}B^{x_2})$
or $({_1}B^{x_1,x_1}_t,{_2}B^{x_2,x_2}_t)$.
Given a positive $\theta>0$,
let us denote the event
\[\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)=\left\{\inf_{(r_1,r_2)\in[0,t]^2}\|Z_1(r_1)-Z_2(r_2)\|\geq\theta\right\}.\]
Almost surely, $\al_t(Z_1,Z_2)\mbf 1_{\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)}=0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo Approximation of arXiv:2411.19543, 'Feller property and convergence for semigroups of time-changed processes'] Let $F_n,\, F$ be the fine supports of $\mu_n,\mu_\infty$, respectively. Assume that $F_n,\, F,\, n\in\mathbb{N}$ are closed. Let $\Pi_n : C_0(F)\to C_0(F_n),\;\, u\mapsto (P_F u)|_{F_n}$. Then for all $u\in C_0(F)$ it holds
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)] 
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in F_n} \left|\check{T}_t^n \Pi_n u(x) - \Pi_n \check{T}_t^\infty u(x) \right| = 0
\]
locally uniformly in $t\in [0,\infty)$.
\item[\rm(2)] For all $\alpha>0$
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in F_n} \left|V_\alpha^n \Pi_n u(x) - \Pi_n V_\alpha^\infty u(x) \right| = 0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Approximation

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton structural argument Result: If the offspring distribution has finite support bounded by D, each coordinate of the distributional map is a polynomial of degree at most D in the color probabilities. Fixed points are therefore a compact real algebraic subset of the probability simplex. In contrast with one variable, polynomial equations may have curves of zeros, so analyticity alone cannot prove finiteness. Check: For example, the algebraic system x-y=0 in a square has a whole line of zeros; this illustrates the logical gap without asserting that this system comes from an automaton. Obstruction: The nonnegative multinomial coefficients and deterministic count assignments constrain which algebraic sets can occur. Neither an admissible positive-dimensional example nor a general exclusion is obtained.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0093-infinitely-many-fixed-points-of-a-finite-color-automaton
No independent review
title: Attempt on Infinitely many fixed points of a finite-color automaton

[Theorem thm:heavy of arXiv:2508.17838, '\bf Edge Universality for Inhomogeneous Random Matrices'] If the IRM matrix  $X$  in Definition~(def:inhomo of the paper)  satisfies  Assumptions~(itm:B1 of the paper)–(itm:B2 of the paper) with $t_N \ll N^{\tfrac13 - \zeta}$ 
 for some $\zeta\in (0, \tfrac13)$, and 
the  entries of $W$ have uniform moments   with  some fixed $\epsilon_0>0$, 
\begin{equation} 
\sup_{i,j}\mathbb{E}\bigl[\lvert W_{ij}\rvert^{\tfrac{4+\epsilon_0}{\zeta}}\bigr]\le C,
\end{equation}
then the largest eigenvalue of \(X\) 
 converges in distribution to the Tracy–Widom law.

body: [Theorem 5.1 ([13]) of arXiv:2511.20698, 'On the Role of Hidden States of Modern Hopfield Network in Transformer'] The norm of the residual of attention-only network ${\textrm{AttnNet}}(\bm{X})$ decays as $\displaystyle\|\textrm{Res}\left({\textrm{AttnNet}}(\bm{X})\right)\|_{1,\infty}\leq\left(rC\right)^{\frac{3^{L}-1}{2}}\|\textrm{Res}\left(\bm{X}\right)\|_{1,\infty}^{3^{L}},$ (13) where $r=\frac{8H}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}$ and $C$ is certain constant. This suggests the double exponential decay of the rank.

Then, almost surely, for every $t \in [0,T]$ and $\varphi \in \mathcal{C}^{1,1}_{\omega,T}(\mathbb{R}^{+} \times \mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$, 
$$\Psi_{t}(\mu^{*}) = 0.$$
Furthermore, $R^{*}=R^{\mu^{*}}$ almost surely, with $R^{\mu^{*}}$ defined as in (equation eq:ressourceùiu of the paper). We thus conclude that almost surely, $(\mu^{*}_{t},R^{*}_{t})_{t \in [0,T]}$ verifies Equations~(equation eq:resslim of the paper) and (equation eq:indivlim of the paper).

body: Let tau be a stopping time with respect to a filtration (F_t)_{t in T} (that is, {tau <= t} is in F_t for every t). The sigma-algebra of events prior to tau, denoted F_tau, is defined as the collection of all A in F such that A intersect {tau <= t} is in F_t for every t in T. F_tau is itself a sigma-algebra, tau is F_tau-measurable, and if sigma and tau are stopping times with sigma <= tau almost surely then F_sigma is a subset of F_tau. [standard, e.g. Karatzas and Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus]
title: The Stopping-Time Sigma-Algebra F_tau

[Thm 228 (\textbf{main result for symmetrized projection pursuit}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The following holds in the Ising (resp. spherical) cases.
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item 
        
        If $\mu \in \ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ (resp. $\ocM^{\sph,\sym}(\alpha)$), for any $\iota > 0$ there exist $L$ large enough and $c$ small enough such that for sufficiently large $N$, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm that $(\iota,1-e^{-cN})$-symmetrically attains $\mu$.
        \item 
        
        For any $\fq \in [1,2)$ and $\iotamsr > 0$, there exists small $\iotasol > 0$ such that the following holds.
        For any $L$, there exists small $c>0$ such that for sufficiently large $N$, all $L$-Lipschitz algorithms are $(\fq, \iotamsr,\iotasol,1-e^{-cN})$-symmetrcally confined to $\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For f(u)=1-exp(-u), P_s the semigroup of dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)VdW, a=1/(3pi), and Q_n the global hybrid ReLU reciprocal kernel, let g_k=P_(v_k)f with arbitrary deterministic v_k in[0,T]. Along its chain from U0=1/(n theta0), fixed theta0 in(0,pi], N<=Tn, sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E|(Q_n-P_(1/n))g_k(U_k)-Cg_k(U_k)/n^2|<=C_(theta0,T)/n. Here C=(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2, b=1/(6pi^2). Assumptions: Independent Gaussian zero-bias ReLU rows/layers, hybrid normalized/ordinary Gram self-loop kernel of C039, n sufficiently large, fixed T. Semigroup tests have bounded polynomially weighted positive-order derivatives of every fixed order, proved from the affine SDE solution. The angle transition uses n independent row pairs x=max(g,0), y=max(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h,0), g,h iid standard Gaussians, independent across layers, and the angle between the resulting vectors. Kill at zero norm or zero angle. For the hybrid kernel use a fixed small concentration box for (mean(x^2+y^2),mean((x-y)^2)/theta^2,mean(x^2-y^2)/theta) at small theta, and ordinary Gram averages at larger theta, each centered at its expectation; self-loop on failure. Limit: New proof of all-state uniformity and accumulation awaits independent audit. This is an accumulated local-defect statement, with finite-moment calculations confined to the hybrid chain. P_s g(u)=E[g(V_s^u)] for dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)VdW,V0=u,a=1/(3pi). The semigroup sensitivity D_t=D P_t f(0)=E[exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t-V_t^0)], f(u)=1-exp(-u).

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:4fa172f7326b7cf343a5dab2ef18c188e23a118bb2655d2c8fd721ca7b379026","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/4f/4fa172f7326b7cf343a5dab2ef18c188e23a118bb2655d2c8fd721ca7b379026.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:af0b975c427f642f8aec1205def6bc54a1a3515149422f6182a41c5f8c3dc067","bundle_entry_key":"relu-all-state-weak-defect","bundle_id":"population.t244-logarithmic-bounded-weak-rate-015","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-relu-all-state-weak-defect","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C042-C043: bounded-observable logarithmic finite-width bias

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target 1, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
All claims below depend on the preceding unaudited C032-C041 calculations
as specified. They require the reviewer's independent check. This is a
bounded-observable result, not an expansion of the infinite raw exact
reciprocal mean. Literature novelty is not asserted.

Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and

    A=(2u+a)D+u^2 D^2,
    B=(10u+6a/5+b/u)D+(11u^2+12au/5+a^2/2)D^2
                                +(4u^3+au^2)D^3+(u^4/2)D^4,
    C=B-A^2/2=(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2.

Let P_s be the semigroup of dV=(2V+a)ds+sqrt(2)V dW, and f(u)=1-exp(-u).
Use C039's global hybrid Gaussian/ReLU kernel Q_n for the reciprocal
U=1/(n theta). Fix theta0 in (0,pi], T<infinity.

## C042: accumulated local weak defect, with no reciprocal upper cutoff

For any deterministic v_k in [0,T], put g_k=P_(v_k)f. Uniformly in
N<=Tn, with U_k the hybrid chain started at U0=1/(n theta0),

    sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E| (Q_n-P_(1/n))g_k(U_k)
                                          -Cg_k(U_k)/n^2 |
                                             <=C_(theta0,T)/n. (1)

The v_k need not be monotone. This is a local-defect estimate along the
chain, sufficient for telescoping bounded tests. It contains no stopping
boundary correction and uses no finite raw reciprocal moment of the exact
network.

### Weighted semigroup derivative bounds

The affine solution V_v^u=V_v^0+uJ_v, J_v=exp(v+sqrt(2)W_v), gives

    D^j g_v(u)=(-1)^(j+1) E[J_v^j exp(-V_v^0-uJ_v)], j>=1.

For every nonnegative integer r and positive integer j,

    sup_(0<=v<=T,u>=0) u^r |D^j g_v(u)| < infinity.             (2)

For r=0 use E J_v^j. For r>0 use (uJ_v)^r exp(-uJ_v)<=r^r exp(-r)
and the finite lognormal moment E J_v^(j-r), uniform for v in [0,T].
Also 0<=g_v<=1. These are uniform all-state bounds, stronger than merely
bounded unweighted derivatives on fixed reciprocal compacts.

### The small-angle expansion with constants uniform in u

Fix the small-angle threshold epsilon of the hybrid kernel and set
theta=1/(nu)<=epsilon, allowing arbitrarily large u. In C032's normalized
concentration box, T_theta(z)=theta/output_angle is between fixed positive
constants, with uniformly bounded coordinate derivatives of every fixed
order needed below. By the chain rule and (2),

    |D_z^ell [g_v(uT_theta(z))]|<=C_T min(u,1), 1<=ell<=5.     (3)

For u<=1 every term contains u^j with j>=1 and a bounded derivative.
For u>=1 use (2) with r=j and the positive lower bound on T_theta.
The same bounds apply to the further finitely many weighted derivatives
needed for the theta-expansion coefficients and their mean-coordinate
variation. No derivative of g_v of order zero is asserted to decay.

Repeat C032's fourth-order centered sample-average expansion, retaining
(3). Its scaled Taylor remainder is C_T min(u,1)n^(-3/2). Freezing the
third- and fourth-moment coefficient at theta=0 costs at most
C_T min(u,1)sqrt(theta)/n. The covariance and coordinate multiplier
second-order theta remainders cost C_T min(u,1)theta^2. Deleted bounded
test terms cost C_T n exp(-cn), uniformly in u. Their polynomial Taylor
terms have the same exponential control by uniform row moments and (3).

The baseline zero-angle coefficients remain precisely C030's terms,
uniformly in u, by the same Taylor expansion and (3). The deterministic
map has displacement

    u theta/F(theta)-u=a/n+b/(n^2 u)+O(1/(n^3 u^2)),

which is O(1/n) uniformly for theta<=epsilon. Its scalar test Taylor
remainder after scaling is bounded by C_T(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2, exactly as
in C036. Thus the identical explicit operators A,B satisfy

    | n(Q_n-I)g_v(u)-Ag_v(u)-Bg_v(u)/n |
      <=C_T[n^(-3/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2+n exp(-cn)],
                                      theta=1/(nu)<=epsilon.  (4)

In simplifying, min(u,1)/sqrt(u)<=1 and
min(u,1)theta^2<=C(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2 were used. The constants in (4)
are independent of any upper cutoff on u. This uniformity is the new
step beyond C036; it is justified by the derivative decay in (2).

### The diffusion step and the large-angle step

The functions Ag_v,A^2g_v,A^3g_v are uniformly bounded by (2), since
their coefficients are polynomials multiplying positive-order derivatives.
Their Ito martingale coefficients are bounded as well, using the bounds
on u times their first derivatives. Iterated Dynkin identities therefore
give, with h=1/n,

    P_h g_v=g_v+hAg_v+h^2 A^2g_v/2+O_T(h^3),                 (5)

uniformly for all u>=0. One can first localize the nonexplosive linear SDE
and then remove the localization by boundedness; no assertion of a
globally analytic semigroup is needed. Combining (4)-(5) proves the
pointwise small-angle defect bound

    |(Q_n-P_h)g_v-Cg_v/n^2|
       <=C_T[n^(-5/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^3+exp(-cn)].           (6)

If theta>epsilon, then u<=1/(n epsilon). The hybrid ratio U_next/u is
bounded, so |Q_n g_v-g_v|<=C_T u<=C_T/n by the bounded first derivative.
Also |P_hg_v-g_v|<=h||Ag_v||_infinity<=C_T/n. From the displayed formula
for C and 1/u=n theta<=n pi, |Cg_v(u)|/n^2<=C_T/n on this range.
Consequently the defect is at most C_T/n for large angles.              (7)

### Sum the defects

C039 gives E theta_k^p<=C_(p,T)/(k+1)^p, and on every hybrid state
1/U_k=n theta_k. Sum (6) at the small-angle states, using the full
positive moment bounds as upper bounds. The resulting terms are

    C_T n^(-3/2), C_T/n^2,
    (C_T/n^2)sum_(k<N)1/(k+1)<=C_T log(n+1)/n^2,
    (C_T/n)sum_(k<N)1/(k+1)^2<=C_T/n,
    C_T n exp(-cn).

For (7), C039 at p=2 bounds the expected number of large-angle visits
by epsilon^(-2)sum E theta_k^2<=C_T. Its total contribution is C_T/n.
All displayed smaller terms are O(1/n), proving (1).

## C043: the terminal bounded-observable rate

For fixed t>0, N=floor(nt), let theta_N be the exact width-n Gaussian
zero-bias ReLU angle with fixed theta0 in (0,pi]. Define its observable
to be f(1/(n theta_N)) on nondegenerate paths and zero after killing.
Then, as n tends to infinity,

    E[f(1/(n theta_N));alive]
       =E[f(V_t^0)] + (D_t/(2pi))log(n)/n+O_(theta0,t)(1/n),   (8)

where

    D_t=D P_t f(0)=E[exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t-V_t^0)]>0.

Any other fixed bounded cemetery value changes (8) only exponentially
through time N, by the same hybrid coupling. In particular the leading
bounded-observable bias is positive and is of order log(n)/n, rather
than a pure c(t)/n expansion. The O(1/n) coefficient is not identified.

Proof. Set t_n=N/n and G_k=P_((N-k)/n)f. The exact semigroup relation
G_k=P_(1/n)G_(k+1) and the Markov property of the hybrid chain give

    E f(U_N)-P_(t_n)f(U0)
      =sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E[(Q_n-P_(1/n))G_(k+1)(U_k)].          (9)

All tests are bounded. Apply (1) to conclude that (9) equals

    (1/n^2)sum_(k=0)^(N-1) E[(C G_(k+1))(U_k)]+O(1/n).      (10)

The k=0 term is O_(theta0,t)(1/n): its singular part is bounded by
C/(n^2 U0)=C theta0/n, and the other terms are smaller. For k>=1,
C041's proof applies also to the one-step shifted test G_(k+1).
Explicitly, its first derivative differs from D_t by at most
C_t[(k+1)/n+u], because |t_n-t|<=1/n. Multiplying by theta_k and
using theta_k U_k=1/n and E theta_k<=C/(k+1) shows a bounded total
weighted error after summation. C040 gives

    sum_(k=1)^(N-1) E theta_k=(1/a)log(n)+O_(theta0,t)(1).

Thus the singular part of (10) is
(b/a)D_t log(n)/n+O(1/n). The remaining parts of C contribute O(1/n),
by bounded first and second test derivatives and the hybrid reciprocal
moment bounds (4) in C040. Since b/a=1/(2pi), this identifies (10).

Finally U0=1/(n theta0). Bounded D P_s f and bounded Af imply

    |P_(t_n)f(U0)-P_t f(0)|<=C_(theta0,t)/n.

This includes the initial-angle and fractional-layer effects at the
remainder order. The global hybrid coupling through N steps fails with
probability at most C_t n exp(-cn). Since f and its cemetery value are
bounded, transfer to the exact chain changes the expectation by that
order, which is smaller than 1/n. This proves (8).

## Scope and review priority

No exact-chain raw reciprocal moment is claimed or used. The proof
performs its martingale estimates on a finite-moment regularization,
then transfers bounded observables. The estimate is for the specified
smooth bounded test, not a total-variation, Wasserstein, joint-output or
full-path quantitative rate. Independent review should check (4)'s
uniformity in unbounded u, the hybrid coupling, and the covariance
calculation underlying B before accepting (8).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:48d5412d05f2566420246d906fe5e2cb5ea63da0a7aee9e2d7460ec5d88ae3f3","revision_digest":"sha256:fe4020fda7ee8bb5bc64e7c9222149cf2937451449a472e5282436a82c485792","source_id":"owner-own-work:T244-w691-C042:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Fix 0<rho<1 and independent standard normal Z_0,...,Z_m. Let X_i=sqrt(rho)*Z_0+sqrt(1-rho)*Z_i and M_m=max_i X_i. Coordinates have variance one and distinct covariance rho. Var(M_m)>=rho, so the field is not superconcentrated. Nevertheless the number of coordinates at deficit at most delta_m=(log m)^(-1/4) from M_m tends to infinity in probability. Thus growing near-peaks with pairwise covariance merely bounded away from one, even at vanishing absolute deficit, are insufficient for superconcentration. This does not refute a criterion requiring overlaps to tend to zero.
Independent standard Gaussian coordinates
Fixed positive common covariance rho
Candidate uses overlap bounded away from one, not overlap tending to zero

body:
[Lem 60 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The set $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$, as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}, is a singleton set consisting of the standard gaussian measure:
$\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)=\{\cN(0,1)\}$.
\begin{proof}
    Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$. By the definition \eqref{e:sM.Lip.q0}, this means that for any $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $L>0$ and a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_{N_j})_{j\ge 1}$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        &\WERR(\cA_{N_j}, \mu)
        =\max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big( \mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu \Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j}), \cP(\{\pm 1\}) \Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon\,, \\
        &q_0(j) \equiv \chi_{\cA_{N_j}}(0) 
        = \frac{\|\bbE \bsig_j\|_2^2}{N_j} 
        \stackrel{j\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 1
        \,,
    \end{align*}
where we abbreviate $\bsig_j\equiv \cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. 
    Define the perturbed (deterministic) algorithm $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ by setting 
    \[
        \tilde{\bsig}_j
        \equiv \tilde\cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux) 
        = \frac{\bbE\bsig_j}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} \,.
    \]
This clearly satisfies $\bbE[\|\tilde{\bsig}_j\|_2^2]  = N_j$, so $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ is a $0$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.
Since $\tilde{\bsig}_j$ is a deterministic vector in $N_j$ dimensions of norm $(N_j)^{1/2}$, we have $\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1)$.
    Note that
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\bbE[
            \|\bsig_j - \tilde{\bsig}_j\|^2]}{N_j} 
        &= \frac{1}{N_j} \bbE\bigg[ \bigg\|
            \bigg(\frac{1}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} - 1 \bigg) 
            	(\bbE\bsig_j)
            - (\bsig_j - \bbE\bsig_j)
        \bigg\|^2 \bigg] \\
        &= \Big(1 - q_0(j)^{1/2}\Big)^2 + \Big(1 - q_0(j)\Big)
        \le 2\Big(1-q_0(j)\Big)\,,
    \end{align*}  
again using that inequality $|x^{1/2}-y^{1/2}| \le |x-y|^{1/2}$ for $x,y\ge0$.
    Then, by Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.approx}, with constants $c_0$, $C_1(\alpha)$, $C_2(\alpha,L)$ as defined therein, we have
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j}),
        	\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1) 
	\Big)
        \le \bigg\{
        C_1(\alpha) 2(1-q_0(j)) + C_2(\alpha,L) e^{-c_0N_j} \bigg\}^{1/2}\,.
    \]
Combined with the assumption that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu) \le \epsilon$ for all $j$, we find $\bbW_2(\mu,\cN(0,1)) \le \epsilon$.
    Since this holds for all $\epsilon > 0$, we conclude $\mu = \cN(0,1)$.
    We have thus shown $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1) \subseteq \{\cN(0,1)\}$.
    The reverse inclusion $\cN(0,1) \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$ is witnessed by the (sequence of) deterministic algorithms
    \[
        \cA_N(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) = (1,\ldots,1) \in \bbR^N\,, 
    \]
    which are $0$-Lipschitz with $\mu(\cA_N) = \cN(0,1)$, $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N) = \delta_1 \in \cP(\{\pm 1\})$, and $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 1$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For a continuous curve gamma:[0,1]->C and r>=0,q>0, E(r,q) is the event that there exist s<t with |gamma(s)-gamma(t)|<=r and diameter(gamma([s,t]))>=q. A nonconstant self-return is equality gamma(s)=gamma(t) with a positive-diameter intervening subcurve. Constant waiting intervals are not nonconstant self-returns.
gamma is continuous on the compact interval [0,1]

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] The function \(K_{\nu,C}\) is a finite positive semidefinite kernel on
\(G\times J\).  It satisfies
\begin{align}
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((ar,j),(as,k)\bigr)
&=
\chi_\alpha(a)^{-1}
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,j),(s,k)\bigr),
\\
K_{\nu,C}\bigl((r,j),(r,j)\bigr)
&=
\chi_\alpha(r)^{-1}p_j.

\end{align}
If further  \(\mathsf T\) acts on \(J\), with the action denoted by
\((u,j)\mapsto uj\), \(\nu\) is \(B\)-invariant  and  
\[
C_{uj}=B^uC_j,
\qquad u\in\mathsf T,\quad j\in J,
\]

Let M(X) be the essential supremum of the density of X (M = infinity if there is no bounded density). (Thm 1) For independent random vectors X_1,...,X_n in R^d: M(X_1+...+X_n)^{-2/d} >= (1/e) sum_k M(X_k)^{-2/d}. (Cor 2) If M(X_k) <= M for all k and sum a_k^2 = 1, then M(sum a_kX_k) <= e^{d/2} M. (Closing remark, from Rogozin's theorem and Ball's cube slicing) For real X_k: M(S_n)^{-2} >= (1/2) sum_k M(X_k)^{-2}, and 1/2 is best possible (two independent uniforms on intervals of equal length give equality). 1/e is the dimension-free constant; for fixed d >= 2 the sharp constant is Gamma(1+d/2)^{2/d}/(1+d/2) (Madiman-Melbourne-Xu), which decreases to 1/e as d -> infinity.

Assumes: independence; random vectors in R^d (Thm 1, Cor 2); real variables (the 1/2 remark)

body:
Author-proved reduction awaiting independent review. In a proper strictly positive weighted graph, if a bigeodesic gamma uses an edge e of weight t_e, replacing only that weight by s in (0,t_e) preserves the entire bigeodesic. A finite straddling segment decreases by Delta=t_e-s; a simple competitor decreases by either Delta if it uses e or zero if it avoids e. Thus every e-avoiding competitor has new excess cost at least Delta. A subsegment on one side stays minimizing because it sits inside a minimizing straddling segment. In iid nonatomic positive FPP, positive probability of a bigeodesic through e implies positive probability of such a uniformly pinned bigeodesic under the same iid law: choose a<b<c with F(b)>0 and P(A_e,t_e>=c)>0, where a is the essential infimum, then independently resample s with law F. The event has probability F(b)*P(A_e,t_e>=c)>0 and penalty at least c-b. This multiplication uses exactly the fresh independent coordinate. No planar exclusion of these pinned paths is proved.

Every probability law F with bounded support, absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and symmetric about its mean is n-completely mixable for all sufficiently large n. No density floor or unimodality is assumed. A positive-measure density level set A on the positive half-line supplies a bounded odd-order zero-sum reserve by convolving differences until they reach A; global sign and coordinate permutation give a symmetric dominated marginal. The residual is symmetric and pairs, so the odd-order reserve lemma applies. The threshold depends on F; the nonsymmetric case is not resolved.

Statement. Let F be an absolutely continuous probability law with bounded support, symmetric about its mean mu. Then there is a finite N(F) such that F is n-CM for every integer n>=N(F). No pointwise lower bound on its density, no support interval without gaps, and no unimodality are assumed.

We will construct one odd-order symmetric reserve H with bounded density dominated by a positive multiple of f, and apply D0007-C002. The main open piece of D0007 is the nonsymmetric case, for which the residual-pair argument is unavailable.

1. Normalize mu=0. Write f for a symmetric version of the density, so f(-x)=f(x) almost everywhere. Choose M>0 bounding the support. Since F is absolutely continuous, it has no atom at zero and its mass in (0,M] is 1/2. There are eps>0 and a measurable set A subset (0,M] of positive Lebesgue measure a such that f(x)>=eps almost everywhere on A and also on -A. For example some level set {x in (0,M]:f(x)>=1/j} has positive measure, since the union of these sets carries all positive-half mass. Put u(x)=1_A(x)/a. This is a bounded probability density.

2. Let v=u*tilde(u), with tilde(u)(x)=u(-x). It is the density of Y-Y' for independent Y,Y' with density u. It is continuous and v(0)=1/a>0. To justify continuity directly, v(t)=|A intersect (A+t)|/a^2, and the absolute difference of v(t) and v(s) is bounded by ||1_A(.-t)-1_A(.-s)||_1/a^2. Translations are continuous in L1 for every finite-measure measurable set: approximate 1_A in L1 by finite linear combinations of bounded-interval indicators, whose translation continuity follows from the interval symmetric-difference bound, and use the triangle inequality. Thus choose delta>0 and c>0 with v(t)>=c for |t|<=delta.

3. Choose an integer k>=1 with k delta>M. The k-fold convolution v^{*k} is strictly positive at every t in (-k delta,k delta). Indeed v>=c 1_{[-delta,delta]}, so v^{*k}>=c^k (1_{[-delta,delta]})^{*k}; the latter is strictly positive in that open interval. For k>=2 this follows by integrating over a small open neighborhood of the first k-1 coordinates equal to t/k, leaving the last also within (-delta,delta); k=1 is immediate. Consequently

    Z=integral_A u(y) v^{*k}(y) dy

is positive. It is finite since every convolution density here is bounded above by ||u||_infinity=1/a.

4. An exact zero-sum probability vector. Draw a vector (Y_1,...,Y_{2k}) with joint density

    [ product_{i=1}^{2k} u(y_i) ] u(s(y)) / Z,
    s(y)=sum_{i=1}^k y_i - sum_{i=k+1}^{2k} y_i.

It integrates to one because s under the unweighted product law has density v^{*k}, and E[u(s)]=Z. Set Y_0=s(Y). The weight u(s) forces Y_0 in A, while all Y_i are in A almost surely. Form the odd vector W of length m=2k+1 with entries

    (Y_1,...,Y_k, -Y_{k+1},...,-Y_{2k}, -Y_0).

Its sum is exactly zero.

5. Each magnitude marginal has a bounded density on A. For any i from 1 to 2k, integrate the displayed joint density in every other variable. Conditional on y_i, the integral of u(s) over the remaining independent variables is at most ||u||_infinity=1/a. Thus the marginal density q_i(y) is <=u(y)/(aZ)<=1_A(y)/(a^2 Z). For Y_0, its density is q_0(y)=u(y)v^{*k}(y)/Z, with the same bound because ||v^{*k}||_infinity<=1/a. The sign in W changes support to -A where appropriate, without changing the bound.

6. Multiply W by an independent equiprobable sign, then apply an independent uniform permutation. The resulting vector has sum zero and identical symmetric marginals H. Their common density h is supported on A union -A and satisfies

    h(x)<=1/(2a^2 Z) almost everywhere on A union -A.

The factor 1/2 follows because A and -A are disjoint, and each globally randomized coordinate is a symmetric magnitude law with density q_i(|x|)/2. Averaging over coordinates preserves the bound. Hence H is symmetric and m-CM.

7. Set p=min(1/2,eps*a^2*Z)>0. Then p h<=eps/2<=f on A union -A, and p h=0 elsewhere. The residual density g=(f-ph)/(1-p) is a symmetric probability density with bounded support. Apply D0007-C002: F is n-CM for all even n and for every odd n with n>=m and np>=m. Thus N(F)=ceil(m/p) is a valid finite threshold. Translate all coordinates back by mu.

Proof checks: Z is positive by actual convolution mass on A, not by a conditional event claimed to have positive probability; the zero-sum law is defined by an explicit normalized density on 2k free coordinates. No conditioning on a zero-probability event is used. The result asserts existence of a finite threshold depending on f; it does not provide a uniform threshold for all symmetric laws.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:f4e31481a3746642e28f09563c5c3ae05905e7977db3ac4a873fc90af5355286","revision_digest":"sha256:fe6a033debb2bc4152ecdd5c46b00d58f6423fd0d901170fce4d015ee9a192dd","source_id":"owner-own-work:w662:D0007-C004:v1","source_revision":"v1 2026-10-14","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 13 (Robust separated batch) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] Suppose that for some $\eta>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \min\{\theta-x,\ x+a-\theta,\ \theta-(x+a-b)\}\ge\eta.
 
\end{equation}
Use the separated supports above, but let the actual initial left voltage
and aggregate input magnitudes be $x'$, $A\ge0$, and $B\ge0$.  Suppose that
under both orderings the continuous drift rate before a first hit has
magnitude at most $L_{\rm dr}$ and that
\begin{equation}
 |x'-x|+|A-a|+|B-b|+4L_{\rm dr}\varepsilon<\eta,
 \qquad 4\varepsilon<\rho.
 
\end{equation}
Then the target fires exactly once in the excitatory-first system and does
not fire in the inhibitory-first system on $[0,4\varepsilon]$.

[Theorem thm:dlsc of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho\in \mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$, a compact $K\subset \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$, and $\epsilon > 0$. Then on $K$, almost surely the half-space directed landscape $\mathcal{L}^\rho(x, s; y, t)$ is H\"older-$(1/2-\epsilon)$ continuous in $x$ and $y$ and H\"older-$(1/3-\epsilon)$ continuous in $s$ and $t$.
		
		Moreover, for any $b > 0$ there exists $c > 0$ and a random number $M > 0$ satisfying
		$
		\mathbb{P}(M > a) \le 2\exp(-ca^{3/2})
		$
		for all $a > 0$, such that for all $u = (x, t; y, t + s) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ with $s \le b$ we have
		$$
		\left|\mathcal{L}^\rho(u) + (x-y)^2/s \right|\le M s^{1/3} \log^{2}\left(\frac{2\|u\|_2}{s}\right).
		$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem HALFGODHALFSOUVLAKI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$
  and $0 < \theta < 1$. Assume that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^{\theta}} \log \mathbb{E} [H
    \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N
    (A))] = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then, for every $k \in
  \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th moment of the random measure $N^{- \theta} \sum_{i =
  1}^N \delta \left( N^{- 1} \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges, as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in
  probability to $\Psi^{(k)} (0) / (k - 1) !$.

Let $I=(r_0,r_1)$ and let $w_1,w_2$ be regular weights for the same reference
diffusion.  If $w_2/w_1$ is nondecreasing on $I$, then
\begin{equation*}
 C_{w_2,I}(X)\leq C_{w_1,I}(X).
\end{equation*}
In particular, the assertion is understood in $[0,\infty]$, with no prior
finiteness assumption on either side.
